```rust
pub struct SvmSpec { pub ver: u16, pub id: SvmId, pub name: String /* UTS nodename, <= 15 chars for NetBIOS */,
    pub ipspace: IpspaceId, pub home_node: NodeId, pub template: SvmTemplate /* Datastore | File | Backup | Custom */,
    pub protocols: BTreeSet<Proto> /* Iscsi | NvmeTcp | Fc | Nfs3 | Nfs41 | Smb | S3 */,
    pub root_volume: VolId, pub junctions: Vec<Junction>, pub lifs: Vec<LifSpec>,
    pub identity: Identity /* Standalone { users: Vec<LocalUser> } | Ad { realm, workgroup, rid_base } */,
    pub nfs: NfsCfg, pub smb: SmbCfg, pub s3: S3Cfg, pub exports: Vec<Export>, pub shares: Vec<Share>,
    pub slice: SliceCfg /* cpu_weight, memory_max, memory_high, tasks_max */, pub qos: Vec<(VolId, QosPolicy)> }
pub struct Junction { pub path: String /* "/vm/iso" */, pub volume: VolId }
pub trait SvmLifecycle {                            // implemented by nbladed's svm module; one call per Raft transition
    fn create(&mut self, spec: &SvmSpec) -> Result<(), SvmErr>;
    fn start(&mut self, id: SvmId, presence: Presence) -> Result<(), SvmErr>;      // idempotent; resumes a Failed start
    fn stop(&mut self, id: SvmId, deadline: Duration) -> Result<(), SvmErr>;        // the ladder T1..T6 with per-step timeouts
    fn apply(&mut self, id: SvmId, delta: &SvmDelta) -> Result<(), SvmErr>;         // protocol toggles, LIF, export, share, QoS
    fn delete(&mut self, id: SvmId) -> Result<(), SvmErr>;
    fn state(&self, id: SvmId) -> SvmState;
    fn exported_state(&self, id: SvmId) -> Vec<StateBlob>;                          // for ProtocolBlade::exported_state
}
```

##### 2.3 Junction paths and the global namespace

The SVM view, built by `otap-nsinit` and pivoted into with `pivot_root`:

```
/                     tmpfs, private, size=1M: the SVM view root
├─ usr bin sbin lib lib64 etc var dev proc sys     recursive binds of the host's, made rslave
├─ etc/{nfs.conf,exports,idmapd.conf,resolv.conf,hosts,krb5.conf,passwd,group,nsswitch.conf,samba/smb.conf}
│                     file binds from /run/opentap/svm/<id>/etc (generated from Raft at every start)
├─ run                private tmpfs: rpcbind.sock, samba/{winbindd,ncalrpc,*.pid}, systemd/notify (bind of the host socket)
├─ var/lib/nfs        tmpfs; sm, sm.bak, state, nfsdcld bound from the root volume's .otap/nfs; rpc_pipefs mounted here
├─ proc/fs/nfsd       the per-netns nfsd instance, mounted from inside the netns
├─ vol/<svm>_root     recursive bind, rslave, of the host's root-volume mount (daemon state under .otap)
└─ /vm /home /backup  one bind per top-level junction: /vol/<svm>_root/<top> -> /<top>
```

A junction `/vm/iso` is a volume mounted by `nbladed` in the host namespace at `/vol/<svm>_root/vm/iso`, where `vm` is a directory in the root volume's XFS, or inside the `vm` volume if `/vm` is itself a junction. Mount order is path depth; nesting is unlimited; the mount point directory is created by `nbladed` when the junction is declared. Propagation does the rest: the host's mounts are shared (the systemd default), the SVM view's binds are slaves, so a volume mounted later on the host under `/vol/<svm>_root` appears in the SVM view in the same syscall, and the SVM's private overlays never propagate back. A 40-line test in C2 proves this on 6.12 before anything depends on it. The host's `/vol` is itself a tmpfs so that mount-point directories never land on the boot disk.

Top-level junction names are reserved against `usr bin sbin lib lib64 etc var dev proc sys run tmp root home boot opt srv mnt media vol lost+found .otap .snapshot` and must match `[a-z0-9_-]{1,64}`; the Raft validator refuses the rest. Paths seen by the protocols are SVM-view paths: NFSv3 clients mount `svm:/vm` through mountd; NFSv4.1 clients see `/vm` through the pseudo-root that mountd synthesizes from the exported paths with `NFSEXP_V4ROOT` (0x10000 on 6.12 [verified: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/include/uapi/linux/nfsd/export.h]); no `fsid=0` export of the tmpfs root, so `ls svm:/` lists only exported junctions [believed, nfs-utils `v4root` behaviour since 1.2.2]. Each export carries `fsid=<volume UUID>` in the 32-hex-digit form [verified: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/exports.5.html]; the UUID is the identity that survives a move and receives the nvfail generation of 2.11. SMB shares use `path = /home/projects`; the S3 gateway root is `/backup/veeam` with `--versioning-dir /backup/.versions`, outside the gateway root but on the same volume so one CP covers both [verified: https://github.com/versity/versitygw/wiki/Posix-Backend]. No volume is ever visible in two SVM views; `volume rehost` is a Phase B administrative operation with the uid caveat of 2.6. Snapshot mounts follow R21: outside share and bucket roots at `/vol/<svm>_root/.otap/snap/<vol>/@GMT-YYYY.MM.DD-HH.MM.SS`, read-only clone LUNs mounted `ro,nouuid,norecovery`, exposed to Windows by `vfs_shadow_copy2` with an absolute `shadow:snapdir` and `shadow:basedir`; an ONTAP-style `.snapshot` inside the junction is Phase B.

Cost: 20 to 30 mounts per SVM, 64 SVMs are about 2,000 mounts on the node, none of which appear in the host's mount table.

##### 2.4 What lives on the root volume versus what is declarative in Raft

The rule: the root volume holds everything a daemon mutates by itself; Raft holds everything an operator declares; `nbladed` never reconciles between the two, because daemon-owned files are opaque blobs that travel with the SVM and declared state is regenerated into tmpfs on every start.

| Item | Where | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `secrets.tdb`, `schannel_store.tdb` (machine account; rotated by winbindd every 604800 s by default [verified: smb.conf(5)]) | root volume `.otap/samba/private` | Samba writes it without telling us |
| `krb5.keytab` (`cifs/`, `nfs/`, `HOST/` SPNs) | root volume `.otap/samba/private` | written by `net ads join` and keytab rotation |
| `winbindd_idmap.tdb`, `group_mapping.tdb`, `share_info.tdb`, `account_policy.tdb`, `registry.tdb` | root volume `.otap/samba/state` | allocated ids and Windows-set share ACLs are Samba's |
| `gencache.tdb`, `winbindd_cache.tdb` | root volume `.otap/samba/cache` | rebuildable; kept for a warm start after a move |
| statd `sm/`, `sm.bak/`, `state` | root volume `.otap/nfs/statd` | the NSM state number must stay monotonic across nodes |
| nfsdcld `main.sqlite` | root volume `.otap/nfs/nfsdcld` | NFSv4 client reclaim database [verified: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man8/nfsdcld.8.html] |
| `passdb.tdb` (local SMB users) | regenerated at start from Raft (sealed NT hashes rendered in smbpasswd format, imported with `pdbedit -i smbpasswd: -e tdbsam:`) | the root-volume copy is a cache |
| `smb.conf`, `exports`, `nfs.conf`, `idmapd.conf`, `krb5.conf`, `resolv.conf`, `hosts`, `passwd`, `group`, nftables ruleset, versitygw arguments and `users.json` | Raft, rendered into `/run/opentap/svm/<id>/etc` | declared, never edited in place |
| TLS certificate and key, S3 root keys, CHAP secrets, local-user NT hashes | Raft, sealed with the cluster key (R23), materialized 0600 into tmpfs | the witness never holds plaintext |
| AD join credentials | nowhere; used once by `net ads join` | |
| Junction mount-point directories | root volume (directories only) | |

The root volume is 1 GiB thin and typically under 100 MiB used: tdbs under 10 MiB, nfsdcld under 1 MiB for 1,000 clients, one `sm` file per NFSv3 client. It ships in the same consistency group as the SVM's data volumes (question to Storage and Consensus in section 6).

##### 2.5 knfsd per network namespace

| Daemon | Invocation inside the SVM view | State |
|---|---|---|
| rpcbind | `rpcbind -f` | `/run/rpcbind.sock`, `/run/rpcbind/*.xdr` in the private `/run` |
| rpc.statd | `rpc.statd -F -L -P /vol/<svm>_root/.otap/nfs/statd -p 32765 -o 32766 --nlm-port 4045 --nlm-udp-port 4045` (`-L` is the no-notify flag; `-N` runs sm-notify and exits) [verified: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man8/rpc.statd.8.html] | root volume |
| rpc.mountd | `rpc.mountd -F -p 20048 -s /var/lib/nfs -N 4` (datastore) or `-N 2 -N 3` (file) [verified: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man8/rpc.mountd.8.html] | `etab`, `rmtab` in tmpfs |
| nfsdcld | `nfsdcld -F -p /var/lib/nfs/rpc_pipefs -s /vol/<svm>_root/.otap/nfs/nfsdcld` [verified: nfsdcld(8)] | root volume |
| rpc.idmapd | `rpc.idmapd -f -S` (server side only) | none |
| rpc.nfsd | `rpc.nfsd 16` with the `nfs.conf` overlay below; oneshot, `ExecStop=rpc.nfsd 0` | kernel |

Everything in this table is per instance: `threads`, `portlist`, `versions`, `nfsv4leasetime`, `nfsv4gracetime` and `v4_end_grace` are files of the per-netns `nfsd` filesystem, and the netlink handlers `nfsd_nl_threads_set_doit`, `nfsd_nl_listener_set_doit` and `nfsd_nl_version_set_doit` exist on 6.12 for nfs-utils to use instead [verified: nfsctl.c above]. lockd's `fs.nfs.nlm_grace_period` and `nlm_tcpport` are single global values, but the grace timer is armed per network namespace in `lockd_up_net()` [verified: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/fs/lockd/svc.c], so every SVM gets its own 20 s NLM grace on the same port number, which is fine because each netns has its own port space. The kernel registers nfsd with rpcbind through `/run/rpcbind.sock` resolved in the mount namespace of the process that called `nfsd_svc()`, falling back to 127.0.0.1:111 of the netns [believed], which is why `lo` is up before rpcbind starts. `rpc.nfsd --scope` is unnecessary because rpc.nfsd already runs in the SVM's UTS namespace; it is accepted as an explicit equivalent.

```ini
#### /etc/nfs.conf overlay for a file SVM (keys believed; the command-line equivalents are verified)
[general]  pipefs-directory=/var/lib/nfs/rpc_pipefs
[nfsd]     threads=16  vers3=n  vers4=y  vers4.0=n  vers4.1=y  vers4.2=n  grace-time=20  lease-time=10  port=2049
[mountd]   port=20048  state-directory-path=/var/lib/nfs
[statd]    port=32765  outgoing-port=32766  state-directory-path=/vol/hv01_root/.otap/nfs/statd  no-notify=1
[lockd]    port=4045  udp-port=4045
[nfsdcld]  storagedir=/vol/hv01_root/.otap/nfs/nfsdcld
```

Templates: a datastore SVM is NFSv3 only with 32 threads (ESXi and Proxmox; ESXi uses no NLM, Proxmox's qemu does); a file SVM is NFSv4.1 only with lease 10 s and grace 20 s, delegations off, exactly R8. Fixed ports make the nftables ruleset static: 111, 2049, 20048, 32765, 4045 TCP and UDP.

**Grace after a start or move.** nfsd starts in grace in the new netns; `nbladed` writes `v4_end_grace` as soon as every client in the nfsdcld database has reclaimed (its tally comes from `/proc/fs/nfsd/clients`), and an empty database skips grace (Appendix A). Because the nfsdcld database and the data volumes are in one consistency group, a client can never hold state newer than the data it reclaims against.

**NFSv3 lock recovery after a move.** Order: LIF addresses up, then `nbladed` runs `sm-notify -f -P /vol/<svm>_root/.otap/nfs/statd` inside the netns. Without `-v`, sm-notify uses "the mon_name recorded when the remote was monitored" and a wildcard source address [verified: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man8/sm-notify.8.html], so each client is told about the server name it actually used, whichever LIF that was; the state number in `state` increments on the root volume, so it is monotonic across nodes; clients reclaim within lockd's 20 s grace. The hole, shared with ONTAP: a client that recorded a LIF address the SVM no longer owns is never notified and loses its locks silently; `nbladed` alerts on `sm` entries whose `my_name` is not a current LIF.

##### 2.6 Samba 4.22 multi-instance and the identity collisions

Directories that must be separate per instance, all settable in smb.conf [verified: smb.conf(5)]: `private dir` (`secrets.tdb`, `passdb.tdb`), `state directory` (persistent tdbs), `cache directory`, `lock directory` (safe on tmpfs), `pid directory`, `ncalrpc dir`, `winbindd socket directory`, plus `dedicated keytab file` with `kerberos method = secrets and keytab`. With the private `/run` and the root-volume binds, the generated file is:

```ini
[global]
netbios name = HV01            ; = UTS nodename; 15-character limit enforced on SVM names
workgroup = LAB                 ; realm = LAB.EXAMPLE.ORG ; security = ads   (or security = user when standalone)
kerberos method = secrets and keytab
dedicated keytab file = /vol/hv01_root/.otap/samba/private/krb5.keytab
private dir = /vol/hv01_root/.otap/samba/private
state directory = /vol/hv01_root/.otap/samba/state
cache directory = /vol/hv01_root/.otap/samba/cache
lock directory = /run/samba ; pid directory = /run/samba ; ncalrpc dir = /run/samba/ncalrpc
winbindd socket directory = /run/samba/winbindd      ; and WINBINDD_SOCKET_DIR in the unit environment
logging = systemd@1 ; disable netbios = yes ; smb ports = 445
server min protocol = SMB3_00 ; server signing = mandatory
idmap config * : backend = tdb ; idmap config * : range = 3000000-3999999
idmap config LAB : backend = rid ; idmap config LAB : range = 10000000-19999999   ; base from Raft per domain
machine password timeout = 604800 ; kernel oplocks = no ; kernel share modes = no
```

Per SVM: `smbd -F --no-process-group -s /etc/samba/smb.conf` and, when AD-joined, `winbindd -F --no-process-group -s ...`; never nmbd. Each SVM joins AD as its own computer object (`net ads join -s <smb.conf>` run inside the namespaces), so it owns its SPNs `cifs/hv01.lab.example.org`, `nfs/hv01.lab.example.org` and `HOST/HV01`, its machine password and its keytab.

Identity collisions found, and the rule for each:

1. SVM names must be unique cluster-wide and at most 15 characters: they are UTS nodenames, NFSv4 server scopes, NetBIOS names and AD computer objects. Two SVMs with one name would make an NFSv4.1 client treat them as one server and attempt trunking.
2. AD computer objects: delete must run `net ads leave`, or the stale object blocks a re-created SVM of the same name.
3. `krb5.conf` is per SVM (default realm differs per tenant); `KRB5_CONFIG` is set in the unit environment and the file is overlaid.
4. Winbind socket: `libnss_winbind` and `libwbclient` connect to `/run/samba/winbindd`; each SVM's private `/run` makes that the SVM's own winbindd; host tools never see it, so `nbladed` queries with `nsenter` or `WINBINDD_SOCKET_DIR`.
5. Idmap: two SVMs joined to the same domain must map one SID to one uid, or `volume rehost` and host-side backup break; therefore `rid` with a per-domain base kept in Raft, never `autorid`, and the `*` tdb range disjoint from every domain range.
6. Local SMB users need Unix accounts: `/etc/passwd` and `/etc/group` are generated per SVM from Raft with uids in 1000000 to 1999999; the host's accounts are not visible except `root`, `nobody` and `daemon`.
7. NFS `sec=sys` uids come from clients and are not mapped (UNIX security style); SMB local uids and AD RID uids are in disjoint ranges from anything a NFS client is likely to send.
8. S3 objects are written as versitygw's process uid (or `--chuid` per user [verified: Posix-Backend wiki]); S3 buckets live on S3-only volumes, the same rule as the two SMB share classes.
9. Machine password rotation versus replication lag (Phase B): a rotation inside the lost window leaves the partner with a password the DC no longer accepts ("the trust relationship failed"). `nbladed` watches `secrets.tdb` with inotify 0.11.5 [verified: https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/inotify] and requests an immediate CP and ship of the root volume; the fallback knob is `machine password timeout = 0`.
10. Windows-set share permissions land in `share_info.tdb` on the root volume, not in Raft; `otapctl share show` reads both and flags drift.
11. Port and socket collisions are gone by construction: 445, 111, 2049 and the unix sockets are per namespace.
12. DNS: each SVM registers its own A record from its own netns with its own credentials (`net ads dns register`); `/etc/hosts` carries the SVM's own FQDN so Kerberos works before DNS does.

Durable handles keep R8's rule: `kernel oplocks = no` and `kernel share modes = no` are the 4.22 defaults [verified: smb.conf(5)], SMB-only shares get durable handles and leases, multiprotocol shares are Phase 3 (R20). `winbind offline logon` stays off.

##### 2.7 versitygw per SVM

versitygw v1.8.0 (2026-09-04) is the latest release [verified: https://github.com/versity/versitygw/releases]. Per SVM, inside the namespaces: `versitygw --access <root> --secret <root> --port :443 --cert /run/opentap/svm/<id>/tls/cert.pem --key .../key.pem --iam-dir /run/opentap/svm/<id>/iam --region <r> --health /health posix /backup/veeam --versioning-dir /backup/.versions`, flags per the wiki [verified: https://github.com/versity/versitygw/wiki/Global-Options and the Posix-Backend page]. The admin API is not exposed (`--admin-port` unset); S3 users are declared in Raft with sealed secret keys and rendered into the IAM directory at start, so the daemon-owned mutable set stays small. Each SVM has its own certificate (SAN = the SVM's FQDN), stored sealed in Raft and materialized 0600 into tmpfs; rotation is a versitygw restart (connections reset; Veeam retries). `GOMEMLIMIT` is set to 80% of the slice's `MemoryMax`.

Object Lock and Veeam. Veeam requires versioning plus Object Lock enabled at bucket creation, uses Compliance mode per object, and forbids bucket default retention and lifecycle rules [verified: https://helpcenter.veeam.com/docs/backup/vsphere/os_immutability_limitations.html]. Two caveats: `--object-lock-mode` is publish locking for conditional writes, not S3 Object Lock, and POSIX versioning is labelled experimental [verified: Posix-Backend wiki]; and the fix that stores bucket default retention on each object at write time (PR #2479) merged on 2026-10-08, after v1.8.0 [verified: https://github.com/versity/versitygw/pull/2479]. Veeam does not use default retention, so v1.8.0 is usable for the Phase C Veeam test, but the shipped binary is pinned to the first release containing #2479, and the "experimental versioning" label stays on the product page. Sizing: about two cores per GB/s (round 2), 150 MiB idle RSS [believed], Veeam jobs at 10GbE need 1 GiB of heap, hence the backup template's 6 GiB slice.

##### 2.8 Where the block targets live: LIO portals, nvmet ports, Fibre Channel

Verified on 6.12: `iscsit_setup_np()` creates the listening socket with `sock_create(sockaddr->ss_family, np->np_sock_type, np->np_ip_proto, &sock)` [verified: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/target/iscsi/iscsi_target_login.c], `nvmet_tcp_add_port()` with `sock_create(port->addr.ss_family, SOCK_STREAM, IPPROTO_TCP, &port->sock)` [verified: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/nvme/target/tcp.c], and `sock_create()` is `__sock_create(current->nsproxy->net_ns, ...)` [verified: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/net/socket.c]. The `mkdir` of `/sys/kernel/config/target/iscsi/<iqn>/tpgt_1/np/<ip>:3260` and the link of an nvmet port to a subsystem therefore bind in the namespace of the writing task. `nbladed` writes those entries from a thread that has entered the SVM's netns; everything else in configfs is node-global and written from `init_net`.

Decision: iSCSI and NVMe/TCP are SVM protocols. One target per SVM (`iqn.2026-10.org.opentap:<cluster>.<svm>`, `nqn.2026-10.org.opentap:<cluster>.<svm>`), the SVM's block LIFs as portals, initiator groups as LIO ACLs with per-initiator LUN maps, ALUA groups per aggregate as in round 2. Two consequences of the verified code. First, `iscsit_get_np()` walks the global `g_np_list` and matches on address, port and transport only, with no namespace in the match, and `iscsit_add_np()` returns the existing portal with `np_exports` incremented [verified: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/target/iscsi/iscsi_target.c]: two SVMs in different IPspaces that both declare 10.0.0.5:3260 would silently share one socket in the first SVM's namespace, so the Raft validator requires block LIF addresses to be unique cluster-wide, across IPspaces, and the installer's documentation says why. Second, a socket created with `sock_create()` holds a reference on its netns [believed], so a portal left behind keeps a dead SVM's namespace, interfaces and addresses alive on the wire; the stop ladder removes portals and ports (T3) and deletes the LIF devices (T4) before the pins go. nvmet resolves IPv6 scope ids against `init_net` [verified: tcp.c above], so IPv6 link-local port addresses are refused until Phase B.

Fibre Channel has no namespace. FC targets stay at node level in Phase C step 3: the physical port's WWPN as the target, the SVM's LUNs mapped to its initiators through ACLs, `nbladed` writing the `qla2xxx` fabric directory from `init_net`. An NPIV virtual port per SVM as an FC LIF that moves with the SVM is a Phase B item owned with Fabrics (section 6).

Phase A split: ALUA standby paths need the SVM's target present on the partner while the NAS half is not, hence `Presence::BlockStandby` in 2.2: the partner instantiates the SVM's namespaces with block LIFs only (ONTAP's SAN LIFs do not migrate either). In Phase B, with private disks, a standby path would be a lie (round 2), so the SVM runs on one node and its block LIFs move with it: when the LIF reappears on node B, the initiator's retransmits meet B's kernel, which answers RST, and the initiator re-logs in within one retransmission interval; no RST proxy is needed for planned moves.

##### 2.9 LIF implementation

| Option | MAC | Cost at 10GbE | Where it fits |
|---|---|---|---|
| macvlan, bridge mode, on `bond0.<vlan>` | per LIF, locally administered, assigned by Raft | about 0.3 us per packet: 0.25 core at 1500 B line rate, 0.04 core at 9000 B [believed] | the default on bare metal |
| ipvlan L2 | shares the parent's MAC | same as macvlan | OpenTAP as a VM on a vSwitch that rejects MAC changes and forged transmits |
| veth plus bridge | per LIF | about twice macvlan (two devices plus bridge forwarding) [believed] | only where the operator already runs a Linux bridge |
| SR-IOV VF moved into the netns | per LIF, set by the PF (`ip link set <pf> vf N mac <mac> vlan <vid> spoofchk on`) | zero software cost; VLAN filtering in hardware | opt-in per port; ixgbe 63 VFs, i40e 128, mlx5 127 [believed] |

MAC persistence is the point. A LIF's MAC is `02:4f:54:` plus three bytes of `hash(cluster_uuid, lif_id)`, locally administered, multicast bit clear, stored in `LifSpec`, and brought up on whichever node and port hosts the LIF; a move is then a MAC move that every switch handles by table update, and no client ARP cache changes at all. Gratuitous ARP is still sent, three replies at 0, 300 ms and 1 s from an AF_PACKET socket opened on an `nbladed` thread inside the netns (socket2 crate [believed]), plus `arp_notify=1` on the device; it only matters for ipvlan, where the MAC does change and clients must accept the update (Linux and ESXi update existing entries; Windows behaviour is documented as [believed]). Broadcast domains are `(port, vlan)`: `nbladed` creates `bond0` (802.3ad) and `bond0.<vlan>` devices in `init_net` from Raft, the installer leaves data ports unconfigured, and the LIF device is created with `IFLA_NET_NS_FD` straight into the SVM's netns (rtnetlink 0.23.0 [verified: https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/rtnetlink]). MTU follows the broadcast domain (9000 recommended for datastores). Per-SVM nftables 1.1.3-1 [verified: https://packages.debian.org/trixie/nftables] rulesets are stateless (accept by LIF address and service port, drop the rest, no `ct` so no conntrack per netns), loaded with `nft -f` under `nsenter` (the nftables crate 0.6.3 renders the JSON [verified: https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/nftables]). IPv4 only in Phase C.

```toml
[svm]      name = "hv01"  ipspace = "default"  home_node = "node-a"  template = "datastore"  protocols = ["iscsi", "nfs3"]
[svm.root_volume]  volume = "hv01_root"
[[svm.lif]]  name = "lif1"  port = "bond0"  vlan = 100  impl = "macvlan"
             address = "10.10.100.21/24"  gateway = "10.10.100.1"  mac = "02:4f:54:3a:91:21"  services = ["nfs", "iscsi"]
[[svm.junction]]  path = "/vm"  volume = "hv01_vm01"
[[svm.export]]    path = "/vm"  clients = ["10.10.100.0/24"]  options = "rw,sync,no_root_squash,no_subtree_check,sec=sys"
[svm.nfs]   threads = 32  nlm_grace_s = 20
[svm.slice] cpu_weight = 200  memory_max = "1 GiB"  memory_high = "768 MiB"
[[svm.qos]] volume = "hv01_vm01"  max_iops = 20000  max_mbps = 800  burst_ms = 100
```

##### 2.10 Resource governance: slices and the per-volume QoS that fills the gap

| Consumer | Governed by `svm-<id>.slice`? | Why |
|---|---|---|
| smbd, winbindd, rpcbind, statd, mountd, nfsdcld, idmapd, versitygw CPU and RSS | yes: `CPUWeight`, `MemoryMax`, `MemoryHigh`, `TasksMax` | ordinary processes |
| Page cache written by smbd and versitygw | yes | charged to the cgroup that instantiated it; cgroup writeback is implemented on xfs [verified: https://docs.kernel.org/admin-guide/cgroup-v2.html] |
| nfsd kernel threads CPU | no | kthreads live in the root cgroup; root threads compete as nice-weighted pseudo-children, so 32 nfsd threads outweigh any slice [verified: cgroup-v2.html]; migrating them is refused only for `PF_NO_SETAFFINITY` threads [verified: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/kernel/cgroup/cgroup.c], but moving kthreads into tenant cgroups is unsupported practice and not done |
| Page cache written by nfsd | no | root cgroup; bounded node-wide by `vm.dirty_bytes` 2 GiB and `vm.dirty_background_bytes` 1 GiB, consistent with `dirty_expire` 2 s |
| Engine I/O, ublk handlers, CP flusher | no | isolated cores per R16; never in a slice |

Per-volume QoS fills the gap at the one point every protocol passes: the ublk queue handler in `dbladed`. `QosPolicy { max_iops: u32, max_mbps: u32, burst_ms: u16 }` is a token bucket per volume refilled every 1 ms, enforced by delaying completion of the request that overdraws it, never by failing it, with a hold cap of 1 s so that initiator timers (ESXi 10 to 35 s, Windows 60 s, NFS clients' RPC retransmit) are never approached; the initiator's own queue depth then throttles the source. Minimum enforceable rate is queue depth per second (QD 32 gives 32 IOPS); added jitter is at most 1 ms. For NAS volumes the throttle acts on XFS writeback, so page cache absorbs bursts until `dirty_bytes` and NFS COMMIT or SMB flush latency grows: that is the intended signal. SVM-level buckets (a sum across its volumes) are Phase B; floors (`min_iops`) are deferred. Defaults per template: datastore `CPUWeight=200`, `MemoryMax=1 GiB`; file 100 and 4 GiB; backup 50 and 6 GiB; `svm.slice` itself `MemoryMax=36 GiB` on a 64 GB node (2.13).

##### 2.11 nvfail from the client's side

Goal: after a rollback to the last applied CP, no client may silently resume against a filesystem behind its own journal. The posture per protocol, applied to each volume whose dirty-since-CP bit was set:

| Protocol, client | At nvfail | What the client sees | After `otapctl nvfail clear` |
|---|---|---|---|
| iSCSI, ESXi 8 | the LUN is unmapped from the TPG; LIO answers LOGICAL UNIT NOT SUPPORTED (05h/25h/00h) [believed: `TCM_NON_EXISTENT_LUN`] | PDL within one path evaluation (at most 5 s): VM I/O errors, datastore marked PDL, PDL AutoRemove may remove the device [verified: https://knowledge.broadcom.com/external/article/318712] | remap, rescan, power VMs off and on; never resume |
| iSCSI, Proxmox 8 and 9, Debian | same | TUR fails, path down, `no_path_retry 12` in the shipped multipath.conf fails I/O after 60 s, qemu `werror=stop` pauses the VM [believed] | remap; the VM must be reset, not resumed; the clear command prints this |
| iSCSI, Windows 11 | same | disk errors after MaxRequestHoldTime 60 s; NTFS marks the volume dirty | rescan, chkdsk, restart applications |
| NFSv3, ESXi | export removed | datastore inaccessible (hang, no writes land) | re-export with `fsid=<uuid>` replaced by the next generation (UUID with the last byte incremented): every cached handle is ESTALE, the datastore stays inaccessible until unmounted and remounted, VMs restart |
| NFS, Proxmox, Debian | same | hang, then ESTALE: qemu I/O errors, VM stopped | `umount -f`, remount, restart VMs |
| SMB, Windows 11 | share `available = no`, `smbcontrol smbd reload-config` | STATUS_BAD_NETWORK_NAME; open handles invalid; delayed-write failures for leased files | `available = yes`; users reopen |
| S3, Veeam | versitygw stopped for that SVM | connection refused; Veeam job fails and retries | restart; lock metadata is file metadata at the CP |

NOT READY (02h/04h) is rejected because ESXi treats a device without PDL sense as APD and keeps retrying until the LUN returns, then resumes silently, which is the hazard nvfail exists to prevent [verified: KB 318712]. Changing the LUN serial would force a VMFS resignature on ESXi and a new WWID on Linux, the strongest possible forcing function, but it renames datastores and is offered only as `nvfail_policy = strict` per LUN, later. The NFS generation lives beside the volume UUID in the superblock (question to Storage).

|---|---|---|

| Proxmox 8.4 and 9.0 | open-iscsi, multipath-tools with the shipped `multipath.conf` (`alua`, `tur`, `no_path_retry 12`), LVM on the LUN | 24 h soak; live migration between two PVE hosts on the shared LUN; nvfail fails I/O after 60 s with the VM paused |
| Windows 11 24H2 | Microsoft initiator, mutual CHAP, NTFS, defaults (hold 60 s) | 24 h diskspd soak; 100 `svm stop/start` cycles with a pause at most 15 s and zero errors |
| Debian 13 | open-iscsi plus dm-multipath; libiscsi `iscsi-test-cu` | the LIO baseline suite passes; `dm-log-writes` through the LUN: 1,000 cut points mount clean on ext4 and XFS |
| All | one node, 10GbE | 1.0 GB/s sequential per port on at most two cores for target, ublk and engine front end; 50,000 4 KiB IOPS at QD32 on at most three cores; LIF move between two ports of the node pauses at most 2 s; 100 `svm stop/start` cycles resume every initiator within 15 s |

|---|---|---|
| ESXi 8 | NFSv3 datastore on a datastore SVM; NFS 4.1 datastore as a non-default test [believed: supported] | VM boot, clone, snapshot soak 24 h; 4 KiB FILE_SYNC write p50 at most 300 us; 1.0 GB/s per port with knfsd on at most three cores; 100 `svm stop/start` cycles with a pause at most 5 s and zero errors; nvfail leaves the datastore inaccessible and ESTALE after clear |
| Proxmox 8.4 and 9.0 | NFSv3 with NLM, and NFSv4.1 | 50 SVM restarts with qcow2 VMs holding locks: every lock reclaimed inside the 20 s grace after `sm-notify`, no "failed to get lock"; v4.1 clients reclaim inside grace |
| Debian 13 | NFSv4.1 file SVM, 20 clients with opens and locks; NFSv3; cifs.ko SMB3 | 100 SVM restarts: all state reclaimed, early grace end within 5 s once every client has reclaimed, a client idle 60 s keeps its state (the N1 courteous-server measurement), no STALE_CLIENTID loops |
| Windows 11 24H2 | SMB 3.1.1, signing and encryption, SMB-only share class, standalone then AD | durable handle reconnect keeps a copy running through a 10 s LIF blip; 100 SVM restarts reconnect within 20 s with open-handle errors as documented; Previous Versions lists three manual snapshots; robocopy of 1 TiB at 0.6 GB/s per smbd |
| AD matrix | two SVMs in one domain, one in a second | identical uids for one SID in both same-domain SVMs (`wbinfo -S` through `nsenter`), separate computer objects and keytabs, Kerberos logons on all three, SVM-1 processes cannot reach SVM-2's winbind socket |

**Step 3, FC-SCSI client targets via `tcm_qla2xxx`** (with Fabrics): ESXi 8 and Proxmox 8 and 9 with QLogic initiators, Debian 13 with an HBA; Windows 11 is out of the matrix. My exit criteria: the SVM's LUNs mapped through the node-level target with per-initiator ACLs; 100 cable pulls with re-login under 5 s; nvfail presents the same unmapped-LUN sense; the SVM stop ladder removes FC LUN maps before the namespaces go. Fabrics owns firmware, `qlini_mode`, claim rules and `Disk.MaxLUN`.

##### 2.13 Memory model for a 64 GB node

| Consumer | Size | Assumption |
|---|---|---|
| Namespaces, pins, tmpfs view, nftables per SVM | 2 MiB | `lo` plus two macvlans, 25 mounts, no conntrack |
| rpcbind, statd, mountd, nfsdcld, idmapd | 14 MiB | RSS 2, 2, 5, 3, 2 MiB [believed] |
| nfsd threads | 18 MiB (16 threads), 35 MiB (32) | 1 MiB payload buffer plus stack per thread; root cgroup |
| smbd | 12 MiB plus 10 MiB per connection | fork per connection in 4.22 [believed]; 50 clients is 0.5 GiB |
| winbindd | 25 MiB plus 5 MiB per domain child | |
| versitygw | 150 MiB idle, `GOMEMLIMIT` 0.8 x `MemoryMax` | Go heap [believed] |
| Fixed cost per SVM | 25 MiB standalone, 60 MiB with AD; 64 SVMs at most 4 GiB | the installer caps SVMs at 64 per node |
| `svm.slice` `MemoryMax` | 36 GiB | 64 minus 8 (arena) minus 6 (map cache) minus 0.3 minus 0.6 minus 1.5 (md stripe cache) minus 0.5 (daemons) minus 8 (headroom) is 39.1, rounded down 3 GiB for knfsd's unattributed cache; Storage's revised engine budget may return the 8 GiB inbound ring |
| Node dirty pages | `vm.dirty_bytes` 2 GiB, `vm.dirty_background_bytes` 1 GiB | 2 s of `dirty_expire` at 1 GB/s |
| Template `MemoryMax` | datastore 1 GiB, file 4 GiB, backup 6 GiB | `MemoryHigh` at 75% so page cache is reclaimed before anything is killed |

##### 2.14 Crates and kernel interfaces

Crates, all on crates.io today: rustix 1.1.5 (namespaces, mounts, `sethostname` via nix 0.31.3), zbus 5.19.0 (transient units, slices), rtnetlink 0.23.0 (bond, vlan, macvlan, ipvlan, VF, addresses, routes, `IFLA_NET_NS_FD`), tokio 1.53.2 (control plane), nftables 0.6.3 (ruleset JSON for `nft`), toml 1.1.8 (configuration rendering and export), inotify 0.11.5 (`secrets.tdb`, APTPL), socket2 for GARP [believed] [verified for the versions: https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/rustix, nix, zbus, rtnetlink, tokio, nftables, toml, inotify]. Kernel interfaces: `/proc/<pid>/ns/{net,uts,mnt}`, `unshare(2)`, `setns(2)`, `sethostname(2)`, `mount(2)` with `MS_BIND|MS_REC|MS_SLAVE`, `pivot_root(2)`, `open_tree(2)` and `move_mount(2)`; `/proc/fs/nfsd/{threads,portlist,versions,nfsv4leasetime,nfsv4gracetime,v4_end_grace,clients}` and the `nfsd` genetlink family; `/var/lib/nfs/rpc_pipefs/nfsd/cld`; `/proc/net/rpc/{nfsd.export,nfsd.fh,nfs4.nametoid,nfs4.idtoname}`; sysctls `fs.nfs.nlm_grace_period`, `fs.nfs.nlm_tcpport`, `fs.nfs.nlm_udpport`, `net.ipv4.conf.<lif>.arp_notify`; `/sys/kernel/config/target/iscsi/<iqn>/tpgt_<n>/np/<ip>:<port>` and `/sys/kernel/config/nvmet/ports/<n>/{addr_trtype,addr_adrfam,addr_traddr,addr_trsvcid,subsystems/}` written from inside the SVM netns; `/sys/class/net/<pf>/device/sriov_numvfs`; cgroup v2 `cpu.weight`, `memory.max`, `memory.high`, `pids.max` through systemd.

#### 3. Bottlenecks and edge cases

1. **Portal address collision across IPspaces.** Two SVMs declaring one `ip:port` share one kernel socket in the first SVM's netns; the second serves nothing and no error is returned (the global list match of 2.8). Assumption: `g_np_list` keyed by address, port and transport only on 6.12 (verified). Mitigation: the Raft validator; a nightly check that every declared portal has a socket in its own netns (`ss -ltn` under `nsenter`).
2. **Lingering namespaces.** A portal, an nvmet port or a stuck nfsd thread left in a namespace keeps it alive after its pins are gone, with its LIF address still answering ARP on the old node: a split identity during a Phase B move. Assumption: user sockets pin the netns [believed]. Mitigation: the ladder order T2 to T4 and a post-stop check that `lsns -t net` shows no namespace with the SVM's interfaces.
3. **XFS log replay at start.** A clean stop leaves clean logs and mounts take about 50 ms each; an unplanned Phase B start replays logs: 20 volumes with 128 MiB logs at 0.5 GB/s of HDD reads is 5 s in parallel and 50 s serialized. Assumption: replay reads at array speed. Mounts run in parallel per depth level; the engine's read cache (map and log segments) should keep the replay reads off the HDDs (question to Storage).
4. **nfsd threads to zero waits for held requests.** A throttled or QoS-held WRITE delays `svm stop` by up to the 1 s QoS cap or the 2 s stall bound; a wedged volume leaves threads in D state and the netns cannot die. Mitigation: LIF addresses are removed first (no new RPCs), the 10 s step budget, then `Stuck` is reported rather than hidden.
5. **Grace on every start.** A file SVM's clients wait up to 20 s for new opens after any start unless early end fires; one absent client defeats early end (round 2). Assumption: lease 10 s, grace 20 s per R8. A datastore SVM pays nothing (no v4 state).
6. **NLM clients not notified.** Clients that locked through a LIF address since removed from the SVM lose locks silently after a move; a client that cannot be reached within sm-notify's retry window likewise. Numbers: sm-notify retries for 15 min by default [verified: sm-notify(8)]; lockd grace is 20 s, so late notifications reclaim nothing.
7. **Machine password rotation versus lag.** Default rotation every 604800 s; a Phase B window of one CP interval plus ship time (5 to 30 s) means a probability of about 1 in 20,000 per rotation of landing in the window; the inotify-triggered root-volume CP closes it to the CP latency.
8. **macvlan CPU at 1500 B.** 0.25 core per 10GbE port at line rate with small frames [believed]; jumbo frames cut it to 0.04. SR-IOV removes it on supported NICs. Mitigation: MTU 9000 by default for datastores, SR-IOV opt-in.
9. **GARP acceptance under ipvlan.** Only the VM-hosted profile changes the MAC on a move; a client that ignores unsolicited ARP waits for its own neighbour timeout (Linux 30 s base reachable time, ESXi comparable, Windows variable) [believed]. Mitigation: macvlan or SR-IOV with persistent MACs everywhere else; the VM profile is documented as "pause up to the client's ARP timeout".
10. **The root cgroup outweighs slices.** 32 nfsd threads at nice 0 count as 32 pseudo-children against a slice of weight 100, so CPU weights only arbitrate userspace against userspace; a backup SVM's versitygw can never starve a datastore's nfsd, but it can starve another SVM's smbd. Assumption: cgroup v2 root-thread rule (verified). The per-volume QoS and the isolated engine cores carry the real isolation.
11. **smbd per-connection memory under `MemoryMax`.** 400 connections at 10 MiB exceed a 4 GiB file slice once page cache is charged too; `MemoryHigh` reclaims cache first, and `OOMPolicy=continue` turns an overrun into one disconnected client (durable reconnect) rather than a stopped service.
12. **versitygw Object Lock gaps.** Default retention computed at delete time before PR #2479; `GetObjectLockConfiguration` returning an empty `Rule` element (issue #2397) breaks some SDK clients [verified: https://github.com/versity/versitygw/issues/2397]. Mitigation: pin the post-#2479 release, run the Veeam test as the gate, never enable default retention.
13. **Many SVMs.** 64 SVMs are about 2,000 private mounts, 200 pins, 64 nfsd instances (1,024 kthreads), 64 winbindds each polling a DC every `winbind cache time` 300 s [verified: smb.conf(5)], and at most 4 GiB of fixed memory; the homelab needs 2 to 8.

#### 4. What I would cut or defer

Cut: PID, user, IPC, cgroup and time namespaces per SVM; nmbd, NetBIOS name service and SMB1; cgroup `io.max` and `io.weight` on ublk devices (the engine's QoS is the single governor); the round-2 RST proxy for planned moves (the new node's own RSTs do it; it stays for silent nodes); `rpc.nfsd --scope` as a mechanism (the UTS namespace already does it); the ESXi NFS 4.1 datastore as a default (tested, not recommended); ksmbd (round 2).

Defer: NFSv4.0 and v4.2 (4.2's sparse and clone operations are a Phase B feature); Kerberos NFS and rpc.gssd (needs AD per SVM first; Phase B); multiprotocol shares (Phase 3, R20); SR-IOV LIFs to a Phase C stretch after macvlan passes; ipvlan to the VM-hosted qualification of Phase 2; IPv6 LIFs (nvmet scope-id resolution against `init_net`, verified); NPIV FC LIFs per SVM (Phase B, with Fabrics); NVMe/TCP in SVMs (Phase 2, the trait slot exists); ONTAP-style `.snapshot` inside junctions and NFS snapshot visibility (Phase B); SVM-level QoS buckets and `min_iops` floors (Phase B); `volume rehost` (Phase B, uid caveat); `nvfail_policy = strict` serial bump (later, opt-in); S3 IAM via the versitygw admin API (never; Raft-declared users only); SVM administrator roles and RBAC (Phase B with the management API); a test of overlapping addresses across IPspaces (the construction supports it, the Phase C matrix does not test it).

#### 5. Phase C work items, then what Phase B and Phase A add

In order, each with its exit test:

- **C1 `svm::ns`: namespaces, pins, the view.** Exit: 1,000 create and destroy cycles leak no namespace (`lsns` count unchanged) and no mount; build time at most 5 ms; a volume mounted on the host under `/vol/<svm>_root/vm` is visible at `/vm` in the SVM view within 10 ms; the SVM's overlays are invisible on the host.
- **C2 LIFs and firewall.** Exit: a macvlan LIF with its Raft MAC is reachable within 100 ms of `svm start`; 1,000 up and down cycles; a move between two ports of the node pauses an NFSv3 client at most 2 s; SVM-A cannot reach SVM-B's LIF except through the switch; the nftables ruleset drops everything but the service ports (nmap from the client VLAN).
- **C3 Junctions and volumes.** Exit: 50 volumes nested three deep mount within 3 s with clean logs and 10 s with 128 MiB logs to replay, in both views at the right paths; reserved names refused; unmount order proven by `svm stop` with all 50 mounted.
- **C4 iSCSI blade in the SVM.** Exit: the step 1 table of 2.12, plus configfs portals created from inside the netns and removed by the stop ladder, plus the address-collision validator test.
- **C5 NFS blade.** Exit: the NFS rows of step 2, plus the `v4_end_grace` early end, plus `sm-notify` reclaim after `svm stop/start`, plus the ESTALE generation test.
- **C6 SMB blade.** Exit: the SMB and AD rows of step 2, plus 100 `svm stop/start` cycles with the machine account surviving, plus `passdb.tdb` regeneration from Raft matching `pdbedit -L`.
- **C7 S3 blade.** Exit: the Veeam row of step 2 with versitygw pinned past PR #2479, TLS per SVM, IAM from Raft.
- **C8 Slices and QoS.** Exit: versitygw at 1 GB/s in the backup SVM leaves the datastore SVM's 4 KiB QD1 NFS write p99 under 2 ms; a 1,000 IOPS cap on a volume holds at 1,000 plus or minus 5% over 10 min with no request held over 1 s; a smbd child over `MemoryMax` is killed alone and its client reconnects.
- **C9 Lifecycle integration and `otapctl svm`.** Exit: 1,000 cycles of create, start, stop, delete with no leaks; `svm stop` within 6 s with 2 GiB dirty; the `Stuck` path reported correctly with an injected D-state volume; configuration export and import reproduce the SVM byte-for-byte in the generated files.
- **C10 FC client targets (step 3, with Fabrics).** Exit: the step 3 criteria.

**Phase B adds** for my area: the move (stop on A, final CP and ship, start on B) with its client-visible numbers: iSCSI and NFSv3 about 8 to 15 s (ladder 6 s plus ship plus one retransmission interval), NFSv4.1 plus grace up to 20 s unless early end, SMB reconnect 10 to 20 s; the root volume as a consistency-group member and the inotify-triggered CP; NFS and LUN nvfail per volume after an unplanned takeover with the generation bump; NPIV FC LIFs; `volume rehost`; the ipvlan VM profile; the SVM timer table rows (start 5 s, stop 10 s, move 15 s block-visible, NFSv4.1 lease 10 s and grace 20 s, NLM grace 20 s, sm-notify retry 15 min, GARP 0, 300 ms, 1 s).

**Phase A adds**: `Presence::BlockStandby` on the partner (the SVM's target and portals live on both nodes, NAS on the owner only); ALUA group flip as the SAN takeover with no LIF move; PR policies per R9; the shelf's XFS mounts on the survivor after fence evidence; NFS and SMB still move as SVM restarts on the partner with the shared root volume, so Phase A's NAS story is Phase B's without the ship step.

### Opus-Fabrics

#### Opus-Fabrics, Session 03: asynchronous transfer and Fibre Channel

##### 1. Executive take

The pivot deletes the hardest half of my round-2 design and makes the other half ordinary. With no synchronous mirror on the acknowledgement path there is no put-to-Placed latency to chase, no inbound ring that must outlive a daemon, no per-record acknowledgement, no unknown-fate quarantine, no 20 ms link heartbeat, no busy-polled mirror core, no RDMA leg to justify a ConnectX-3, and no reason for `otap-ringd` to exist. What replaces it is a bulk mover: every 5 to 15 s a Consistency Point produces a delta of hundreds of megabytes to a few gigabytes, and the transport's job is to get it onto the partner's disk at line rate, resume it from any byte after any failure, prove it arrived intact, and cost as little CPU per byte as possible. That is a TCP problem, and on Linux 6.12 it is a well-solved one: `IORING_OP_SEND_ZC` with registered buffers lets the CP's own hugetlbfs arena be the send source with no copy, and the receiver's one copy is the only copy in the whole path. Fibre Channel changes role too: as a replication transport it would move at most 1.45 GB/s (16G) through a kernel target, a staging file and a polling scanner, for a cost that a 25GbE DAC beats at the price of two used NICs; as a client fabric it is exactly what the round-2 facts say it is, in-box and buildable in Phase C as protocol step 3.

My top five positions:

1. The replication stream is one versioned frame format over plain TCP sockets, with chunk-indexed resume cursors owned by the receiver, implicit flow control through per-connection credits, CRC32C per chunk and a BLAKE3 digest per CP; TCP is the only transport in Phases C, B and A, and FC as a transport is not built.
2. Zero-copy send from the hugetlbfs arena via `IORING_OP_SEND_ZC` with `IORING_RECVSEND_FIXED_BUF` is the default plaintext path, arena slot reuse is gated on the `IORING_CQE_F_NOTIF` completion, and `IORING_SEND_ZC_REPORT_USAGE` tells us when the NIC path silently copied so the sender can fall back to a plain send; TLS and compression run through a registered bounce buffer at the cost of one pass.
3. FC client targets in Phase C load `qla2xxx` with `qlini_mode=disabled` on every port, use explicit per-initiator ACLs, keep vendor "LIO-ORG" so multipath-tools' built-in entry claims the LUNs on Proxmox, and advertise implicit-only ALUA with a single Active/Optimized group from day one so that nothing on the client changes when a second node arrives.
4. FC LIFs are NPIV virtual ports per SVM only where a switch exists, because the 6.12 driver refuses a vport unless the fabric login advertised NPIV; they do not migrate, they come in pairs (one per node) and ALUA decides which path is live, exactly as ONTAP does.
5. `otap-ringd` is retired: the arena is a hugetlbfs file created by systemd units and survives `dbladed` without a guardian process, so the data path is `dbladed` alone with the shipper and the receiver as reactors inside it, beside `nbladed` and `otap-ctl`.

##### 2. Design

###### 2.1 Bulk async transport trait

####### What the transport moves

The transport is blind to how Storage defines the delta. A delta is an ordered list of extents `(vol, lba, len, crc32c, source)` between a base CP the receiver already holds and a target CP; the source is either an arena slot (the frozen CP write set, the steady-state case) or an on-disk physical address (a map walk for `birth_cp > base`, the catch-up and resync case). Both appear to the shipper through one `DeltaSource` trait, sorted by `(vol, lba)` and stable for a given `(base, target)` pair, which is what makes a mid-delta resume well defined: chunk `i` of delta `(base, target)` is always the same bytes.

Chunks are 1 MiB runs of consecutive manifest extents (up to 256 extents of 4 KiB, or one 1 MiB extent). A manifest entry is 32 bytes, so a 4 GiB delta of 64 KiB average extents has a 2 MiB manifest and a 4 GiB delta of 4 KiB random writes has a 32 MiB manifest; manifests above 64 MiB are split into parts by LBA range so no single frame exceeds 64 MiB.

####### Framing

Every frame is a 64-byte little-endian `repr(C)` header followed by an optional payload. Header: `magic u32, ver u16, kind u8, flags u8, rel u32, conn u16, _r u16, cp u64, base u64, idx u32, count u32, wire_len u32, raw_len u32, payload_crc u32, hdr_crc u32, _pad [u8; 8]`. `payload_crc` is CRC32C over the raw (uncompressed, plaintext) payload; `hdr_crc` covers the other 60 bytes; `flags` carries the codec (none, lz4, zstd). Kinds: `Hello`, `HelloAck`, `DeltaBegin`, `Manifest`, `Chunk`, `DeltaEnd`, `Landed`, `Committed`, `Abort`, `Ping`, `Pong`. The format carries `ver` and follows the round-2 N/N+1 promise; it is frozen with golden vectors and property tests before any code depends on it, and the parser is safe Rust with no `unsafe`, fuzzed in CI.

####### Flow control

Three layers. TCP's own windows, with `net.ipv4.tcp_wmem` and `tcp_rmem` maxima raised to 64 MiB in the platform profile. A receiver credit window per connection, initially 64 chunks (64 MiB): the receiver grants credits in `Landed` frames as it writes chunks into fresh segments of the destination aggregate, so sender memory in flight is bounded by how fast the destination disk absorbs, not by how fast the NIC delivers. And the arena pin: a chunk sent with `SEND_ZC` keeps its arena slots pinned until the notification CQE arrives, which for TCP means after the peer acknowledged the bytes; with 64 MiB per connection and a 100 ms worst-case acknowledgement on a LAN, four connections pin at most 256 MiB, 3% of an 8 GiB arena.

The arena is never the only copy. The CP commits the data to disk before its slots are freed (round-2 slot lifetime), so when Storage reclaims a slot that the shipper has not yet sent, the extent's source flips from `Arena` to `Disk` and the shipper reads it back through `DeltaSource::read_disk`. Shipping never holds back ingest, and the partner being away for a day costs disk space (Storage's base-snapshot pinning), not memory.

####### Resumability mid-CP

The receiver owns the cursor. It records, per relationship, `applied` (the CP its replica is at), `landing` (the delta in progress, if any), `landed_contig` (highest chunk index below which every chunk has been written) and a short sparse list of landed ranges above it. The in-memory cursor is persisted at every receiver CP in a 4 KiB per-relationship resume page kept with the aggregate's metadata (Storage's area). `Hello` is answered with the cursor; the sender restarts from the lowest unlanded chunk. Chunks landed after the receiver's last CP but lost with its memory are simply re-sent; landing is idempotent because every landed extent goes to a new physical address (never-overwrite) and the receiver's pending log is keyed by `(cp, extent index)`. A sender restart loses nothing either: the sender re-describes the delta from the same frozen CP (or the same map walk) and the manifest is identical by construction. The receiver applies atomically: `commit(cp)` after a verified `DeltaEnd` is one map-root switch plus a superblock write, so the replica is always at a CP boundary and a crash mid-landing leaves only orphan segments that GC reclaims.

####### Integrity

CRC32C per chunk and per extent, BLAKE3 per CP. Per extent, the CRC already exists: round-2 records carry `payload_crc` per slot and every read from disk is CRC-verified (R19), so the manifest's per-extent CRC costs no data pass. The chunk CRC is `crc32c_combine` over its extents' CRCs (crc32c 0.6.8 exposes `crc32c_combine(crc_a, crc_b, len_b)` [verified: https://docs.rs/crc32c/latest/crc32c/]), again no data pass on the zero-copy path. The receiver verifies the chunk CRC after decompression and before landing, and verifies each extent's CRC when it reads the extent back for any later purpose. Per CP, `DeltaEnd` carries a BLAKE3 digest (blake3 1.8.7 [verified: https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/blake3]) over the manifest bytes, which include every extent's CRC and position, so a receiver that landed every chunk with matching CRCs and matches the manifest digest holds the delta the sender described. Frames with a bad header CRC drop the connection; a bad chunk CRC returns `Abort(Corrupt, idx)` and the sender resends from that chunk on a fresh connection.

####### Optional TLS and compression

TLS 1.3 through rustls 0.23.45 [verified: https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/rustls] with the aws-lc-rs provider, mutual authentication against the cluster CA that R23 already requires on every control path; the stream reuses the node certificates. The plaintext goes from the arena through AES-128-GCM into a registered 4 MiB bounce buffer (two per connection, ping-pong) and is sent with `SEND_ZC` from the bounce, so TLS costs exactly one pass over the data. AES-GCM with AES-NI and PCLMUL runs at about 2 to 4 GB/s per core on 2017-class cores and 5 to 8 GB/s with VAES [believed], so TLS at 10GbE is about 0.4 of a core per side and at 25GbE about one core. Default: `tls = true` on every endpoint; `tls = false` is accepted only on an endpoint declared `direct = true` (a point-to-point DAC with no switch in between), which is the installer's default topology for the replication link.

Compression per chunk with lz4_flex 0.14.0 [verified: https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/lz4_flex] or zstd 0.14.2 [verified: https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/zstd] (libzstd linked from Debian 13's `libzstd1`). Assumptions: LZ4 compresses at 0.6 to 1 GB/s per core and decompresses at 2 to 4 GB/s; zstd level 3 at 250 to 350 MB/s per core, decompressing at 1 to 1.5 GB/s [believed]; VM datastore blocks compress 1.5 to 2.5:1, media and already-encrypted data 1.0:1 [believed]. Policy `auto`: at 1GbE, zstd level 3 on two worker threads (600 MB/s of raw input, which at 2.5:1 saturates 110 MB/s of wire); at 10GbE, LZ4 on up to four workers only while a 64-chunk sample every 1,000 chunks shows a ratio above 1.2:1; at 25GbE and above, off. Compressed output lands in the bounce buffer and is sent with `SEND_ZC` from there; the engine's future at-rest compression (the reserved `plen`) would let compressed extents ship as-is without this pass.

####### Zero-copy send from the hugetlbfs arena

The 8 GiB arena is registered with io_uring as eight 1 GiB entries (the 6.12 huge-page coalescing in Appendix A), once, by the engine's main ring, and cloned into each connection thread's ring with `IORING_REGISTER_CLONE_BUFFERS` (opcode 30 on 6.12 [verified: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/include/uapi/linux/io_uring.h]), so no connection thread re-pins 8 GiB. A chunk is one `IORING_OP_SEND_ZC` SQE with `IORING_RECVSEND_FIXED_BUF` ("Use registered buffers, the index is stored in the buf_index field" [verified: same header]) and `IORING_SEND_ZC_REPORT_USAGE`, whose notification reports `IORING_NOTIF_USAGE_ZC_COPIED` when the data "was copied (at least partially)" [verified: same header]. Each send yields two CQEs: the send result flagged `IORING_CQE_F_MORE`, then the notification flagged `IORING_CQE_F_NOTIF`, which is when "the memory associated with the send is safe to get reused" [verified: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man3/io_uring_prep_send_zc.3.html]. The io-uring crate 0.7.15 (2026-09-07) exposes `opcode::SendZc::new(fd, buf, len).buf_index(Some(idx)).zc_flags(..)` [verified: https://docs.rs/io-uring/latest/io_uring/opcode/struct.SendZc.html and https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/io-uring]. Because the arena is 2 MiB folios, a 1 MiB chunk is one or two bvec entries, which keeps the skb fragment count trivial. The copied-usage counter is a Prometheus metric; if more than half of the last 1,000 sends report copied (a veth or bridge path, a NIC without scatter-gather), the connection falls back to `IORING_OP_SEND` from the arena, which costs one copy but saves the second CQE.

The receive side is plain: `IORING_OP_RECV` into a registered landing buffer, then `IORING_OP_WRITE_FIXED` with O_DIRECT into the destination segment. `RECV_ZC` is 6.15 (Appendix A), so the receiver's copy stays and sets the ceiling at 25GbE and above.

####### Parallel connections

`connections = auto` gives one connection at 10GbE and below and four at 25GbE and above, on the assumption that one TCP stream with GRO on a modern core moves 1.2 to 2 GB/s and the receiver's copy is the limit [believed]. Chunks are dealt round-robin to connections; order does not matter because landing is by chunk index and apply happens only at `DeltaEnd`; manifests and `DeltaBegin`/`DeltaEnd` go on connection 0; each connection has its own credit window; a dead connection's un-landed chunks are re-queued on the survivors and the delta continues without a session restart.

####### Link selection and fallback

A relationship names endpoints in priority order, by default the direct DAC first and the LAN second. Connect budget 1 s (TCP, TLS and `Hello`); a connection with data pending that receives nothing for 3 s is dead; an idle connection sends `Ping` every 1 s. On death: two reconnect attempts to the same endpoint 1 s apart, then the next endpoint, then back-off doubling from 1 s to 30 s. Fail-back to the preferred endpoint after 30 s of successful probes (the round-2 "fail-back after a link flip" row), by closing and reconnecting; the cursor makes the switch invisible to the delta. Active/standby only, never striping across endpoints, because a 10GbE DAC and a 1GbE LAN have nothing useful to share.

####### Throughput targets per link class

Sustained delta shipping, 1 MiB chunks, 1500-byte MTU unless noted, destination disk not the bottleneck, per-direction payload.

| Link | Payload ceiling (assumption) | Target, TLS off | Target, TLS on | Connections | Cores per side |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1GbE | 118 MB/s (1460/1538 = 94.9% of 125 MB/s) | 110 MB/s | 110 MB/s | 1 | 0.15 |
| 10GbE | 1.18 GB/s (1.23 GB/s at 9000 MTU) | 1.1 GB/s | 1.0 GB/s | 1 | sender 0.5 (zero-copy), receiver 1.0 |
| 25GbE | 2.95 GB/s | 2.6 GB/s | 2.0 GB/s | 4 | 2 to 3 (receiver copy-bound) |
| 40/100GbE | 4.7 / 11.8 GB/s | 4 GB/s, not promised | 3 GB/s | 8 | needs `RECV_ZC` (6.15) to go further |
| 8GFC, if ever built | 800 MB/s single direction (FCIA, 8.5 GBd 8b/10b) [verified: https://fibrechannel.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/FCIA-Speedmap-V24-July-2023.pdf] | 0.7 GB/s | n/a | 1 | receiver 1 (LIO) plus scanner |
| 16GFC | 1,600 MB/s (14.025 GBd 64b/66b) [verified: same] | 1.45 GB/s | n/a | 1 | same |
| 32GFC | 3,200 MB/s (28.05 GBd) [verified: same] | 2.9 GB/s | n/a | 1 | same; PCIe 3.0 x8 |

The destination usually sets the real number: a 12-drive RAID6 lands 1.2 to 2 GB/s empty and 0.3 to 0.5 GB/s aged (Appendix A), so beyond 10GbE the link only matters for flash pools. Ship time for a 4 GiB delta: 39 s at 1GbE, 3.9 s at 10GbE, 1.65 s at 25GbE, 2.9 s at 16GFC. The Phase B lag bound is one CP interval plus delta divided by the slower of link and destination plus apply (a segment flush and two superblock writes, 100 to 300 ms on HDD), so a 300 MB/s ingest with a 10 s CP over 10GbE sits at about 13 s; the rollback a takeover can cause is that lag plus the 3 s lease TTL.

When ingest exceeds the link for more than two CP intervals the shipper coalesces: instead of CP N+1 then N+2 it ships one map-walk delta from the last applied CP to the newest committed CP, which collapses overwrites of hot blocks and bounds the backlog by the changed set rather than the write volume. Consensus decides when the resulting lag flips the relationship to Lagging.

####### Memory model for a 64 GB node

The transport's slice of the round-2 budget, two relationships, four connections each:

| Consumer | Size | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Send source | 0 | the arena (8 GiB, Storage's line) is the source; pins at most 256 MiB in flight |
| TLS and codec bounce buffers | 2 x 4 MiB x 8 connections = 64 MiB | registered, hugetlbfs-backed for `SEND_ZC` |
| Disk-sourced read staging (catch-up) | 64 MiB | registered |
| Manifests in flight | up to 64 MiB per delta, 128 MiB cap | mirrors the frozen dirty index Storage already holds |
| Receiver landing buffers | 64 chunks x 1 MiB x 8 connections = 512 MiB worst case, 128 MiB typical | credits cap it |
| Receiver pending-extent table | 48 B x extents, up to 48 MiB per landing delta | until `commit` |
| Kernel socket buffers | 2 x 16 MiB x 8 = 256 MiB worst case | `tcp_rmem`/`tcp_wmem` |
| Total | about 0.5 GiB typical, 1.1 GiB worst case | |

The round-2 inbound ring (8 GiB tmpfs, mlocked) is gone. My recommendation for the freed 8 GiB: 4 GiB to the map and read caches and 4 GiB to the per-SVM slice headroom, but that is Storage's and Protocols' call; the transport claims under 1 GiB.

####### State machines

Sender session, one per relationship:

| State | Event | Action | Next |
|---|---|---|---|
| Idle | relationship enabled and a CP above `applied` exists | pick the preferred healthy endpoint | Connecting |
| Connecting | TCP, TLS and `Hello`/`HelloAck` within 1 s | read cursor; choose delta (coalesce if more than 2 CPs queued) | Describing |
| Connecting | timeout or refusal, second attempt failed | next endpoint; back-off 1 to 30 s when all fail | Connecting / Idle |
| Describing | `DeltaBegin` and manifest sent | start at `landed_contig` | Streaming |
| Streaming | credits available | send next chunk, zero-copy or via bounce | Streaming |
| Streaming | `Landed(idx, credits)` | advance, grant | Streaming |
| Streaming | `Sent(token)` (notification CQE) | release the arena pin | Streaming |
| Streaming | last chunk landed | send `DeltaEnd(digest)` | Ending |
| Ending | `Committed(cp)` | unpin old base, pin `cp` as base; report lag to `otap-ctl` | Idle |
| Streaming / Ending | endpoint dead | keep delta and cursor; mark endpoint | Connecting |
| any | `Abort(NoSpace / BaseMismatch / Version)` | stop; report Broken | Broken |
| Broken | resync order from Consensus | rebase to the common snapshot | Connecting |

Receiver landing, one per inbound relationship:

| State | Event | Action | Next |
|---|---|---|---|
| Listening | `Hello(rel)` authenticated by the cluster CA | `HelloAck(cursor)` | Sessioned |
| Sessioned | `DeltaBegin` with `base == applied` and `bytes` below free space minus GC reserve | open pending log, accept manifest | Landing |
| Sessioned | `DeltaBegin` with `base != applied` or no space | `Abort(reason)` | Sessioned |
| Landing | new chunk, CRC ok | write extents to new segments, append pending log, `Landed` | Landing |
| Landing | duplicate chunk | drop, `Landed` | Landing |
| Landing | chunk CRC mismatch | `Abort(Corrupt, idx)` | Landing |
| Landing | `DeltaEnd`, digest ok, all chunks landed | flush segments; `commit` (map root switch, superblock); `Committed(cp)` | Sessioned |
| Landing | connection lost | keep pending log; cursor persisted at the next receiver CP | Listening |
| Landing | receiver restart | rebuild cursor from the last persisted resume page | Listening |

Endpoint selection:

| State | Event | Action | Next |
|---|---|---|---|
| Preferred | 3 s silence with data pending, or two failed connects | mark unhealthy; connect secondary | Secondary |
| Secondary | preferred probes succeed for 30 s | close, reconnect on preferred (cursor resumes) | Preferred |
| Secondary | secondary dies | back-off 1 s doubling to 30 s | Down |
| Down | any endpoint probe succeeds | connect | that endpoint |

####### Trait sketches

```rust
pub enum ExtentSrc { Arena(RingRef), Disk(Pba) }
#[repr(C)] pub struct ManifestEntry { pub vol: u32, pub len: u32, pub lba: u64, pub crc: u32, pub flags: u32, pub _r: u64 } // 32 B
pub struct DeltaExtent { pub m: ManifestEntry, pub src: ExtentSrc }
pub struct DeltaDesc { pub rel: RelId, pub base: CpSeq, pub target: CpSeq, pub extents: u64, pub bytes: u64, pub parts: u16 }
pub trait DeltaSource {                      // implemented by the engine (Storage); consumed by the shipper
    fn describe(&self, rel: RelId, base: CpSeq, target: CpSeq) -> Result<DeltaDesc, SrcErr>;   // frozen write set or map walk
    fn extents(&self, d: &DeltaDesc, from: u64, out: &mut Vec<DeltaExtent>) -> usize;           // sorted (vol, lba); stable per (base, target)
    fn read_disk(&self, pba: Pba, len: u32, dst: &mut [u8]) -> Result<(), SrcErr>;              // CRC-verified; used when a slot was reclaimed
    fn pin(&self, rel: RelId, cp: CpSeq) -> Result<SnapId, SrcErr>;   fn unpin(&self, s: SnapId);
}
```

```rust
pub struct StreamCaps { pub zero_copy: bool, pub tls: bool, pub codec: Codec, pub max_chunk: u32, pub connections: u8 }
pub struct Cursor { pub applied: CpSeq, pub landing: Option<(CpSeq, CpSeq)>, pub landed_contig: u32, pub landed_sparse: Vec<(u32, u32)> }
pub enum Event { Sent(ChunkToken), Landed { idx: u32, credits: u32 }, Committed(CpSeq), Reconnected(Cursor), Dead(EndpointId), Aborted(AbortReason) }
pub trait DeltaStream: Send {               // impl: TcpStream (Phases B and A); the format is transport-blind
    fn caps(&self) -> StreamCaps;
    fn open(&mut self, rel: RelId) -> Result<Cursor, StreamErr>;                              // Hello / HelloAck
    fn begin(&mut self, d: &DeltaDesc, manifest: &[ManifestEntry]) -> Result<(), StreamErr>;
    fn send(&mut self, d: &DeltaDesc, idx: u32, c: ChunkRef<'_>) -> Result<ChunkToken, StreamErr>; // non-blocking; Err(Window) without credits
    fn end(&mut self, d: &DeltaDesc, digest: [u8; 32]) -> Result<(), StreamErr>;
    fn poll(&mut self, out: &mut Vec<Event>) -> usize;                                         // Sent(token): arena slots reusable
    fn close(&mut self);
}
pub trait DeltaSink {                       // receiver, engine-facing; Storage implements
    fn cursor(&self, rel: RelId) -> Cursor;
    fn begin(&mut self, d: &DeltaDesc, manifest: Vec<ManifestEntry>) -> Result<(), SinkErr>;   // refuses BaseMismatch, NoSpace
    fn land(&mut self, d: &DeltaDesc, idx: u32, raw: &[u8]) -> Result<u32 /* credits */, SinkErr>; // idempotent; new segments; pending log
    fn commit(&mut self, d: &DeltaDesc) -> Result<(), SinkErr>;                                // one map-root switch; replica at a CP boundary
    fn abort(&mut self, d: &DeltaDesc);
}
// Never leaked through these boundaries: socket descriptors, TLS state, codec choice, connection count,
// the receiver's segment layout, or any timer of the transport.
```

####### Configuration

```toml
[[relationship]]
name        = "hv/vm-prod -> node-b/aggr1"
source      = { svm = "hv", volume = "vm-prod" }
destination = { node = "node-b", aggregate = "aggr1" }
schedule    = "every-cp"            # or "5m", "hourly": ship the newest CP at that cadence
coalesce_after_cps = 2
compression = "auto"                # none | lz4 | zstd:3 | auto (link class and sample ratio)
connections = "auto"                # 1 at <= 10GbE, 4 at >= 25GbE
window_chunks = 64                  # per connection; chunks are 1 MiB
[[relationship.endpoints]]
addr = "10.255.0.2:7430"; direct = true;  tls = false     # DAC, no switch
[[relationship.endpoints]]
addr = "192.168.10.12:7430"; direct = false; tls = true   # LAN fallback
```

Crates: io-uring 0.7.15, crc32c 0.6.8, blake3 1.8.7, rustls 0.23.45, zstd 0.14.2, lz4_flex 0.14.0, memmap2 0.9.11 [verified: https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/memmap2], rustix 1.1.5 [verified: https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/rustix], postcard 1.1.3 for the control enums [verified: https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/postcard], tokio 1.53.2 for the control plane only [verified: https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/tokio]; the data path is io_uring threads, not tokio.

###### 2.2 FC as a transport

The concrete mechanism, the only one available on 6.12 with QLogic cards: the receiver exports a landing LUN through `tcm_qla2xxx` (a `fileio` backstore on a 2 to 4 GiB tmpfs file, the round-2 S2 path, or `iblock` on a spare NVMe namespace); the sender's HBA port runs as an initiator, logs in, and writes chunk frames with `IORING_OP_WRITE_FIXED` and O_DIRECT at `idx x 1 MiB` offsets inside a ring laid out in the LUN; the receiver's reactor polls the landing file for CRC-valid frames and lands them as it would TCP chunks; `DeltaBegin`, `DeltaEnd`, credits and `Landed` ride the mTLS TCP control link, because FC carries no IP and target-mode LIO cannot speak to the writer except through SCSI status. FC-NVMe would be cleaner but is impossible: on 6.12 `qla_nvme.c` registers only an NVMe-FC host local port (`nvme_fc_register_localport`) and defines no `nvmet_fc_target_template`; there is no `nvmet_fc_register_targetport` anywhere under `drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/` [verified: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/qla_nvme.c]; only Emulex's lpfc has an NVMe target side.

Port arrangement without dual mode on one port: load the module with `qlini_mode=dual`, which is the only setting under which the per-port sysfs attribute `/sys/class/scsi_host/hostN/qlini_mode` is visible (`qla_host_attr_is_visible` hides `qlini_mode`, `ql2xiniexchg` and `ql2xexchoffld` unless `ql2x_ini_mode == QLA2XXX_INI_MODE_DUAL`) [verified: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/qla_attr.c], then write `disabled` to every client port and to the inbound replication port and `enabled` to the outbound replication port, before any TPG is enabled, because a port with active target mode answers "Target Mode is active. Unable to change Mode" and an accepted change triggers an ISP abort of that port [verified: same file]. Each port is then single-role. Per node that is one target port for clients plus the partner's inbound writes and one initiator port for outbound, on a switch; without a switch, a crossed pair (A port 2 to B port 1, B port 2 to A port 1) consumes both ports of a dual-port card on each node and clients need a second card.

Cost: 8 to 10 engineer-weeks and a lab with four HBAs and two cables. The initiator leg with udev timers (2 s command timeout, `fast_io_fail_tmo=1`, `dev_loss_tmo=5`) and the abort, LUN reset, target reset, ISP abort ladder that can stall a port for up to R_A_TOV 10 s; the in-LUN ring format and scanner; asymmetric N2N login testing on 6.12 for 16G and 32G pairs (public history exists for 8G, Appendix A); the receiver's kernel copy through `vfs_iter_write` into tmpfs (about 15% of a core at 1.6 GB/s, round 2) plus the scanner. Benefit: at most 0.7, 1.45 or 2.9 GB/s, every one of which a 10GbE or 25GbE DAC matches at the cost of two used NICs and zero kernel-target plumbing, and the async stream does not care about the 80 to 200 us FC command latency that made FC attractive to nobody even in round 2.

Recommendation: do not build it in Phase C, B or A. The frame format is transport-blind (chunks addressed by index), so an FC landing ring could be added after v0.3 without changing the stream if a user demonstrates an FC-only interconnect with no Ethernet between the nodes, which I have never seen in a homelab. The `FcLink` capability bits of round 2 are dropped from the trait rather than carried.

###### 2.3 Fibre Channel client target mode

####### Module parameters and the boot profile

`qlini_mode` is a module-wide string parameter accepting `exclusive`, `disabled`, `enabled` (the default) and `dual`; "disabled" means initiator mode will never be enabled, which is what a pure target node wants [verified: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/qla_target.c]. Phase C profile, `/etc/modprobe.d/opentap-qla2xxx.conf`: `options qla2xxx qlini_mode=disabled ql2xnvmeenable=0 ql2xmqsupport=1`, with `ql2xfwloadbin=1` added per family rule below, and `tcm_qla2xxx` in `/etc/modules-load.d/opentap-fc.conf`. `ql2xnvmeenable` defaults to 1 when `CONFIG_NVME_FC` is set and only adds NVMe-FC host discovery noise on a target-only port; `ql2xexchoffld` (target exchanges) and `ql2xiniexchg` default to 1024 each [verified: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/qla_os.c]; sixteen ESXi hosts at queue depth 64 is 1,024 outstanding commands, so the profile raises `ql2xexchoffld` to 4096 on 16G and 32G cards (the per-host attribute clamps to `FW_MAX_EXCHANGES_CNT` [verified: qla_attr.c]; the firmware ceiling itself I have not verified [believed]). `qla2xxx` is in the initramfs under `MODULES=most`, so every change to the drop-in is followed by `update-initramfs -u` [believed]. Enabling a TPG on a physical port calls `qlt_enable_vha`, which for the base port sets `ISP_ABORT_NEEDED`, wakes the DPC thread and waits for the HBA to come back online, a 2 to 5 s port reset [verified: qla_target.c]; a virtual port is enabled with `qla24xx_disable_vp` and `qla24xx_enable_vp` instead, no ISP abort [verified: same]. So the physical TPG is enabled once at boot and never toggled; access control is LUN maps and ALUA, never `enable`.

####### Firmware facts per generation

| Family | Cards | Firmware source on Debian 13 | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| ISP24xx, 4G | QLE2460/2462 | `ql2400_fw.bin` from `firmware-qlogic` 20250410 | tolerated, no promises; loop or point-to-point only |
| ISP25xx, 8G | QLE2560/2562 | `ql2500_fw.bin` 8.07.00, loaded by `request_firmware` before flash with no version comparison (Appendix A) | `ql2xfwloadbin=1` when the installer reads a flash version above 8.07.00, else the blob; floor 8.03 for target mode [believed] |
| ISP83xx, 16G | QLE2670/2672 | flash first; no Debian blob (Appendix A) | floor 8.08, 9.x recommended [believed] |
| ISP2261, 16G | QLE2690/2692/2694 | flash first; no Debian blob | floor 8.08, 9.x recommended [believed] |
| ISP27xx, 32G | QLE2740/2742/2770/2772 | flash first; no Debian blob | 9.x in flash on anything shipped after 2018 [believed]; PCIe 3.0 x8 |

The installer records model, flash firmware, `port_type`, `speed` and mode per port from `/sys/class/fc_host/hostN/` and `/sys/class/scsi_host/hostN/` into the node's hardware inventory and `otapctl hba show` warns below the floor; firmware updates are the operator's job with Marvell's tools under Marvell's licence, never redistributed (R24).

####### NPIV virtual ports per SVM as FC LIFs

`tcm_qla2xxx` registers two fabrics, `qla2xxx` and `qla2xxx_npiv` [verified: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/tcm_qla2xxx.c]. The physical fabric allows only `tpgt_1` ("In non NPIV mode, a single TPG=1 is used for HW port mappings"), the NPIV fabric any tpgt [verified: same]. An NPIV lport directory is named `<physical wwpn>@<npiv wwpn>:<npiv wwnn>`: the part before `@` is parsed strictly as the physical WWPN, the part after must be exactly 16 hex digits, a colon and 16 hex digits [verified: same]; the physical part uses the colon-separated byte form that targetcli shows for the base fabric [believed]. The kernel creates the vport with `vport_id.roles = FC_PORT_ROLE_FCP_INITIATOR` and `vport_type = FC_PORTTYPE_NPIV` and then runs it as a target [verified: same]. Preconditions, all enforced by the driver: the physical port must not be in `enabled` (pure initiator) mode, because `qlt_lport_register` skips any host whose `qlini_mode == QLA2XXX_INI_MODE_ENABLED` [verified: qla_target.c]; the HBA must report `npiv_supported`; the switch must have advertised NPIV in the FLOGI accept ("Check up whether npiv supported switch presented", `VPCERR_NO_FABRIC_SUPP` otherwise); the WWPN must be unique on the HBA; and `num_vhosts` must stay under `max_npiv_vports` [verified: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/qla_mid.c]. A vport only comes up when the base port's topology is fabric (`qla24xx_enable_vp` bails unless `ha->current_topology & ISP_CFG_F`) [verified: same]. So NPIV FC LIFs exist on a switch and nowhere else.

WWPN allocation: NAA 2 format, the first two bytes `2x:xx` vendor-specified, then the 3-byte OUI and 3 bytes of vendor serial [verified: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Wide_Name]. OpenTAP derives a LIF's WWPN as `2A:LL:` followed by the OUI and serial of the home node's lowest physical WWPN, `LL` being the LIF index 0x01 to 0xFF, and the WWNN as `2A:00:` plus the same six bytes; physical QLogic ports use `21:00` and `21:01` in that field, so no collision with any physical port on the fabric is possible, and the pair is stored in Raft at LIF creation and never regenerated. Direct attach has no vports; there the physical WWPN is the SVM's target port and SVMs sharing one port are separated by initiator ACLs only.

Mobility: FC LIFs do not move. Like ONTAP, each SVM gets one vport per node (two WWPNs, one WWNN) and the LUN's ALUA group decides which is live; takeover is a group flip and no fabric state changes. A true move (`rmdir` on the old node, `mkdir` on the new one with the new physical prefix, FDISC with the same WWPN, a new N_Port_ID, RSCN, initiators re-PLOGI and PRLI) is mechanically possible in 2 to 5 s plus the initiators' rediscovery [believed], but it only helps a host with a single path and it interacts with switch features such as port-based zoning; it is an opt-in experiment for Phase B, not a design centre.

####### ALUA target port groups for Phases C, B and A

LIO's per-device `alua/<group>/` directories expose `alua_access_state`, `alua_access_status`, `alua_access_type`, `alua_support_transitioning`, `alua_support_offline`, `alua_support_lba_dependent`, `alua_support_unavailable`, `alua_support_standby`, `alua_support_active_nonoptimized`, `alua_support_active_optimized`, `alua_write_metadata`, `nonop_delay_msecs`, `trans_delay_msecs`, `implicit_trans_secs`, `preferred`, `tg_pt_gp_id` and a read-only `members`; a configfs write to `alua_access_state` is refused "while TPGS_IMPLICIT_ALUA is disabled" [verified: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/target/target_core_configfs.c]. States: Active/Optimized 0x0, Active/Non-optimized 0x1, Standby 0x2, Unavailable 0x3, LBA-dependent 0x4, Offline 0xe, Transitioning 0xf; `implicit_trans_secs` at most 255, default `nonop_delay_msecs` 100 [verified: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/target/target_core_alua.h]. Each LUN names its group through `lun_N/alua_tg_pt_gp` [verified: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/target/target_core_fabric_configfs.c].

Policy: implicit-only (`alua_access_type=1`, LIO's `TPGS_IMPLICIT_ALUA` 0x10), so no initiator can issue SET TARGET PORT GROUPS and fight `nbladed`; `alua_support_active_optimized`, `_standby`, `_unavailable` and `_transitioning` set, `_active_nonoptimized` clear so a stale replica is never a usable path; `implicit_trans_secs=10` to match the hard hold bound; `preferred=1` on the home node's group. Phase C: one group `otap_n1` (id 1), Active/Optimized, TPGS advertised from day one, so ESXi claims the device with VMW_SATP_ALUA and Proxmox multipath uses `prio alua` immediately and nothing on any client changes when the second node arrives. Phase B: byte-identical trees on both nodes (R9); the partner's group `otap_n2` (id 2) is Standby for every LUN it replicates; takeover flips `otap_n1` to Unavailable (or the node is simply silent) and `otap_n2` to Active/Optimized after the rollback gate; Transitioning for at most 2 s then the flip (R7). Phase A: identical, with the shared disks behind both nodes; still Standby, never Active/Non-optimized, because the standby does not own the aggregate. Round-2 `pr_survival` keeps its meaning: the LUN is mapped on the partner only at takeover and APTPL metadata follows under `dbroot`.

####### Direct attach without a switch

QLogic 8G ports negotiate loop or point-to-point; 16G and 32G are point-to-point only [believed].
