With one initiator per port the SVM's target is the physical WWPN, the N2N login is decided by `fcport_is_bigger` (round 2), and an ESXi host needs one port per OpenTAP node to get two ALUA paths, so two hosts on two nodes consume four target ports. ESXi supports direct-attached FC in principle, and the one hard fact is a regression in exactly this topology: Broadcom KB 323068 reports that `qlnativefc` 5.2.46.0, 5.3.1.0 and 5.3.2.0 on ESXi 8.0.x cannot log into direct-attached targets because the driver skips session creation before the adapter is marked online, fixed in 5.4.80 (ESXi 7.0: 4.1.37.0 and later broken, 5.3.80 fixed) [verified: https://knowledge.broadcom.com/external/article/323068]; the client matrix pins the driver. No NPIV in direct attach (above), so multiple SVMs on one directly attached port share one TPG and are separated by ACL-mapped LUN numbers per initiator.

####### ESXi specifics

`Disk.MaxLUN` defaults to 1024, is an exclusive upper bound on scanned LUN IDs, and can be raised to 16384 [verified: https://docs.vmware.com/en/VMware-vSphere/8.0/vsphere-storage/GUID-B538B4B4-FEE2-4C50-9752-50B210118314.html and https://knowledge.broadcom.com/external/article/342823]; OpenTAP allocates LUN IDs 0 to 255 and always maps LUN 0 for every initiator. VMware's default PSP for devices claimed by VMW_SATP_ALUA is VMW_PSP_MRU [verified: https://docs.vmware.com/en/VMware-vSphere/8.0/vsphere-storage/GUID-9B19EF2E-DA5A-43D2-B41F-8E7C112D2E00.html; https://knowledge.broadcom.com/external/article/339621], and Round Robin on ALUA devices "by default will use only the active optimized paths" [verified: KB 339621], so the shipped recipe adds one rule: `esxcli storage nmp satp rule add -s VMW_SATP_ALUA -V LIO-ORG -M OpenTAP -P VMW_PSP_RR -O iops=1 -c tpgs_on -e "OpenTAP"`, syntax [believed] from vendor examples with the same options. LUN classes stay `Esxi512e` before ESXi 9.0 (R18). FC path death on ESXi is RSCN-driven on a fabric and timer-driven on direct attach; the unplanned numbers in the round-2 NDO matrix (RSCN within 1 s plus the ladder) stand. The nvfail presentation on FC (Unavailable versus a PDL sense) is Protocols' question 2 below.

####### Proxmox specifics

Proxmox VE 8 runs bookworm's multipath-tools 0.9.4, Proxmox VE 9.0 (released 5 August 2025, Debian 13, kernel 6.14.8) and 9.1 (19 November 2025, Debian 13.2, kernel 6.17.2) run trixie's multipath-tools 0.11.1-2 [verified: https://pve.proxmox.com/wiki/Roadmap; https://packages.debian.org/trixie/multipath-tools]. multipath-tools 0.11.1 carries a built-in hardware-table entry for vendor `(LIO-ORG|SUSE)`, product `.*`: `GROUP_BY_PRIO`, `PRIO_ALUA`, checker `DIRECTIO`, `no_path_retry 12`, immediate failback, checker detection off [verified: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/opensvc/multipath-tools/0.11.1/libmultipath/hwtable.c]. That is why vendor stays "LIO-ORG" (8 characters, `INQUIRY_VENDOR_LEN`) and the product becomes "OpenTAP" (`INQUIRY_MODEL_LEN` 16) [verified: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/include/target/target_core_base.h]; both are set through `wwn/vendor_id` and `wwn/product_id` and LIO refuses to change them once the device is exported [verified: target_core_configfs.c], so this is a day-one decision. Proxmox's own guidance is to start from an empty `/etc/multipath.conf` with `find_multipaths "strict"`, add each LUN with `multipath -a <wwid>`, install `multipath-tools-boot` for FC LUNs and run `update-initramfs -u -k all` after changes, then `pvcreate`/`vgcreate` on `/dev/mapper/<name>` and mark the LVM storage shared [verified: https://pve.proxmox.com/wiki/Multipath]. `no_path_retry 12` with the default 5 s polling queues for 60 s, four times our 15 s hard bound, then fails I/O, which is the behaviour nvfail wants. PVE 9.0 adds snapshots as qcow2 volume chains on thick LVM over iSCSI or FC LUNs as a technology preview (a storage property, thick snapshot volumes, new disks only) [verified: Roadmap], which closes the main functional gap of FC LUNs under Proxmox.

####### targetcli versus direct configfs writes from nbladed

Direct configfs writes, for three reasons. R9 needs `set_access` and `stop_exporting` under 50 ms, and a Python rtslib round trip plus `saveconfig` rewriting the whole tree is hundreds of milliseconds. `nbladed` is the sole writer of configfs by ruling, and both Debian packages install a competing writer: `python3-rtslib-fb` 2.1.76 ships `rtslib-fb-targetctl.service` and `/usr/bin/targetctl`, which restore `/etc/rtslib-fb-target/saveconfig.json` at boot, and `targetcli-fb` ships `targetclid.service` and `.socket` [verified: https://packages.debian.org/trixie/all/python3-rtslib-fb/filelist; https://packages.debian.org/trixie/all/targetcli-fb/filelist]. The installer does not install either and masks `rtslib-fb-targetctl.service` if an operator adds them; `targetcli ls` is welcome in a support bundle. The `blade_fc` applier shares the core-backstore and ALUA code with `blade_lio` and adds the fabric directory:

```
/sys/kernel/config/target/
  dbroot                                  <- "/var/target" (Phase C); must be set before any device exists
  core/iblock_0/vm-ds1/                   mkdir; control <- "udev_path=/dev/ublkb3"
    wwn/{vendor_id=LIO-ORG, product_id=OpenTAP, revision=0001, vpd_unit_serial=<uuid>}   before enable
    attrib/{emulate_write_cache=1, emulate_tpu=1, emulate_tpws=1, block_size=512|4096, ...}
    alua/otap_n1/{tg_pt_gp_id=1, alua_access_type=1, alua_access_state=0, preferred=1,
                  alua_support_active_optimized=1, alua_support_standby=1, alua_support_unavailable=1,
                  alua_support_transitioning=1, alua_support_active_nonoptimized=0, implicit_trans_secs=10}
    alua/otap_n2/{tg_pt_gp_id=2, ..., alua_access_state=2}             Phase B and A: the partner's group
    enable <- 1
  qla2xxx/21:00:00:24:ff:3a:1b:c0/tpgt_1/                              physical port (direct attach, or no NPIV)
  qla2xxx_npiv/21:00:00:24:ff:3a:1b:c0@2a010024ff3a1bc0:2a000024ff3a1bc0/tpgt_1/   one per SVM LIF on a fabric
    attrib/{generate_node_acls=0, cache_dynamic_acls=0, demo_mode_write_protect=1, demo_mode_login_only=1}
    lun/lun_0 -> ../../../../core/iblock_0/vm-ds1 ;  lun/lun_0/alua_tg_pt_gp <- "otap_n1"
    acls/21:00:00:24:ff:7e:11:22/lun_0 -> ../../lun/lun_0                 mapped LUN 0 for this initiator
    enable <- 1                                                           last; ISP abort on a physical port only
```

The attribute names `generate_node_acls`, `cache_dynamic_acls`, `demo_mode_write_protect`, `prod_mode_write_protect` and `demo_mode_login_only` are the fabric's; `fabric_prot_type` sits one level up and accepts 0, 1 or 3 [verified: tcm_qla2xxx.c]. Mapped LUNs are symlinks handled by `target_fabric_mappedlun_link`, with a `write_protect` attribute per mapping [verified: target_core_fabric_configfs.c]. `nbladed` writes with `std::fs` and rustix 1.1.5; no Python in the data-plane control path.

####### What persists across reboot

Nothing in configfs; it is rebuilt by `nbladed` from Raft within 5 s of `dbladed` reporting its ublk devices ready, in Phase C from a one-voter Raft. What does persist: the modprobe and modules-load drop-ins and the initramfs copy of them; the firmware in the cards' flash and the Debian blob for ISP25xx; the Raft records for LIF WWPNs and WWNNs, initiator ACLs, LUN maps, LUN serials and desired ALUA states; LIO's database root, default `/var/target` with `/etc/target` preferred if it exists [verified: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/target/target_core_internal.h], which holds the PR APTPL files `pr/aptpl_<serial>` (Appendix A) and in Phase A must point at state the partner can read; the fabric's N_Port_IDs are assigned at every FLOGI and FDISC and nothing persists them, and zoning is by WWPN so nothing needs to. Boot order: `qla2xxx` loads in the initramfs in target-only mode and the ports stay quiet (no initiator login, no target until a TPG is enabled); `opentap-dbladed.service` recovers the arena and the ublk devices; `opentap-nbladed.service` applies the tree and enables the physical TPGs, one ISP abort per port, about 10 to 15 s after boot the paths are back and initiators see them through RSCN or their own rescans.

###### 2.4 The fate of otap-ringd and the data-path process topology

`otap-ringd` existed for three reasons, and the pivot removes all three. It owned the RDMA protection domain, memory regions and queue pair, which cannot survive a process; there is no RDMA leg. It ran the TCP receiver so that a `dbladed` restart on the partner never became a GrantUnmirrored; an async receiver that is away for the 2 to 5 s restart budget just lags, and the sender's cursor resumes. It was "the process that must not die" because Placed acknowledgements were in flight; nothing acknowledged to a client now depends on any other process. The arena itself never needed a guardian: it is a hugetlbfs file on a mount created by `run-opentap-arena.mount` (`hugetlbfs`, `pagesize=2M`, `size=8G`) and initialised by `opentap-arena-setup.service` (allocate, write the arena superblock and slot-state page), and a hugetlbfs file's contents live as long as the mount and the file do, not as long as any process that mapped it (R4 already placed creation in systemd for that reason). `dbladed` opens it, maps it `MAP_SHARED`, registers it once and rebuilds the dirty index from the slot-state page and the records' CRCs after a crash, exactly the round-2 re-attach minus the partner.

Proposed topology, per data node:

| Process | Owns | Must not | Restart |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dbladed` | ublk queues, reactors, arena, dirty index, CP, GC, read cache; the shipper reactors (one per outbound relationship) and the receiver reactors (one per inbound relationship) | hold configfs, netns or systemd handles | supervised, 2 s target, 5 s hard (R4); client I/O resumes from the arena, streams resume from cursors |
| `nbladed` | configfs, sysfs, modprobe.d, netns, systemd units, the FC and iSCSI target trees, LIFs | touch the data path | any time; the tree is reconciled, never torn down |
| `otap-ctl` | Raft, leases, epoch page, fence executor, watchdog pet, relationship state thresholds | hold a data-path descriptor | any time |
| per-SVM slices | knfsd, smbd, versitygw | | per SVM |

The shipper and receiver are reactors inside `dbladed` because both sides need the engine: the shipper reads the frozen dirty index and the arena and falls back to CRC-verified disk reads, the receiver writes segments, appends the pending log and switches a map root. Isolating them in a separate process would mean exporting the segment writer and the map over an IPC that round 2 explicitly refused to build before a third node exists. The security argument for a separate receiver (it parses network input) is answered by mTLS peers only, a parser in safe Rust, fuzzing, and each reactor running `catch_unwind` so a parser panic breaks the relationship rather than the engine. Cores: the shipper and receiver threads run on the non-isolated cores at a `CPUWeight` below the ublk reactors and do not busy-poll; one such thread sustains 10GbE and three sustain 25GbE. The round-2 "one mirror core" is returned to the reactor pool. In-flight `SEND_ZC` at a `dbladed` crash completes or is dropped by the kernel, the socket closes, and the receiver's cursor tells the restarted shipper where to continue; no slot can be reused by a restarted `dbladed` until it re-registers the arena, which is after every old notification has been consumed by the kernel on close.

##### 3. Bottlenecks and edge cases

1. Receiver copy at 25GbE. One `recv` copy at 5 to 10 GB/s memcpy plus TCP processing gives 1.2 to 2 GB/s per core [believed]; four connections on three cores reach 2.6 GB/s; the sender is cheaper because it does not copy. 40GbE and 100GbE are not promised until `RECV_ZC` arrives with a 6.15 or later Debian kernel.
2. Destination write rate below the link. A 12-drive RAID6 at 80% full under uniform overwrite lands 0.3 to 0.5 GB/s (Appendix A), a quarter of 10GbE. Credits throttle the sender to that rate and lag grows; coalescing after two queued CPs bounds the backlog by the changed set. The dashboard shows both "ship rate" and "land rate" so the operator sees which side limits.
3. Manifest size under 4 KiB random writes. 1 GB/s of 4 KiB writes is 262,000 extents per second, 2.6 million per 10 s CP, an 84 MB manifest; the 64 MiB part cap splits it, and the memory is the frozen dirty index Storage already holds, not new. Sequential coalescing in the dirty index (adjacent LBAs merged) is Storage's lever.
4. Notification latency pins the arena. `SEND_ZC` releases a buffer only when TCP has received the peer's acknowledgement; a 0.1% loss rate with a 200 ms minimum RTO can pin a chunk for 200 to 400 ms. With 64 MiB in flight per connection, four connections pin 256 MiB worst case, 3% of the arena; a lossy LAN never stalls ingest.
5. Silent copies. Over veth, a Linux bridge, a VLAN on a NIC without scatter-gather, or with TSO off, every notification reports `ZC_COPIED` and the sender pays a copy (about 0.3 of a core per GB/s [believed]); the usage counter triggers the fallback to `IORING_OP_SEND` after 500 copied sends in 1,000.
6. TLS and compression cost. At 10GbE TLS adds about 0.4 of a core per side (AES-GCM 2 to 4 GB/s per core [believed]); zstd level 3 at 1GbE needs two workers to feed 110 MB/s at a 2.5:1 ratio; LZ4 on incompressible data wastes 1 GB/s of CPU per core for nothing, which is why `auto` samples before it commits.
7. TPG enable and `qlini_mode` changes reset the port. `qlt_enable_vha` on a physical port is an ISP abort with a wait for the HBA to come back (2 to 5 s), and a mode change is refused while target mode is active [verified: qla_target.c, qla_attr.c]; both happen only at boot, never on takeover, which is why access control is ALUA and LUN maps.
8. Exchange exhaustion. `ql2xexchoffld` 1024 by default [verified: qla_os.c]; sixteen ESXi hosts at queue depth 64 fill it and the firmware returns QUEUE FULL to the initiators, which ESXi treats as a congestion event and throttles; the profile sets 4096 on 16G and 32G cards and documents the knob.
9. NPIV limits. `max_npiv_vports` comes from the firmware (254 on ISP25xx [believed]) and switches limit logins per F_Port (Brocade 126 by default, Cisco 256 [believed]); OpenTAP caps vports at 32 per physical port and refuses a LIF on a port whose fabric did not advertise NPIV (`VPCERR_NO_FABRIC_SUPP` surfaces as a clear error, not a hang).
10. `Disk.MaxLUN` is exclusive at 1024 [verified]; OpenTAP never allocates above 255, and a LUN mapped above an operator's lowered value simply never appears, which the client-matrix checklist calls out.
11. The ESXi direct-connect driver regression (KB 323068, fixed in `qlnativefc` 5.4.80 on 8.0) [verified]; the matrix pins the driver and the installer's docs warn that a direct-attached ESXi host that sees no target after a driver update is this bug, not a cabling fault.
12. Proxmox queueing. `no_path_retry 12` from the built-in LIO entry queues 60 s then fails [verified entry; the 5 s interval is multipath's default, believed]; a VM on a LUN that nvfail took Unavailable gets I/O errors after 60 s, which is the intended signal, and a 15 s takeover never reaches it.
13. Replica size on the standby. LIO iblock reads the ublk device's size at configure time and 6.12 ublk has no `UPDATE_SIZE` (Appendix A); when a source volume grows, the standby's ublk device for that LUN is re-created at the next apply, which is safe only because Standby paths carry no I/O; in Phase A the shared-disk standby has the same constraint.
14. Single-path hosts on direct attach have no transparent failover: no fabric means no vport move and the second node's port is a different WWPN; documented, not solved.
15. A delta larger than the receiver's free space minus the GC reserve is refused at `DeltaBegin` (`Abort(NoSpace)`) and the relationship goes Broken rather than half-landing; orphan segments from any earlier partial landing are GC-reclaimable, so the refusal is advisory on space, never on correctness.
16. Divergent CPs after a takeover. An old owner that returns holds CPs above the common base; the stream refuses any `DeltaBegin` whose `base` is not the receiver's `applied`, and a `Rebase` to the common snapshot (Consensus decides direction) makes the old owner discard its divergent CPs before it accepts a delta; the format carries the base explicitly so this cannot happen by accident.
17. Intra-node relationships (aggregate 1 to aggregate 2 on one node, the Phase C test vehicle) share one `dbladed`; the loopback path still copies at the receiver, so 1 GB/s intra-node costs about one core, and the two aggregates' CP flushers contend for the same HBA; the exit test measures that.

##### 4. What I would cut or defer

Cut, with no plan to return: FC as a replication transport in any phase; the RDMA stream leg (RoCE and InfiniBand) and the ConnectX-3 qualification, because TCP at 25GbE is three cores and `RECV_ZC` closes the rest later; per-record acknowledgements, the Placed contract, the inbound tmpfs ring, the slot quarantine and the unknown-fate bound; `otap-ringd` and `otap-ringrecv`; the busy-polled mirror core and io_uring NAPI registration; the 20 ms ring heartbeat; `LocalNvmeRing` as a transport implementation (if Storage keeps a local NVMe log for single-node durability it is a `Backstore` concern, not a link); the FC control sideband and the FC LUN mailbox; the `FcLink` capability bits; the dual-mode N2N spike S1 (replaced by the far smaller "asymmetric host-to-target N2N" check in F2 below); endpoint striping.

Deferred: vport migration (Phase B experiment, opt-in); a `FileSink` and an S3 object sink for the same frame format (R21's "objects to S3"), cheap once the format is frozen but not needed before Phase B's second node; `RECV_ZC` and kernel-TLS, both kernel-version-gated; compression tuning beyond the sample rule; NVMe/TCP and NVMe-oF client targets (Protocols' roadmap, unchanged); `pr_survival` for FC to Phase A where PR matters; `ql2xexlogins` and extended logins until someone has more than 1,024 initiator logins per port.

##### 5. Phase C work items, then what Phases B and A add

Phase C, in order, each with an exit test. The stream items come first because the format must freeze before the engine's CP code depends on it; the FC items are protocol step 3 and can run in parallel on lab hardware.

1. `otap-stream` v1: the 64-byte frame, manifest entry, chunking, cursor, codec flags, `DeltaSource`/`DeltaStream`/`DeltaSink` traits, golden vectors, property tests (reordering across connections, duplicates, truncation, torn frames, version N and N+1) and a cargo-fuzz target for the parser. Exit: 10,000 synthetic deltas round-trip bit-exact through a loopback pair; one million random frame mutations without a panic; the format document and vectors are committed and no later change passes review without a `ver` bump.
2. Shipper and receiver reactors inside `dbladed` with an intra-node relationship (aggregate 1 to aggregate 2 on the same node) over a loopback TCP endpoint. Exit: 100 CPs at 1 GB/s ingest streamed intra-node; `kill -9` of `dbladed` at random points in 50 of them; after every restart the replica is at a CP boundary and a BLAKE3 over the replica volume equals the source snapshot's for every committed CP; the receiver's duplicate counter equals the resend count; no manifest part above 64 MiB; one core per 1 GB/s measured.
3. HBA inventory and the FC boot profile: modprobe and modules-load drop-ins, initramfs rebuild, `otapctl hba show` with per-port model, flash firmware, mode, topology and speed, and the firmware floors. Exit: 20 reboots each on a QLE2562 and a QLE2692 pair; every port reports target mode within 15 s of boot; the switch log shows no initiator FLOGI from an OpenTAP port; no ISP abort after the single boot-time enable.
4. `blade_fc` in `nbladed`: the physical-fabric tree, iblock on ublk, vendor "LIO-ORG" and product "OpenTAP", per-initiator ACLs with LUN 0 always mapped, implicit-only ALUA with one Active/Optimized group, TPGS advertised. Exit: an ESXi 8.0 U3 host (qlnativefc at or above 5.4.80) sees the LUN both through a Brocade switch and direct-attached, `esxcli storage nmp device list` shows VMW_SATP_ALUA, a VMFS6 datastore is created, and a one-hour fio inside a VM sustains 700 MB/s sequential on 8G, 1.4 GB/s on 16G, and 50,000 4 KiB IOPS on a flash pool at p99 under 2 ms; `otapctl` applies the whole tree in under 5 s after reboot.
5. Proxmox recipe: PVE 8.4 and 9.1, empty `multipath.conf` (built-in LIO-ORG entry), `multipath -a`, `multipath-tools-boot`, LVM shared, PVE 9 volume-chain snapshots. Exit: two PVE nodes live-migrate a VM on the FC LVM; snapshot create and rollback succeed on 9.1; `multipath -ll` shows `prio alua` groups with the OpenTAP path Active.
6. NPIV vports per SVM on a fabric. Exit: two SVMs, one vport each on one physical port; an initiator zoned to SVM A's vport cannot see SVM B's LUNs; vport create to online under 3 s; 100 create and delete cycles with no ISP abort of the base port and no initiator path flap on the other SVM.
7. Transition behaviour under load: `set_access(Transitioning)` for 2 s then Active/Optimized, 100 times, against ESXi and Proxmox. Exit: no client I/O error; I/O resumes within 2.5 s of each flip; `implicit_trans_secs` honoured.
8. Reboot persistence: `rtslib-fb-targetctl.service` absent or masked, `dbroot` set before the first device, the APTPL file written under it, and a configuration export that reproduces the FC tree on a fresh install. Exit: a from-scratch install plus import yields byte-identical configfs trees (diffed by a script) and the same WWPNs.

Phase B adds, for my area: the two-node stream on real links (items B1 to B3: the `SEND_ZC` fixed path with usage telemetry and fallback, exit 1.1 GB/s on 10GbE with the sender under 0.6 of a core and under 1% copied; TLS and compression as endpoint options, exit 1.0 GB/s with TLS at 1.1 cores per side and 200 MB/s raw over 1GbE with zstd on a 2.5:1 VM corpus; endpoint fallback and resume, exit 100 cable pulls at 80% of line rate with every delta completing, resume within 3 s and zero duplicate applies); the relationship cursor persisted at the receiver's CP; the stream's rows in the timer table (connect 1 s, dead 3 s, back-off 1 to 30 s, fail-back 30 s, lag reported every 1 s) and Consensus's Lagging and Broken thresholds; byte-identical FC trees on both nodes with the partner group in Standby, vport pairs per SVM, the group flip on takeover and giveback with a client-visible FC pause of at most 3 s planned; the vport-migration experiment behind a flag.

Phase A adds: PR for FC LUNs with APTPL under a `dbroot` the partner can read, `pr_survival` for WSFC-class initiators, the shared-shelf standby presenting the same LUN serial on Standby paths, and the FC rows of the round-2 NDO matrix re-measured on the shelf (RSCN within 1 s plus the ladder; logins freed only by the dead node's reset).

##### 6. Questions for the other three personas

To Opus-Storage:
1. Can the shipper consume the frozen dirty index of CP N directly as the manifest, sorted by `(vol, lba)` with each entry's existing `payload_crc`, so that steady-state shipping touches no data on the sender, or does the CP assembly reorder or merge entries after the freeze?
2. After a CP commits, how long do its slots stay resident when the arena has headroom, and may the shipper ask for "retain up to X MiB until shipped" without affecting ingest, or should it always expect to flip to disk reads?
3. On the receiver, can `commit(cp)` be exactly one map-root switch plus a superblock write, and what does the pending log per landed extent look like so that a crash mid-landing leaves only reclaimable orphan segments?
4. What is the read rate of a `birth_cp > base` map walk on an aged HDD pool when the extents are 4 KiB and scattered (my estimate is 100 to 200 random reads per second per drive, 10 to 20 MB/s per drive)? This decides whether catch-up from HDD can ever feed 10GbE or whether coalescing must also sort by physical address.
5. When a source volume grows, how do you want the standby's ublk device re-sized on 6.12 without `UPDATE_SIZE`: re-create at the next apply while the LUN is Standby, or pre-size the replica to the volume's maximum?

To Opus-Protocols:
1. Should an FC LIF (a vport WWPN and WWNN per SVM per node) and an IP LIF share one Raft record type with a transport-specific body, so that SVM placement, home port and mobility rules are written once?
2. For nvfail on FC, which presentation do you want: ALUA Unavailable on every path, or a PDL sense (LOGICAL UNIT NOT SUPPORTED) that ESXi treats as permanent loss? LIO gives us the former for free; the latter needs the LUN unmapped, which is a different `stop_exporting`.
3. Do you accept vendor "LIO-ORG" and product "OpenTAP" as the permanent INQUIRY identity? LIO refuses to change them once exported, and the choice buys the built-in multipath entry on every Debian and Proxmox host.
4. Will an XFS-on-LUN NAS volume ever also be exported as an FC or iSCSI LUN (the same ublk device under both), or are block LUN classes only `Esxi512e` and `Native4k` on dedicated volumes?
5. Where should `dbroot` live in Phase A: the SVM root volume, a replicated directory, or should APTPL be exported as a Raft blob by `exported_state()`?

To Opus-Consensus:
1. The stream reports `lag_bytes`, `lag_cps`, `last_applied_cp`, RTT and throughput every 1 s; which thresholds flip Lagging and Broken, and do you want hysteresis inside the stream or in `otap-ctl`?
2. For FC, is "partner group Standby, own group Unavailable" acceptable as the `stop_exporting` state (sub-50 ms, no ISP abort), with TPG disable reserved for teardown? Any fence that needs the port to vanish from the fabric costs a 2 to 5 s reset.
3. After an old owner returns with divergent CPs, who names the common base and orders the discard: the stream can only refuse a `DeltaBegin` whose base is not the receiver's `applied`, and apply a `Rebase` it is told to.
4. Should relationship cursors stay on the destination aggregate (my position) or be mirrored into Raft, given that a lost cursor costs only a re-send?
5. Under `max_auto_takeover_lag`, do you prefer the stream to ship CPs in order (more recovery points, larger backlog) or to coalesce to the newest CP after two queued (smaller rollback at takeover, fewer points)? I recommend coalescing and keeping the skipped CPs as local snapshots on the source.

### Opus-Consensus

#### 1. Executive take

The pivot removes the partner from the acknowledgement path, and that changes my area more than any other. In round 2 the control plane sat inside the write path (Placed-gated cuts, `GrantUnmirrored`, credits, a 20 ms ring heartbeat); now a client write is acknowledged from local DRAM at 5 to 10 us and nothing I own is consulted except one seqlock page. Leases and epochs become a pure ownership-and-fencing mechanism, the "degraded" apparatus collapses into a protection *report*, and the thing the control plane must get right moves to the takeover decision itself: every unplanned takeover with private disks promotes a copy that is behind the acknowledged state, so takeover needs a gate, a loss printout, an nvfail posture per volume class and a divergence story for the returning node. The SVM is now the unit that moves, so migration is a choreography of netns, mounts, daemons, addresses and grace periods rather than a group flip. Single-node-first means the same control plane must cost nothing in Phase C while staying byte-identical in code. And the witness, which round 2 treated as a vote, becomes a relay: the severed-inter-node-link case turns from an outage into a non-event.

Top five positions:

1. With private disks the lease is the fence; the only new thing between lease expiry and promotion is a rollback gate: automatic takeover when the replica is at most `max_auto_takeover_lag` (default 60 s) behind, manual with an exact loss printout beyond that, and nvfail on by default for datastore-class volumes after any unplanned takeover.
2. The no-quorum posture is `stop` for Phase B (the lease is the only arbiter between two private copies, and "freeze" is a split brain waiting for the first isolated node) and `freeze` for Phase A (the PR reservation is the arbiter); `freeze` in Phase B is permitted only behind a confirmed power fence.
3. The witness fsyncs only on votes and log entries, never on heartbeats, never on replication progress (lag numbers never enter Raft), and it relays Raft and lease RPC between A and B when their direct paths die, so a partition with a live witness costs zero takeovers.
4. Planned SVM migration is pre-copy to a final delta of at most 256 MiB, quiesce, final CP, ship, Raft cutover, mount, LIF move with gratuitous ARP that `nbladed` sends itself: at most 3 s client-visible for block, 2 to 4 s for NFSv3, at most 8 s for NFSv4.1 with reclaim, 10 to 20 s for SMB; unplanned adds 2 to 5 s to the block ladder, and resync always runs survivor to returner with the returner's divergent CPs pinned as a snapshot, never merged.
5. Phase C runs the identical `otap-ctl` with Raft membership `{A}`: zero network RPC, zero witness, one 4 KiB epoch page checked in about 5 ns per I/O, fsync only when an operator changes configuration; going to Phase B is `add_learner` plus a joint-consensus membership change, not a reinstall.

#### 2. Design

##### 2.1 Focus 1: the 3-voter cluster and the failure matrix

**Topology.** Raft membership `{A, B, W}` on openraft 0.9.25, still the newest stable release on crates.io (0.9.25 published 2026-07-28; 0.10 is at 0.10.0-alpha.37 as of 2026-10-10) [verified: https://crates.io/crates/openraft]. W runs `otap-ctl --witness` with `enable_elect = false` (confirmed in round 2, Appendix A), so it votes and acknowledges entries but never campaigns; the leader is always A or B. Leases are granted by the leader after `ensure_linearizable()`, which "confirms the node's leadership at the time of invocation by sending heartbeats to a quorum of followers" [verified: https://docs.rs/openraft/0.9.25/openraft/raft/struct.Raft.html], with no log write. Control paths are `TcpMtls` on the LAN (A-W, B-W, A-B) and on the direct DAC (A-B only); W is 1GbE and never sees the DAC. The Raft configuration maps onto `Config::heartbeat_interval = 100`, `election_timeout_min = 1000`, `election_timeout_max = 2000` (milliseconds; the field names are those of openraft 0.9.25) [verified: https://docs.rs/openraft/0.9.25/openraft/struct.Config.html]; the election window is longer than round 2's 0.5 to 1 s because it must exceed ten times the witness RTT *through the relay* (two hops of 100 ms).

**The relay.** `RaftNetwork` is application-implemented through `RaftNetworkFactory`, one instance per target node, with a default 500 ms constant backoff on `Unreachable` [verified: https://docs.rs/openraft/0.9.25/openraft/network/trait.RaftNetwork.html]. OpenTAP's implementation keeps two routes per target: direct (LAN, then DAC) and `CtlMsg::Relay { to, inner }` through W. AppendEntries, Vote and the lease RPCs may ride the relay; the replication stream never does (a Pi's 1GbE cannot carry it, and it must not). Cost: two extra witness RTTs, at most 200 ms nominal and 400 ms at p99 jitter, against a lease renewed every 500 ms with a 3 s TTL, so a holder tolerates five consecutive misses. Relay traffic is about 30 messages per second per node at about 1 KiB each, 60 KB/s through the witness.

**How the cluster tells the three faults apart.** Each node has four evidence sources: direct control heartbeats per path (100 ms, dead at 2 s), the witness's liveness view of both nodes (`last_heard_ms: {A, B}` piggybacked on every AppendEntries response and relay frame), the leader's lease table (last grant per aggregate on the leader's `CLOCK_MONOTONIC`), and BMC power state (positive evidence only when it reads Off). The rule is three-way and is the heart of the matrix: a partner that is silent on every direct path is **dead** only if W is reachable and W has not heard it for at least 2 s either; if W still hears it, it is a **partition** and the relay takes over; if W is unreachable too, it is **no quorum** and section 2.7 applies.

| Fault | What A, B and W see | Raft and leases | Replication | Client-visible | Alert |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| W down (host rebooted, card died) | A and B hear each other on 2 paths; W silent | leader keeps 2 of 3; leases unchanged | unaffected | nothing | WARN `witness_down` at 2 s, CRIT after 10 min (next fault is no quorum) |
| DAC down only | control on LAN fine | unchanged | stream fails over to the LAN per Fabrics' policy, else `Lagging` | nothing | WARN link |
| LAN switch dead, DAC up | A and B on the DAC; W unreachable from both | A and B keep 2 of 3 between them | unaffected (stream on the DAC) | LIFs on that switch are unreachable, which is a client network fault, not a storage one | WARN witness |
| A-B fully severed, both reach W | direct silent both ways; W hears both | relay engaged; no election; leases renewed via W | stream dead at 3 s, `Lagging`; both keep serving their own aggregates; **no takeover** | nothing | CRIT `internode_partition` |
| A isolated (reaches neither B nor W) | B: A silent, W does not hear A; A: no leader | A's renewals fail: hold, Transitioning, stop acking at TTL, final local CP; B+W: L1/L2 at 4.3 s, rollback gate, takeover | A's unshipped CPs become divergent on its return | A's paths vanish; B serves at about 5 s p50 | CRIT takeover with loss printout |
| A dead (power) | same as above plus BMC Off | BMC Off is positive evidence: the RST proxy may run | same | 5 s p50, 9 s p99 block | CRIT |
| A wedged (on the wire, not petting) | heartbeats answered by nothing useful | lease lapse at 3 s, watchdog 5 s, reset about 3 s; B takes over at 4.3 s regardless | same | 11 to 13 s, hard 15 s | CRIT |
| W down and A-B severed (no quorum) | each node alone, 1 of 3 | no leader can run `ensure_linearizable()`; posture per 2.7 (`stop` in Phase B) | stream dead | hold at 3 s, Transitioning, resume within 1 s of quorum returning | CRIT `no_quorum` |
| W and A die together (same host or PDU) | B alone | `stop` | n/a | outage until W or A returns | CRIT; the install check in 2.6 exists for this |
| W paused or snapshotted | as "W down" for the duration | leader resends missing entries or a snapshot on resume | unaffected | nothing | WARN |
| A-B flapping (one flap per 20 s) | relay engaged and released | never a takeover: W hears both | stream hysteresis 30 s stable before fail-back | nothing after the first | one alert |

Witness constraints and storage are in 2.6; the no-quorum posture is argued in 2.7. The install guide's one hard recommendation follows from the third row: a direct DAC (about 20 to 40 dollars for an SFP+ cable [believed]) carrying both the stream and a control path turns "switch dead" into "witness down" (zero interruption) instead of "no quorum" (stop). With Ethernet-only nodes on one switch, no-quorum coincides with "no client can reach us either", which is why `stop` costs little there.

##### 2.2 Focus 2: the degraded posture without throttling, with honest alerts

**What `unmirrored_flush = placed` means now.** In the async design every acknowledgement is local: "placed" means placed in the hugetlbfs arena with the dirty index updated, 5 to 10 us. There is no mirrored acknowledgement to fall back from, so nothing degrades in the write path when the partner leaves; what degrades is *protection*. Consequences for round 2: `GrantUnmirrored`, `RevokeUnmirrored`, the three-grants-in-ten-minutes hysteresis, the forced 2 s CP interval and the `Credit` contract are deleted. The control plane never throttles and never changes the CP interval on relationship state; the engine may still shorten CPs on its own arena high-water mark (Storage's call). `local_nvme` survives as Storage's optional PLP log that makes the local acknowledgement crash-durable; `cp` is dropped because the owner ruled out throttling.

**Protection state** is computed per aggregate by the owner's `otap-ctl` from stream heartbeats (1 s), published in the epoch page (`protection` field, alert-only, never gating I/O) and in Prometheus, and never written to Raft.

| State | Event | Action | Next |
|---|---|---|---|
| Single (Phase C, or no relationship by policy) | relationship created and baseline complete | label "one copy" removed | Protected |
| Protected | replica's newest complete CP older than `insync_lag_max` (2 × CP interval: 20 s HDD, 10 s flash), or stream link dead 3 s | WARN with seconds of acknowledged writes in one copy, bytes unshipped, volumes dirty since the last shipped CP | Exposed |
| Exposed | lag exceeds `max_auto_takeover_lag` (60 s) | CRIT: "a failure of this node is now a manual recovery"; reminder hourly | Exposed (CRIT) |
| Exposed | CP applied on the replica within `insync_lag_max` | clear alert (rate-limited: one per transition) | Protected |
| Exposed | partner absent longer than `break_after` (24 h) or the source drops the base under Storage's spill policy | CRIT: relationship Broken, replica unusable | Unprotected |
| Unprotected | operator `otapctl rel baseline` completes | INFO | Protected |

**Relationship state** has a Raft-resident label (changes only on transitions, a handful per week) and a runtime part that never enters Raft:

```rust
// Raft-resident: small, versioned, changes only on state transitions.
pub struct Relationship { pub ver: u16, pub id: RelId, pub src: VolRef, pub dst: VolRef,
    pub policy: RelPolicy, pub state: RelState, pub base: Option<BaseId>, pub src_epoch: u64 }
pub struct RelPolicy { pub insync_lag_max: Duration, pub max_auto_takeover_lag: Option<Duration>,
    pub break_after: Duration, pub precopy_final_delta_max: u64, pub precopy_rounds_max: u8 }
pub enum RelState { Baseline, Idle /* InSync or Lagging: decided at runtime */, Quiesced,
    Resync { from: NodeId, to: NodeId, base: BaseId }, Broken { reason: BreakReason } }
pub struct BaseId { pub cp_seq: u64, pub owner_epoch: u64, pub snap: SnapId }   // the common base both sides pin
// Runtime, on the owner and the replica, from the 1 s stream heartbeat; never in Raft:
pub struct RelLive { pub src_committed_cp: u64, pub dst_applied_cp: u64, pub dst_applied_age: Duration,
    pub unshipped_bytes: u64, pub link: LinkHealth, pub dirty_vols_1s: VolBitSet,
    pub sub: SubState /* InSync | Lagging */ }
```

| State | Event | Action | Next |
|---|---|---|---|
| Baseline | full transfer completes at a CP boundary | pin base on both sides; Raft `SetRel(Idle)` | Idle/InSync |
| Idle/InSync | replica CP age > `insync_lag_max` or link dead 3 s | protection to Exposed; no Raft write | Idle/Lagging |
| Idle/Lagging | CP applied within threshold | protection to Protected | Idle/InSync |
| Idle (either) | planned migration starts | pre-copy rounds, then quiesce | Quiesced |
| Quiesced | final CP applied on the destination | Raft `Takeover{planned}`; direction reversed; base = final CP | Idle/InSync (reversed) |
| Idle (either) | unplanned takeover committed | survivor is source; Raft `SetRel(Resync{B->A, base = promote CP})` | Resync |
| Resync | returning node rolls back to base and applies the first CP of the new epoch | eligibility resumes from that CP | Idle |
| Idle/Lagging | `break_after` elapsed or base dropped | Raft `SetRel(Broken)`; CRIT | Broken |
| Broken | operator baseline | full transfer | Baseline |

**Alert thresholds and takeover eligibility.** WARN at lag > `insync_lag_max` sustained 30 s; CRIT at lag > `max_auto_takeover_lag`, at link dead > 60 s, and at Broken; INFO at each 10% of a resync. Every alert carries the four facts the owner asked for: seconds of acknowledged writes that exist in one copy only, bytes unshipped, the volumes written since the last shipped CP, and the one-line command that forces the next step. Eligibility: InSync is automatic; Lagging at most 60 s is automatic; Lagging beyond 60 s is manual with the printout; Resync is eligible only from the newest complete CP of the *current* source epoch, under the same 60 s rule; Baseline and Broken are impossible (no promote point); Phase A shared disks are always eligible (the shelf holds the last CP) with nvfail applied to the DRAM window only.

```toml
[cluster]
id = "otap-7f3a"                       # voters a, b; witness w
no_quorum_posture = "stop"             # "freeze" needs fence.power = "confirmed" (Phase B) or media = "shelf_pr" (Phase A)

[witness]
addr = "10.0.0.9:7443"
kind = "pi"                            # pi | container | vm
relay = true                           # Raft and lease RPC may route through the witness

[raft]
heartbeat_interval_ms = 100
election_timeout_ms = [1000, 2000]
lease_ttl_ms = 3000
lease_renew_ms = 500
lease_margin_ms = 100

[takeover]
mode = "auto"                          # auto | manual
max_auto_takeover_lag = "60s"          # "0s" = manual only; per-SVM override
nvfail_after_takeover = { datastore = "on", file = "off", object = "off" }
auto_giveback_delay = "600s"
business_hours = "08:00-18:00 Mon-Fri"

[replication]
insync_lag_max = "20s"                 # default 2 x cp_interval
alert_warn_lag = "20s"
alert_crit_lag = "60s"
break_after = "24h"
precopy_final_delta_max = "256MiB"
precopy_rounds_max = 5
divergent_snapshot_keep = "7d"
```

##### 2.3 Focus 3: SVM mobility and LIF failover

**Placement rule.** In Phase B an SVM's root volume and data volumes live on aggregates owned by one node; the SVM's `placement` in Raft equals the owner of its root aggregate, and a volume on the other node's aggregate is refused by the API. An SVM therefore moves with its aggregate, planned or unplanned; LIF-only migration stays cut (section 4).

**Warm standby.** The partner holds a skeleton for every SVM it may receive: the network namespace (`otap-svm-<id>`), the UTS namespace for `rpc.nfsd --scope` (Protocols decides whether that is systemd's `ProtectHostname=`, which "sets up a new UTS namespace for the executed processes" [verified: https://manpages.debian.org/trixie/systemd/systemd.exec.5.en.html], or an explicit unshare), units that join the netns with `NetworkNamespacePath=` ("the invoked processes are added to the network namespace referenced by that path"; system services only) [verified: same page] in state `inactive`, no addresses, and the volume LUNs' ublk devices pre-created with the gate closed. systemd in trixie is 257.13-1~deb13u1 [verified: https://packages.debian.org/trixie/systemd]. Kernel memory for a skeleton is about 50 to 100 KiB per netns [believed]; fifty skeletons cost under 10 MiB.

```rust
pub enum SvmPhase { Standby, Preparing, Quiescing, Active, Draining, Torn }
pub trait SvmMobility {                      // nbladed; idempotent; driven by Raft SvmState.placement
    fn ensure_standby(&mut self, svm: &SvmSpec) -> Result<(), MobErr>;   // netns, utsns, inactive units, gate closed
    fn drain(&mut self, svm: SvmId, deadline: Duration) -> Result<DrainReport, MobErr>;
        // NAS LIFs down, smbd and versitygw SIGTERM, `rpc.nfsd 0` in the netns, clean XFS unmount
    fn activate(&mut self, svm: SvmId) -> Result<ActivateReport, MobErr>;
        // mounts, nfsd in grace from the root volume's nfsdcld db, smbd, versitygw, LIFs up with GARP
    fn lif_up(&mut self, lif: &LifSpec) -> Result<(), MobErr>;    // RTM_NEWADDR in the netns, then 3 GARP + 3 unsolicited NA
    fn lif_down(&mut self, lif: &LifSpec) -> Result<(), MobErr>;  // RTM_DELADDR; under 50 ms
    fn end_grace(&mut self, svm: SvmId) -> Result<(), MobErr>;    // writes "Y" to /proc/fs/nfsd/v4_end_grace in the netns
}
```

**LIF move mechanics.** Addresses are added and removed with netlink (`rtnetlink` 0.23.0 [verified: https://crates.io/crates/rtnetlink]) inside the SVM's netns, entered with `setns(2)` (`nix` 0.31.3 or `rustix` 1.1.5 [verified: https://crates.io/crates/nix, https://crates.io/crates/rustix]; the exact wrapper is [believed]). The kernel will not announce the move for us: `arp_notify` and `ndisc_notify` only "generate gratuitous arp requests when device is brought up or hardware address changes", not when an address is added [verified: https://elixir.bootlin.com/linux/v6.12/source/Documentation/networking/ip-sysctl.rst]. So `nbladed` sends the announcements itself: three gratuitous ARP requests and three ARP replies over 300 ms from an `AF_PACKET` socket in the netns (about 60 lines), with `arping -U` and `-A` from iputils-arping 3:20240905-3 ("Unsolicited ARP mode to update neighbours' ARP caches"; `-A` the same with replies) as the reference behaviour and the fallback [verified: https://manpages.debian.org/trixie/iputils-arping/arping.8.en.html, https://packages.debian.org/trixie/iputils-arping]. Block portals do not move: iSCSI and NVMe/TCP portals are node-level, and ALUA does the switch (Protocols' configfs-namespace question decides whether that stays true).

**Planned sequence with timings** (assumptions: 200 MB/s ingest, which is a hypervisor burst and four times a homelab average; 10GbE stream at 1 GB/s payload; HDD RAID6 draining 1.2 GB/s when empty).

| Step | Where | Action | Duration | Client-visible |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P0 | leader | preflight vetoes: relationship not Idle, GC urgent, S3 job running, open SMB handles above threshold, business hours | 0 | no |
| P1 | A to B | pre-copy: CP and ship, repeat until the delta is at most 256 MiB or 5 rounds; 2 GB (2 s), then 400 MB (0.4 s), then 80 MB: done after round 2 | about 3 s | no |
| P2 | A | NAS drain: NAS LIFs down first (clients fail fast and retry instead of hanging on a half-torn SVM), smbd and versitygw SIGTERM, `rpc.nfsd 0`, clean XFS unmount | 0.5 to 2 s | NAS pause starts |
| P3 | A | block quiesce: TPGs to Transitioning (`alua_access_state`, which calls `core_alua_do_port_transition` and requires implicit ALUA [verified: https://elixir.bootlin.com/linux/v6.12/source/drivers/target/target_core_configfs.c]); hold new writes under the 2 s budget; drain in-flight | 50 to 200 ms | block pause starts |
| P4 | A | final CP: at most 256 MiB plus writes during P3, full stripes at 1.2 GB/s, map pages, FUA superblock | 250 to 500 ms | yes |
| P5 | A to B | ship and apply atomically as B's own CP | 250 to 500 ms | yes |
| P6 | Raft | commit `Takeover{planned, agg, B, e+1}`: one witness RTT plus the witness's append fsync | 100 to 250 ms | yes |
| P7 | B | epoch e+1 in the page, takeover superblock, TPGs Active/Optimized on B and Standby on A; multipath switches on the next I/O | 100 to 300 ms | block pause ends: 1.0 to 1.5 s p50, budget 3 s |
| P8 | B | XFS mounts (clean logs, 100 to 300 ms each, in parallel), `rpc.nfsd N --scope` in the netns (grace starts), smbd 0.5 to 1 s, versitygw 0.5 to 2 s | 1 to 3 s | yes |
| P9 | B | NAS LIFs up plus GARP; switches relearn in milliseconds | 50 ms | NFSv3 pause ends: 2 to 4 s total |
| P10 | B | NFSv4.1 reclaim; `otap-ctl` writes `v4_end_grace` once nfsdcld shows every prior-epoch client reclaimed | I/O on reclaimed state within 8 s; new opens up to 20 s | yes |
| P11 | clients | SMB sessions reconnect; files open at cutover get errors (the disruptive label stands) | 10 to 20 s | yes |
| P12 | A, Raft | A's role to Replica; relationship reversed with base = the final CP (no divergence by construction) | 0 | no |

Giveback is the same sequence in the other direction. If pre-copy does not converge (a 1GbE fallback link at 110 MB/s under 200 MB/s ingest never gets below 256 MiB), the migration is refused with the number; a `--force` that would hold clients for delta divided by link rate, over 10 s, is not offered.

**Unplanned sequence with the rollback gate.** 0 s: A dies. 0.1 to 2 s: heartbeats missing on every path; W stops hearing A. 1.0 to 2.2 s: if A was leader, B wins the election with W (election timeout plus the witness's vote fsync). 2 s: partner silent on all direct paths and in W's view. 4.3 s p50, 5.3 s p99: L1 (TTL plus margin after the new term) or L2 (last grant plus 3.1 s when B was already leader) satisfied; B runs the rollback gate on its *local* replica state, under 1 ms and without RPC:

```rust
pub enum Eligibility { Auto { lag: Duration, loss: Loss }, Manual { lag: Duration, loss: Loss, reason: &'static str },
    Impossible { reason: &'static str } }
pub struct Loss { pub seconds: f32, pub bytes_min: u64, pub bytes_max: u64, pub vols_possibly_affected: Vec<VolId> }
pub struct GateInput<'a> { pub agg: AggId, pub rel: &'a RelState, pub live: &'a RelLive, pub replica_sb: &'a ReplicaSuper,
    pub policy: &'a TakeoverPolicy, pub evidence: &'a [FenceEvidence], pub media: &'a Media }
pub fn rollback_gate(i: GateInput<'_>) -> Eligibility;    // pure function; property-tested; no clocks but CLOCK_MONOTONIC
// lag = (now_mono - replica_sb.recv_mono_of_last_complete_cp) + replica_sb.cp_age_at_send   (no wall clock, no skew)
```

If automatic and eligible, B proposes `Takeover{unplanned, agg, B, e+1, promote_cp, loss}` and it commits at about 4.5 s. B flips the epoch, writes the promote superblock at epoch e+1 with `nvfail_pending` set for nvfail-on volumes, raises Active/Optimized for nvfail-off LUNs, and leaves nvfail-on LUNs Unavailable with the PDL-style presentation Protocols specifies; NAS SVMs mount (XFS log replay on a crash-consistent image, 0.5 to 3 s), start nfsd in grace, smbd, versitygw, LIFs plus GARP. Block resume stays at 5 s p50 and 9 s p99; NAS resume is 2 to 5 s later. If ineligible, the aggregate enters `TakeoverPending{LagExceeded}`, a CRIT alert repeats every 5 minutes with the exact command and the exact seconds and bytes it would discard, B's exports stay Standby so clients hold, and if A returns first it resumes as owner at the same epoch with zero loss and the pending state is cancelled.

**Epoch page on survivor and returner.** The survivor writes e+1 before any export; the stream receiver rejects every CP record whose `owner_epoch` is below e+1, so A's in-flight delta for CP K+1 is dropped and the promote point is the last complete CP K. The returning node boots with every slot `Fenced` (the page is initialised before `dbladed` starts), joins as a follower, and compares Raft's `(owner, epoch)` with its superblock: equal means it requests a lease and becomes `Owner` again (A was simply away; the replica catches up); Raft epoch higher means role `Divergent`: it never exports, pins its local head as snapshot `divergent-e<epoch>-cp<K+m>`, rolls its map root back to the common base K (the last CP A recorded as acknowledged-applied by B, which Storage must keep in A's superblock), and accepts B's stream from K. Superblock epoch above Raft's is impossible unless Raft lost data, and is refused with an alert.

```rust
#[repr(C, align(64))] pub struct AggSlot {       // 60 slots in one 4 KiB seqlock page; MAP_SHARED; written by otap-ctl only
    pub agg: u64, pub epoch: u64,
    pub role: u32,          // Single | Owner | Replica | Divergent | Fenced
    pub state: u32,         // Owned | Standby | Transitioning | Fenced   (checked at submission and completion)
    pub serving: u32,
    pub protection: u32,    // Single | Protected | Exposed | Unprotected   (alerts only; never gates I/O)
    pub lease_expiry_mono_ns: u64, pub gate_seq: u64,
    pub nvfail_pending_vols: u64,   // bitset of the first 64 volumes; bit 63 set means "all"
    pub _pad: [u8; 8] }
// check(agg, epoch, now_ns): role in {Single, Owner} and state == Owned and now_ns < lease_expiry (Single: no lease).
// Readers re-read CLOCK_MONOTONIC after every blocking call (paused-VM rule, carried from round 2).
```

##### 2.4 Focus 4: Phase C, the same control plane with one voter

`Raft::initialize` "will work for single-node or multi-node cluster formation" and the initialised node then enters Candidate state and elects itself [verified: https://docs.rs/openraft/0.9.25/openraft/raft/struct.Raft.html]. Phase C is membership `{A}`: the same `otap-ctl`, the same `ClusterState`, the same reconciler in `nbladed`, the same epoch page, the same `SvmMobility` minus the cross-node half. "No clustering overhead" means, concretely: no network RPC in any I/O path (true in every phase; the lease is read from the page); no Raft network traffic at all; `ensure_linearizable()` is a local round with a quorum of one, so the 500 ms lease renewal is a function call; per-I/O cost is one seqlock read, two loads and a compare, about 5 ns [believed; measured in C1]; no witness, no relay, no stream heartbeat; no dedicated core (`otap-ctl` shares the housekeeping core at under 0.5% CPU); `otap-ctl` RSS at most 64 MiB and `nbladed` at most 64 MiB; one fsync per operator configuration change through redb's `Durability::Immediate`, which "guarantee[s] persistence as soon as `WriteTransaction::commit` returns" (redb 4.3.0, 2026-09-15; 2.6.4 of 2026-10-02 is the maintenance line) [verified: https://docs.rs/redb/4.3.0/redb/enum.Durability.html, https://crates.io/crates/redb]. What stays because it is not clustering: the watchdog (5 s, pet 500 ms) with data-path check-ins, because a wedged single node must reset itself so clients get it back within their own timeouts; the daemon restart budget (ublk `USER_RECOVERY` and `REISSUE`, Appendix A); nvfail after a dirty boot. What leaves the timer table in Phase C: leases over the network, election, partner silent, witness RTT, stream heartbeat, pre-copy, the rollback gate. Upgrade to Phase B is `otapctl cluster add-node b` and `add-witness w`: `add_learner` for each, then `change_membership({a, b, w})`, which "proposes a joint config" and then a uniform one [verified: same Raft page]; existing aggregates get `home = a`, relationships are created per volume and baseline; no reformat, no page format change.

##### 2.5 Fence evidence, `max_auto_takeover_lag`, the default, nvfail, divergent writes and resync direction

**Fence evidence with private disks.** `Lease` is necessary and sufficient: the old owner cannot write the survivor's disks, and L3 (page check at completion) plus L4 (no watchdog pet while export-active past expiry) stop it acknowledging clients after TTL plus margin. "Lease" is defined as: TTL plus margin elapsed since the last grant the leader knows of (or since the new term began), *and* the partner silent on every direct path, *and* W reporting the same silence, for at least 2 s. `PowerOffConfirmed` and `WatchdogDeadlinePassed` only accelerate the RST proxy. Phase A adds the mandatory media fence: PR preempt-and-abort on every member with `sg_persist` from sg3-utils 1.48-3~deb13u1 [verified: https://packages.debian.org/trixie/sg3-utils] before the `DataReady` barrier.

**`max_auto_takeover_lag`.** Lag is the age of the newest complete CP the replica holds, computed from the replica's own monotonic clock plus the sender-reported age of that CP at send time, so it needs no synchronised wall clocks. Default 60 s, per-SVM override, `0s` means manual only, unset means always automatic (lab use). Why 60 s: it is three to six CP intervals, it is what a single congested minute looks like, and a rollback of one minute of a datastore is what nvfail exists for; beyond it, a rollback is a restore-from-backup event the operator must choose while the alternative (wait for A) loses nothing.

**Automatic or manual.** Automatic within the lag bound, manual beyond, both with nvfail by class. Not manual-only (ONTAP's SnapMirror default) because the owner asked for storage that continues; not always-automatic because unbounded rollback is not a storage decision. This is owner decision D6 (the number) with D5 (the nvfail defaults).

**nvfail after takeover.** Borrowed from ONTAP, where NVFAIL on takeover brings the volume's LUNs offline "to block FC/iSCSI access to LUNs in a volume that may have lost the latest nvlog updates" until `lun online`, with host-side consistency checks the administrator's responsibility [verified: https://docs.netapp.com/us-en/ontap-ems/lun-nvfail-events.html, https://docs.netapp.com/us-en/ontap-metrocluster/manage/concept_monitoring_and_protecting_database_validity_by_using_nvfail.html]. OpenTAP: `datastore` class (iSCSI and FC LUNs, NFSv3 datastores) is on: LUNs Unavailable with Protocols' PDL presentation, exports withheld, until `otapctl nvfail clear --agg X` prints the window and the operator restarts the VMs; `file` class (NFSv4.1, SMB) is off by default, because home-directory clients tolerate a crash-consistent rollback and the alternative is an outage, with Protocols' fsid bump as the opt-in; `object` is off (versitygw multipart state lives on the volume). Auto-clear is the same install-time opt-in as R5.

**Divergent writes.** A's unshipped CPs K+1 to K+m (the DRAM window at death is simply gone) are pinned on return as `divergent-e<epoch>-cp<K+m>`, mountable read-only through `otapctl snapshot mount` for salvage, kept `divergent_snapshot_keep = 7d` or until the aggregate crosses `write_stop`, never merged automatically. Typical size is lag times ingest: 60 s at 100 MB/s is 6 GB.

**Resync direction rules.** R-a: the Raft owner at the current epoch is always the source. R-b: destination content newer than the common base is discarded after being pinned, which is exactly `snapmirror resync`, where the default "finds the most recent common Snapshot copy" and removes destination snapshots newer than it under a data-loss warning [verified: https://docs.netapp.com/us-en/ontap-cli-9171/snapmirror-resync.html]. R-c: the common base is the newest CP the source knows the destination applied *and* still holds; absent that, Baseline. R-d: a planned migration hands over at a CP boundary, so its resync is instant. R-e: direction reverses only through a planned migration, never by "resyncing toward" a returning node while the survivor serves. R-f: resync rides the ordinary stream at link rate, and eligibility during it is the newest complete CP of the current epoch.

##### 2.6 Witness constraints: Pi on an SD card, container, VM, arm64, what it stores

The witness fsyncs twice per event class and never otherwise: `save_vote`, where "the vote must be persisted on disk before returning", and `append`, where "when the callback is called, the entries must be persisted on disk" [verified: https://docs.rs/openraft/0.9.25/openraft/storage/trait.RaftLogStorage.html]. Heartbeats carry no entries and trigger no flush, and because leases, lag and CP progress never enter the log, a steady-state day has zero fsyncs on the witness and a busy day with planned operations has under 100. The arithmetic that justifies the rule [believed, with the assumptions stated]: a per-heartbeat fsync at 10 Hz is 864,000 commits per day of about 12 KiB each (two redb headers plus one leaf), 10 GB logical, and with a consumer card's write amplification of 10 to 30 for 4 KiB writes that is 100 to 300 GB per day against 16 to 96 TBW endurance: months, not years. The latency argument is stronger still: microSD fsync is 5 to 50 ms with garbage-collection stalls past 500 ms, which inside a 100 ms heartbeat loop would cause spurious elections; moved to rare entry commits it costs at most a few hundred milliseconds on a takeover's commit path, inside the 9 s p99.

Form factors: a Raspberry Pi 4 or 5 on Raspberry Pi OS Lite 64-bit, which has been Debian 13 trixie with the 6.12 kernel since October 2025 [verified: https://www.cnx-software.com/2025/10/06/raspberry-pi-os-debian-13-trixie/], ext4 `data=ordered`, no swap, a USB SSD recommended but not required; a Proxmox LXC container, unprivileged, one bind mount, inbound and outbound TCP 7443 only, no capabilities, no hugepages, no watchdog; a VM with 1 vCPU, 512 MB and 2 GB of disk. The install check `otapctl witness check` refuses a witness whose declared hypervisor host equals a data node's (relevant only when OpenTAP itself runs as a VM) and prints the separate-power, separate-switch guidance. The binary is the same `otap-ctl` cross-built for `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`, a Tier 1 target with host tools [verified: https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/rustc/platform-support.html], from the same crates (openraft 0.9.25, redb 4.3.0, tokio 1.53.2, rustls 0.23.45, postcard 1.1.3, axum 0.8.9 [verified: https://crates.io/crates/tokio, https://crates.io/crates/rustls, https://crates.io/crates/postcard, https://crates.io/crates/axum]); CI runs an arm64 QEMU lane and ships `otap-witness_<ver>_arm64.deb` version-locked to the release with N and N-1 accepted across an upgrade.

What it stores, and only this: the vote (term, node), the log (entries are rare), the `ClusterState` snapshot (under 1 MB), its mTLS certificate and key signed by the cluster CA, and the nightly rehearsal records that the leader commits. Never: leases, lag, CP progress, replication cursors, client state, data, or any secret in plaintext (R23 stands).

##### 2.7 The no-quorum posture: freeze versus stop, Phase B versus Phase A

| | Phase B, private disks | Phase A, shared disks with PR |
|---|---|---|
| `stop` (the lease is the fence) | **default.** At TTL: hold at most 2 s, Transitioning, Unavailable at the 10 s hard bound; a final CP to local disks at TTL so the node itself loses nothing; resume within one renewal of quorum returning, same epoch, no takeover, no resync. | allowed; the final CP lands on the shelf, so a later takeover by the partner is lossless. |
| `freeze` (serve what you own, never take over) | only with a confirmed power fence on both nodes; a takeover after any no-quorum interval then requires `PowerOffConfirmed`; the installer refuses `freeze` without it. | **default.** PR preempt is the arbiter: a frozen node's late writes fail with RESERVATION CONFLICT, which it treats as "I am no longer the owner" and stops acknowledging; its unflushed window (at most one CP interval) is lost and flagged by nvfail. |

The justification is one sequence. Under `freeze` with private disks, A loses both W and B (A is isolated; B and W still see each other). A, seeing no quorum, keeps serving its clients. B and W, seeing A silent, take over from the replica at 4.3 s. Two nodes now acknowledge writes for the same LUN identity to the same multipath clients in overlapping real time, and nothing physical arbitrates: that is a split brain, and it needs only one fault, not two. The lease-expiry stop is precisely what makes B's later takeover safe, so `freeze` is safe only where something other than the lease arbitrates: a PR reservation (Phase A) or a confirmed power-off (Phase B with iDRAC, IPMI, Redfish or a PDU through fence-agents 4.16.0-3, a transitional package to fence-agents-all [verified: https://packages.debian.org/trixie/fence-agents]). Phase A also has the `ShelfMailbox` control path, so "A-B severed but both alive with the shelf" cannot occur; the only way A goes silent on the mailbox is losing the shelf, which means it cannot serve anyway. ONTAP's precedent is the same shape: with the ISL and the mediator both down, MetroCluster IP performs no switchover and remote plexes go offline [verified: https://kb.netapp.com/on-prem/ontap/mc/MC-KBs/MetroCluster_IP__Is_there_any_impact_for_when_the_ISL_and_mediator_connection_is_down], while the sites keep their own aggregates because shared mailbox disks and SyncMirror plexes arbitrate [believed]. What `stop` costs the clients: hold at 3 s, paths Transitioning by 5 s, Unavailable by 13 s; ESXi iSCSI holds VM I/O through APD for 140 s by default, Windows 60 s, Linux dm-multipath with the shipped `no_path_retry queue` indefinitely, ESXi NFSv3 113 to 130 s (Appendix A timers). A witness reboot of 60 s is survived by every client class except Windows without MPIO, and the chance of a no-quorum event is the product of two independent faults. This is owner decision D7.

##### 2.8 Phase C: one voter and "no clustering overhead" in numbers

Section 2.4 gives the design; the numbers in one table so the owner can test the claim.

| Cost | Phase B | Phase C |
|---|---|---|
| Per-I/O control-plane cost | one seqlock read, about 5 ns | identical |
| Network RPC per second (control) | about 30 per node plus Raft heartbeats at 10 per peer | 0 |
| Fsyncs per day on `otap-ctl` | planned operations only, under 100 | configuration changes only |
| Cores | one pinned to `otap-ctl` | none; housekeeping core, under 0.5% |
| RSS `otap-ctl` / `nbladed` | at most 128 MiB each, `MemoryMax=256M` / `512M` | at most 64 MiB each |
| Witness | VM, container or Pi | none |
| Timers kept | all of 2.10 | watchdog, daemon restart, CP (Storage), nvfail |

##### 2.9 Relationship states, alert thresholds and takeover eligibility

Section 2.2 holds the two state tables, the TOML and the eligibility rule. One addition the owner should see: the states are deliberately few (Baseline, Idle with its runtime InSync/Lagging sub-state, Quiesced, Resync, Broken) because every state that lives in Raft costs a witness fsync per transition and an operator concept; InSync versus Lagging is a runtime label derived from one number, lag, against one threshold, and the same number drives the alert, the dashboard and the gate.

##### 2.10 Planned and unplanned migration timings and the revised timer table

The sequences are in 2.3. The table below replaces round 2's 6.3 and keeps `otap-ctl` as its single owner.

| Item | Phase B value | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Control heartbeat | 100 ms per path (LAN, DAC; W over LAN) | an answered RPC is liveness; hardware acks never are |
| Raft heartbeat / election timeout | 100 ms / 1 to 2 s | `heartbeat_interval`, `election_timeout_min/max`; at least 10 × witness RTT through the relay |
| Partner silent | 2 s on all direct paths and in W's view | W's view piggybacked on Raft RPC |
| Lease TTL / renew / margin | 3 s / 500 ms / 100 ms | renewals may ride the relay; skip a renewal while one is in flight |
| RPC timeout direct / relayed | 400 ms / 1 s | |
| L1 new-leader wait | TTL plus margin after the term starts | earliest takeover 4.3 s p50, 5.3 s p99 |
| Rollback gate | at L1/L2; under 1 ms from local state | no RPC, no wall clock |
| Stream heartbeat | 1 s | committed cp_seq, applied cp_seq, cp age at send, unshipped bytes, per-volume dirty bitset |
| Stream link dead | 3 s | Lagging plus Fabrics' link fallback; fail-back after 30 s stable |
| CP interval | 10 s HDD, 5 s flash | MediaProfile; never changed by the control plane |

| `break_after` | 24 h, or Storage's space policy | Broken |
| Pre-copy | until the delta is at most 256 MiB, at most 5 rounds | refuse with the number otherwise |

| Planned cutover, NAS | NFSv3 2 to 4 s; NFSv4.1 at most 8 s on reclaimed state; SMB 10 to 20 s | new NFSv4.1 opens up to 20 s unless early grace end |
| Unplanned block resume | 5 s p50, 9 s p99 silent; 11 to 13 s wedged; hard 15 s | nvfail-on LUNs stay Unavailable until cleared |
| Unplanned NAS resume | plus 2 to 5 s | XFS log replay, nfsd, smbd, GARP |
| Throttle / stall / hard bound | 2 s / 2 s / 10 s | unchanged |
