The reverse cannot happen (a write after the last shipped CP always sets the bit before the ack), so the list is safe but over-inclusive by up to two CP intervals per volume.
FIX: the heartbeat carries `acked_bytes` since the last *shipped* CP per volume (Storage's superblock already has it) and the printout lists volumes with `acked_bytes > 0` as affected and the rest of `write_active` as "idle, bit not yet cleared".
SEVERITY: minor.

##### Cross-persona contradictions

| Topic | Persona A says | Persona B says | What must be decided |
|---|---|---|---|
| Chunk unit and stream format | Storage: one staged stripe image, 16 B per-block summary, no manifest | Fabrics: 1 MiB chunks, 32 B `ManifestEntry` frames up to 64 MiB | One format owner before either item 1; envelope from Fabrics, payload from Storage (F2) |
| Send source and slot lifetime | Storage: staging pool; slots freed when staged | Fabrics: the arena, registered as 8 x 1 GiB and cloned; slots freed after CP commit; `read_disk` fallback | Which buffer is registered and when a slot may be reused |
| Hold release | Storage 2.2: send notification plus disk write; Storage Q3: receiver apply | Fabrics: `Landed` credit after the receiver's segment write | Release on landed; hold budget recomputed (S2) |
| Receiver apply point | Storage: at the receiver's next own CP | Fabrics: `commit(cp)` immediately; Consensus P5 assumes 250 to 500 ms | A receiver CP trigger on `CpEnd` |
| Lag arithmetic | Storage: 10 to 19 s; Fabrics: about 13 s | Consensus: `insync_lag_max` 20 s | One formula: CP plus ship plus apply, after the apply point is fixed |
| `max_auto_takeover_lag` and alerts | Storage: 2 x CP + 30 s; warn 60 s, crit 600 s | Consensus: 60 s; warn 20 s sustained 30 s, crit 60 s | One row in the timer table (Consensus owns it) |
| nvfail class defaults | Storage: file `alert`, SVM root `on`, NFSv3 datastore `on` | Consensus: file `off`, no root class | Root volume `alert` (S8); "alert" and "off" are the same thing and should have one name |
| nvfail presentation | Storage: Unavailable and exports withdrawn; Consensus: Unavailable "with PDL-style presentation" | Fabrics: Unavailable is free, PDL needs the LUN unmapped | PDL by unmap for ESXi LUNs, `no_path_retry 12` for Proxmox, fsid bump for NFS on clear (F5, C3) |
| Relationship granularity | Storage: per-volume direction, transport per aggregate pair; Consensus: per-volume `Relationship` in Raft | Fabrics: per-volume relationship with its own connections and windows | Consistency group = SVM; transport per aggregate pair (S9, F3) |
| Owner epoch on the wire | Consensus: every CP header carries `owner_epoch` | Storage's `CpBegin` and Fabrics' frame header have no epoch field | Add `owner_epoch` and `cp_id` to the envelope (S1) |
| Gate inputs on disk | Consensus: `applied_cp_seq`, `applied_owner_epoch`, `cp_age_at_send`, `recv_mono` in the replica superblock | Storage's superblock carries `promote_hint` only | Storage adds the four fields to the superblock v2 |
| Process topology | Storage and Fabrics: `otap-ringd` cut, receiver inside `dbladed` | Consensus: keep an arena-owner process under a new name | Cut; the hugetlbfs file outlives the daemon by construction (R4) |
| Memory for SVM slices | Storage: about 28 to 32 GiB | Consensus: 18 GiB cap per node; Fabrics: "4 GiB to caches, 4 GiB to slices" | One table (C6) |
| Block portals | Consensus: node-level, never move | Fabrics: FC LIFs per SVM per node; portals bind in the creator's netns (C5) | Per-SVM block LIFs, static per node, ALUA switches |
| `qlini_mode` | Round-2 R13: module `dual`, client ports `disabled` | Fabrics: module `disabled` everywhere | Re-rule R13 for the no-FC-transport world (Fabrics is right) |
| Proxmox multipath | Round-2 recipe and Consensus 2.7: `no_path_retry queue` | Fabrics: built-in LIO-ORG entry `no_path_retry 12` [verified: https://packages.debian.org/trixie/multipath-tools is 0.11.1-2] | `12`; withdraw `queue` (F5) |
| `.snapshot` placement | R21: outside share and bucket roots | Storage: inside the volume root | Volume root with shares and the S3 root as subdirectories, explicit per-snapshot exports (S7) |

##### What I would change in my own design after reading theirs

1. **Drop the UTS namespace as a load-bearing mechanism.** My round-2 position ("SVM = network namespace plus UTS namespace, `rpc.nfsd --scope`") still works, but 6.12 exposes the scope over nfsd's generic netlink, and `nbladed` already speaks netlink for addresses. Scope = SVM UUID set by `nbladed` from inside the SVM netns; the UTS namespace stays only so `sm-notify -v` and Samba's `netbios name` have a tidy nodename, and no SVM unit ever carries `ProtectHostname=`.
2. **Adopt Fabrics' INQUIRY identity** (vendor `LIO-ORG`, product `OpenTAP`) as permanent; the built-in multipath entry is worth more than a vanity string, and `vendor_id` is refused once exported anyway.
3. **WCE=1 moves from the LIO tree to the ublk params.** `blade_lio` stops writing `emulate_write_cache` on iblock and instead asserts the ublk queue's `write_cache` before linking a LUN; nvmet's VWC follows the same bit.
4. **nvfail from the client's side becomes one rule per protocol:** iSCSI and FC datastore LUNs are unmapped (PDL, 05/25/00); NFS datastores get the export withdrawn and an `fsid` bump on clear, which knfsd honours because the fsid is in the file handle [believed: exports(5) semantics]; SMB shares go offline with `smbcontrol close-share`; `stop` and ordinary takeovers use Unavailable, never PDL. One target IQN per SVM with LUN 0 always mapped, so PDL is detectable.
5. **The client recipe grows three lines:** `Disk.PathEvalTime=30`, guest disk timeouts 190 s (already in Appendix B), and `no_path_retry 12` on Proxmox instead of `queue`.
6. **`.snapshot` is explicit, not `crossmnt`.** Per-snapshot exports with `fsid=hash(volUuid, snapUuid)`, shares and the S3 root as subdirectories of the volume root, `shadow:snapdir` absolute, and only `Fsfreeze`-kind snapshots exposed; Storage's automount idea is kept because knfsd does trigger it under `crossmnt`, but the fsid must be ours.
7. **The replication consistency group is the SVM** (root plus data volumes), which answers Storage's question 4 and Consensus's resync rules in one stroke; `secrets.tdb` and nfsdcld are always at the same sender CP as the data.
8. **Volume size has a `size_max`.** Every ublk device is created at `size_max` (thin), XFS grows inside it, and no NAS or LUN resize ever recreates a device on 6.12.
9. **One LIF record type** with a transport body (`Ip` or `Fc`), MACs allocated at creation from a locally administered range and stored like WWPNs; iSCSI portals live in the SVM netns, static per node.
10. **Planned migration order for SMB:** SIGTERM smbd before the LIF goes down (clean disconnect, 1 to 2 s reconnect) and NFS LIFs down first as Consensus has it; `sm-notify` runs after the LIF is up on the new node, from the root volume's state directory.
11. **The fsfreeze budget of 3 s is acceptable** for ESXi NFSv3 (heartbeat 12/10/5) and SMB, but only once the cut no longer waits for a flush (S3); until then I refuse scheduled NAS snapshots on aggregates with a CP older than 2 s in flight rather than take a crash-consistent one silently.
12. **I accept Consensus's 18 GiB slice cap** and derive per-SVM `MemoryMax` from it, provided the memory table is reconciled (C6).

### By Opus-Fabrics

#### Opus-Fabrics cross-examination, Session 03: holes in the Storage, Protocols and Consensus designs

Scope: the three designs as reproduced in the brief, read against `04-project-brief-async-svm.md` and rulings R1 to R24 with the 6.3 timer table. Everything I assert about a kernel, package or client is marked `[verified: <url>]` or `[believed]`; where my refutation rests on a fetched source I quote the line that matters. Numbers carry their assumption. The four owner focus areas are tagged (a) snapshot deltas under continuous ingest, (b) permissions and identity across SVMs, (c) client timeouts during lag and failover, (d) hardware RAID against the sequential CP flusher; (e) marks contradictions, missing failure modes and arithmetic.

What I verified for this document, so the other personas can check my footing: the 6.12 uapi header has `IORING_OP_SEND_ZC`, `IORING_RECVSEND_FIXED_BUF`, `IORING_CQE_F_NOTIF` and `IORING_REGISTER_CLONE_BUFFERS = 30`, and has no `IORING_OP_WRITEV_FIXED` or `READV_FIXED`, so Storage's staging argument is right [verified: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/include/uapi/linux/io_uring.h]. `iscsit_get_np()` matches through `iscsit_check_np_match()` on address, port and `np_network_transport` only, with no namespace, and `iscsit_build_sendtargets_response()` skips a TPG only when `generate_node_acls == 0 && demo_mode_discovery == 0` and the initiator has no ACL [verified: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/target/iscsi/iscsi_target.c]; `TA_DEMO_MODE_DISCOVERY` is 1 and `TA_GENERATE_NODE_ACLS` is 0 [verified: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/include/target/iscsi/iscsi_target_core.h]. `transport_lookup_cmd_lun()` returns `TCM_NON_EXISTENT_LUN` only when `orig_fe_lun != 0`; LUN 0 falls through to `tpg_virt_lun0` with "Force WRITE PROTECT for virtual LUN 0" returning `TCM_WRITE_PROTECTED` for any direction other than `DMA_FROM_DEVICE` or `DMA_NONE` [verified: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/target/target_core_device.c]. `ublks_max` is a `0644` module parameter bounded by `UBLK_MAX_UBLKS = UBLK_MINORS = 1 << MINORBITS`, and `ublk_ctrl_add_dev` returns `-EACCES` past it [verified: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/block/ublk_drv.c]. multipath `no_path_retry`: a number is "Number of retries until disable I/O queueing", `queue` is "never stop I/O queueing", default `fail`, `polling_interval` 5 s [verified: https://manpages.debian.org/trixie/multipath-tools/multipath.conf.5.en.html]. Broadcom's APD/PDL article: ESXi marks PDL on ASC/ASCQ 0x25/0x0 or 0x68/0x0 only, "indefinitely retries SCSI I/O" during APD including guest I/O, and "If an I/O request is issued from a guest, the operating system should timeout and stop the I/O" [verified: https://knowledge.broadcom.com/external/article/318712]. VMware Tools raises the Linux guest disk timeout to 180 s through a udev rule, with documented cases where the rule did not take effect and the value stayed at 30 s [verified: https://kb.vmware.com/kb/1009465, https://answers.launchpad.net/bugs/1790145]. The default BBU mode on IBM-branded MegaRAID (ServeRAID M) uses a non-transparent learn cycle during which "the controller will change the cache mode to write-through", and Oracle's Exadata guidance says the same [verified: https://www.ibm.com/support/pages/node/860080, https://docs.oracle.com/en/engineered-systems/exadata-database-machine/dbmmn/monitoring-hard-disk-controller-write-caching-mode.html].

##### 1. Opus-Storage

**S1. HOLE: `CpEnd` can reach the receiver before the sender's superblock commits, so a torn CP N is re-issued as a different CP N and the replica diverges silently.** (a) SCENARIO: HDD pool, 1 GB/s ingest, 10 s CP. CP 1,204 stages 10 GB; chunks are "queued to the shipper and to the flusher at once", and the shipper on 25GbE finishes 10 GB in 4 s while the data stripes are still landing at 1.2 GB/s. `CpEnd` goes out; the receiver verifies the digest and enters `Committing(1204)`. The sender loses power 2 s later, before its FUA superblock. On boot the sender's max-select falls back to CP 1,203 (the torn-CP rule), the arena is gone, clients write again, and the next CP is stamped `cp_seq = 1204` with different content. WHY IT BREAKS: the receiver already holds a "1204" at the sender's `CpBegin` base check; the new 1204's `CpBegin` carries `base = 1203`, which the receiver rejects or, if it has already switched roots at its own CP, accepts as a duplicate sequence; either way, blocks that the first 1204 shipped and the second did not stay on the replica with `birth = 1204` and no later overwrite, and nothing in `diff(base)` ever revisits them. The weekly `SuperblockDigest` compare catches it days later. FIX: `CpEnd` is emitted only after the sender's superblock completion (chunks may stream early, the commit marker may not); every CP carries a 64-bit `cp_nonce` (`cut_seq` folded with `opened_stamp`) in `CpBegin`, `CpEnd` and the receiver's `(cp, nonce, cursor)` resume record, so a re-issued sequence number is a base mismatch by construction. I carry the nonce in the frame header. SEVERITY: blocker.

**S2. HOLE: the staging hold is released by two different events in the same document, and the stricter one makes HDD steady state impossible.** (a) SCENARIO: 2.2 says a buffer is released "when the disk write and the send notification have both completed"; question 3 to me says "I release staging holds on your acknowledgement of the receiver's apply". Apply happens at the receiver's own next CP (2.2, "the shadow roots become the visible roots at the receiver's next own CP"), up to 10 s after `CpEnd` on HDD. At 1 GB/s ingest the apply-gated hold is 10 GB of sender CP plus 9 s of ship plus up to 10 s of receiver CP, 20 to 29 GB against a 2 GiB budget. WHY IT BREAKS: the relationship detaches at the first CP and lives in `CatchUp` forever on any HDD pair with sustained ingest above about 70 MB/s (2 GiB over 29 s), which contradicts "steady-state lag is one CP interval plus ship time". FIX: the hold is released by the `IORING_CQE_F_NOTIF` CQE (the kernel no longer references the pages) and the disk completion, exactly as 2.2 says; any resend after a receiver crash or digest failure comes from disk through the map walk (the data is committed by then under S1). The receiver's apply acknowledgement advances the base and the lag counters only. I report `link_up_apply_stalled` separately (my answer to question 3). SEVERITY: major.

**S3. HOLE: the catch-up walk ships only the newest state, so every scheduled snapshot taken on the sender during lag is missing on the replica and the "Broken is recoverable from a daily schedule" claim does not hold.** (a) SCENARIO: link down 3 h on a volume with hourly snapshots at :05. Base is CP 100 (snapshot `h09`); snapshots `h10`, `h11`, `h12` are cut at CPs 460, 820, 1,180; the link returns and the walk pins T = CP 1,300 and emits entries with `birth > 100`, "later births win by construction". WHY IT BREAKS: a block written at CP 500 and overwritten at CP 1,250 ships once, with its 1,250 content; the receiver materializes `SnapEvent`s `h10..h12` from `CpBegin`, but their roots are the T root, so `h10` on the replica differs from `h10` on the sender for every block overwritten after CP 460. Common snapshots are now pairs whose content differs, resync after a takeover from such a pair is wrong, and the replica's Previous Versions lie. OpenZFS and SnapMirror both avoid this by sending snapshot-to-snapshot increments in order. FIX: `CatchUp { from, to }` becomes a sequence of increments over the pinned snapshot roots: for each retained snapshot S_i in `(base, T]` in order, walk S_i's pinned page index for `birth in (S_{i-1}, S_i]` (the CoW page index per pinned root exists already), then the live root for `(S_last, T]`. Cost: intermediate overwrites ship, bounded by the per-interval churn, 3 x 10 MB/s x 3,600 s = 108 GB worst case in the scenario versus the compacted walk; snapshots not retained on the sender are skipped legitimately. SEVERITY: blocker for snapshot semantics on the replica.

**S4. HOLE: a `Snapshot(id)` trigger waits behind an in-flight CP, and under HDD back-pressure that wait is 8 to 13 s, so `fsfreeze` snapshots overrun their 3 s budget and the fallback does not help.** (a) SCENARIO: 80%-full RAID6 draining 0.4 GB/s, 4 GiB half in flight (10 s), NFSv3 ingest 0.8 GB/s. The scheduler issues `FIFREEZE` on the XFS, the page-cache sync takes 2 s, then requests the cut. The active generation cannot be frozen until the frozen one is released (two generations, 2.1), so the cut waits for CP N to finish: 8 more seconds. `freeze_timeout_ms` fires at 3 s and "thaws and takes a crash-consistent snapshot", but that snapshot needs the same cut and waits the same 8 s. WHY IT BREAKS: NFS WRITEs block in the frozen filesystem for 3 s, every nfsd thread of a 32-thread datastore SVM is parked in `xfs_file_write_iter` (ESXi keeps 32 or more writes outstanding), so reads for every other VM on the SVM stall too; then the snapshot is not even consistent. FIX: order the freeze after the engine's promise: `Allocator::cut_within(deadline)` returns `Ok` only when no CP is in flight or the in-flight one will commit inside the deadline (its drain rate is known from the last three CPs); the scheduler freezes only after `Ok`, otherwise defers the snapshot to the next commit and logs the skip; three generations (active, frozen, draining) make the cut independent of the flush at the cost of one more 160 MiB index. SEVERITY: major.

**S5. HOLE: applied lag is 10 to 29 s on HDD, not 10 to 19, because the receiver switches roots only at its own CP; Consensus's `insync_lag_max` of 20 s then reports Exposed in healthy steady state.** (a)(e) SCENARIO: sender CP 10 s, ship 9 s, receiver CP timer 10 s; a sender CP cut at t=0 is complete at the receiver at t=19 and visible at the receiver's next CP, anywhere in t=19..29. The gate's lag and the alert read the applied CP. WHY IT BREAKS: at 1 GB/s every HDD pair alternates Protected/Exposed every CP, the alert rate limit hides it, and `max_auto_takeover_lag` effectively shrinks by 10 s. FIX: either the receiver forces its own CP on `CpEnd` when the inbound CP is larger than 25% of its half-arena or older than 5 s (apply latency under 1 s), or Consensus sets `insync_lag_max = 3 x CP interval` and the gate promotes a `Committing(N)` CP by forcing the switch at promotion. Numbers must agree in the timer table. SEVERITY: major.

**S6. HOLE: the torn-CP rule only rewinds when the map roots fail to verify; a write-back controller without cache protection can land the superblock before the data, roots verify, and the pool serves EIO instead of rolling back.** (d) SCENARIO: PERC with "always write back" and a dead battery, `cache_protection = none` accepted with the acknowledgement. CP N: 1,600 data stripes, CP log, FUA superblock. The controller's cache drains by dirty-line policy, not by submission order, so on a power cut the superblock (one 2.5 MiB line) is on disk and 300 data stripes are not. Boot: max-select picks N (roots verify), reads of those 300 stripes fail CRC against the map. WHY IT BREAKS: the "`none` is accepted ... and then the torn-CP rule is what saves the previous CP" promise in 2.6 is false for exactly the controller it was written for; the clients get medium errors on data the engine acknowledged, with no nvfail. FIX: on a dirty boot the selected CP's summary pages are read and CRC-checked before export (12 KiB per HDD stripe, 20 MB for a 4 GiB CP, under 2 s); any failure rewinds to N-1 and raises nvfail with the reason. Cheap, and it also catches misdirected writes at mount time. SEVERITY: major.

**S7. HOLE: the write-amplification probe writes S-aligned, S-sized runs without saying they are randomly placed; a write-back cache coalesces sequential runs, so every S is within 10% of the best, the probe picks 256 KiB, and the wrong geometry is discovered only when the controller drops to write-through.** (d) SCENARIO: PERC H730, 2 GB cache, VD of 8 data drives at 256 KiB strip (2 MiB full stripe), probe candidates written sequentially at QD 8: the cache merges consecutive 256 KiB commands into full stripes before they reach the drives, and 256 KiB wins. The flusher then pads CP tails to 256 KiB and accounts segments in 256 KiB stripes. Thirty days later the learn cycle (S8) puts the VD in write-through. WHY IT BREAKS: in write-through every 256 KiB command is a read-modify-write on a 2 MiB stripe: two reads and two writes per strip, drain 150 to 300 MB/s instead of 1.2 GB/s, exactly the knee the probe was meant to find. FIX: the probe places each S-sized write at a random S-aligned offset over a span of at least 4 x cache size (16 GiB stands) so coalescing is impossible, and records both the write-back and, when the operator can toggle it, the write-through result; `GeomSource::Probe` carries `placement = random`. SEVERITY: major.

**S8. HOLE: the drain curve the back-pressure model assumes (1.2 GB/s empty, 0.3 to 0.5 GB/s aged) is suspended for hours by three controller-internal activities the engine cannot observe: the BBU learn cycle, patrol read and rebuild.** (d) SCENARIO: default BBU mode, learn cycle every 30 days, several hours in write-through [verified: IBM ServeRAID M page above]. Ingest 0.6 GB/s on a pool whose write-through drain is 0.25 GB/s (S7 numbers). The 4 GiB half fills in 7 s, drains in 17 s; the ZFS-shaped delay reaches the 2 s cap within the second CP and the ports go Transitioning under R7; ESXi datastore latency alarms fire for the duration of the learn cycle, once a month, with no OpenTAP alert naming the cause. Patrol read (default on, weekly) and a rebuild at the default 30% rate take 20 to 50% of the drain on the same curve. WHY IT BREAKS: `k` is recomputed from the last three CPs, so the throttle adapts, but the operator sees "storage slow" with no reason, and the MediaProfile's `inflight_stripes` of 32 (80 MiB in flight) is far too deep for a write-through controller doing RMW, which inflates per-request latency rather than throughput. FIX: the attestation records `learn_mode = transparent | write_through_fallback | unknown` and the installer prints the vendor instruction to set a transparent learn cycle (IBM modes 1 and 3) or CacheVault; the CP engine publishes `drain_rate_bytes_s` and raises WARN "drain below 50% of the pool's probed rate for 3 CPs" with the three likely causes; `inflight_stripes` is derived from the measured drain and a 200 ms queue target (0.25 GB/s x 0.2 s = 50 MB, 20 stripes) rather than fixed; and the optional `storcli`/`perccli` integration is an opt-in exec path when the operator installs the vendor tool. SEVERITY: major.

**S9. HOLE: the attestation protects the controller cache and says nothing about the drives' own write caches, which the kernel never flushes because the VD reports no write cache.** (d) SCENARIO: PERC VD, "Disk Cache Policy: Disk's Default" (enabled on most SATA and many SAS drives) [believed], BBU healthy, `queue/write_cache` reads "write through" so no SYNCHRONIZE CACHE or FUA is ever issued (sd.c, Storage's own 2.6). CP N commits: the controller acknowledged every stripe from its protected cache, drained them to the drives, and the drives acknowledged from their volatile caches. Power is lost. WHY IT BREAKS: whether the controller issues drive-cache flushes before acknowledging a drain is firmware-specific and not something the kernel can see or force; a BBU-protected controller with drive caches enabled is the documented way to lose data on MegaRAID, and the superblock's "FUA" never reached a drive. Storage's model has no field for it. FIX: `cache_protection` becomes a struct `{ controller: Bbu | FlashBacked | None, disk_cache: Disabled | Enabled | Unknown }`; `Enabled` and `Unknown` are refused for HDD VDs unless the operator attests "drives have power-loss protection"; the installer prints the vendor command. SEVERITY: major.

**S10. HOLE: "one flush, then the superblock" is wrong once a metadata class exists on a second device, and `RWF_DSYNC` on a block device costs an extra flush on every CP.** (d) SCENARIO: data on `/dev/sdb` (PERC), CP log, map pages and superblocks on `/dev/nvme1n1p1`. The CP issues `FSYNC` on the pool fd and then the superblock with `RWF_DSYNC` on the NVMe. The CP log pages written to the NVMe before the superblock are behind the NVMe's volatile write cache (consumer NVMe, VWC set) and are not covered by the pool flush. WHY IT BREAKS: a power cut after the superblock lands and before the NVMe drains its cache leaves a committed superblock pointing at CP-log pages that are not there; replay fails and the pool rewinds or refuses to mount. Also: in 6.12 a direct write with `IOCB_DSYNC` gets `REQ_FUA` on the bio and `blkdev_write_iter` still calls `generic_write_sync`, which issues a second device flush [believed; `dio_bio_write_op` and `blkdev_fsync`], so the superblock path costs FUA plus a flush, which on HDD-only pools is 10 to 30 ms per CP that the design does not count. FIX: `Backstore::flush` is called per device class in order (pool, then metadata class), then the superblock with `REQ_FUA` through `IORING_OP_WRITE_FIXED` with `RWF_DSYNC` only on the metadata device; count both in the CP budget. SEVERITY: major (correctness), minor (cost).

**S11. HOLE: the stream records lack the fields Consensus's gate and my framing need, and the single `(cp, chunk idx, byte offset)` cursor cannot describe four connections with out-of-order chunks.** (e) SCENARIO: 4 connections, chunks 17, 18, 19, 20 in flight on separate connections; connection 2 dies with chunk 18 half-sent while 19 and 20 completed. A single cursor is either 17 (re-sending 19 and 20, 5 MiB wasted per event, harmless) or 20 (losing 18). Separately, `CpBegin` has no `owner_epoch` or direction epoch (2.5 says `begin` rejects an older direction epoch, but the struct has no field), and `Heartbeat` has no `cp_age_at_send` and no per-volume dirty bitset, which Consensus's gate and alert list consume. WHY IT BREAKS: a late un-fenced sender's `CpBegin` cannot be refused at the data layer as promised; the gate's lag formula has no input. FIX (my framing): frame header `{ magic, ver, rel_id, direction_epoch, owner_epoch, cp, cp_nonce, chunk_idx, len, crc32c }`; resume is a per-CP bitmap of completed chunk indexes plus one byte offset for each open connection; chunk-aligned resume is the contract, byte-level resume is an optimization within a connection. `Heartbeat` gains `cp_age_at_send_ms` and `dirty_vols: VolBitSet` (1 KiB). SEVERITY: major (contract).

**S12. HOLE: "optional TLS and compression" are priced as free on top of `SEND_ZC`, but both remove the zero copy.** (e) SCENARIO: TLS on, rustls in userspace: every chunk is copied into a TLS record buffer and encrypted (AES-GCM, about 2 to 4 GB/s per core with AES-NI [believed]), then sent from the record buffer, not from the registered staging pool; with kernel TLS (`tls` ULP) software mode, `tls_sw_sendmsg` copies plaintext into its own scatterlist before encrypting [believed], so `SEND_ZC` on that socket is a copy too. Compression is a copy by definition. WHY IT BREAKS: the shipper's CPU budget changes from 0.1 core to about 0.5 to 1 core per GB/s, and the hold release moves from `CQE_F_NOTIF` to "encrypted copy made", which is earlier and simpler. FIX: TLS off is the default on the direct DAC and on; TLS on uses rustls with a 4 MiB record buffer per connection and releases staging on copy; `lz4_flex` only when the link is below 5 Gbit/s. The numbers go into my section. SEVERITY: minor (design), major (budget).

**S13. HOLE: the `write_active` intent write is "one FUA stripe" but on a hardware VD the FUA never reaches the controller, and in write-through mode it costs a full RMW.** (d) SCENARIO: the first write after idle on a PERC VD in write-through (learn cycle): the intent superblock stripe is a partial-stripe write, 2 reads plus 2 writes, 20 to 40 ms before the client's first acknowledgement; 1,000 idle VMs waking at 09:00 pay it in series on one superblock slot. WHY IT BREAKS: the "p99 under 20 ms on HDD" exit test fails on every write-through controller, and the ordering claim rests on the controller, not FUA. FIX: the intent record goes to the metadata class when one exists (0.1 to 0.5 ms), and the superblock stripe is sized to one full stripe of the device that holds it; `nvfail_intent = conservative` becomes the default for write-through backstores. SEVERITY: minor.

##### 2. Opus-Protocols

**P1. HOLE: unmapping a LUN that sits at LUN 0 does not produce PDL; LIO's virtual LUN 0 answers writes with WRITE PROTECTED and reads with LBA errors, which ESXi does not treat as PDL.** (c) SCENARIO: datastore SVM, ESXi datastore on `lun_0` (the usual first mapping), nvfail engages, `nbladed` removes the LUN link from the TPG. ESXi's next WRITE to LUN 0 hits `transport_lookup_cmd_lun`, which for `orig_fe_lun == 0` substitutes `tpg_virt_lun0` and returns `TCM_WRITE_PROTECTED` (DATA PROTECT 07h/27h/00h) for `DMA_TO_DEVICE` [verified: target_core_device.c above]; READs go to the empty virtual device. WHY IT BREAKS: ESXi only checks for 0x25/0x0 and 0x68/0x0 [verified: Broadcom article above], so the datastore is not marked PDL: VMs see write errors on a device that still answers INQUIRY and REPORT LUNS, hostd keeps the datastore mounted, and the first write after `nvfail-clear` and remap lands exactly as if nothing happened, which is the hazard nvfail exists to prevent. FIX: never map a real LUN at 0 (LIO's virtual LUN 0 stays as the REPORT LUNS anchor; ESXi and Linux handle LUN 1..N fine); the Raft validator reserves LUN 0 per TPG, and the step 1 exit test adds "nvfail on the LUN at the lowest mapping yields 05h/25h/00h on the wire". SEVERITY: blocker.

**P2. HOLE: iSCSI SendTargets on any SVM portal discloses every SVM's target IQN and every portal address in every IPspace, because `demo_mode_discovery` defaults to 1 and the response is built from the global target list.** (b) SCENARIO: tenant A's initiator sends SendTargets=All to 10.10.100.21:3260. `iscsit_build_sendtargets_response` walks every tiqn and every TPG; a TPG is skipped only when `generate_node_acls == 0 && demo_mode_discovery == 0` and the initiator has no ACL [verified: iscsi_target.c above]; `TA_DEMO_MODE_DISCOVERY` is 1 [verified: iscsi_target_core.h above]. Portal addresses are reported from `np->np_sockaddr` for non-wildcard portals. WHY IT BREAKS: tenant A learns `iqn.2026-10.org.opentap:lab.tenant-b` and 10.20.7.5:3260 in tenant B's IPspace; identity isolation across SVMs is cosmetic, and the per-netns nftables does not help because the leak rides tenant A's own session. FIX: `nbladed` writes `attrib/demo_mode_discovery = 0` and `attrib/generate_node_acls = 0` on every TPG at creation, and the C4 exit test runs SendTargets from an initiator with an ACL in one SVM and asserts that no other SVM's IQN appears. SEVERITY: major.

**P3. HOLE: the `*` idmap range is a per-SVM tdb, so BUILTIN and well-known SIDs get different uids in two SVMs joined to the same domain; the exit test checks only domain SIDs and passes.** (b) SCENARIO: SVM-1 and SVM-2 in `LAB`, both `idmap config LAB : backend = rid`, both `idmap config * : backend = tdb, range = 3000000-3999999`. A Windows admin sets an ACL with BUILTIN\Administrators (S-1-5-32-544) on a share in SVM-1: winbindd allocates 3000000 from SVM-1's `winbindd_idmap.tdb`. SVM-2 allocated 3000000 to S-1-5-32-545 a week earlier because Users was looked up first there. WHY IT BREAKS: `volume rehost` or a host-side restore of that volume into SVM-2 maps gid 3000000 to Users, and Administrators-only directories become readable by every domain user; `wbinfo -S` on a `LAB` SID in both SVMs is identical and the AD-matrix exit test passes. Trusted domains without their own `rid` block fail the same way. FIX: well-known and BUILTIN SIDs get a fixed, Raft-declared mapping rendered into every SVM at start (`net idmap set` into a freshly generated `winbindd_idmap.tdb`, or `idmap config * : backend = tdb` seeded from a Raft table), trusted domains are enumerated at join and each gets a `rid` base from Raft; the exit test adds S-1-5-32-544 and S-1-5-32-545. SEVERITY: major.

**P4. HOLE: tenant daemons run as host root, inside a mount namespace that recursively binds the host's `/dev`, `/sys` and `/proc`, with no capability bounding set, no device policy and no seccomp; a compromised smbd or versitygw in one SVM owns the node.** (b) SCENARIO: a remote code execution in Samba 4.22's SMB2 parser (the class CVE-2023-3961 and CVE-2024-x were in) in tenant A's smbd. The process is root, `CAP_SYS_ADMIN` intact, with `/dev/ublkb*` of every SVM's volumes, `/sys/kernel/config` and the pins of every other SVM in view. WHY IT BREAKS: pivot 3 sells SVMs as multi-tenancy; R23 requires per-daemon hardening; the transient units in 2.1 carry `KillMode`, `TasksMax` and `OOMPolicy` and nothing from R23. FIX: every `StartTransientUnit` carries `CapabilityBoundingSet` per daemon (smbd needs `CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE CAP_CHOWN CAP_FOWNER CAP_SETUID CAP_SETGID CAP_SYS_RESOURCE` and nothing else, versitygw only `CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE`), `NoNewPrivileges=yes`, `DevicePolicy=closed` with `DeviceAllow=/dev/null rw` and the like, `ProtectKernelTunables`, `ProtectKernelModules`, `ProtectControlGroups`, `RestrictNamespaces=yes` (the namespaces are entered by `nsenter` before `execve`, so the daemon never needs to create one), `SystemCallFilter=@system-service`; the SVM view masks `/dev` to a minimal tmpfs devtmpfs subset and masks `/run/opentap` except the SVM's own directory. nfsd needs none of this because it is a kernel thread. SEVERITY: major.

**P5. HOLE: the shipped `multipath.conf` says `no_path_retry 12`, Consensus's no-quorum argument assumes `queue`, and nvfail on Proxmox depends on which one it is.** (c)(e) SCENARIO: nvfail unmaps the LUN; the `tur` checker gets LOGICAL UNIT NOT SUPPORTED, marks both paths down; with `12` the queue fails after 12 x 5 s = 60 s [verified: multipath.conf(5) above], qemu returns errors, the VM stops, as Protocols' table says. Under Consensus's `stop` posture (witness reboot, link flap), the same `12` fails every Proxmox VM's I/O at 60 s, while Consensus's table says "Linux dm-multipath with the shipped `no_path_retry queue` indefinitely". With `queue`, nvfail on Proxmox hangs forever instead of failing after 60 s. WHY IT BREAKS: one file cannot deliver both behaviours; the owner's D7 argument ("a 60 s witness reboot is survived by every client class except Windows without MPIO") is false with the file as shipped. FIX: ship `no_path_retry queue` plus `dev_loss_tmo infinity` (the hold posture), and make nvfail explicit on Linux by deleting the LUN *and* sending a REPORT LUNS DATA HAS CHANGED unit attention so the initiator's SCSI layer removes the device, which fails I/O immediately regardless of `no_path_retry`; test both rows. SEVERITY: major.

**P6. HOLE: Phase B block moves are a LIF move plus an initiator re-login, so the planned block pause is the 8 to 15 s Protocols gives, not the 3 s Consensus promises, and the two documents cannot both be in the timer table.** (c)(e) SCENARIO: planned move of a datastore SVM; T1 removes the block LIF on A; the initiator's next segment to 10.10.100.21 goes unanswered; when the LIF appears on B (S7, about 3 to 6 s later), B's kernel answers RST, ESXi tears the session down and re-logs in: with the round-2-verified ESXi timers (NOP-Out 15 s interval, 10 s timeout, recovery 10 s) the observed pause is the ladder plus the RST plus one login, 5 to 15 s; Windows holds in `LinkDownTime` 15 s. WHY IT BREAKS: the 3 s "planned takeover" promise in 6.6 is broken for every block client in Phase B. FIX: the ONTAP SAN model: block LIFs do not migrate; each node carries its own block LIF for the SVM (`Presence::BlockStandby` extended to Phase B), the replica's TPG reports ALUA Standby (legal: INQUIRY, REPORT TPGS and TUR served, media access refused with NOT READY/ALUA state), and the planned cutover is an ALUA flip at the CP boundary as Consensus's P7 already assumes; the two addresses are the two paths ESXi and dm-multipath are built for. The per-SVM namespace then exists on both nodes with block LIFs only, which Protocols already designed for Phase A. SEVERITY: major.

**P7. HOLE: "clients see link loss, not errors" at T1 is right, but "fail fast and retry" (Consensus P2) is wrong, and the NFSv3 and SMB pause numbers omit the client's TCP retransmission back-off and the loss of SMB open handles.** (c) SCENARIO: NFSv3 over TCP; the address vanishes; the client's TCP retransmits with exponential back-off (200 ms, 400, 800, 1.6 s, 3.2 s); if the LIF reappears on B at t=3.5 s the client's next probe is at t=6.4 s, when B's RST ends the connection and the RPC is retried: the pause is the ladder plus up to one back-off interval, 2 to 8 s, not 2 to 4. SMB: the client reconnects the same way; durable handles are keyed in `smbXsrv_open_global.tdb` under `lock directory` in the SVM's private tmpfs `/run`, which does not travel, and I believe the db is cleared on the first smbd start [believed], so every planned move is "open handle errors", not "reconnect". FIX: before T1, `nbladed` sends TCP RST to every established client connection on the LIF from inside the netns (`ss -K` needs `CONFIG_INET_DIAG_DESTROY`, in Debian's kernel config [believed]; otherwise an `AF_PACKET` RST per connection), so clients reconnect on the first probe after the LIF returns; document SMB moves as handle loss until a persistent-handle design exists. SEVERITY: minor (NFS), major (the SMB promise).

**P8. HOLE: the NFS nvfail forcing function assumes ESXi stays stuck on ESTALE after the `fsid` bump; if the ESXi NFSv3 client re-issues MOUNT on reconnect it gets a fresh root handle and resumes silently.** (c) SCENARIO: export removed, VM paused, export re-added with the next fsid generation; ESXi's heartbeat (NULL RPC every 12 s) succeeds, its cached root FH returns ESTALE; whether ESXi then re-MOUNTs the volume by path (it mounts by server and path, not by fsid) and transparently recovers is not documented in the design [believed: unknown]. WHY IT BREAKS: if it does, the datastore comes back without a remount and VMs with cached dirty data write over the rolled-back image. FIX: the C5 exit test must prove the behaviour on ESXi 8.0 U3 and Proxmox 9; if ESXi recovers, nvfail for NFS datastores must present the export at a *new path* (`/vm` becomes `/vm@gen2`) or keep the export withheld until the operator clears. SEVERITY: major if ESXi recovers; the test decides.

**P9. HOLE: three memory numbers for the same slice and three QD1 numbers for the same write.** (e) `svm.slice` is 36 GiB (Protocols 2.13), the per-SVM slices are 32 GiB in Phase C and 28 GiB in Phase B (Storage 2.8), and Consensus caps per-node SVM slices at 18 GiB so both nodes' SVMs fit on the survivor (2.11). A 64 GB node with 36 GiB of SVM memory cannot absorb the partner's 36 GiB. iSCSI 4 KiB QD1 write is 70 to 100 us at the initiator (Protocols 1), 100 to 200 us (Storage 2.7), and "p50 at most 100 us in the guest" (Protocols' ESXi exit row), where the guest adds PVSCSI and vmkernel, 20 to 50 us [believed]. FIX: one memory table owned by Storage with Consensus's survivor rule applied (18 GiB per node in Phase B, 36 GiB in Phase C), and one latency ladder: engine 3 to 5 us, initiator 100 to 150 us p50 at 10GbE, guest 150 to 250 us p50; the exit test measures at the initiator. SEVERITY: minor each, major together because exit tests are written against them.

##### 3. Opus-Consensus

**C1. HOLE: the rollback gate reads `recv_mono` from the replica's superblock, but `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` restarts at boot, so after any replica reboot the computed lag is garbage and can be small enough to pass the 60 s gate.** (c)(e) SCENARIO: B applied CP K at B's uptime 400,000 s, recorded `recv_mono = 400,000 s`, `cp_age_at_send = 4 s`; B reboots for a kernel update (uptime restarts at 0), 15 minutes later A dies; B's uptime is 900 s; `lag = 900 - 400,000 + 4` underflows in `u64` arithmetic or, if signed and clamped, reads as about 4 s. WHY IT BREAKS: "lag without clocks" promotes a replica that is 15 minutes stale as if it were in sync; the loss printout says 4 s. FIX: persist `(boot_id, recv_mono)`; a `boot_id` mismatch makes lag `Unknown`, which is `Manual` with a printout "replica rebooted since last apply; last applied CP K at wall time W", where W is the sender's wall clock from the CP header (used only for the operator's eyes). The 1 s heartbeat refreshes `recv_mono` only while the stream is up. SEVERITY: blocker.

**C2. HOLE: the no-quorum `stop` argument says a 60 s hold is survived by every client class except Windows without MPIO; the guests inside ESXi and the Proxmox VMs are not in that list and do not survive it.** (c) SCENARIO: witness reboot and DAC flap together; both nodes stop at 3 s, Unavailable at 13 s, back at 61 s. ESXi "indefinitely retries SCSI I/O" including guest I/O, and "the operating system should timeout and stop the I/O" [verified: Broadcom article above]: a Windows guest fails its disk at 60 s (`TimeOutValue`), a Linux guest at 30 s unless the VMware Tools udev rule set 180 s, which Launchpad bug 1790145 shows silently not happening on Ubuntu [verified: links above]; Proxmox with Protocols' `no_path_retry 12` fails I/O at 60 s (P5) and qemu stops the VM. WHY IT BREAKS: D7 is argued on the initiator's timers while the damage happens one layer up; "costs little" is not what the owner will see. FIX: state the guest timers in the no-quorum row of the timer table (Linux guest 30 or 180 s, Windows guest 60 s, Proxmox 60 s under `12`), make the shipped guest guidance part of the ESXi recipe (the udev rule, verified by `cat /sys/block/sd*/device/timeout`), and keep `stop`, because the alternative is a split brain; but the owner decides D7 with these numbers, not with "little". SEVERITY: major.

**C3. HOLE: "block portals do not move; ALUA does the switch" contradicts Protocols' verified decision that portals bind in the SVM's netns and move with the SVM in Phase B, and the planned 1.0 to 1.5 s block cutover depends on standby paths that Protocols removed.** (c)(e) SCENARIO: see P6; P7's "TPGs Active/Optimized on B and Standby on A; multipath switches on the next I/O" requires an existing path to B, which in Protocols' Phase B does not exist until the LIF arrives on B. WHY IT BREAKS: the 3 s planned promise and the 5 s p50 unplanned promise for block are both unmet by the ladder as designed by the other persona. FIX: adopt the per-node block LIF model of P6 (`BlockStandby` in Phase B); Consensus's P3 and P7 then stand as written. SEVERITY: major.

**C4. HOLE: warm-standby units use `NetworkNamespacePath=` and `ProtectHostname=` as the UTS mechanism; Protocols verified that systemd 257 has no directive to join an existing mount or UTS namespace and that the mount namespace is required, and `ProtectHostname=` does not set a different nodename.** (e) `ProtectHostname=yes` creates a UTS namespace that makes the hostname read-only; the nodename stays the host's [verified by Protocols' quoted page: it "sets up a new UTS namespace", nothing more], so knfsd's scope would be the node name, not the SVM's, unless `rpc.nfsd --scope` is used. FIX: one mechanism, Protocols' `nsenter --net --uts --mount` wrapper from pinned namespaces; the standby skeleton is the pin set plus inactive transient units, which is cheaper than Consensus's estimate anyway. SEVERITY: minor (it is a wording fix), but it must be one design.

**C5. HOLE: `Relationship.base: Option<BaseId>` lives in Raft, and the base advances on every applied CP in Steady state, so the witness fsyncs per CP and "zero log entries per day" is false; Storage keeps the base on the superblocks and nothing in Raft is load-bearing for it.** (e) SCENARIO: HDD pair, 10 s CPs, 8,640 applied CPs per day; if `base` is updated on each, that is 8,640 `append` fsyncs on a microSD witness, the exact number Consensus computed as unacceptable for heartbeats. If `base` is updated only on transitions, the Raft copy is stale by hours and must never be read by the gate or the resync. WHY IT BREAKS: either the witness wears or the field is a lie that someone will read. FIX: remove `base` from Raft; Raft holds `src_epoch` (the direction epoch) and the relationship label; the common base is computed by the two superblocks' snapshot tables as Storage specifies, and `otapctl rel show` reads it from the engine. SEVERITY: major.

**C6. HOLE: the nvfail class defaults disagree with Storage's table, and the SVM root volume has no class.** (e) Consensus: `datastore = on, file = off, object = off`; Storage: block LUN `on`, NAS datastore `on`, NAS file `alert`, object `alert`, SVM root `on`. "off" and "alert" are different behaviours (alert still raises the CRIT with the window). Protocols' 2.11 adds an NFS `fsid` generation that Consensus calls "opt-in for file". The root volume carries `secrets.tdb` and `nfsdcld`: a promoted replica whose root volume is one CP behind its data volumes refuses NFSv4.1 reclaims for clients that connected in the last interval (Consensus 3.8) and may hold a machine password the DC no longer accepts (Protocols 2.6.9); it is the one volume where a silent rewind is a tenant outage. FIX: one table, owner decision D5, with `alert` as the third value, and the root volume in the same consistency group as its data volumes (Protocols' question 1 to Storage, which Storage's `CpBegin`-per-aggregate design already answers yes for volumes on one aggregate). SEVERITY: minor, but it is an owner decision that must be presented once.

**C7. HOLE: P5 "ship and apply atomically as B's own CP, 250 to 500 ms" assumes the receiver commits on `CpEnd`; Storage's receiver switches roots at its next own CP, up to 10 s later.** (e) SCENARIO: planned move at 200 MB/s ingest; the final 256 MiB delta ships in 250 ms; the receiver stages it and waits for its 10 s timer; the Raft `Takeover{planned}` at P6 commits against an unswitched root; B exports at P7 with the previous CP visible. WHY IT BREAKS: the first writes on B land on a root one CP behind the quiesced final CP; A's final CP is then divergent and the "no divergence by construction" claim fails. FIX: `DeltaSink::end` takes `commit: Immediate | NextCp`; Quiesced transfers and `max_auto_takeover_lag` promotions use `Immediate` (the receiver forces its own CP, 100 to 300 ms on flash, 300 to 500 ms on HDD for a 256 MiB apply); the P5 number holds only with it. SEVERITY: major.

**C8. HOLE: the gate's inputs are not on Storage's heartbeat, and `max_auto_takeover_lag` has two proposed values.** (e) Storage's `Heartbeat { cp_committed, acked_seq, write_active, lag_hint_bytes }` lacks `cp_age_at_send` and the per-volume dirty bitset; Storage proposes `max_auto_takeover_lag = 2 x CP + 30 s` (50 s HDD, 40 s flash), Consensus 60 s. FIX: S11's heartbeat; 60 s as the single default with the CP-derived value shown in the alert. SEVERITY: minor.

**C9. HOLE: "ublk `USER_RECOVERY` and `REISSUE` through the arena owner" names a process Storage cut; R4's mechanism (systemd creates the files, `dbladed` re-attaches) needs no holder.** (e) The new `dbladed` re-opens `/dev/ublkcN`, issues `UBLK_CMD_START_USER_RECOVERY`, re-attaches the hugetlbfs arena and staging files and the slot-state page, and ends recovery; no process outlives it and nothing is lost that the CP had not lost already. FIX: strike the arena owner from the Phase C item 3 text; the exit test stands. SEVERITY: minor.

##### Cross-persona contradictions

| Topic | Persona A says | Persona B says | What must be decided |
|---|---|---|---|
| Where block portals live and how block cutover works | Protocols: portals bind in the SVM netns, block LIFs move with the SVM in Phase B, no standby path (8 to 15 s move) | Consensus: portals are node-level, ALUA Standby/AO flip, 1.0 to 1.5 s p50, 3 s budget | Adopt per-node non-migrating block LIFs with `BlockStandby` in Phase B and the ALUA flip (P6, C3) |
| Unit entry into namespaces | Protocols: `nsenter --net --uts --mount` from pins; mount ns required; systemd has no join directive | Consensus: `NetworkNamespacePath=` plus `ProtectHostname=`, `rpc.nfsd --scope` | Protocols' mechanism (C4) |
| `multipath.conf` on Linux and Proxmox | Protocols: `no_path_retry 12` (fail at 60 s) | Consensus: `no_path_retry queue` (indefinite) | `queue`, with nvfail delivered by LUN deletion plus unit attention (P5) |
| Replication base location | Storage: pinned in both snapshot tables, nothing in Raft load-bearing | Consensus: `BaseId` in the Raft `Relationship` | Superblocks only; Raft holds the direction epoch (C5) |
| Steady-state replica lag | Storage: 10 to 19 s HDD | Consensus: `insync_lag_max` 20 s = 2 x CP; receiver apply at its own CP adds up to 10 s | Force the receiver CP on `CpEnd` or set 3 x CP (S5) |
| Receiver commit on the final delta | Storage: roots switch at the receiver's next own CP | Consensus: P5 apply in 250 to 500 ms | `DeltaSink::end(commit: Immediate)` for quiesced transfers and promotions (C7) |
| nvfail class defaults | Storage: LUN on, NFS datastore on, file alert, object alert, root on | Consensus: datastore on, file off, object off | One table with on/alert/off, root volume `on` (C6) |
| `max_auto_takeover_lag` | Storage: 2 x CP + 30 s | Consensus: 60 s | 60 s (C8) |
| SVM memory | Protocols: `svm.slice` 36 GiB; Storage: 28 to 32 GiB | Consensus: 18 GiB per node so both fit on the survivor | 18 GiB in Phase B, 36 GiB in Phase C, one table (P9) |
| iSCSI 4 KiB QD1 write | Protocols: 70 to 100 us; exit test "at most 100 us in the guest" | Storage: 100 to 200 us at the initiator | One ladder, measured at the initiator (P9) |
| Snapshot mount location and `vfs_shadow_copy2` | Storage: `/vol/<svm>/<vol>/.snapshot/@GMT-...` inside the volume, `crossmnt`, relative `shadow:snapdir`, Phase C | Protocols: `/vol/<svm>_root/.otap/snap/<vol>/@GMT-...` outside share roots, absolute `shadow:snapdir` and `basedir`, `.snapshot` in the junction is Phase B | R21 says outside share roots; Protocols' layout in Phase C, Storage's `.snapshot` junction view in Phase B |
| The arena holder process | Storage: cut `otap-ringd`, systemd creates the files | Consensus: keep a holder under a new name; recovery "through the arena owner" | No holder (C9) |
| Hold release in the shipper | Storage 2.2: disk write plus `CQE_F_NOTIF` | Storage question 3: receiver apply acknowledgement | `NOTIF` plus disk; resend from disk (S2) |
| Election timeout | Round-2 table: 0.5 to 1 s | Consensus: 1 to 2 s for the relay | Consensus owns the table; record the change against R7's "one owner" rule |
| Heartbeat content | Storage: `cp_committed, acked_seq, write_active, lag_hint_bytes` | Consensus: committed and applied cp, `cp_age_at_send`, unshipped bytes, per-volume dirty bitset, `owner_epoch` per CP header | Fabrics' frame and heartbeat carry the union (S11) |

##### What I would change in my own design after reading theirs

1. **Commit marker after commit, nonce per CP.** My frame header gains `cp_nonce`, `owner_epoch` and `direction_epoch`; the `CpEnd` record is sent only when Storage reports the superblock completion for that CP, while chunks stream from staging as soon as they are packed (S1). The receiver's resume record is `(cp, nonce, completed-chunk bitmap, per-connection byte offset)`; chunk-aligned resume is the contract (S11).
2. **Hold release on `IORING_CQE_F_NOTIF` and disk completion, never on apply.** I answer Storage's question 3: my window is bounded by the kernel's socket memory (4 connections x 16 MiB `SO_SNDBUF`), far below the 2 GiB hold; the hold is Storage's and is consumed only while the link is slower than the flusher. When the link is up but the receiver's apply stalls, I report `apply_stalled_ms` on the heartbeat and Storage's base stops advancing; nothing else changes (S2).
3. **`SEND_ZC` cost, answered.** One 2.5 MiB chunk is one SQE with `IORING_RECVSEND_FIXED_BUF` from the registered staging pool (2 MiB huge pages give one or two bvecs each [believed]); at 1 GB/s that is 400 sends and 800 CQEs per second, under 1% of the mirror core; the notification arrives when TCP has been acknowledged by the peer, so on a lossy LAN path holds stretch by the retransmission time, which is why the DAC is first. With TLS on, zero copy is gone and I budget 0.5 to 1 core per GB/s (S12); TLS defaults off on the DAC and on over the LAN.
4. **The heartbeat carries Consensus's gate inputs**: `src_committed_cp`, `dst_applied_cp`, `cp_age_at_send_ms`, `unshipped_bytes`, `dirty_vols` (1 KiB bitset), `link: LinkHealth`, plus Storage's `write_active` and `acked_bytes` for nvfail; one record, 1 s, never through the relay (S11, C8).
5. **`DeltaSink::end(commit)`** with `Immediate | NextCp` is part of my sink contract so planned cutovers and promotions are at the shipped CP (C7).
6. **Block LIFs per node, not per move.** My FC design already has NPIV ports per SVM that cannot migrate in under seconds; the iSCSI side should follow the same ONTAP rule (P6, C3): one block LIF per node per SVM, ALUA does the cutover, and `BlockStandby` is a Phase B presence, not Phase A only. The FC NPIV port on the partner is then the same standby path.
7. **FC as a replication transport stays deferred**, and I now put a number on why: the kernel-target-into-tmpfs receive path costs a copy and a scan that the TCP `DeltaSink` in `dbladed` does not, and 16GFC (1.6 GB/s) beats 10GbE (1.1 GB/s) by less than the difference between an empty and an aged HDD pool's drain; it is worth building only for sites with 25GbE absent and FC present, after Phase B's TCP exit tests.
8. **I will carry the link-selection hysteresis Consensus asked for**: fail-over to the LAN after 3 s link-dead, fail-back after 30 s stable plus one probe chunk, and the switch is invisible to the relationship because my heartbeat is per relationship, not per path.


### By Opus-Consensus

#### Opus-Consensus: cross-examination of Storage, Protocols and Fabrics (Session 03)

Every kernel claim below was checked against the v6.12 tree today unless marked [believed]; I read the brief (sections 4 and 6) and rulings R1 to R24 first. Holes follow the owner's order: (a) snapshot deltas under high ingest, (b) identity across SVMs, (c) client timeouts under lag and failover, (d) hardware RAID against the sequential flusher, then (e) contradictions, missing failure modes and numbers.

##### 1. Opus-Storage

###### S1. (e) The ublk data path as written does not exist on 6.12
HOLE: `IORING_OP_READ_FIXED` and `WRITE_FIXED` on `/dev/ublkcN` are refused; the plain fallback is punted to a worker thread.
SCENARIO: Phase C, any 4 KiB WRITE. The reactor issues `READ_FIXED` on the char device into a registered hugetlbfs slot. `ublk_check_and_get_req()` returns `-EACCES` for any iterator that is not user-backed (`if (!user_backed_iter(iter)) return ERR_PTR(-EACCES);`); io_uring fixed buffers are bvec iterators [verified: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/block/ublk_drv.c]. Every write and every read (the check is shared by `write_iter`) fails. If the daemon falls back to `IORING_OP_READ`, `ublk_ch_fops` has no `.poll` and `ublk_ch_open` sets no `FMODE_NOWAIT`, so `io_file_get_flags()` leaves `REQ_F_SUPPORT_NOWAIT` clear unless the fd was opened `O_NONBLOCK`; `__io_read` then returns `-EAGAIN` ("If the file doesn't support async, just async punt") and the request runs on io-wq [verified: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/io_uring/rw.c and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/io_uring/io_uring.c].
WHY IT BREAKS: the 2.5 to 5.3 us budget assumes an inline copy; an io-wq hop is a context switch per request (5 to 20 us) on a core outside the reactor and defeats `SINGLE_ISSUER` locality. Exit test 10 (p50 under 5 us) cannot pass.
FIX: open `/dev/ublkcN` with `O_NONBLOCK` and use `IORING_OP_READ`/`WRITE` with a plain user pointer into the arena (ITER_UBUF passes `user_backed_iter`; `ublk_copy_user_pages` does one `copy_from_user` per page, no pinning), or `pread64`/`pwrite64` synchronously from the reactor (about 1 us plus the copy). Delete the "pin one huge page" line of the cost table.
SEVERITY: blocker as written; a one-line fix once known.

###### S2. (a) A snapshot under continuous ingest holds the NAS freeze for the whole CP drain
HOLE: the cut waits for the in-flight CP and `fsfreeze` is taken before the cut.
SCENARIO: HDD pool at 80% full, drain 0.3 to 0.5 GB/s (Storage's number), 0.8 GB/s NFSv3 ingest from a Proxmox datastore SVM. CP N (a 4 GiB half) starts draining at t=0 and finishes at t=8 to 13 s. The hourly snapshot fires at t=1: `nbladed` issues `FIFREEZE` (writers block until thaw) and requests `Snapshot(id)`, which 2.8 makes "immediate unless a CP is in flight, then at the next one". The cut lands at t=8 to 13; NFS WRITEs stall 7 to 12 s, four to six times R7's 2 s bound. `freeze_timeout_ms = 3000` fires first, so the snapshot is taken crash-consistent. On an aged HDD pool under load every scheduled NAS snapshot degrades, and "freeze window p99 under 3 s" (item 9) passes only on an empty pool.
WHY IT BREAKS: the arena is double-buffered, so a third generation has nowhere to live, and the cut is tied to CP admission instead of to the epoch flip.
FIX: decouple the cut from CP admission. A cut is the epoch flip alone (under 50 us); closed generations queue and the CP engine drains them in order, several per half if needed (slots, not generations, are the budget). Freeze, flip, thaw: the window is the page-cache sync alone (2 to 3 s worst case as budgeted). The queue is also the third buffer `BackToBack` needs.
SEVERITY: major.

###### S3. (a) Shipping stripe images verbatim ships GC relocations and other volumes' blocks
HOLE: the staged stripe images are not the CP's client write set.
SCENARIO 1 (GC): aged pool, ingest 0.3 GB/s, GC relocating 0.4 GB/s through the same CP assembler (it must: never-overwrite, full stripes). The summary stamps `birth = cp_seq`, so a block relocated in CP 50 is indistinguishable from one born in CP 50. The steady shipper sends 0.7 GB/s, 0.4 of it data the receiver already holds; on 10GbE the relationship goes `Lagging` within one CP although client ingest is a third of the link. If GC instead preserves the logical birth in the map while the summary says 50, stream and map disagree and the weekly digest compare fires.
SCENARIO 2 (mixed direction): aggregate `agg0` carries V (A to B) and W (B to A, applied on A by A's CP assembler). A's CP 51 stripe images hold W's received blocks beside V's new ones. Sent verbatim, W's blocks go back to B; `DeltaSink::begin` accepts (base matches for V) and `apply_chunk` has no per-volume direction filter, so B overwrites its own W with A's copy under A's `birth`. Volumes with no relationship cross the link for nothing.
WHY IT BREAKS: 2.4's identity "write set equals entries with birth == N" holds only if every CP write is a client write; GC, scrub rewrites, receiver applies and patch merges all produce stripes.
FIX: a 2-bit `kind` per summary entry (`Ingest | Relocate | Applied | Merge`) and a per-stripe volume bitmap; the shipper sends only stripes holding `Ingest` blocks of outbound volumes, the receiver drops entries whose volume is not inbound, and outbound ingest is packed into its own stripes so a mixed aggregate does not halve the useful link.
SEVERITY: major.

###### S4. (c) nvfail-on-promote in `precise` mode can bring an unsafe volume online
HOLE: `promote_hint.write_active` is up to one heartbeat old; the intent write is local only.
SCENARIO: Phase B, ESXi datastore LUN V, `nvfail = on`, idle for two CPs. t=0.00 a guest writes; A writes the intent superblock and acknowledges at 0.01 s; the heartbeat carrying the bit is due at 0.90 s; A loses power at 0.50 s. B's last hint says V idle; Storage's table: "promoted, bit clear → export → Online(idle)". V comes online at CP K with the VMFS journal ahead of the disk: exactly the hazard nvfail exists for.
WHY IT BREAKS: a set that must be exact at promotion cannot be shipped asynchronously; the 1 s heartbeat narrows the window, it does not close it.
FIX: on promotion treat `write_active` as advisory for the byte estimate only; the nvfail set is "every writable volume not provably idle", where idle means two consecutive `CpBegin`s with the bit clear and no later heartbeat reporting a write. That is conservative for busy volumes and precise for genuinely idle ones; say so in the class table.
SEVERITY: major (safety).

###### S5. (e) Intent writes collide with the four-slot superblock ring
HOLE: an intent superblock carries the same `(epoch, cp_seq)` as the committed one.
SCENARIO: CP N commits to slot A1; one second later volume V's first write needs an intent superblock. (i) Written to B0: two valid superblocks carry `(epoch, N)` and R19's max-select has no tiebreak, so a dirty boot may pick A1 and miss V. (ii) Written in place to A1: a power cut mid-stripe tears the only copy of CP N; max-select falls back to N-1 and the node silently discards up to one CP of acknowledged, committed data because of an intent write. Three bursty volumes also evict N-1 and N-2 from the ring, so "a real rewind" no longer holds.
FIX: superblock slots for commits only. `write_active` lives in a separate two-slot 4 KiB FUA page with a monotonic `intent_seq` and CRC; boot takes the union of the superblock and any newer intent page. On md that is one FUA 4 KiB write (one member plus parity), not a 2.5 MiB stripe, and it no longer queues behind 80 MiB of in-flight stripes, which is what would have made "intent p99 under 20 ms on HDD" fail under load (67 ms of queue by Storage's own figure).
SEVERITY: major.

###### S6. (d) RAID6 write hole under the metadata stream
HOLE: the torn-CP rule assumes a torn write damages only its own blocks; on raid456 without a journal a torn sub-stripe write leaves the parity of the whole stripe inconsistent.
SCENARIO: mdadm RAID6 10+2, no metadata class. CP N's metadata stream (CP log record, segment-table delta, 16 KiB map pages) is not stripe-sized and lands in stripe S beside CP N-1's map pages. Power fails mid-RMW on S. Boot falls back to N-1; the map pages read fine. Before a scrub, drive 7 dies: reconstruction of its chunk of S uses the inconsistent parity and returns garbage for N-1's map page; the CRC catches it, the page is gone, the volume will not mount. PPL closes this "For RAID5 only" and only `--write-journal` covers RAID6 [verified: https://manpages.debian.org/trixie/mdadm/mdadm.8.en.html and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/Documentation/driver-api/md/raid5-ppl.rst]; the write-intent bitmap only schedules a resync that trusts parity.
FIX: metadata writes are full stripes too (log-structured metadata segments, padded; 2.5 MiB per CP is noise), or the flash metadata class is mandatory on RAID6, or `--write-journal` is required. Pick one; "on the pool otherwise" is the hole.
SEVERITY: major on RAID6 HDD pools.

###### S7. (d) Hardware RAID: commands are 128 KiB, and write-through is scheduled, not a fault
HOLE: megaraid_sas caps `max_hw_sectors_kb` at `MEGASAS_MAX_SECTORS_IEEE = 256` sectors (128 KiB) whenever the firmware reports IEEE SGLs, and the `max_sectors` parameter can only lower it except on two GEN2 IDs [verified: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/scsi/megaraid/megaraid_sas.h and megaraid_sas_base.c, `megasas_io_attach`]. The probe set starts at 256 KiB, so it cannot see a 128 KiB knee; a 2.5 MiB stripe is 20 commands.
SCENARIO: PERC H700 (R12's used-market node) or LSI 9260/ServeRAID M5015 with iBBU08, write-back, probe passed. Every 90 days the learn cycle runs 1 to 12 h and the controller "will change the cache mode to write-through during the calibration cycle" (iBBU08 default mode 4) [verified: https://www.ibm.com/support/pages/battery-mode-changes-ibbu08-ibm-system-x]; Dell: H700 and earlier "automatically switch to Write-Through mode when the battery charge is low because of a learn cycle" [verified: https://www.dell.com/support/kbdoc/en-us/000141687/dell-perc-controller-learn-cycle-mode]; Exadata documents the same quarterly 1 to 12 h window [verified: https://docs.oracle.com/cd/E40166_01/html/E40167/z4001567134162202.html]. PERC 8 and later are transparent but still drop to write-through when the battery degrades ("Write policy ... was changed to Write Through") [verified: https://www.dell.com/support/kbdoc/en-us/000038067/faulty-perc-battery-on-dd3300]. In write-through nothing coalesces the 20 commands; each is a parity RMW; drain falls from 1.2 GB/s to 150 to 300 MB/s (Storage's own figure). At 0.5 GB/s ingest the half fills in 8 s, the throttle reaches 2 s, ports go Transitioning and ESXi flaps paths for hours, four times a year, with no fault anywhere.
FIX: extend the probe to 64 KiB and record `max_hw_sectors_kb`; make the VD rule mandatory for write-back controllers too (strip times data disks at most `max_hw_sectors_kb`: 8 data drives at 16 KiB strips); treat a write-policy change as an event (lengthen the CP timer, raise the throttle threshold, alert) rather than flapping ports; document that only "always write back" keeps the probe result year-round, with its risk.
SEVERITY: major.

###### S8. (d) md over hardware-RAID single-drive VDs loses the flush chain and skips the attestation
HOLE: 2.6 treats md as "exact; no probe needed" and the attestation applies to "non-md backstores only".
SCENARIO: PERC H710 (no HBA mode), eight SATA drives as eight RAID0 VDs, RAID6 on top: the common homelab layout. The VD returns no caching page; sd assumes "write through" and sets neither `BLK_FEAT_WRITE_CACHE` nor `BLK_FEAT_FUA` [verified: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/scsi/sd.c, `sd_read_cache_type`, `sd_set_flush_flag`]. md advertises both regardless (`md_init_stacking_limits`) and forwards each flush as a `REQ_PREFLUSH` bio per member [verified: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/md/md.c]; the member queue completes it without issuing anything ("An empty flush ... may translate into nothing if the underlying device does not advertise a write-back cache") [verified: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/block/blk-flush.c]. The PERC's Disk Cache Policy for SATA members defaults to Enabled [believed; Dell KB 000136726 snippet: enabled by default for SATA, disabled for SAS]. Power cut: the drives' volatile caches hold the FUA superblock and the last stripes; nothing ever asked them to flush; the four slots then max-select a CP whose segments are partly missing and the CRC turns it into "no valid superblock".
FIX: run the attestation on md members: if a member's `queue/write_cache` reads "write through" and its vendor string is a RAID controller (DELL, LSI, AVAGO, PERC, MegaRAID, Adaptec, HPE LOGICAL VOLUME), require `cache_protection` and the operator's confirmation that the member disk cache policy is Disabled; refuse `unknown`.
SEVERITY: major (safety).

###### S9. (e) Numbers that do not add up
HOLE: an 8 GiB double-buffered arena cannot hold the 10 GB CP the replication arithmetic assumes. 2.8 says `ArenaHalfFull` fires at "the active half at 50%, 4 GiB"; the half is 4 GiB, 50% is 2 GiB, so at 1 GB/s a CP is cut every 2 s, not 10. 2.2's "a CP is 10 GB and ships in 9 s", 3.1 and the lag table assume 10 s CPs. With 2 s CPs steady lag is 2 to 4 s (better), but the CP log, flush and superblock run five times as often and `cps_behind` thresholds must become seconds. Also the page-index entry is 8 B but must hold a 48-bit PBA and a 32-bit `max_birth`: make it 16 B (40 MB per 10 TB).
FIX: state the interval as min(timer, 2 GiB / ingest) everywhere and recompute.
SEVERITY: minor.

###### S10. (b) `nvfail = on` for the root volume takes every SVM down on every dirty boot
HOLE: nothing in Protocols' ladder starts an SVM whose root is NvFailed.
SCENARIO: single node, no UPS, file SVM with `alert` shares. Power cut; the root volume was in `write_active` (statd wrote `sm/` 3 s earlier) → NvFailed; `svm start` fails at S2 (root mount gets EIO); every share, including the `alert` class chosen because "an outage costs more than a notice", is down until an operator clears the root. Protocols' 2.11 has no row and 2.2 no state for it.
FIX: the root's class follows the strictest data volume in the SVM; the tenant-state rewind check is done by content (the root's CP generation versus the one recorded at the last successful start) and alerts.
SEVERITY: major (operational).

##### 2. Opus-Protocols

###### P1. (e) The namespace pins cannot be created as 2.1 describes
HOLE: the helper bind-mounts `/proc/self/ns/{net,uts,mnt}` onto `/run/opentap/svm/<id>/ns/*` after `unshare(CLONE_NEWNS)` and `pivot_root`.
SCENARIO: `otap-nsinit` unshares, builds the view with a private tmpfs `/run`, pivots, then binds `/proc/self/ns/mnt` to `/run/opentap/svm/1/ns/mnt`. That mount exists in the helper's new mount namespace, on the SVM's private `/run`; the host's `/run/opentap` is private-propagation by the design's own requirement, so nothing reaches the host. The helper exits, the namespaces die, `nsenter --mount=...` fails with ENOENT, and C1's "1,000 cycles leak no namespace" never completes the first. util-linux solves exactly this: `unshare --mount=FILE` forks a child that stays in the parent mount namespace, waits for the parent's `mnt` inode to change, then bind-mounts `/proc/<ppid>/ns/*` from there (`bind_ns_files_from_child`, selected when `npersists && (unshare_flags & CLONE_NEWNS)`) [verified: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/util-linux/util-linux/v2.41/sys-utils/unshare.c].
FIX: `nbladed`, in the host namespaces, binds `/proc/<helper>/ns/*` while the helper blocks on a pipe, then releases it to build the view; or exec util-linux 2.41.5 `unshare --net= --uts= --mount= --propagation slave` as the helper.
SEVERITY: blocker as written; a thirty-line fix.

###### P2. (b) One lockd thread serves every SVM
HOLE: lockd is a single global `svc_serv` with one thread (`svc_set_num_threads(serv, NULL, 1)` in `lockd_get()`); `lockd_up_net()` adds per-net sockets and a per-net grace timer only; `nlm_grace_period` and the NLM ports are global [verified: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/fs/lockd/svc.c].
SCENARIO: datastore SVMs A and B, Proxmox with NLM. A's volume stalls (2 s throttle, a 5 s `dbladed` restart per R4, or an nvfailed LUN not yet unexported). A host sends NLM_LOCK for a qcow2 whose inode is cold; lockd's `nlm_fopen` → `nfsd_open` → `fh_verify` → `xfs_iget` blocks on the stalled device. For 2 to 5 s every NLM request of SVM B (image opens with `lock=on`, reclaims after B's own move) waits on the same thread; a B move during A's stall spends part of its 20 s grace on nothing. 2.10 lists nfsd threads as unattributed; lockd is not listed at all.
FIX: document the shared thread; unexport a stalled volume's NLM scope before the other ladder steps; add a lockd row to 2.10. Per-net lockd threads do not exist on 6.12; anything newer is a CI lane (R12).
SEVERITY: major (isolation), no in-box fix.

###### P3. (c) The planned move ships after it stops, and block clients time out on a backlog
HOLE: 2.2's move is "stop on A, final CP and ship, start on B", with T1 removing addresses first and no lag check.
SCENARIO: Phase B datastore SVM, two ESXi hosts on iSCSI, one on NFSv3; the relationship is `Lagging` 40 GB after a backup window. T1 at t=0; the final CP plus backlog take 40 GB / 1.1 GB/s = 36 s, plus Storage's receiver switch at its next CP (up to 10 s). ESXi marks the path dead at 10 to 35 s and the NFS datastore enters APD; Windows holds 60 s. At t≈46 s B raises the LIF with the same MAC, but an initiator whose TCP backoff (RTO min 200 ms default, exponential [verified: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/Documentation/networking/ip-sysctl.rst]) has reached 6.4 to 12.8 s learns of B's RST only at its next retransmit, so the "8 to 15 s" of section 5 becomes 50 to 60 s, past Windows' hold time.
FIX: pre-copy then cut over: `otap-ctl` refuses `svm move` unless `Steady` with lag under one CP; the ladder is ship-to-Steady, portal close (T3 before T1, so initiators get a FIN and re-login in 2 to 5 s instead of a NOP timeout), final CP of one CP's worth, ship, switch on `CpEnd` (not at the receiver's next CP). Publish "6 s ladder plus one CP ship plus switch".
SEVERITY: major.

###### P4. (c) Every Phase B NAS takeover pays XFS log replay
HOLE: a replica built from crash-consistent CPs always has a dirty log unless the CP was fsfreeze-cut; edge 3 treats replay as an unplanned-start special case.
SCENARIO: file SVM, 20 volumes with 128 MiB logs, HDD replica. A dies, B promotes, S4 mounts in parallel: 20 x 128 MiB of log reads plus the metadata they reference; 5 s if the array gives 0.5 GB/s to 20 readers, 50 s when each read costs a cold 16 KiB map read first (Storage's edge 4). Add 20 s of grace unless early end. ESXi NFSv3 survives (113 to 130 s hold) but 6.6's 11 to 13 s bound is gone for NAS and nothing replaces it.
FIX: the receiver pre-replays (per applied CP: writable clone, mount, let XFS replay, snapshot as the promotable root, discard the clone, all off the client path), or every N-th CP is fsfreeze-cut and promotion picks the newest clean-log CP when the lag gate allows; until measured the table says "NAS unplanned takeover 15 to 60 s".
SEVERITY: major.

###### P5. (b) BUILTIN and well-known SIDs get different ids in every SVM
HOLE: `idmap config * : backend = tdb` allocates on first sight per `winbindd_idmap.tdb`, per SVM; rid "can NOT be used as the default backend" and "one usually needs to define a writeable default idmap range ... in order to be able to map the BUILTIN sids" [verified: https://www.samba.org/samba/docs/current/man-html/idmap_rid.8.html].
SCENARIO: SVMs A and B in LAB. An admin grants `BUILTIN\Administrators` on `\\A\projects`; the xattr stores A's allocation (say 3000005); on B the same group became 3000012 because `Users` was seen first. `volume rehost` (Phase B), host-side backup and restore across SVMs, and DR re-creation all produce ACLs naming the wrong group; Everyone and Authenticated Users likewise.
FIX: at SVM creation `nbladed` pre-seeds the `*` backend from a fixed Raft table (`net idmap set` for S-1-5-32-544..551, S-1-1-0, S-1-5-11, S-1-5-2, S-1-3-0/1); rehost refuses when the two tdbs disagree.
SEVERITY: minor now, major with rehost.

###### P6. (b) The NFSv4 scope is welded to the NetBIOS name
HOLE: scope = UTS nodename = `netbios name`, 15 characters, unique only inside one cluster.
SCENARIO: lab and DR clusters each have `hv01`; a Debian client mounts both. NFSv4.1 clients compare `server_scope` and `server_owner.major_id`, both `nn->nfsd_name`, assume one server and attempt session trunking across the two; after a DR test the stale side can win. No validator sees the other cluster.
FIX: `rpc.nfsd --scope=<svm>.<cluster-uuid8>`: nfs-utils implements it as `unshare(CLONE_NEWUTS)` plus `sethostname(scope)` inside rpc.nfsd [verified: https://sources.debian.org/data/main/n/nfs-utils/1:2.8.3-1/utils/nfsd/nfsd.c], so Samba keeps its 15-character name and NFS gets a global one. Protocols calls `--scope` unnecessary; it is the fix.
SEVERITY: minor.

###### P7. (c) The NFS nvfail row is mislabelled and the clear step has a gap
HOLE: "export removed → hang". Removing the export makes `fh_verify` fail at `rqst_exp_find` with `-ENOENT`, returned as `nfserr_stale` immediately [verified: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/fs/nfsd/nfsfh.c]; `nvfail_generation`, which the fsid bump needs, is absent from Storage's superblock.
SCENARIO: ESXi datastore; at nvfail the export goes and ESXi gets STALE at once (acceptable). After an operator clear, a reconciler pass re-adds the export with the volume UUID before any generation exists; the cached root handle is valid again and VMs resume against the rolled-back disk.
FIX: the generation is part of the fsid from day one (volume table, bumped on every rollback: Storage adds it); if APD semantics are wanted, drop packets with the per-SVM nftables ruleset instead of removing the export.
SEVERITY: minor.

###### P8. (b) nfsdcld must be on the pipe within one second of `rpc.nfsd`
HOLE: `nfsd4_cld_tracking_init` waits 10 x 100 ms for a pipe reader; on timeout legacy tracking is refused in a non-init netns, `client_tracking_ops` becomes NULL, `nfs4_state_start_net` ignores the return value, and `nfsd4_client_record_check` answers `-EOPNOTSUPP` for every reclaim [verified: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/fs/nfsd/nfs4recover.c and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/fs/nfsd/nfs4state.c].
SCENARIO: file SVM start on a loaded node; nfsdcld's SQLite open on a cold root volume takes 1.2 s; `rpc.nfsd 16` starts beside it. Grace runs, 20 clients' reclaims are refused with RECLAIM_BAD, opens and locks are lost, and the only trace is a `pr_warn`.
FIX: `-nfsd@` `Requires=`/`After=` `-nfsdcld@` with readiness defined as the nfsdcld PID holding the `cld` pipe open; alert on the warning string.
SEVERITY: minor.

##### 3. Opus-Fabrics

###### F1. (a/e) The stream is specified against a delta source Storage does not produce
HOLE: Fabrics' chunk is 1 MiB of consecutive manifest extents from arena slots with `crc32c_combine`; Storage's is a 2.5 MiB (HDD) or 256 KiB (flash) stripe image with summary pages from the staging pool, slots freed at staging.
SCENARIO: steady state at 1 GB/s. The 84 MB manifest per 10 s CP is built from "the frozen dirty index", which Storage drains and frees while staging; `ExtentSrc::Arena(RingRef)` points at slots reused within the interval; `read_disk(pba)` needs a PBA that exists only after commit; "chunk i is always the same bytes" is false once staging is released unless the chunk is the on-disk stripe (Storage's property, which Fabrics does not use); `crc32c_combine` does not cover summary pages. Two framings, two cursors, two commit semantics cannot both freeze in item 1.
FIX: adopt the stripe image as the payload (`Chunk{cp, idx}` = one stripe, resumable from disk by `(seg, stripe_idx)` after any sender failure, per-4 KiB CRCs inside the summary), keep Fabrics' 64-byte frame, credits, endpoint selection and BLAKE3-over-summaries, delete the manifest, chunk-aligned resume only.
SEVERITY: major.

###### F2. (e) `tls = false` contradicts R21 and leaves the receiver unauthenticated
HOLE: R21 says the stream is "streamed over TLS"; 2.1 accepts plaintext on an operator-asserted `direct = true` endpoint, and `Hello` is authenticated only by TLS.
SCENARIO: the "direct" DAC is a switch port in the lab VLAN after a recable. Any host reaching 10.255.0.2:7430 sends `Hello(rel)`, reads the cursor, sends `DeltaBegin` with `base == applied` and chunks whose CRCs it computed itself. The receiver lands and commits: the replica is attacker-chosen bytes at a valid CP boundary, promoted at the next takeover. CRCs cannot detect this.
FIX: TLS everywhere (Fabrics' own 0.4 core per side at 10GbE), or a keyed BLAKE3 MAC over header and payload CRC under the cluster key on plaintext endpoints (64 B per chunk), and no unauthenticated `Hello`.
SEVERITY: major (security; contradicts R21).

###### F3. (c) `Committed(cp)` means different things on the two sides
HOLE: Fabrics commits at `DeltaEnd` (100 to 300 ms) and derives lag, rollback and the 13 s figure from it; Storage switches roots at the receiver's next own CP (10 s timer on HDD).
SCENARIO: 300 MB/s ingest, 10 s CPs, 10GbE: Fabrics' lag 13 s; under Storage's receiver the applied age at A's death is up to 23 s, plus the 3 s TTL: 26 s of rollback, while the dashboard built on Fabrics' numbers shows 13. My takeover gate reads whichever number the stream reports.
FIX: `applied` = roots switched and superblock written; switch on `CpEnd` when no own CP is in flight, else at the next (the receiver shortens its CP timer to 2 s while a relationship is inbound); report `applied_age_s` and `landed_age_s` separately.
SEVERITY: major.
