###### F4. (a) Credits are granted for landing that is not on disk
HOLE: "credits as it writes chunks into fresh segments" bounds the sender "by how fast the destination disk absorbs", but 1 MiB chunks are sub-stripe on HDD, so the receiver must stage (Storage's receiver does) and `Landed` is a memory event.
SCENARIO: HDD receiver at 80% full lands 0.4 GB/s and grants credits at memory speed; with 4 x 64 MiB windows the sender is throttled only by TCP once Storage's 2 GiB receiver staging is full, which Fabrics' table (128 to 512 MiB of landing buffers, no staging) does not contain.
FIX: credits = free receiver staging stripes, granted per staged stripe; 64 MiB becomes 25 HDD stripes.
SEVERITY: minor once F1 is settled.

###### F5. (c) Phase B block presentation: standby paths or LIF moves
HOLE: Fabrics gives each SVM an FC vport per node with the partner's group Standby ("takeover is a group flip"); Protocols says in Phase B "a standby path would be a lie", so iSCSI LIFs move and no target exists on the partner; R9 wants byte-identical trees with pre-created devices.
SCENARIO: a Proxmox host with FC and iSCSI to one SVM (2.2 allows the set) sees an FC Standby path on B and no iSCSI path; at takeover FC is Active/Optimized within the ALUA transition (2 to 3 s), iSCSI after a LIF move plus login (5 to 15 s, P3). `prio alua` puts them in different groups of one device (same serial) and fails over on its own schedule. Fabrics' edge 13 (replica LUN size without `UPDATE_SIZE`) applies to both.
FIX: one rule: standby paths for both (a ublk device over the replica root on B at every applied CP, LIO group Standby, same serial, resize by re-creation while Standby), so takeover is the ALUA flip for all block protocols and the LIF move is NAS-only.
SEVERITY: major (contradiction with Protocols and R9).

###### F6. (e) A corrupt source re-sends forever
HOLE: "a bad chunk CRC returns Abort(Corrupt, idx) and the sender resends"; the sender never recomputes.
SCENARIO: a DRAM bit flip in a staged stripe after its summary CRC was computed; every resend carries the same bytes; the relationship never advances; the alert blames the link.
FIX: after three resends of one chunk the sender verifies against its own summary CRCs, marks the block bad, skips it and raises a media alert.
SEVERITY: minor.

##### Cross-persona contradictions

| Topic | Persona A says | Persona B says | What must be decided |
|---|---|---|---|
| Replication chunk | Storage: staged stripe image, 2.5 MiB HDD, self-describing, cursor `(cp, idx, byte)` | Fabrics: 1 MiB extent runs from arena slots, 32 B manifest entries, chunk-indexed cursor | one payload before item 1 of either plan (F1) |
| Receiver commit | Storage: at the receiver's next own CP (up to 10 s) | Fabrics: at `DeltaEnd`, 100 to 300 ms | the definition of `applied` the takeover gate reads (F3) |
| Replication memory | Storage: 2.5 GiB staging plus 2 GiB receiver staging | Fabrics: 0.5 to 1.1 GiB, "send source 0"; Protocols' slice math (36 GiB) ignores Storage's 8 GiB read cache (Storage: 32 GiB) | Fable's 64 GB table |
| TLS | Storage: Fabrics owns | Fabrics: `tls = false` on direct links | R21 says TLS: keep it or MAC the frames (F2) |
| Timers | Storage: link down > 10 s → Lagging, warn 60 s, crit 600 s, 1 s heartbeat | Fabrics: connect 1 s, dead 3 s, back-off 1 to 30 s, fail-back 30 s; round-2 table: link dead 1 s | one table (R7), owner `otap-ctl` |
| Phase B block paths | Protocols: LIF moves, no standby target | Fabrics: vport pairs, partner Standby; R9: byte-identical trees | standby for both or LIF move for both (F5) |
| nvfail defaults | Storage: file and object `alert`, SVM root `on` | Protocols 2.11: PDL, ESTALE, share-offline for every dirty volume; no root-volume state | the class table with the root rule (S10) |
| `nvfail_generation` | Storage: absent | Protocols: required for the fsid bump | Storage adds it to the volume table (P7) |
| Snapshot latency | Storage: at most one CP, "under 4 s" | Protocols: 3 s freeze budget | decouple cut from CP (S2) |
| QD1 iSCSI write | Storage: 100 to 200 us client-visible | Protocols: p50 at most 100 us as an exit criterion | one number |
| Catch-up order | Storage: data read in PBA order per volume | Fabrics: manifest sorted by `(vol, lba)` and stable | chunk order = PBA order; stability from the on-disk stripe (F1) |
| `.snapshot` exposure | Storage: inside the junction via `crossmnt`, Phase C item 9 | Protocols: outside share roots in `.otap/snap`, in-junction is Phase B | one path, one phase |
| Shipper core | Storage: shipper inside the CP program on reactors | Fabrics: non-isolated cores, no busy-poll, R16's mirror core returned | the core table in the platform profile |

##### What I would change in my own design after reading theirs

1. Nvfail source of truth. I accept Storage's position with the S5 intent page: the aggregate's on-disk state is authoritative for nvfail and for the operator's clear; the Raft `NvFail` op becomes a mirror carrying the alert and the audit of who cleared. Phase C's "same control plane with one voter" then has concrete content: the voter may be down and the node still boots, evaluates nvfail and serves.
2. Promotion set. I drop `promote_hint` as a gate and adopt S4's conservative rule; `write_active` only sizes the alert. `max_auto_takeover_lag` is redefined on applied age (F3): automatic below two CP intervals plus the receiver's CP interval plus 30 s, manual above; the stream reports `applied_age_s` on my 1 s control heartbeat rather than its own channel (Storage's question 1).
3. Direction epoch. Raft holds `(volume, direction, epoch)`; every flip increments it and no flip is possible during a no-quorum freeze, so Storage's `DeltaSink::begin` check is the data-layer fence for Phase B. The no-quorum posture is freeze ownership, keep serving, keep shipping (Storage's question 5): shipping cannot create a promotable replica without quorum, and `Hello` carries the epoch so a partitioned old owner is refused later rather than fenced now.
4. Planned move. I sequence it with P3's pre-copy rule: veto unless `Steady` and lag under one CP, portals closed before addresses removed, receiver switch on `CpEnd`. Timer rows: move block-visible 6 s ladder plus one CP ship plus switch; NAS unplanned takeover 15 to 60 s until P4 is measured; stream connect 1 s, dead 3 s; control link dead 1 s; lag warn 60 s, crit 600 s.
5. Fence evidence in Phase B. With private disks the dangerous residue is identity, not media: a lingering netns with a LIO portal keeps answering ARP for a moved LIF (Protocols' edge 2; `sock_create` sockets hold a netns reference, `sk_net_refcnt = kern ? 0 : 1` [verified: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/net/core/sock.c]). `Fenced(evidence)` gains "three unanswered ARP probes per moved LIF address from the survivor before GARP"; the RST proxy runs only on that evidence, as R9 says.
6. Witness content. The witness stores relationship names, direction epochs and base snapshot UUIDs, never cursors (Fabrics' question 4: cursors stay on the destination aggregate). Lagging and Broken thresholds and their hysteresis live in `otap-ctl`, not in the stream.
7. Barriers. I withdraw the takeover-triggered CP and the four data steps that assumed an inbound ring: takeover is `Fenced`, promote at K and evaluate nvfail, `BlockServing` (an ALUA flip for every block protocol if F5 is decided that way), `NasServing`.

## Fact-check claims and verdicts (40 claims: PARTIALLY-CORRECT 25, CONFIRMED 14, REFUTED 1)

### [C01] PARTIALLY-CORRECT
- Claim: ESXi 8.0 U3 declares Permanent Device Loss only when every path to the device returns a PDL sense code (the PDL set being 05h/25h/00h LOGICAL UNIT NOT SUPPORTED, 04h/4Ch/00h, 04h/3Eh/00h, 05h/68h/00h LOGICAL UNIT NOT CONFIGURED per Broadcom KB 318712); a path in Dead state (no response from a powered-off node) prevents PDL and leaves the device in All-Paths-Down; ALUA Unavailable (02h/04h/0Ch) is never a PDL sense; dead paths are re-evaluated only every Disk.PathEvalTime (default 300 s) via TEST UNIT READY, and after Misc.APDTimeout (default 140 s) virtual-machine I/O is still retried indefinitely rather than failed.
- Raised by: Opus-Protocols, Opus-Storage, Opus-Consensus, Opus-Fabrics
- Why it matters: Decides whether nvfail for LUNs can be presented as an unmapped LUN on the surviving node (PDL) or must become a serial/WWID bump, whether ALUA Unavailable is usable as a 'PDL-style' presentation at all, and whether the ESXi recipe must lower Disk.PathEvalTime so VMs do not silently resume on a rolled-back LUN.
- Summary: The mechanics are confirmed by Broadcom's vSphere Storage 8.0 guide and KBs: PDL requires the PDL sense (or, for single-LUN-per-target iSCSI, a 'Target Unavailable' login rejection) on all of the device's paths; without it ESXi treats the loss as APD; Misc.APDTimeout defaults to 140 s (range 20-99999) after which only non-VM I/O is fast-failed while 'Virtual machine I/O continues retrying'; Disk.PathEval sends TEST_UNIT_READY down every path, including Dead ones, every 300 s by default (Disk.PathEvalTime, range 30-1500 s). The claim misquotes KB 318712's PDL set: 04h/3Eh/00h is not listed (the entries are 3Eh/01h and 3Eh/03h), NOT READY (02h) variants of 4Ch/00h and 3Eh/01h,03h are also PDL, and 25h/00h and 68h/00h are matched on ASC/ASCQ alone regardless of sense key; 02h/04h/0Ch (ALUA Unavailable) is indeed absent. 'A Dead path prevents PDL' is a sound inference from the all-paths rule but no source states the mixed case explicitly, and the 8.0 rescan page adds that a rescan removes an unavailable path from the device's path list; 'only every PathEvalTime' is too strong because rescans and failed-I/O TUR probes also change path state.
- Evidence: 1) All-paths rule (vSphere Storage 8.0, 'Detecting PDL Conditions'): "For the device to be considered permanently lost, the sense codes must be received on all its paths." Example given: "H:0x0 D:0x2 P:0x0 Valid sense data: 0x5 0x25 0x0 or Logical Unit Not Supported". For iSCSI arrays with one LUN per target the array rejects login with "Target Unavailable" and "As with the sense codes, this response must be received on all paths for the device to be considered permanently lost." After PDL "the host stops attempts to reestablish connectivity or to send commands to the device"; the client shows operational state "Lost Communication" and "All paths are shown as Dead". When a device fails without sending sense codes "the host cannot detect PDL conditions" and "continues to treat the device connectivity problems as APD even when the device fails permanently." Parent page: ESXi recognises PDL when it "receives appropriate sense codes or a login rejection from storage arrays". PDL causes listed include removal, "a change in the device's unique ID", or unrecoverable hardware error; Disk.AutoremoveOnPDL (default on) removes the device and paths once no open connections remain.

2) PDL sense set (Broadcom KB 318712, Products: ESXi 7.0 and 8.0). Table of "possible SCSI sense codes that determine if a device is in a PDL state": "0x__ /0x25/0x0 *LOGICAL UNIT NOT SUPPORTED"; "0x__/0x68/0x0 *LOGICAL UNIT NOT CONFIGURED"; "0x4/0x4c/0x0 HARDWARE ERROR/LOGICAL UNIT FAILED SELF-CONFIGURATION"; "0x4/0x3e/0x3 HARDWARE ERROR/LOGICAL UNIT FAILED SELF-TEST"; "0x4/0x3e/0x1 HARDWARE ERROR/LOGICAL UNIT FAILURE"; "0x2/0x4c/0x0 NOT READY/LOGICAL UNIT FAILED SELF-CONFIGURATION"; "0x2/0x3e/0x3 NOT READY/LOGICAL UNIT FAILED SELF-TEST"; "0x2/0x3e/0x1 NOT READY/LOGICAL UNIT FAILURE". Footnote: "*ESXi only checks ASC/ASCQ and if it happens to be 0x25/0x0 or 0x68/0x0, it marks device as PDL." There is no 0x3e/0x0 entry and no 0x2/0x4/0xc entry. Same KB: "If PDL SCSI sense codes are not returned from a device... then the device is in an All-Paths-Down (APD) state"; in APD the host "indefinitely retries SCSI I/O, including: Userworld I/O (hostd management agent)" and "Virtual machine guest I/O"; after PDL "The ESXi host no longer attempts to re-establish connectivity or issue commands to the device." The KB also shows the message "Rescan complete, however some dead paths were not removed because they were in use by the system."

3) Dead paths and PathEval (Broadcom KB 316417, ESXi 7.x/8.x): "the Disk.PathEval routine issues a TEST_UNIT_READY command down every path every 300 seconds (which is the default)"; "TEST_UNIT_READY is issued down Dead paths on the same 300 second interval in case a path becomes available again, at which point the path is marked as On instead of Dead"; a failed command causes the host "to send SCSI command 0x0 (TEST_UNIT_READY) down the path where the command failed" and "If the TEST_UNIT_READY command also fails, the path is marked as Dead"; the stack also "marks paths as Dead after a permanent device loss (PDL) check condition returned by the storage array"; an array port that "does not gracefully drop from the fabric" means devices "must wait for their device loss timeout". KB 340491 (seen only in search-engine snippets; the page returned HTTP 404 on fetch): Disk.PathEvalTime "default value is 300 seconds. The value must be between 30 seconds and 1500 seconds", set per host. vSphere Storage 8.0 'Rescan Operations for ESXi Storage': "If you rescan when a path is unavailable, the host removes the path from the list of paths to the device." and "The path reappears on the list as soon as it becomes available and starts working again."; VMFS datastore management operations make "your host or the vCenter Server automatically rescan". The 8.0 'View Storage Device Paths' page defines only Active (I/O), Standby, Disabled and Dead ("Paths that are no longer available for processing I/O") as path statuses; no 'Unavailable' or PDL path status exists.

4) APD timeout (vSphere Storage 8.0, 'Handling Transient APD Conditions' and 'Change Timeout Limits for Storage APD'): "By default, the APD timeout is set to 140 seconds."; "If the device does not recover and the timeout ends, the host stops its attempts at retries and stops any non-virtual machine I/O. Virtual machine I/O continues retrying."; "Even though the device and datastores are unavailable, virtual machines remain responsive."; device shows "Dead or Error" and all paths Dead; "If later the device paths become operational, the host can resume I/O to the device and end the special APD treatment." Parameter Misc.APDTimeout: "You can enter a value between 20 and 99999 seconds."; a change after the device becomes unavailable "does not take effect for that particular APD incident." KB 406100 (vSphere 7.0/8.0): "Misc.APDTimeout. Set to 140 seconds by default"; with Misc.APDHandlingEnable the host "continues to retry I/O commands only for the time period, specified by Misc.APDTimeout"; HA VMCP responses to APD/PDL apply regardless of the deprecated VMkernel.Boot.terminateVMOnPDL. KB 318850 (ESXi 7.0.x/8.0.x/9.x): "By default the APD timer runs for 140 seconds"; afterwards "the host stops its attempts to retry any I/O that is not coming from virtual machines"; vobd logs "has entered the All Paths Down Timeout state after being in the All Paths Down state for 140 seconds. I/Os will now be fast failed."

5) ALUA (Broadcom KB 310442, ESXi 6.x-8.x): Unavailable AAS "is usually seen when the TPG's access to the LUN is restricted as a result of hardware errors or other SCSI device limitations" and "A TPG in this state is unable to transition to AO or ANO until the error subsides"; VMW_SATP_ALUA action_OnRetryErrors "is set to off by default", and when an I/O returns a retryable error the path "remains in an on state even after the I/O is retried indefinitely"; when on, "the path eventually, after a certain timeout, is marked dead". The KB does not give the sense data for Unavailable or state how ESXi classifies such paths; no primary source found describes an 'unavailable' path state or any PDL semantics for 02h/04h/0Ch.

Not found in any primary source: an explicit statement about the mixed case (some paths returning PDL sense while others are transport-Dead); the 'leaves the device in APD' consequence is inferred from the all-paths rule plus the no-sense-codes-means-APD rule.
- Corrected claim: ESXi 8.0 (including U3) registers a SCSI device as Permanent Device Loss only when a PDL response is received on every path of the device: a PDL sense code, or for single-LUN-per-target iSCSI an iSCSI login rejection 'Target Unavailable', on all paths (vSphere Storage 8.0, 'Detecting PDL Conditions'). The PDL sense set per Broadcom KB 318712 is: ASC/ASCQ 25h/00h LOGICAL UNIT NOT SUPPORTED and 68h/00h LOGICAL UNIT NOT CONFIGURED, matched on ASC/ASCQ alone regardless of sense key; plus 4Ch/00h LOGICAL UNIT FAILED SELF-CONFIGURATION, 3Eh/03h LOGICAL UNIT FAILED SELF-TEST and 3Eh/01h LOGICAL UNIT FAILURE under either sense key HARDWARE ERROR (04h) or NOT READY (02h). 3Eh/00h is not in the set, and ALUA 'LOGICAL UNIT NOT ACCESSIBLE, TARGET PORT IN UNAVAILABLE STATE' (02h/04h/0Ch) is not a PDL sense; by default a path returning a retryable error stays On with the I/O retried indefinitely (VMW_SATP_ALUA action_OnRetryErrors=off, KB 310442). A device that stops responding without a PDL sense is treated as APD even if the loss is permanent; therefore, as long as a transport-Dead path (for example to a powered-off node) remains in the device's path list, the all-paths condition cannot be met and the device stays in APD (inference from the documented rules; no primary source states the mixed case explicitly). A rescan performed while a path is unavailable removes that path from the device's path list, although paths in use by the system may not be removed (KB 318712), so a rescan can change the outcome. Dead paths are probed with TEST_UNIT_READY every Disk.PathEvalTime, default 300 s (range 30-1500 s), and return to On when the probe succeeds; a path can also be re-probed immediately after a failed I/O, and rescans (manual, or automatic on VMFS datastore operations) rebuild the path list, so 300 s is the upper bound for noticing a revived path, not the only mechanism. The APD timer (Misc.APDTimeout, default 140 s, range 20-99999 s) only governs non-VM I/O: when it expires the host fast-fails non-virtual-machine I/O and shows the device as 'Dead or Error', while 'Virtual machine I/O continues retrying' with no documented bound, and I/O resumes if the paths become operational again. A PDL device, by contrast, has its open connections closed and is removed (Disk.AutoremoveOnPDL=1) once no references remain; vSphere HA VMCP can additionally terminate or restart VMs on PDL and after APD timeout plus the VMCP delay.
- Design impact: 1) nvfail for LUNs cannot be delivered as 'unmapped on the surviving node = PDL on ESXi' while the failed node's target ports are simply gone: the ESXi device keeps the Dead paths to the powered-off node, the all-paths condition is unmet, and the device sits in APD with VM I/O retrying forever (until an admin rescan removes the dead paths, which ESXi may refuse for in-use paths). To obtain a real PDL every path must answer with a PDL sense, so the design must either have the survivor take over the failed node's target identities (NPIV WWPNs / iSCSI portals, or an iSCSI login rejection on single-LUN-per-target layouts) and answer 25h/00h or 68h/00h on all of them, or fall back to the identity change (new NAA/serial), which the 8.0 guide lists as a PDL cause and which makes the rolled-back LUN a new device rather than a resumption of the old one. 2) ALUA Unavailable (02h/04h/0Ch) must be dropped from any 'PDL-style' presentation: it is not in the PDL set and ESXi's default handling is indefinite retry with the path left On, i.e. APD-like behaviour, never PDL. 3) The ESXi recipe should not present Disk.PathEvalTime as the guard against VMs silently resuming on a rolled-back LUN: lowering it (minimum 30 s) only makes ESXi notice revived paths sooner, and rescans or failed-I/O probes can revive them sooner still; the only guards are a genuine PDL on all paths or a changed device identity. The document should state the 300 s default as an upper bound on path re-evaluation, cite Misc.APDTimeout 140 s with range 20-99999 s and the fact that it does not stop VM I/O, and note the vSphere HA VMCP responses (APD timeout plus delay, PDL) and guest-OS disk timeouts as the actual VM-level consequences. 4) The sense-code list in the design must be corrected to the KB 318712 set (25h/00h and 68h/00h sense-key-agnostic; 4Ch/00h, 3Eh/01h, 3Eh/03h with sense key 04h or 02h; no 3Eh/00h), and the mixed dead/PDL path behaviour plus the rescan effect should be verified on a lab host with esxcli storage core device list and path list before the recipe is finalised, since no primary source documents that case explicitly.

### [C02] PARTIALLY-CORRECT
- Claim: On Linux 6.12 LIO, when the LUN mapped at LUN 0 of a TPG is unmapped, the target still answers for LUN 0 as the 'virtual LUN 0' (REPORT LUNS well-known LUN) in drivers/target/target_core_device.c (transport_lookup_cmd_lun / transport_lookup_tmr_lun) and returns WRITE commands with DATA PROTECT sense 07h/27h/00h (and reads from the virtual LUN) instead of ILLEGAL REQUEST 05h/25h/00h, whereas unmapping a non-zero LUN yields 05h/25h/00h.
- Raised by: Opus-Fabrics, Opus-Protocols
- Why it matters: If true, the planned LUN-unmap nvfail presentation never produces PDL for the most common mapping (LUN 0), so the Raft validator must reserve LUN 0 per TPG and the LUN-ID policy ('LUN 0 always mapped') changes.
- Summary: The core mechanism is confirmed from the v6.12 source (and the function is byte-identical in Debian trixie's shipped linux 6.12.94-1, with no Debian patch touching drivers/target): when the initiator has no mapping for LUN 0, transport_lookup_cmd_lun() falls back to the per-TPG tpg_virt_lun0, returning TCM_WRITE_PROTECTED (DATA PROTECT 07h/27h/00h) for every command whose data direction is neither DMA_FROM_DEVICE nor DMA_NONE and servicing reads/non-data commands from a dummy ramdisk, whereas any other unmapped LUN gets TCM_NON_EXISTENT_LUN (ILLEGAL REQUEST 05h/25h/00h). Two parts of the claim are wrong: transport_lookup_tmr_lun() has no virtual-LUN-0 fallback (a TMR to unmapped LUN 0 fails with LUN DOES NOT EXIST), and the "virtual LUN 0" is not the REPORT LUNS well-known LUN but a per-TPG se_lun backed by a global rd_mcp "virt_lun0" device (rd_pages=8,rd_nullio=1,rd_dummy=1) that reports INQUIRY byte 0 = 3Fh (PQ=001b "not connected"), answers TEST UNIT READY GOOD, returns GOOD for reads of LBA 0-63 (zero-filled on Debian kernels) and 05h/21h/00h beyond. The design consequence holds: unmapping a data LUN presented at LUN 0 can never yield 05h/25h/00h, and VMware documents PDL only for ASC/ASCQ 25h/00h, 68h/00h and listed NOT READY/HARDWARE ERROR codes, so LUN 0 must be reserved.
- Evidence: 1) drivers/target/target_core_device.c, v6.12 tag (GitHub mirror; Debian 6.12.94-1 copy diffed identical), transport_lookup_cmd_lun(), lines 47-139. Lookup is per initiator ACL: L56 "deve = target_nacl_find_deve(nacl, se_cmd->orig_fe_lun);" (target_nacl_find_deve matches "deve->mapped_lun == mapped_lun", L262-271). Mapped read-only LUN: L67-74 "if ((se_cmd->data_direction == DMA_TO_DEVICE) && deve->lun_access_ro) { ... return TCM_WRITE_PROTECTED; }". No mapping: L92-121:
"if (!se_lun) {
	/* Use the se_portal_group->tpg_virt_lun0 to allow for REPORT_LUNS, et al to be returned when no active MappedLUN=0 exists for this Initiator Port. */
	if (se_cmd->orig_fe_lun != 0) {
		pr_err("TARGET_CORE[%s]: Detected NON_EXISTENT_LUN Access for 0x%08llx from %s\n", ...);
		return TCM_NON_EXISTENT_LUN;
	}
	/* Force WRITE PROTECT for virtual LUN 0 */
	if ((se_cmd->data_direction != DMA_FROM_DEVICE) &&
	    (se_cmd->data_direction != DMA_NONE))
		return TCM_WRITE_PROTECTED;
	se_lun = se_sess->se_tpg->tpg_virt_lun0;
	if (!percpu_ref_tryget_live(&se_lun->lun_ref))
		return TCM_NON_EXISTENT_LUN;
	se_cmd->se_lun = se_sess->se_tpg->tpg_virt_lun0; ..."
So the rejection covers all DMA_TO_DEVICE/bidirectional commands (WRITE*, WRITE SAME, UNMAP, COMPARE AND WRITE, MODE SELECT, PERSISTENT RESERVE OUT, XCOPY...), not only WRITE; reads and DMA_NONE commands (TUR, INQUIRY-free paths, REPORT LUNS is DMA_FROM_DEVICE) go to the dummy device.

2) Same file, transport_lookup_tmr_lun(), L142-180: after the same ACL lookup, "if (!se_lun) { pr_debug("TARGET_CORE[%s]: Detected NON_EXISTENT_LUN Access for 0x%08llx for %s\n", ...); return -ENODEV; }" — no LUN-0 special case. target_core_transport.c L2011-2013 "ret = transport_lookup_tmr_lun(se_cmd); if (ret) goto failure;" with the comment "push this work off to process context with TMR_LUN_DOES_NOT_EXIST status." iscsi_target.c L2091-2094: "ret = transport_lookup_tmr_lun(&cmd->se_cmd); if (ret < 0) { se_tmr->response = ISCSI_TMF_RSP_NO_LUN; goto attach; }". tcm_qla2xxx.c L749-751: "case TMR_LUN_DOES_NOT_EXIST: default: mcmd->fc_tm_rsp = FC_TM_FAILED;".

3) Sense mapping, target_core_transport.c sense_detail_table: L3318-3321 "[TCM_NON_EXISTENT_LUN] = { .key = ILLEGAL_REQUEST, .asc = 0x25 /* LOGICAL UNIT NOT SUPPORTED */ }," (no .ascq, so 00h) => 05h/25h/00h; L3391-3394 "[TCM_WRITE_PROTECTED] = { .key = DATA_PROTECT, .asc = 0x27, /* WRITE PROTECTED */ }," => 07h/27h/00h; L3395-3398 "[TCM_ADDRESS_OUT_OF_RANGE] = { .key = ILLEGAL_REQUEST, .asc = 0x21, /* LOGICAL BLOCK ADDRESS OUT OF RANGE */ },". Both fabrics share the path: target_submit_prep() L1760 "rc = transport_lookup_cmd_lun(se_cmd);".

4) What the virtual LUN 0 is. target_core_tpg.c L543-549: "if (se_tpg->proto_id >= 0) { se_tpg->tpg_virt_lun0 = core_tpg_alloc_lun(se_tpg, 0); ... ret = core_tpg_add_lun(se_tpg, se_tpg->tpg_virt_lun0, true, g_lun0_dev);" (created unconditionally for every TPG, lun_access_ro=true; removed only in core_tpg_deregister, L596-598). target_core_device.c core_dev_setup_virtual_lun0() L1007-1031: "char buf[] = \"rd_pages=8,rd_nullio=1,rd_dummy=1\"; ... hba = core_alloc_hba(\"rd_mcp\", 0, HBA_FLAGS_INTERNAL_USE); ... dev = target_alloc_device(hba, \"virt_lun0\"); ... g_lun0_dev = dev;". Vendor L787 "strscpy(dev->t10_wwn.vendor, \"LIO-ORG\", ...)"; target_core_rd.c L658 ".inquiry_prod = \"RAMDISK-MCP\"". target_core_rd.c L610-616: "static u32 rd_get_device_type(struct se_device *dev) { if (RD_DEV(dev)->rd_flags & RDF_DUMMY) return 0x3f; /* Unknown device type, not connected */ else return sbc_get_device_type(dev); }" and target_core_spc.c L749 (standard INQUIRY) "buf[0] = dev->transport->get_device_type(dev);" => INQUIRY byte 0 = 3Fh (PQ=001b, PDT=1Fh). Capacity: rd_get_blocks L618-626 "((rd_dev->rd_page_count * PAGE_SIZE) / dev->dev_attrib.block_size) - 1" => last LBA 63 (64 x 512 B = 32 KiB). Reads: rd_execute_rw L432-435 "if (dev->rd_flags & RDF_NULLIO) { target_complete_cmd(cmd, SAM_STAT_GOOD); return 0; }" (buffer untouched; target_alloc_sgl L2767 zeroes only when zero_page, and L2784 "bool zero_flag = !(cmd->se_cmd_flags & SCF_SCSI_DATA_CDB);" so READ buffers are not explicitly zeroed — but Debian's debian/config/config L7740 has CONFIG_INIT_ON_ALLOC_DEFAULT_ON=y, so pages are zero-filled unless init_on_alloc=0 is set). Out-of-range reads: target_core_sbc.c L1054-1060 "end_lba = dev->transport->get_blocks(dev) + 1; if (... (cmd->t_task_lba + sectors) > end_lba) { ... return TCM_ADDRESS_OUT_OF_RANGE; }" => 05h/21h/00h for LBA > 63. No unit serial is ever configured for virt_lun0, and target_core_spc.c L242-243 emits the NAA designator only "if (dev->dev_flags & DF_EMULATED_VPD_UNIT_SERIAL)", so it carries no NAA. REPORT LUNS, target_core_spc.c L1283-1290: "/* If no LUNs are accessible, report virtual LUN 0. */ if (lun_count == 0) { int_to_scsilun(0, &slun); ..." — otherwise only the initiator's mapped LUNs are listed.

5) Provenance of the dummy behaviour: commit 0aecfa662e43 "scsi: target: Add the DUMMY flag to rd_mcp" (Konstantin Shelekhin, merged by Martin K. Petersen, 2021): "forces a logical unit to report itself as not connected device of an unknown type ... allows users to create devices identical to the device for the virtual LUN 0, making it possible to explicitly create a LUN 0 device and configure its WWNs (e.g. vendor or product name)". Commit 1b5ad814af5e: "Create the device for the virtual LUN 0 using the DUMMY flag. This change makes it possible to remove some special-casing in the INQUIRY code." (removed "buf[0] = 0x3f; /* Not connected */" special case from spc_emulate_inquiry; changed the param string to "rd_pages=8,rd_nullio=1,rd_dummy=1").

6) Debian trixie: tracker.debian.org/pkg/linux lists stable 6.12.94-1 (trixie-security/p-u 6.12.111-1). sources.debian.org data for linux 6.12.94-1: transport_lookup_cmd_lun() body identical to the v6.12 tag (diff empty), same "rd_pages=8,rd_nullio=1,rd_dummy=1"; debian/patches/series (97 patches) contains no patch touching drivers/target.

7) Host-side consequences. Broadcom/VMware KB 318712 "Permanent Device Loss (PDL) and All-Paths-Down (APD) on host": PDL table lists ASC/ASCQ 0x25/0x0 "LOGICAL UNIT NOT SUPPORTED", 0x68/0x0 "LOGICAL UNIT NOT CONFIGURED", 0x4/0x4c/0x0, 0x4/0x3e/0x3, 0x4/0x3e/0x1, 0x2/0x4c/0x0, 0x2/0x3e/0x3, 0x2/0x3e/0x1; footnote "ESXi only checks ASC/ASCQ and if it happens to be 0x25/0x0 or 0x68/0x0, it marks device as PDL"; if PDL codes are not returned "the ESXi host continues to send I/O requests until the host receives a response"; DATA PROTECT / 0x7 0x27 does not appear. The vSphere storage guide PDL topic (docs.vmware.com GUID-45CF28F0, now redirected to techdocs.broadcom.com; sentence seen only in a search excerpt, page not fetched directly): "For the device to be considered permanently lost, the sense codes must be received on all its paths." Linux initiators (drivers/scsi/scsi_scan.c v6.12 L1277-1284): "if (((result[0] >> 5) == 1 || starget->pdt_1f_for_no_lun) && (result[0] & 0x1f) == 0x1f && !scsi_is_wlun(lun)) { ... "peripheral device type of 31, no device added" ..." — so a (re)scan creates no device for LIO's virtual LUN 0; scsi_lib.c L886-887 "case DATA_PROTECT: action = ACTION_FAIL;" — writes fail without retry. Not found in any primary source: how ESXi 8 treats an already-claimed path whose LUN 0 turns into a PQ=1 dummy; elixir.bootlin.com returned only navigation chrome and git.kernel.org plain views returned HTTP 403, so the GitHub mirror of the v6.12 tag and Debian's own orig source were used instead. - Corrected claim: On Linux 6.12 LIO (verified in the v6.12 tag and byte-identical in Debian trixie's linux 6.12.94-1; no Debian patch touches drivers/target), SCSI command LUN resolution is per initiator node ACL (transport_lookup_cmd_lun() -> target_nacl_find_deve(nacl, orig_fe_lun)). If the initiator has no mapped LUN (MappedLUN in its ACL, or TPG LUN in demo mode) for the addressed LUN: (a) LUN != 0 -> TCM_NON_EXISTENT_LUN -> CHECK CONDITION, ILLEGAL REQUEST 05h/25h/00h (LOGICAL UNIT NOT SUPPORTED); (b) LUN 0 never returns 05h/25h/00h: every command whose data direction is neither DMA_FROM_DEVICE nor DMA_NONE (WRITE*, WRITE SAME, UNMAP, COMPARE AND WRITE, MODE SELECT, PERSISTENT RESERVE OUT, XCOPY, ...) gets TCM_WRITE_PROTECTED -> DATA PROTECT 07h/27h/00h, and reads and non-data commands are serviced by the TPG's tpg_virt_lun0 — a read-only se_lun created unconditionally for every TPG (proto_id >= 0) and backed by the kernel-global rd_mcp device "virt_lun0" (rd_pages=8,rd_nullio=1,rd_dummy=1): INQUIRY byte 0 = 3Fh (peripheral qualifier 001b "not connected", device type 1Fh), vendor LIO-ORG / model RAMDISK-MCP, no unit serial and therefore no NAA designator; TEST UNIT READY -> GOOD; READ of LBA 0..63 (64 x 512 B) -> GOOD with an untouched buffer (zero-filled on Debian kernels, CONFIG_INIT_ON_ALLOC_DEFAULT_ON=y); READ beyond LBA 63 -> ILLEGAL REQUEST 05h/21h/00h; REPORT LUNS lists only the initiator's mapped LUNs and reports LUN 0 only when none are mapped. This "virtual LUN 0" is a LIO placeholder at LUN address 0, not the SAM REPORT LUNS well-known LUN. Task management requests differ: transport_lookup_tmr_lun() has no virtual-LUN-0 fallback, so a TMR addressed to unmapped LUN 0 (or any unmapped LUN) completes with TMR_LUN_DOES_NOT_EXIST (iSCSI response "LUN does not exist", tcm_qla2xxx FC_TM_FAILED). ESXi declares PDL only on ASC/ASCQ 25h/00h or 68h/00h (plus the NOT READY/HARDWARE ERROR 3Eh/4Ch codes listed in KB 318712), received on all paths; DATA PROTECT 07h/27h/00h is not a PDL trigger, and Linux initiators create no device for a PQ=1/PDT=1Fh LUN on rescan while an existing device fails writes immediately (ACTION_FAIL).
- Design impact: 1) The LUN-unmap nvfail presentation cannot produce PDL (or any 05h/25h/00h) for a data LUN presented at mapped LUN 0 on any fabric (iSCSI and tcm_qla2xxx share target_submit_prep -> transport_lookup_cmd_lun). Worse than "no PDL": after the unmap the host sees, at the same LUN address, a read-only 32 KiB "not connected" dummy that answers TEST UNIT READY with GOOD (dm-multipath TUR checkers and similar probes keep the path up), returns zeros with GOOD status for reads of LBA 0-63, 05h/21h/00h for reads above, and DATA PROTECT for every write/outbound command, with no NAA identity. So the design must not rely on unmapping LUN 0 for anything. 2) Adopt the LUN-ID policy "LUN 0 is never a data LUN": either leave LUN 0 to LIO's virtual LUN 0 (data LUNs start at 1; REPORT LUNS omits LUN 0 whenever at least one LUN is mapped) or, preferably for client consistency, map a permanent placeholder at LUN 0 in every TPG and every initiator ACL (an rd_mcp backstore with rd_dummy=1, as the 2021 commit intends, so its WWN/vendor/product can be fixed). The Raft config validator must reject any data LUN at mapped LUN 0 and any ACL/MappedLUN change that would leave a data LUN at 0; mappings are per initiator ACL, so the invariant is per (TPG, ACL), not just per TPG. 3) Record the TMR asymmetry in the failure-injection matrix: during an unmap window commands at LUN 0 get DATA PROTECT/GOOD while aborts and LUN resets at LUN 0 get LUN DOES NOT EXIST. 4) For PDL-on-withdrawal of a non-zero data LUN the 05h/25h/00h path is confirmed and ESXi documents it as PDL only once it is seen on all paths, so the unmap must be applied on every TPG/portal of the target before expecting PDL; iSCSI login rejection on all paths is VMware's other documented PDL trigger if a whole target must disappear. 5) Open item for the lab (no primary VMware source found): how ESXi 8 treats an already-claimed path whose LUN 0 turns into a PQ=1 dummy (expected: I/O errors and "Peripheral qualifier 0x1 not supported" on rescan, not PDL); verify with sg_turs/sg_inq/sg_raw against a 6.12 target before any LUN-0 behaviour is relied on. Debian trixie-security's 6.12.111-1 was not diffed but the function has been unchanged since the 2021 dummy-device commits.
