### [C03] PARTIALLY-CORRECT
- Claim: On Linux 6.12 the ublk char device (/dev/ublkcN) read/write path (ublk_check_and_get_req in drivers/block/ublk_drv.c) rejects any iov_iter that is not user-backed with -EACCES, so IORING_OP_READ_FIXED / IORING_OP_WRITE_FIXED against it fail; additionally ublk_ch_fops has no .poll method and the file does not set FMODE_NOWAIT, so a plain IORING_OP_READ/WRITE is punted to an io-wq worker (adding roughly 8 to 20 us) unless the fd was opened O_NONBLOCK, and a synchronous pread/pwrite from the reactor avoids the punt.
- Raised by: Opus-Consensus, Opus-Protocols, Opus-Storage
- Why it matters: The engine's 2.5 to 5.3 us acknowledgement budget and the Phase C exit test (p99 under 15 us, 50 K IOPS on 4 cores) assume an inline fixed-buffer copy from the ublk char device into the arena slot; if refused or punted, the data path must be redesigned (O_NONBLOCK plus user-pointer READ, or pread64).
- Summary: Every mechanical statement in the claim is confirmed against the v6.12 source and Debian's shipped 6.12.111-1 ublk_drv.c: the char-device read/write path returns -EACCES for any iov_iter that is not ITER_UBUF/ITER_IOVEC (so READ_FIXED/WRITE_FIXED, which are ITER_BVEC, fail), ublk_ch_fops has no .poll and never sets FMODE_NOWAIT, a plain IORING_OP_READ/WRITE is therefore punted to io-wq, O_NONBLOCK on the fd makes io_uring run it inline, and pread/pwrite is the documented synchronous path. Two things are not as stated: the "8 to 20 us" punt cost has no primary source (the only published measurement is a 2021 LKML datapoint: io-wq insertion avg 8.98 us, async completion avg 24.7 us vs 7.9 us inline, worst case 59 us), and the claim omits that the path exists only for devices created with UBLK_F_USER_COPY (otherwise -EINVAL) and that for a registered file the O_NONBLOCK flag is captured at IORING_REGISTER_FILES time. libublk 0.4.8 opens /dev/ublkcN without O_NONBLOCK, so the design must set it via fcntl on dev.tgt.fds[0].
- Evidence: 1. ublk rejects non-user-backed iterators (v6.12 tag and Debian 6.12.111-1 source are identical here). ublk_check_and_get_req(): "if (!ub) return ERR_PTR(-EACCES);" then "if (!user_backed_iter(iter))" -> "return ERR_PTR(-EACCES);" then the UBLK_S_DEV_DEAD -EACCES check; q_id/tag/req lookup failures return -EINVAL; the fail: label returns -EACCES. ublk_ch_read_iter body: "req = ublk_check_and_get_req(iocb, to, &buf_off, ITER_DEST); if (IS_ERR(req)) return PTR_ERR(req); ret = ublk_copy_user_pages(req, buf_off, to, ITER_DEST); ... ublk_put_req_ref(ubq, req); return ret;". The check was introduced unexplained by commit 1172d5b8beca "ublk: support user copy" (Ming Lei, 2023-05-19, merged 6.5); the v5 posting says only "Support pread()/pwrite() on ublk char device for reading/writing request io buffer" and gives no rationale for rejecting kernel-backed iterators.

2. What "user-backed" means in 6.12 (include/linux/uio.h): "static inline bool user_backed_iter(const struct iov_iter *i) { return iter_is_ubuf(i) || iter_is_iovec(i); }" (a type test; struct iov_iter has no user_backed field in 6.12). io_uring fixed buffers are bvec iterators: io_uring/rsrc.c io_import_fixed() does "iov_iter_bvec(iter, ddir, imu->bvec, imu->nr_bvecs, offset + len);" and rw.c io_prep_rw_fixed() calls "ret = io_import_fixed(ddir, &io->iter, req->imu, rw->addr, rw->len);". lib/iov_iter.c iov_iter_bvec sets ".iter_type = ITER_BVEC". Hence READ_FIXED/WRITE_FIXED -> -EACCES. Plain READ/WRITE are user-backed: rw.c __io_import_iovec "if (!def->vectored || req->flags & REQ_F_BUFFER_SELECT) {" ... "return import_ubuf(ddir, buf, sqe_len, &io->iter);" and import_ubuf -> iov_iter_ubuf (".iter_type = ITER_UBUF"); vectored ops use __import_iovec (ITER_IOVEC).

3. No poll, no FMODE_NOWAIT. ublk_ch_fops members are exactly ".owner = THIS_MODULE, .open = ublk_ch_open, .release = ublk_ch_release, .read_iter = ublk_ch_read_iter, .write_iter = ublk_ch_write_iter, .uring_cmd = ublk_ch_uring_cmd, .mmap = ublk_ch_mmap". The strings "FMODE_NOWAIT", ".poll", "IOCB_NOWAIT", "ki_flags" and "O_NONBLOCK" do not appear anywhere in ublk_drv.c (v6.12 and Debian 6.12.111-1). ublk_ch_open only does "test_and_set_bit(UB_STATE_OPEN, &ub->state)" (-EBUSY if already open) and "filp->private_data = ub;".

4. io_uring punt logic (v6.12). rw.c io_file_supports_nowait(): "/* If FMODE_NOWAIT is set for a file, we're golden */ if (req->flags & REQ_F_SUPPORT_NOWAIT) return true;" "/* No FMODE_NOWAIT, if we can poll, check the status */" (vfs_poll) "/* No FMODE_NOWAIT support, and file isn't pollable. Tough luck. */" return false. __io_read(): "if (force_nonblock) { /* If the file doesn't support async, just async punt */ if (unlikely(!io_file_supports_nowait(req, EPOLLIN))) return -EAGAIN; kiocb->ki_flags |= IOCB_NOWAIT; }"; io_write has the same with EPOLLOUT and "goto ret_eagain;". io_uring.c io_queue_sqe(): "ret = io_issue_sqe(req, IO_URING_F_NONBLOCK|IO_URING_F_COMPLETE_DEFER);" with comment "We async punt it if the file wasn't marked NOWAIT, or if the file doesn't support non-blocking read/write attempts"; io_queue_async(): "if (ret != -EAGAIN || (req->flags & REQ_F_NOWAIT)) { io_req_defer_failed(req, ret);" else "switch (io_arm_poll_handler(req, 0)) {" ... "case IO_APOLL_ABORTED: io_kbuf_recycle(req, 0); io_queue_iowq(req); break;". poll.c io_arm_poll_handler(): "if (!io_file_can_poll(req)) return IO_APOLL_ABORTED;". io_uring.h io_file_can_poll() -> "file_can_poll(req->file)"; include/linux/poll.h: "static inline bool file_can_poll(struct file *file) { return file->f_op->poll; }". io_queue_iowq ends in "io_wq_enqueue(tctx->io_wq, &req->work);" and io_wq_submit_work issues with "unsigned int issue_flags = IO_URING_F_UNLOCKED | IO_URING_F_IOWQ;" (no NONBLOCK) so the worker thread performs the copy.

5. The O_NONBLOCK escape hatch. io_uring.c io_file_get_flags(): "if ((file->f_flags & O_NONBLOCK) || (file->f_mode & FMODE_NOWAIT))" -> "res |= REQ_F_SUPPORT_NOWAIT;". rw.c io_rw_init_file(): "if (!(req->flags & REQ_F_FIXED_FILE)) req->flags |= io_file_get_flags(file);" and the REQ_F_NOWAIT clause "if (kiocb->ki_flags & IOCB_NOWAIT || ((file->f_flags & O_NONBLOCK && !(req->flags & REQ_F_SUPPORT_NOWAIT))))" is not taken because SUPPORT_NOWAIT is set. For registered files, filetable.h io_fixed_file_set(): "file_slot->file_ptr = (unsigned long)file | (io_file_get_flags(file) >> REQ_F_SUPPORT_NOWAIT_BIT);" so the flag is captured at registration. Since ublk never inspects ki_flags, the inline call with IOCB_NOWAIT completes the copy synchronously. fcntl F_SETFL man page: "On Linux, this operation can change only the O_APPEND, O_ASYNC, O_DIRECT, O_NOATIME, and O_NONBLOCK flags." O_NONBLOCK has no effect on the uring_cmd path: io_uring/uring_cmd.c contains no FMODE_NOWAIT, O_NONBLOCK, REQ_F_SUPPORT_NOWAIT or io_file_supports_nowait reference, and ublk_drv.c has no O_NONBLOCK reference. Trap: include/linux/fs.h kiocb_set_rw_flags(): "if (flags & RWF_NOWAIT) { if (!(ki->ki_filp->f_mode & FMODE_NOWAIT)) return -EOPNOTSUPP; }" so RWF_NOWAIT in sqe->rw_flags fails on this file. io_rw_should_retry (cited by the claim) is not the operative function; it begins "/* never retry for NOWAIT, we just complete with -EAGAIN */" and bails for pollable files or files without FOP_BUFFER_RASYNC; the decision is made in io_file_supports_nowait/io_queue_async.

6. pread/pwrite is the documented synchronous path. include/uapi/linux/ublk_cmd.h (v6.12): "/* Copy between request and user buffer by pread()/pwrite() * Not available for UBLK_F_UNPRIVILEGED_DEV, otherwise userspace may deceive us by not filling request buffer, then kernel uninitialized data may be leaked. */ #define UBLK_F_USER_COPY (1UL << 7)"; comment on ublksrv_io_cmd.addr: "`addr` should not be used when UBLK_F_USER_COPY is enabled, because userspace handles data copy by pread()/pwrite() over /dev/ublkcN." Precondition: __ublk_check_and_get_req() returns NULL (-> -EINVAL) "if (!ublk_need_req_ref(ubq))", where ublk_need_req_ref returns ublk_support_user_copy(ubq) = "ubq->flags & UBLK_F_USER_COPY". Documentation/block/ublk.rst at v6.12 does not mention UBLK_F_USER_COPY at all; zero copy is listed under "Future development". The 6.12 UAPI defines UBLK_F_ flags bits 0..8 only and contains no UBLK_U_IO_REGISTER_IO_BUF/UBLK_F_AUTO_BUF_REG; UBLK_U_IO_REGISTER_IO_BUF (_IOWR('u', 0x23, ...)) first appears in the v6.15 header.

7. Copy mechanics (relevant to the fixed-buffer rationale): ublk_copy_user_pages() pins pages per call, "len = iov_iter_get_pages2(uiter, iter.pages, iov_iter_count(uiter), UBLK_MAX_PIN_PAGES, &off);", ublk_copy_io_pages does "void *pg_buf = kmap_local_page(data->pages[pg_idx]);" and memcpy, then "put_page(iter.pages[i]);". So a registered io_uring buffer would not have avoided per-I/O page pinning anyway.

8. Latency figure: no primary source states 8-20 us. The only measurement found: Olivier Langlois, LKML 2021-06-18, "Single thread, 1 TCP connection, no sqpoll", "QD was set to 256": insert io-wq time "average 8983.82" ns (min 3324, max 87816), async completion "average 24670.47" ns, reissue completion "average 7882.67" ns; "On average reissuing the sqe with the patch code is 1.1uSec faster" and "in the worse case scenario 59uSec faster than placing the request on io-wq". Pre-6.x kernel, different workload; not transferable.

9. libublk 0.4.8 (crates.io: published 2026-08-29, not yanked, newest version) opens the char device with "fs::OpenOptions::new().read(true).write(true).open(&cdev_path)" with no custom_flags/O_NONBLOCK/set_nonblocking anywhere in src/io.rs; the fd is exposed as "tgt.fds[0] = cdev_file.as_raw_fd();" through "pub tgt: UblkTgt" / "pub fds: [i32; 32]", and the crate ships ublk_user_copy_pos ("The built offset is passed to pread() or pwrite() on device of /dev/ublkcN ... Available if UBLK_F_USER_COPY is enabled").

10. Debian 13: tracker.debian.org/pkg/linux lists stable 6.12.94-1, stable-security and stable-proposed-updates 6.12.111-1, stable-backports 7.2.6-1~bpo13+1.
- Corrected claim: On Linux 6.12 (Debian 13 ships 6.12.x; verified against the v6.12 tag and Debian's 6.12.111-1 drivers/block/ublk_drv.c), the /dev/ublkcN read/write path exists only for devices created with UBLK_F_USER_COPY (which is unavailable with UBLK_F_UNPRIVILEGED_DEV); without it __ublk_check_and_get_req() returns NULL and the call fails with -EINVAL. With it, ublk_check_and_get_req() returns -EACCES for any iov_iter for which user_backed_iter() is false, i.e. anything other than ITER_UBUF or ITER_IOVEC. IORING_OP_READ_FIXED/WRITE_FIXED import a registered buffer as ITER_BVEC (io_import_fixed -> iov_iter_bvec), so they complete with -EACCES; IORING_OP_READ/WRITE (import_ubuf -> ITER_UBUF) and READV/WRITEV (ITER_IOVEC) with a plain user pointer into the arena pass the check. ublk_ch_fops defines only open/release/read_iter/write_iter/uring_cmd/mmap (no .poll), the driver never sets FMODE_NOWAIT and never inspects IOCB_NOWAIT/ki_flags. Consequently, for a ublkc fd without O_NONBLOCK, io_file_supports_nowait() is false, __io_read()/io_write() return -EAGAIN on the inline IO_URING_F_NONBLOCK attempt, io_arm_poll_handler() returns IO_APOLL_ABORTED (file not pollable) and io_queue_async() punts the SQE to an io-wq worker thread (io_queue_iowq), which performs the copy. If O_NONBLOCK is set in the file's f_flags (open flag, or fcntl F_SETFL afterwards), io_file_get_flags() sets REQ_F_SUPPORT_NOWAIT and the read/write executes inline in the submitting task with IOCB_NOWAIT, which ublk ignores, so the copy completes synchronously inside io_uring_enter; for a registered (IOSQE_FIXED_FILE) file this flag is captured at IORING_REGISTER_FILES time, so O_NONBLOCK must be set before registration. IOSQE_ASYNC still forces an io-wq punt, and RWF_NOWAIT in sqe->rw_flags fails with -EOPNOTSUPP because the file lacks FMODE_NOWAIT. O_NONBLOCK has no effect on the ublk driver or on the IORING_OP_URING_CMD FETCH/COMMIT path. A direct pread64/pwrite64 runs ublk_ch_read_iter/write_iter synchronously in the caller and is the interface the UAPI header documents ("Copy between request and user buffer by pread()/pwrite()"). In all cases the copy pins the user pages per call (iov_iter_get_pages2, kmap_local_page, memcpy, put_page), so registered buffers would have conferred no pinning advantage. The cost of an io-wq punt is not quantified by any primary source; the only published measurement (LKML, June 2021, one TCP connection, QD 256, pre-6.x kernel) shows io-wq insertion averaging 8.98 us and async completion 24.7 us versus 7.9 us inline, worst case 59 us slower; it must be measured on the target 6.12 kernel. Zero-copy buffer registration (UBLK_U_IO_REGISTER_IO_BUF) is absent from the 6.12 UAPI and first appears in 6.15.
- Design impact: The Phase C data path as written (inline READ_FIXED/WRITE_FIXED from /dev/ublkcN into an arena slot) cannot work on 6.12 and must be redesigned; the 2.5-5.3 us acknowledgement budget and the p99 < 15 us / 50 K IOPS on 4 cores exit test remain reachable only with one of these: (1) keep io_uring but use IORING_OP_READ/WRITE with a plain user pointer to the arena slot and the ublkc fd set O_NONBLOCK, applied with fcntl(F_SETFL) before IORING_REGISTER_FILES because libublk 0.4.8 opens the cdev with a plain OpenOptions read/write (fd reachable via dev.tgt.fds[0]); never set IOSQE_ASYNC or RWF_NOWAIT on these SQEs; (2) issue pread64/pwrite64 from the reactor (libublk provides ublk_user_copy_pos for the offset), costing one syscall per I/O but no completion processing; or (3) drop UBLK_F_USER_COPY and use the default mode, in which the kernel itself copies WRITE payloads into the per-(queue,tag) buffer given in ublksrv_io_cmd.addr (import_ubuf + ublk_copy_user_pages in __ublk_rq_task_work) before completing FETCH/COMMIT_AND_FETCH and copies READ payloads out of it in __ublk_complete_rq, so arena slot = per-tag buffer and no extra syscall or SQE per I/O; evaluate (3) against (1) with the acknowledgement budget. In every option the device must be created with UBLK_F_USER_COPY only for options 1-2 and cannot be an unprivileged device in that case. Replace the "8 to 20 us" figure with a measured number from the Debian 13 6.12.x kernel and add an exit-test assertion that the io_uring:io_uring_queue_async_work tracepoint never fires for ublkc READ/WRITE SQEs in the chosen configuration. Correct the design's citation: the punt decision lives in io_file_supports_nowait()/io_queue_async()/io_arm_poll_handler(), not io_rw_should_retry(). Note for the roadmap that true zero-copy (UBLK_U_IO_REGISTER_IO_BUF) needs 6.15+, i.e. a trixie-backports kernel (7.2.x per tracker), not the baseline.
- Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/block/ublk_drv.c ; https://sources.debian.org/data/main/l/linux/6.12.111-1/drivers/block/ublk_drv.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/include/linux/uio.h ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/lib/iov_iter.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/io_uring/rsrc.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/io_uring/rw.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/io_uring/io_uring.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/io_uring/io_uring.h ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/io_uring/poll.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/io_uring/filetable.h ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/io_uring/uring_cmd.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/include/linux/poll.h ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/include/linux/fs.h ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/include/uapi/linux/ublk_cmd.h ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.15/include/uapi/linux/ublk_cmd.h ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/Documentation/block/ublk.rst ; https://android-kvm.googlesource.com/linux/+/1172d5b8beca6b899deb9f7f2850e7e47ec16198 ; https://lkml.iu.edu/hypermail/linux/kernel/2303.3/04881.html ; https://lkml.iu.edu/hypermail/linux/kernel/2106.2/04093.html ; https://docs.rs/crate/libublk/0.4.8/source/src/io.rs ; https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/libublk ; https://tracker.debian.org/pkg/linux ; https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/F_SETFL.2const.html

### [C04] CONFIRMED
- Claim: In Linux 6.12 ublk_drv supports UBLK_F_USER_COPY, under which request data is transferred by pread/pwrite (or io_uring read/write) on /dev/ublkcN at offset UBLKSRV_IO_BUF_OFFSET plus an encoding of queue id and tag; UBLK_F_USER_COPY cannot be combined with UBLK_F_UNPRIVILEGED_DEV, so the daemon must run privileged.
- Raised by: Opus-Storage
- Why it matters: Determines whether dbladed can copy ublk request data directly into the hugetlbfs arena slot and whether dbladed must run as root.
- Summary: The claim is true as stated, verified against the v6.12 tag of torvalds/linux (read through the GitHub mirror of the tag; git.kernel.org returned 403 and elixir served only navigation text). include/uapi/linux/ublk_cmd.h defines UBLK_F_USER_COPY as "Copy between request and user buffer by pread()/pwrite()" and says it is "Not available for UBLK_F_UNPRIVILEGED_DEV", UBLKSRV_IO_BUF_OFFSET is 0x80000000 with a qid/tag/in-request-offset bit layout, and ublk_ctrl_add_dev in drivers/block/ublk_drv.c returns -EINVAL for USER_COPY+UNPRIVILEGED_DEV (fix 42aafd8b48ad, CVE-2024-50080, present in 6.12) while requiring CAP_SYS_ADMIN for any non-unprivileged device. Two refinements matter for the design: "privileged" means CAP_SYS_ADMIN on the process issuing /dev/ublk-control commands (not uid 0 as such), and io_uring read/write works only with plain user buffers, because registered (fixed) buffers produce a non-user-backed iov_iter that the driver rejects with -EACCES.
- Evidence: 1) Flag and semantics, include/uapi/linux/ublk_cmd.h @ v6.12: "/* Copy between request and user buffer by pread()/pwrite() * Not available for UBLK_F_UNPRIVILEGED_DEV, otherwise userspace may deceive us by not filling request buffer, then kernel uninitialized data may be leaked. */ #define UBLK_F_USER_COPY (1UL << 7)". The ublksrv_io_cmd union comment: "`addr` should not be used when UBLK_F_USER_COPY is enabled, because userspace handles data copy by pread()/pwrite() over /dev/ublkcN." UBLK_F_UNPRIVILEGED_DEV is (1UL << 5).

2) Position encoding, same header: "#define UBLKSRV_IO_BUF_OFFSET 0x80000000"; "#define UBLK_IO_BUF_OFF 0"; "/* single IO buffer max size is 32MB */ #define UBLK_IO_BUF_BITS 25"; "#define UBLK_TAG_OFF UBLK_IO_BUF_BITS"; "/* so at most 64K IOs for each queue */ #define UBLK_TAG_BITS 16"; "#define UBLK_QID_OFF (UBLK_TAG_OFF + UBLK_TAG_BITS)"; "/* max 4096 queues */ #define UBLK_QID_BITS 12"; "#define UBLKSRV_IO_BUF_TOTAL_BITS (UBLK_QID_OFF + UBLK_QID_BITS)". The 6.12 UAPI header has no ublk_pos() helper; the driver decodes with ublk_pos_to_hwq = "((pos - UBLKSRV_IO_BUF_OFFSET) >> UBLK_QID_OFF) & UBLK_QID_BITS_MASK", ublk_pos_to_tag = "((pos - UBLKSRV_IO_BUF_OFFSET) >> UBLK_TAG_OFF) & UBLK_TAG_BITS_MASK", ublk_pos_to_buf_off = "(pos - UBLKSRV_IO_BUF_OFFSET) & UBLK_IO_BUF_BITS_MASK". Userspace side: ublksrv include/ublksrv.h "static inline __u64 ublk_pos(__u16 q_id, __u16 tag, __u32 offset) { ... return UBLKSRV_IO_BUF_OFFSET + ((((__u64)q_id) << UBLK_QID_OFF) | (((__u64)tag) << UBLK_TAG_OFF) | (__u64)offset); }" and the kernel selftest patch "selftests: ublk: add support for user copy to kublk" (Dec 2025): "ublk_user_copy_offset(q_id, tag) = UBLKSRV_IO_BUF_OFFSET + ((__u64)q_id << UBLK_QID_OFF | (__u64)tag << UBLK_TAG_OFF)", used as "copied = pread(q->ublk_fd, addr, copy_len, off)" for UBLK_IO_OP_WRITE and "pwrite(...)" for UBLK_IO_OP_READ; its message: "On writes, issue pread() calls to copy the write data into the ublk_io's buffer before dispatching the write... On reads, issue pwrite() calls to copy read data from the ublk_io's buffer before committing the request."

3) Driver support and the copy path, drivers/block/ublk_drv.c @ v6.12: UBLK_F_ALL ORs UBLK_F_USER_COPY (and UBLK_F_ZONED); ublk_ctrl_get_features reports "u64 features = UBLK_F_ALL & ~UBLK_F_SUPPORT_ZERO_COPY;" (so USER_COPY is advertised). ublk_ch_fops = { .open = ublk_ch_open, .release = ublk_ch_release, .read_iter = ublk_ch_read_iter, .write_iter = ublk_ch_write_iter, .uring_cmd = ublk_ch_uring_cmd, .mmap = ublk_ch_mmap }. ublk_check_and_get_req: "if (!user_backed_iter(iter)) return ERR_PTR(-EACCES);", "if (ub->dev_info.state == UBLK_S_DEV_DEAD) return ERR_PTR(-EACCES);", decodes tag/q_id/buf_off from iocb->ki_pos, rejects "q_id >= ub->dev_info.nr_hw_queues" and "tag >= ubq->q_depth" with -EINVAL, then "if (!ublk_check_ubuf_dir(req, dir)) goto fail;" (-EACCES). __ublk_check_and_get_req: "if (!ublk_need_req_ref(ubq)) return NULL;" ... "if (offset > blk_rq_bytes(req)) goto fail_put;". ublk_need_req_ref: "/* read()/write() is involved in user copy, so request reference has to be grabbed */ return ublk_support_user_copy(ubq);" (so the read/write path only functions on USER_COPY devices). ublk_copy_user_pages pins with "len = iov_iter_get_pages2(uiter, iter.pages, iov_iter_count(uiter), UBLK_MAX_PIN_PAGES, &off);" (UBLK_MAX_PIN_PAGES 32) and copies via ublk_copy_io_pages, marking pages dirty for ITER_DEST. In __ublk_ch_uring_cmd, FETCH_REQ: "} else if (ub_cmd->addr) { /* User copy requires addr to be unset */ ret = -EINVAL;" and COMMIT_AND_FETCH_REQ: "else if (req_op(req) != REQ_OP_ZONE_APPEND && ub_cmd->addr) { /* User copy requires addr to be unset when command is not zone append */ ret = -EINVAL;".

4) Incompatibility and privilege, ublk_ctrl_add_dev @ v6.12: "if (capable(CAP_SYS_ADMIN)) info.flags &= ~UBLK_F_UNPRIVILEGED_DEV; else if (!(info.flags & UBLK_F_UNPRIVILEGED_DEV)) return -EPERM;" and "if (info.flags & UBLK_F_UNPRIVILEGED_DEV) { info.flags &= ~(UBLK_F_USER_RECOVERY_REISSUE | UBLK_F_USER_RECOVERY); /* For USER_COPY, we depends on userspace to fill request buffer by pwrite() to ublk char device, which can't be used for unprivileged device */ if (info.flags & UBLK_F_USER_COPY) return -EINVAL; }". ublk_ctrl_uring_cmd routes every control command except UBLK_U_CMD_GET_FEATURES and ADD_DEV through ublk_ctrl_uring_cmd_permission: "if (!unprivileged) { if (!capable(CAP_SYS_ADMIN)) return -EPERM; ...". The only other capable() calls are in ublk_open (block device open) and ublk_mark_io_ready ("if (capable(CAP_SYS_ADMIN)) ub->nr_privileged_daemon++;"); none is on the /dev/ublkcN open/uring_cmd/read/write/mmap path. ublk_ctrl_start_dev: "/* don't probe partitions if any one ubq daemon is un-trusted */ if (ub->nr_privileged_daemon != ub->nr_queues_ready) set_bit(GD_SUPPRESS_PART_SCAN, &disk->state);". Upstream fix commit 42aafd8b48ad "ublk: don't allow user copy for unprivileged device": "UBLK_F_USER_COPY requires userspace to call write() on ublk char device for filling request buffer, and unprivileged device can't be trusted. So don't allow user copy for unprivileged device." Cc: stable, Fixes: 1172d5b8beca ("ublk: support user copy", Link 20230519065030.351216-8-ming.lei@redhat.com, merged for 6.5). Debian security tracker CVE-2024-50080: trixie 6.12.107-1 fixed, trixie (security) 6.12.111-1 fixed.

5) io_uring read/write: io_uring/rw.c @ v6.12, io_prep_rw: "rw->kiocb.ki_pos = READ_ONCE(sqe->off);" and __io_read ends in "return file->f_op->read_iter(&rw->kiocb, iter);". __io_import_iovec: non-vectored ops use "return import_ubuf(ddir, buf, sqe_len, &io->iter);" (ITER_UBUF), READV/WRITEV use "__import_iovec(...)" (ITER_IOVEC); io_prep_rw_fixed calls io_import_fixed, which builds "iov_iter_bvec(iter, ddir, imu->bvec, imu->nr_bvecs, offset + len);" (ITER_BVEC). include/linux/uio.h: "static inline bool user_backed_iter(const struct iov_iter *i) { return iter_is_ubuf(i) || iter_is_iovec(i); }". Therefore IORING_OP_READ/WRITE/READV/WRITEV on /dev/ublkcN work; IORING_OP_READ_FIXED/WRITE_FIXED fail with -EACCES.

6) User-buffer pinning for a hugetlbfs destination: lib/iov_iter.c __iov_iter_get_pages_alloc: "if (likely(user_backed_iter(i))) { ... res = get_user_pages_fast(addr, n, gup_flags, *pages);"; mm/gup.c @ v6.12 has gup_fast_pmd_leaf/gup_fast_pud_leaf in the fast walkers and gup_fast_folio_allowed notes "hugetlb neither requires dirty-tracking nor can be secretmem", so hugetlb-backed user mappings are pinnable by this path.

7) Documentation/block/ublk.rst @ v6.12 does not describe USER_COPY at all (it documents UBLK_F_UNPRIVILEGED_DEV and GET_DEV_INFO2 only), so the header comments and driver code are the authoritative description.

8) Debian: tracker.debian.org lists linux 6.12.94-1 in stable (trixie) and 6.12.111-1 in stable-security; sources.debian.org debian/config/config for 6.12.94-1 contains, under "## file: drivers/block/Kconfig", "CONFIG_BLK_DEV_UBLK=m". The ublk-char class ("static const struct class ublk_chr_class = { .name = \"ublk-char\", };") sets no .devnode mode override.
- Corrected claim: Linux 6.12 ublk_drv (shipped by Debian trixie as ublk_drv.ko, CONFIG_BLK_DEV_UBLK=m) supports UBLK_F_USER_COPY (1UL << 7), advertised by UBLK_U_CMD_GET_FEATURES. With it, FETCH_REQ/COMMIT_AND_FETCH_REQ carry no buffer address (addr must be 0, except zone append) and the server moves request data itself through /dev/ublkcN: pread() for a WRITE request (request pages -> user buffer) and pwrite() for a READ request (user buffer -> request pages), performed before COMMIT_AND_FETCH, at position UBLKSRV_IO_BUF_OFFSET (0x80000000) + (q_id << 41) + (tag << 25) + byte_offset_in_request, i.e. (q_id << UBLK_QID_OFF) | (tag << UBLK_TAG_OFF) | offset with UBLK_IO_BUF_BITS=25 (max 32 MiB per request), UBLK_TAG_BITS=16 and UBLK_QID_BITS=12. The same transfers may be issued as io_uring IORING_OP_READ/WRITE (or READV/WRITEV) with sqe->off set to that position, but only with plain user-memory buffers: the driver requires a user-backed iov_iter, so IORING_OP_READ_FIXED/WRITE_FIXED with registered buffers fail with -EACCES. UBLK_F_USER_COPY cannot be combined with UBLK_F_UNPRIVILEGED_DEV (UBLK_CMD_ADD_DEV returns -EINVAL; commit 42aafd8b48ad, CVE-2024-50080, included in 6.12), and a non-unprivileged device can only be created and controlled (ADD_DEV, SET_PARAMS, START/STOP/DEL_DEV, recovery) by a process holding CAP_SYS_ADMIN; therefore the dbladed control process must have CAP_SYS_ADMIN (root or an equivalent file/ambient capability), while the /dev/ublkcN I/O path itself (open, FETCH/COMMIT uring commands, pread/pwrite, mmap) carries no capability check beyond device-node permissions.
- Design impact: No change to the decision: dbladed (or at least the process that issues /dev/ublk-control commands) must run with CAP_SYS_ADMIN, and UBLK_F_UNPRIVILEGED_DEV is off the table while USER_COPY is used; the design text should say "CAP_SYS_ADMIN" rather than "root" and may drop every other capability. Copying directly into a hugetlbfs arena slot is feasible: pread(ublkc_fd, slot_ptr, len, ublk_pos(q, tag, 0)) or IORING_OP_READ with sqe->addr = slot pointer, since the kernel pins the destination with get_user_pages_fast (32 pages per iteration; hugetlb PMD/PUD leaves handled) and copies request pages into it. Two constraints must be written into the design: (1) do not register the arena as an io_uring fixed buffer for these transfers, because READ_FIXED/WRITE_FIXED yield an ITER_BVEC iterator and ublk returns -EACCES; use IORING_OP_READ/WRITE with plain pointers (fixed buffers may still be used toward the backend, e.g. NVMe/io_uring file I/O, just not toward /dev/ublkcN); (2) leave addr = 0 in FETCH_REQ/COMMIT_AND_FETCH_REQ and keep per-request offsets below 32 MiB (25-bit field), queue ids below 4096 and tags below 65536. The transfer direction is fixed by the request type (pread for WRITE, pwrite for READ) and must complete before COMMIT_AND_FETCH; afterwards the position is invalid. If the design ever splits a CAP_SYS_ADMIN control process from unprivileged queue threads, that is permitted on the I/O path, but the kernel then sets GD_SUPPRESS_PART_SCAN on /dev/ublkbN (no partition probing) because nr_privileged_daemon != nr_queues_ready. Device nodes /dev/ublk-control and /dev/ublkcN get default devtmpfs/udev ownership (the ublk-char class sets no mode), so a udev rule is only needed if a non-root I/O thread must open /dev/ublkcN. Runtime probing: check UBLK_F_USER_COPY in the GET_FEATURES mask before enabling it.
- Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/include/uapi/linux/ublk_cmd.h ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/block/ublk_drv.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/Documentation/block/ublk.rst ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/include/linux/uio.h ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/io_uring/rw.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/io_uring/rsrc.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/lib/iov_iter.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/mm/gup.c ; https://github.com/torvalds/linux/commit/1172d5b8beca6b899deb9f7f2850e7e47ec16198 ; https://github.com/torvalds/linux/commit/42aafd8b48adac1c3b20fe5892b1b91b80c1a1e6 ; https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2024-50080 ; https://tracker.debian.org/pkg/linux ; https://sources.debian.org/data/main/l/linux/6.12.94-1/debian/config/config ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ublk-org/ublksrv/master/include/ublksrv.h ; https://lkml.iu.edu/hypermail/linux/kernel/2512.1/06675.html

### [C05] PARTIALLY-CORRECT
- Claim: In Linux 6.12 drivers/scsi/sd.c sets BLK_FEAT_WRITE_CACHE only when the caching mode page reports WCE=1 and BLK_FEAT_FUA only when DPOFUA is also set; when the mode-page query fails sd logs 'Assuming drive cache: write through'; writing /sys/block/<disk>/queue/write_cache changes only the kernel's view, and when the queue has no write cache blk_insert_flush (block/blk-flush.c) strips REQ_PREFLUSH/REQ_FUA and completes empty flushes without issuing any command to the device.
- Raised by: Opus-Storage, Opus-Fabrics, Opus-Consensus
- Why it matters: On a device reporting WCE=0 the kernel issues neither flushes nor FUA, so the CP commit ordering (data stripes, flush, FUA superblock) and the receiver's 'flush segments; commit' are enforced only by the controller's cache protection, which drives the installer's attestation requirement.
- Summary: The substance is confirmed from the Linux v6.12 sources (Debian trixie ships linux-image-amd64 6.12.111-1): sd derives BLK_FEAT_WRITE_CACHE from the Caching mode page WCE bit and BLK_FEAT_FUA from WCE plus the DPOFUA header bit (sd_set_flush_flag), the fallback path logs "Assuming drive cache: write through" and zeroes WCE/RCD/DPOFUA, /sys/block/<disk>/queue/write_cache only toggles the in-kernel BLK_FLAG_WRITE_CACHE_DISABLED flag, and when the queue has no (enabled) write cache the block layer strips REQ_PREFLUSH/REQ_FUA and completes empty flushes without reaching the driver. Corrections: the stripping happens first at bio level in submit_bio_noacct() (block/blk-core.c), with blk_insert_flush() as the request-level backstop; the write-through message and WCE=0 fallback apply only when the host driver has not set sdev->wce_default_on (usb-storage quirks set it, producing "Assuming drive cache: write back" and WCE=1); FUA additionally requires !broken_fua and READ/WRITE(10/16); WCE is forced 0 on write-protected disks; and the sd cache_type attribute ("temporary write back") can override WCE in-kernel without touching the device.
- Evidence: All quotes are from the v6.12 tag. git.kernel.org returned HTTP 403 to the fetcher and elixir.bootlin.com pages were truncated to their navigation header, so the tagged tree was read from the raw.githubusercontent.com mirror of torvalds/linux at tag v6.12 (identical content); Debian trixie's kernel was confirmed as "6.12.111-1" depending on "linux-image-6.12.111+deb13-amd64".

1. drivers/scsi/sd.c, sd_read_cache_type(): early exit "if (sdkp->cache_override) return;". Page selection: TYPE_RBC uses "modepage = 6; dbd = 8;", otherwise "modepage = 8; dbd = 0;". Parsing: page 8 -> "sdkp->WCE = ((buffer[offset + 2] & 0x04) != 0);" and "sdkp->RCD = ((buffer[offset + 2] & 0x01) != 0);"; page 6 (RBC) -> "sdkp->WCE = ((buffer[offset + 2] & 0x01) == 0); sdkp->RCD = 0;". Header bit: "sdkp->DPOFUA = (data.device_specific & 0x10) != 0;" followed by "if (sdp->broken_fua) { sd_first_printk(KERN_NOTICE, sdkp, "Disabling FUA\n"); sdkp->DPOFUA = 0; } else if (sdkp->DPOFUA && !sdkp->device->use_10_for_rw && !sdkp->device->use_16_for_rw) { ... "Uses READ/WRITE(6), disabling FUA\n"); sdkp->DPOFUA = 0; }" and "/* No cache flush allowed for write protected devices */ if (sdkp->WCE && sdkp->write_prot) sdkp->WCE = 0;". Summary log: "Write cache: %s, read cache: %s, %s\n" with "enabled"/"disabled" and "supports DPO and FUA" / "doesn't support DPO or FUA". Failure paths: "bad_sense:" logs "Cache data unavailable\n" (ILLEGAL_REQUEST, asc 0x24) or "Asking for cache data failed\n" and falls through to "defaults:"; defaults is also reached for "No Caching mode page found\n", "Incomplete mode parameter data\n", and skip_ms_page_8 with TYPE_RBC or skip_ms_page_3f. defaults: "if (sdp->wce_default_on) { sd_first_printk(KERN_NOTICE, sdkp, "Assuming drive cache: write back\n"); sdkp->WCE = 1; } else { sd_first_printk(KERN_WARNING, sdkp, "Assuming drive cache: write through\n"); sdkp->WCE = 0; } sdkp->RCD = 0; sdkp->DPOFUA = 0;".

2. sd.c, sd_set_flush_flag() verbatim: "if (sdkp->WCE) { lim->features |= BLK_FEAT_WRITE_CACHE; if (sdkp->DPOFUA) lim->features |= BLK_FEAT_FUA; else lim->features &= ~BLK_FEAT_FUA; } else { lim->features &= ~(BLK_FEAT_WRITE_CACHE | BLK_FEAT_FUA); }". sd_revalidate_disk() calls "sd_read_cache_type(sdkp, buffer);" then "sd_set_flush_flag(sdkp, &lim);" then "blk_mq_freeze_queue(sdkp->disk->queue); err = queue_limits_commit_update(sdkp->disk->queue, &lim); blk_mq_unfreeze_queue(...)". sd_probe() initialises "sdkp->WCE = 0;". sd_shutdown()/sd_suspend_common() issue SYNCHRONIZE CACHE only "if (sdkp->WCE && sdkp->media_present)".

3. sd.c, cache_type_store() (/sys/class/scsi_disk/<hctl>/cache_type): input prefixed "temporary " sets "sdkp->cache_override = 1;", "sdkp->WCE = wce; sdkp->RCD = rcd;" (wce = "(ct & 0x02) && !sdkp->write_prot ? 1 : 0") and commits limits via sd_set_flush_flag + "queue_limits_commit_update(sdkp->disk->queue, &lim)"; without the prefix it calls "scsi_mode_select(sdp, 1, sp, buffer_data, len, SD_TIMEOUT, ...)" (a MODE SELECT to the device) and then "sd_revalidate_disk(sdkp->disk);".

4. include/scsi/scsi_device.h: "unsigned wce_default_on:1; /* Cache is ON by default */", "unsigned broken_fua:1; /* Don't set FUA bit */". drivers/usb/storage/scsiglue.c device_configure(): "if (us->fflags & US_FL_WRITE_CACHE) sdev->wce_default_on = 1;" and for US_FL_ALWAYS_SYNC "sdev->skip_ms_page_8 = 1; sdev->skip_ms_page_3f = 1; /* assume sync is needed */ sdev->wce_default_on = 1;". (Only setter verified; no exhaustive search was possible.)

5. block/blk-settings.c, blk_validate_limits(): "if (!(lim->features & BLK_FEAT_WRITE_CACHE)) lim->features &= ~BLK_FEAT_FUA;". blk_stack_limits(): "t->features |= (b->features & BLK_FEAT_INHERIT_MASK);" and include/linux/blkdev.h "BLK_FEAT_INHERIT_MASK (BLK_FEAT_WRITE_CACHE | BLK_FEAT_FUA | BLK_FEAT_ROTATIONAL | ...)".

6. include/linux/blkdev.h: "/* supports a volatile write cache */ #define BLK_FEAT_WRITE_CACHE ((__force blk_features_t)(1u << 0))"; "/* supports passing on the FUA bit */ #define BLK_FEAT_FUA ((__force blk_features_t)(1u << 1))"; "/* do not send FLUSH/FUA commands despite advertising a write cache */ #define BLK_FLAG_WRITE_CACHE_DISABLED ((__force blk_flags_t)(1u << 0))"; "static inline bool blk_queue_write_cache(struct request_queue *q) { return (q->limits.features & BLK_FEAT_WRITE_CACHE) && !(q->limits.flags & BLK_FLAG_WRITE_CACHE_DISABLED); }"; "bdev_write_cache(bdev) { return blk_queue_write_cache(bdev_get_queue(bdev)); }"; "bdev_fua(bdev) { return bdev_get_queue(bdev)->limits.features & BLK_FEAT_FUA; }".

7. block/blk-sysfs.c, queue_wc_store(): accepts "write back" (disable = false) or "write through"/"none" (disable = true), else -EINVAL; then "lim = queue_limits_start_update(disk->queue); if (disable) lim.flags |= BLK_FLAG_WRITE_CACHE_DISABLED; else lim.flags &= ~BLK_FLAG_WRITE_CACHE_DISABLED; err = queue_limits_commit_update(disk->queue, &lim);". It never touches BLK_FEAT_WRITE_CACHE and issues no command to the device. queue_wc_show() prints "write back" iff blk_queue_write_cache(). "QUEUE_RW_ENTRY(queue_wc, "write_cache"); QUEUE_RO_ENTRY(queue_fua, "fua");" with fua = "!!(disk->queue->limits.features & BLK_FEAT_FUA)". Documentation/ABI/stable/sysfs-block, /sys/block/<disk>/queue/write_cache: "Writing to this file can change the kernels view of the device, but it doesn't alter the device state. This means that it might not be safe to toggle the setting from "write back" to "write through", since that will also eliminate cache flushes issued by the kernel." /queue/fua: "[RO] Whether or not the block driver supports the FUA flag for write requests."

8. block/blk-core.c, submit_bio_noacct(): "Filter flush bio's early so that bio based drivers without flush support don't have to worry about them." -> "if (op_is_flush(bio->bi_opf)) { ... if (!bdev_write_cache(bdev)) { bio->bi_opf &= ~(REQ_PREFLUSH | REQ_FUA); if (!bio_sectors(bio)) { status = BLK_STS_OK; goto end_io; } } }"; end_io: "bio->bi_status = status; bio_endio(bio);". include/linux/blk_types.h: "static inline bool op_is_flush(blk_opf_t op) { return op & (REQ_FUA | REQ_PREFLUSH); }". block/blk-flush.c, blkdev_issue_flush(): "bio_init(&bio, bdev, NULL, 0, REQ_OP_WRITE | REQ_PREFLUSH); return submit_bio_wait(&bio);" (an empty flush bio, so it is subject to the same filter).

9. block/blk-flush.c header comment: "If the device doesn't have writeback cache, PREFLUSH and FUA don't make any difference. The requests are either completed immediately if there's no data or executed as normal requests otherwise." blk_insert_flush(): "bool supports_fua = q->limits.features & BLK_FEAT_FUA;" ... "if (blk_queue_write_cache(q)) { if (rq->cmd_flags & REQ_PREFLUSH) policy |= REQ_FSEQ_PREFLUSH; if ((rq->cmd_flags & REQ_FUA) && !supports_fua) policy |= REQ_FSEQ_POSTFLUSH; }" ... "rq->cmd_flags &= ~REQ_PREFLUSH; if (!supports_fua) rq->cmd_flags &= ~REQ_FUA;" ... "case 0: /* An empty flush handed down from a stacking driver may translate into nothing if the underlying device does not advertise a write-back cache. In this case, simply complete the request. */ blk_mq_end_request(rq, 0); return true;" ... "case REQ_FSEQ_DATA: ... return false;" (processed as a normal write). Call site in block/blk-mq.c blk_mq_submit_bio(): "if (op_is_flush(bio->bi_opf) && blk_insert_flush(rq)) return;".

10. Documentation/block/writeback_cache_control.rst: "For devices that do not support volatile write caches there is no driver support required, the block layer completes empty REQ_PREFLUSH requests before entering the driver and strips off the REQ_PREFLUSH and REQ_FUA bits from requests that have a payload." Blk-mq: "When the BLK_FEAT_WRITE_CACHE flag is set, REQ_OP_WRITE | REQ_PREFLUSH requests with a payload are automatically turned into a sequence of a REQ_OP_FLUSH request followed by the actual write by the block layer."; without BLK_FEAT_FUA "a REQ_OP_FLUSH request is sent by the block layer after the completion of the write request for bio submissions with the REQ_FUA bit set."
- Corrected claim: In Linux 6.12 (Debian 13 trixie: linux-image-amd64 6.12.111-1), drivers/scsi/sd.c sd_read_cache_type() takes sdkp->WCE from the Caching mode page (page 8, byte 2 bit 2; page 6 with inverted sense for RBC devices) and sdkp->DPOFUA from the DPOFUA bit of the mode-parameter header; DPOFUA is then cleared for devices quirked broken_fua or limited to READ/WRITE(6), and WCE is cleared for write-protected devices. If MODE SENSE fails, the page is absent or truncated, or the device is quirked to skip it, sd falls back to defaults: it logs "Assuming drive cache: write through" (KERN_WARNING) and sets WCE=0, RCD=0, DPOFUA=0, unless the host driver set sdev->wce_default_on (usb-storage quirks do), in which case it logs "Assuming drive cache: write back" and sets WCE=1 (DPOFUA still 0). sd_revalidate_disk() then applies sd_set_flush_flag(): BLK_FEAT_WRITE_CACHE is set iff WCE, BLK_FEAT_FUA iff WCE and DPOFUA, and blk_validate_limits() clears BLK_FEAT_FUA whenever BLK_FEAT_WRITE_CACHE is absent. The SCSI-disk attribute /sys/class/scsi_disk/<hctl>/cache_type can override this: with the "temporary " prefix it changes WCE/RCD only in the kernel; without it, it sends MODE SELECT to the device and re-validates. Writing /sys/block/<disk>/queue/write_cache only sets or clears BLK_FLAG_WRITE_CACHE_DISABLED on the queue limits; it issues no command and, per the sysfs-block ABI, "doesn't alter the device state". Whenever bdev_write_cache() is false (no BLK_FEAT_WRITE_CACHE, or the sysfs disable flag set), submit_bio_noacct() in block/blk-core.c strips REQ_PREFLUSH|REQ_FUA from every bio and completes empty flush bios (including blkdev_issue_flush()) with BLK_STS_OK before any request exists; at request level blk_insert_flush() in block/blk-flush.c always removes REQ_PREFLUSH from the request, removes REQ_FUA unless BLK_FEAT_FUA is set, schedules pre/post flush commands only when blk_queue_write_cache(q), and ends a request with neither data nor flush work via blk_mq_end_request(rq, 0) without dispatching it to the driver. Consequently, for a disk that reports WCE=0 the kernel issues no SYNCHRONIZE CACHE (not even at shutdown/suspend, which are gated on sdkp->WCE) and no FUA writes; durability and ordering of the CP commit sequence and the receiver's "flush segments; commit" then rest entirely on the device or controller's own cache protection.
- Design impact: The design's conclusion and the installer attestation requirement stand; the text needs these precision edits. (1) Attribute the stripping to submit_bio_noacct() (block/blk-core.c, bio level, which also ends empty flush bios such as blkdev_issue_flush()) with blk_insert_flush() (block/blk-flush.c) as the request-level backstop, and quote the blk-flush.c header: "If the device doesn't have writeback cache, PREFLUSH and FUA don't make any difference." (2) Replace "only when the caching mode page reports WCE=1" with the sd_set_flush_flag rule (WRITE_CACHE iff WCE; FUA iff WCE and DPOFUA) and list the inputs to WCE/DPOFUA: mode page, the wce_default_on fallback, the broken_fua and READ/WRITE(6) FUA disables, the write-protect guard, and the scsi_disk cache_type override. (3) State that the "Assuming drive cache: write through" message is conditional on wce_default_on being clear. (4) The installer's attestation and diagnostics should capture, per physical sd device: the sd log line "Write cache: ..., read cache: ..., supports DPO and FUA / doesn't support DPO or FUA" or the "Assuming drive cache" fallback line; /sys/block/<disk>/queue/write_cache ("write back"/"write through") and /sys/block/<disk>/queue/fua (0/1); and /sys/class/scsi_disk/<hctl>/cache_type. Treat queue/write_cache strictly as a read-only diagnostic: writing "write through" to it on a WCE=1 disk silently eliminates kernel flushes without changing the device, so the installer and runtime must never do that, and the attestation should flag BLK_FLAG_WRITE_CACHE_DISABLED (write_cache reads "write through" while the sd log says "Write cache: enabled") as a misconfiguration. (5) If defense-in-depth flushes on a WCE=0 device are wanted, the only in-kernel knob that does not touch the device is "temporary write back" written to the scsi_disk cache_type attribute (WCE=1 in kernel; FUA still requires DPOFUA as read); whether the device does anything useful with SYNCHRONIZE CACHE remains a controller property, so this does not replace attestation. (6) Because BLK_FEAT_WRITE_CACHE and BLK_FEAT_FUA are in BLK_FEAT_INHERIT_MASK, dm/md/LVM devices stacked on WCE=0 disks also report no write cache and the same stripping happens at the top of the stack; the attestation must therefore be evaluated on the underlying physical sd devices, and any CP/receiver durability argument must not assume a stacked device adds flushes. (7) Scope caveat: this verification covers SCSI disks handled by sd (SAS, SATA via libata, FC, RAID-controller LUNs); NVMe namespaces are driven by the nvme driver, not sd.c, and their write-cache/FUA feature derivation was not verified here, so the design should cite a separate check for NVMe data devices.
- Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/scsi/sd.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/block/blk-flush.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/block/blk-core.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/block/blk-sysfs.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/block/blk-settings.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/block/blk-mq.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/include/linux/blkdev.h ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/include/linux/blk_types.h ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/include/scsi/scsi_device.h ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/usb/storage/scsiglue.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/Documentation/block/writeback_cache_control.rst ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/Documentation/ABI/stable/sysfs-block ; https://packages.debian.org/trixie/linux-image-amd64 ; https://elixir.bootlin.com/linux/v6.12/source/drivers/scsi/sd.c (fetched; returned only the navigation header) ; https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/stable/linux.git/plain/drivers/scsi/sd.c?h=v6.12 (fetched; HTTP 403)

### [C06] PARTIALLY-CORRECT
- Claim: MegaRAID (LSI/Avago/Broadcom) and Dell PERC virtual drives report WCE=0 in the SCSI caching mode page regardless of the VD write policy (write-back or write-through), or on some firmware return no caching mode page at all, so Linux shows /sys/block/<vd>/queue/write_cache as 'write through' and dmesg prints 'Write cache: disabled' or 'Assuming drive cache: write through'; they report discard_max_bytes = 0; and the separate PERC 'Disk Cache Policy' (member drives' own volatile cache) defaults to Enabled for SATA members and Disabled for SAS members.
- Raised by: Opus-Storage, Opus-Fabrics, Opus-Protocols, Opus-Consensus
- Why it matters: Underpins the hardware-RAID attestation rule, the Discard::Never default, and the exemption of md backstores from attestation; if firmware reports WCE=1 the flusher would receive real flush/FUA semantics, and if SATA member caches default to enabled, md on single-drive RAID0 VDs silently loses the flush chain.
- Summary: The core of the claim is confirmed by Dell's own PERC 9, 10 and 11 User's Guides ("All RAID volumes are presented as write-through to the operating system (Windows and Linux) independent of the actual write cache policy of the virtual disk") and by their troubleshooting entry documenting that the firmware does not answer the Linux caching-page request ("sdb: asking for cache data failed" / "assuming drive cache: write through"); the Linux 6.12 sd.c/blk-sysfs.c source confirms the resulting 'Write cache: disabled' / 'Assuming drive cache: write through' messages, write_cache = 'write through' and loss of flush/FUA. Two parts need correction: discard_max_bytes = 0 is not universal, because Broadcom MegaRAID 7.7+ firmware (9460/9560-class silicon, the PERC 10/11 generation) can report VDs built from SAS SSDs as UNMAP-capable, which makes Linux expose a non-zero discard_max_bytes; and the SATA-Enabled/SAS-Disabled Disk Cache Policy default is a Dell PERC policy, whereas retail Broadcom MegaRAID defaults to "Unchanged/default" (the drive's own factory setting). No Broadcom primary statement about write-through presentation on non-Dell cards was found, so that part rests on Dell docs plus the shared firmware lineage and field reports.
- Evidence: 1. Linux v6.12 kernel source (torvalds/linux tag v6.12, raw files). drivers/scsi/sd.c sd_read_cache_type(): summary line "Write cache: %s, read cache: %s, %s" with sdkp->WCE ? "enabled" : "disabled"; on MODE SENSE failure: "Cache data unavailable" (ILLEGAL REQUEST 24h/00h) else "Asking for cache data failed"; then at the defaults label: `if (sdp->wce_default_on) { "Assuming drive cache: write back"; sdkp->WCE = 1; } else { "Assuming drive cache: write through"; sdkp->WCE = 0; } sdkp->RCD = 0; sdkp->DPOFUA = 0;` (other messages: "No Caching mode page found", "Missing header in MODE_SENSE response"). The function returns early when sdkp->cache_override is set. sd_set_flush_flag(): `if (sdkp->WCE) { lim->features |= BLK_FEAT_WRITE_CACHE; if (sdkp->DPOFUA) lim->features |= BLK_FEAT_FUA; else lim->features &= ~BLK_FEAT_FUA; } else { lim->features &= ~(BLK_FEAT_WRITE_CACHE | BLK_FEAT_FUA); }` -> with WCE=0 the device never receives flush or FUA. block/blk-sysfs.c queue_wc_show(): prints "write back" iff blk_queue_write_cache(), otherwise "write through"; discard_max_bytes prints limits.max_discard_sectors << SECTOR_SHIFT. read_capacity_16(): `if (buffer[14] & 0x80) { /* LBPME */ sdkp->lbpme = 1; ...}`; sd_discard_mode(): `if (!sdkp->lbpme) return SD_LBP_FULL;`; sd_config_discard(): SD_LBP_FULL/SD_LBP_DISABLE leave max_blocks = 0 so `lim->max_hw_discard_sectors = max_blocks * ...` = 0 -> discard_max_bytes = 0 exactly when the VD does not set LBPME in READ CAPACITY(16). Documentation/scsi/sd-parameters (docs.kernel.org): cache_type "write through" = WCE 0/RCD 0; `echo "temporary write back" > cache_type` overrides the kernel's view without persisting to the device.

2. megaraid_sas driver v6.12: no MODE SENSE / caching-page / WCE handling in the driver (non-read/write LD commands are passed to firmware as MFI_CMD_LD_SCSI_IO). megasas_queue_command(): `if ((scmd->cmnd[0] == SYNCHRONIZE_CACHE) && MEGASAS_IS_LOGICAL(scmd->device) && (!instance->fw_sync_cache_support)) { scmd->result = DID_OK << 16; goto out_done; }` i.e. SYNCHRONIZE CACHE to a VD is completed in the driver, never reaching the controller, when firmware does not advertise sync-cache support. megaraid_sas_fusion.c megasas_ioc_init_fusion(): `instance->fw_sync_cache_support = (scratch_pad_1 & MR_CAN_HANDLE_SYNC_CACHE_OFFSET) ? 1 : 0;` and dev_info "FW supports sync cache\t: %s" (Yes/No). megasas_set_dynamic_target_properties(): `if (!raid->flags.isEPD) sdev->no_write_same = 1;` for logical drives.

3. Dell primary docs, write-through presentation. PERC 9 User's Guide (H330/H730/H830), PERC 10 User's Guide (H345/H740P/H745/H840) and PERC 11 User's Guide (H755/H750/H355/H350), section "Virtual disk write cache polic(y|ies)": "All RAID volumes are presented as write-through to the operating system (Windows and Linux) independent of the actual write cache policy of the virtual disk." "PERC cards manage the data in cache independently of the operating system or any applications." "The default cache setting for virtual disks is Write-back caching." PERC 11 adds: "Write-back caching is also supported for single drive RAID 0 virtual disks." The same sentence appears in the PERC H700/H800 Technical Guide as quoted in a 2011 Dell community post ("All RAID volumes will be presented as Write-Through (WT) to the operating system (Windows and Linux) independent of the actual write cache policy of the virtual disk"). Search-engine snippets indicate the note also appears in the PERC 12/13 (H965/H975) guide, but that page returned 404 and was not read.

4. Dell primary docs, no caching page returned. PERC 9, PERC 10 and PERC 11 User's Guides, troubleshooting entry "Virtual disk policy is assumed as write-through (error message)": Error: "<Date:Time> <HostName> kernel: sdb: asking for cache data failed" / "kernel: sdb: assuming drive cache: write through". Corrective action: "The error message is displayed when the Linux Small Computer System Interface (SCSI) mid-layer asks for physical disk cache settings. The controller firmware manages the virtual disk cache settings on a per controller and a per virtual disk basis, so the firmware does not respond to this command. The Linux SCSI mid-layer assumes that the virtual disk's cache policy is Write-Through." "Except for this message, there is no effect of this behavior on normal operation. The cache policy of the virtual disk and the I/O throughput are not affected by this message. The cache policy settings for the PERC SAS RAID system remain unchanged."

5. Field corroboration. oVirt users list, 24 Oct 2018 (Dell PERC): `cat /sys/block/sdb/device/scsi_disk/0:2:1:0/cache_type` -> "write through" while perccli shows "Current Cache Policy: WriteBack, ReadAdaptive, Cached, Write Cache OK"; poster: these controllers "always report cache policy as writethrough to the OS, no matter if write back is effectively enabled or not". LKML 2005-10-13 (Vendor: MegaRAID Model: LD 0 RAID1, megaraid 2.20.4.5): "sda: asking for cache data failed" / "sda: assuming drive cache: write through". LKML 2008-02-22 (LSI MegaRAID SATA 150-4, "configured for Write Back Caching"): "sd 0:1:0:0: [sda] Asking for cache data failed" / "Assuming drive cache: write through". linux.org.ru 2012 (PERC 6, "Dell VIRTUAL DISK 1028"): "[sda] Got wrong page" / "[sda] Assuming drive cache: write through". kldp.org 2010 (MegaRAID LD 0 RAID0 at sd 0:2:0:0): same pair of messages. Note: older kernels print lowercase "asking"; 6.12 prints "Asking for cache data failed" and, for a wrong page code, "No Caching mode page found" (not "Got wrong page").

6. Disk Cache Policy defaults. PERC 9 User's Guide, "Setting up virtual disks": "The default hard drive cache policy for a virtual disk with SAS hard drives is disabled, and the cache policy for a virtual disk with SATA hard drives is enabled. The Virtual Disk parameter cannot be changed in the BIOS Configuration Utility Ctrl R. Use Dell OpenManage Storage Management for the hard drive cache setting operation." OMSA Storage Management 9.4 User's Guide, "Disk Cache Policy": "The default setting for Disk Cache Policy for virtual disks based on SATA drives is Enabled; and for virtual disks based on SAS drives is Disabled."; options Enabled / Disabled / Unchanged, with "Unchanged" "applicable only for PERC 9 and later" with latest firmware. Retail Broadcom MegaRAID is different: 12Gb/s MegaRAID Tri-Mode SW UG "Virtual Drive Policies": Drive Cache values "Unchanged, Enable, and Disable" (no stated default); StorCLI "Add Virtual Drives Commands": "[pdcache=on|off|*default]" where the asterisk marks the default, and "[wt|*wb|awb]" with "Write back is the default." So Dell's SATA-Enabled/SAS-Disabled split is a PERC firmware policy; Broadcom's default leaves the drive's own (factory) WCE setting in place.

7. Discard. Dell KB 000179248 "Is TRIM supported on PERC9 controller in RAID mode" (last modified 17 Dec 2024): "There have been reports that TRIM is only supported in HBA mode and not in RAID mode." "As of January 2017, support for the TRIM command is not implemented in most hardware-based RAID technologies." "the TRIM feature is supported only on the pass-through SSDs." Dell 16G Troubleshooting Guide: "The TRIM or UNMAP command must be supported by the operating system, the drive, and the controller in order to work." (and says currently shipped Dell enterprise SSDs do not yet support them). BUT Broadcom 12Gb/s MegaRAID Tri-Mode SW UG, "Online Firmware Upgrade and Downgrade": "The UNMAP implementation was modified in MegaRAID 7.7 firmware to ensure all SSDs in the VD support UNMAP." "After the reboot, the VD will not be reported as supporting UNMAP." "UNMAP is supported on SAS SSDs only." Broadcom StorCLI2 sample `show all` output, "Supported VD operations": "Support Unmap for single drive RAID 0 VDs = Yes", "Support Unmap for RAID 0 VDs = Yes", "Support Unmap for RAID 1/10 VDs = Yes", "Support Unmap for RAID 5/50/6/60 VDs = Yes", plus "Support Writesame Unmap ... = Yes", "Support Changing Disk Cache Policy = Yes", "Support SSD Ld Disk Cache Change = Yes". Lenovo Press LP0652 (ThinkSystem RAID 930 = "Broadcom MegaRAID 9460 adapter family", SAS3508) and LP1282 (RAID 940 = MegaRAID 9560, SAS3908/SAS3916): "Supports UNMAP command for SAS SSDs (JBOD and RAID volumes)"; "Supports TRIM command for SATA SSDs (JBOD)". A VD "reported as supporting UNMAP" sets LBPME, so Linux computes a non-zero discard_max_bytes and will issue UNMAP. Not verified: whether Dell's PERC 10/11 firmware builds enable this (Dell docs are silent); the Red Hat sysadmin article reporting all-zero `lsblk -dD` DISC values on a PERC H730P VD was only seen as a search summary (page 404).

8. Not found / unverifiable: a Broadcom primary statement that retail MegaRAID VDs are presented as write-through (only Dell documents it; the driver passes MODE SENSE to firmware, and field reports on LSI cards match); the DPOFUA bit state on PERC VDs; Dell KB 000136726 (cache policies in TTY log) returned 404 on every locale, though its search snippet repeats the SATA-enabled/SAS-disabled default.
- Corrected claim: Dell PERC virtual disks (documented by Dell for PERC H700/H800 and for PERC 9, 10 and 11: H330/H730/H830, H345/H740P/H745/H840, H755/H750/H355/H350) are presented to the operating system as write-through independent of the VD's actual write-back/write-through policy: the firmware either returns the caching mode page with WCE=0 or does not answer the MODE SENSE for it at all. Linux 6.12 therefore sets WCE=0, logs either "Write cache: disabled, read cache: enabled, ..." or "Asking for cache data failed" (or "No Caching mode page found") followed by "Assuming drive cache: write through", clears BLK_FEAT_WRITE_CACHE and BLK_FEAT_FUA, and /sys/block/<vd>/queue/write_cache reads "write through", so no flush or FUA ever reaches the controller; in addition megaraid_sas completes SYNCHRONIZE CACHE to VDs inside the driver when the firmware does not advertise sync-cache support ("FW supports sync cache: No"). Retail Broadcom/LSI/Avago MegaRAID cards share the firmware lineage and field reports match, but no Broadcom primary statement was found, so they are probe-and-verify, not assumed. discard_max_bytes is 0 only when the VD does not set LBPME in READ CAPACITY(16), which holds for HDD-backed VDs, SATA-SSD VDs, and PERC 9-era or older firmware; MegaRAID 7.7+/7.8+ firmware (SAS3508/SAS3516 9460-class and SAS3908/SAS3916 9560-class, the PERC 10/11 silicon) can report VDs built entirely from SAS SSDs as UNMAP-capable, in which case Linux exposes a non-zero discard_max_bytes and will issue UNMAP. The member-drive "Disk Cache Policy" default of Enabled for SATA and Disabled for SAS is a Dell PERC policy (PERC 9 User's Guide, OpenManage Storage Management); retail Broadcom MegaRAID defaults to "Unchanged/default", i.e. the drive's own factory WCE setting (typically on for SATA), and PERC 9+ also offers "Unchanged".
- Design impact: (1) The hardware-RAID attestation rule stands and is strengthened: with WCE=0 the kernel never emits flush/FUA to a PERC/MegaRAID VD, so durability depends entirely on the controller's protected write-back cache. Attestation must be out-of-band via perccli/storcli (`/cX/vY show all`): VD write policy and current state ("WriteBack ... Write Cache OK" vs forced WT during BBU learn/failed battery/reconstruction), BBU/CacheVault health, and the per-VD Disk Cache Policy, which must be verified as Disabled for every member type, not only SATA; on retail MegaRAID "Unchanged/default" must be resolved against the drives' actual WCE. Record dmesg "FW supports sync cache: Yes/No" in the attestation report. (2) Never use the `cache_type` sysfs override ("temporary write back") as a remediation on these VDs: it changes only the kernel's view, the firmware semantics are unchanged, and SYNCHRONIZE CACHE may be swallowed in megaraid_sas. (3) Do not use discard_max_bytes == 0 as a fingerprint for "hardware RAID VD" and do not encode discard_max_bytes == 0 as an invariant or test expectation; identify VDs by SCSI INQUIRY vendor/model (DELL PERC, AVAGO/LSI/MR9xxx) and the megaraid_sas driver binding (channel 2 LD addressing). Keep Discard::Never as the default for hardware-RAID backstores, but the code must tolerate VDs that advertise UNMAP (lbpme=1, non-zero discard_max_bytes) and treat discard enablement as an explicit opt-in. (4) The md exemption needs tightening: md over single-drive RAID0 VDs (write-back is supported on those too per PERC 11) still has WCE=0 members, so md passes no flush/FUA down and the only protection is the controller's BBU-backed cache plus member disk cache Disabled; either keep md-over-hardware-RAID inside the attestation scope or document it as unsupported unless Disk Cache Policy = Disabled and cache health are verified. (5) Documentation: list both dmesg variants and the modern spellings ("Asking for cache data failed", "No Caching mode page found", "Assuming drive cache: write through"), cite the Dell PERC 9/10/11 guides as the normative source, and mark retail MegaRAID write-through presentation and PERC 12/13 behaviour as verified-by-probe rather than documented.
