### [C07] PARTIALLY-CORRECT
- Claim: The Linux 6.12 megaraid_sas driver completes SYNCHRONIZE CACHE for RAID virtual disks inside the driver (returning success without forwarding the command to controller firmware) and only forwards it for JBOD/passthrough drives.
- Raised by: Opus-Protocols
- Why it matters: If the host cannot reach drive caches behind a write-through VD, a power loss can tear both CP N and CP N-1, so the torn-CP fallback rule's premise fails and the attestation must also cover the physical disk cache policy.
- Summary: The 6.12 megaraid_sas driver short-circuits SYNCHRONIZE_CACHE for virtual disks only when the firmware did NOT advertise the canHandleSyncCache bit; on Fusion-class controllers whose firmware sets MR_CAN_HANDLE_SYNC_CACHE_OFFSET (0x01000000) in outbound scratch pad 1 at IOC init, the driver forwards VD SYNCHRONIZE_CACHE to firmware (behaviour since v4.10, commit d0fc91d67c59, Nov 2016). JBOD/passthrough commands are always forwarded (commit 1e793f6fc0db, Oct 2016). However, the commit that introduced the forwarding documents that firmware, for a VD, "does not send SYNCHRONIZE_CACHE to drives" and simply "returns SUCCESS", so in neither branch does a host flush reach the physical-disk caches behind a VD; the claim's wording is incomplete but its consequence for the design is right (and holds regardless of firmware version).
- Evidence: 1. Linux v6.12 drivers/scsi/megaraid/megaraid_sas_base.c, megasas_queue_command(): "if ((scmd->cmnd[0] == SYNCHRONIZE_CACHE) && MEGASAS_IS_LOGICAL(scmd->device) && (!instance->fw_sync_cache_support)) { scmd->result = DID_OK << 16; goto out_done; }" — followed by "return instance->instancet->build_and_issue_cmd(instance, scmd);". So the in-driver completion is conditional on fw_sync_cache_support being false; otherwise the VD SYNCHRONIZE_CACHE is built and issued like any other command. Only one SYNCHRONIZE_CACHE reference exists in the file; SYNCHRONIZE_CACHE_16 is not special-cased at all. The identical block is present in Debian trixie's linux 6.12.94-1 (tracker 'stable') and 6.12.107-1 (sources.debian.org trixie listing).
2. v6.12 megaraid_sas.h: "#define MEGASAS_IS_LOGICAL(sdev) ((sdev->channel < MEGASAS_MAX_PD_CHANNELS) ? 0 : 1)", "#define MEGASAS_MAX_PD_CHANNELS 2", "bool fw_sync_cache_support;" in struct megasas_instance, "#define MR_CAN_HANDLE_SYNC_CACHE_OFFSET 0X01000000".
3. v6.12 megaraid_sas_fusion.c, megasas_ioc_init_fusion(): "scratch_pad_1 = megasas_readl(instance, &instance->reg_set->outbound_scratch_pad_1);" ... "instance->fw_sync_cache_support = (scratch_pad_1 & MR_CAN_HANDLE_SYNC_CACHE_OFFSET) ? 1 : 0;" ... dev_info "FW supports sync cache\t: %s\n" with "Yes"/"No". This is the only place the flag is set; the MFI (non-Fusion, Gen2/Gen2.5) init path never sets it, so legacy adapters always take the in-driver completion branch. There is no module parameter touching this (the 15 module params are msix_disable, msix_vectors, allow_vf_ioctls, throttlequeuedepth, resetwaittime, smp_affinity_enable, rdpq_enable, dual_qdepth_disable, scmd_timeout, perf_mode, event_log_level, enable_sdev_max_qd, poll_queues, host_tagset_enable, max_sectors).
4. Commit d0fc91d67c59068ce6d42e41ce66a4c471e5bc74 "scsi: megaraid_sas: Send SYNCHRONIZE_CACHE for VD to firmware" (Kashyap Desai, committed Nov 8 2016 by Martin K. Petersen; in v4.10): "Older versions of MegaRaid firmware (Gen2 and Gen2.5) set the WCE bit for Virtual Disks but the firmware does not report correct completion status for a SYNCHRONIZE_CACHE command." "We use the canHandleSyncCache firmware flag in the scratch pad register at offset 0xB4." New behaviour: "IF 'JBOD' Driver sends SYNCHRONIZE_CACHE command to the firmware / Firmware sends SYNCHRONIZE_CACHE to drive / Firmware obtains status from drive and returns same status back to driver / ELSEIF 'VirtualDisk' IF firmware supports new API bit called canHandleSyncCache / Driver sends SYNCHRONIZE_CACHE command to the firmware / Firmware does not send SYNCHRONIZE_CACHE to drives / Firmware returns SUCCESS / ELSE Driver does not send SYNCHRONIZE_CACHE command to the firmware / Driver return SUCCESS for that command". No module parameter was added.
5. Commit 1e793f6fc0db920400574211c48f9157a37e3945 "scsi: megaraid_sas: Fix data integrity failure for JBOD (passthrough) devices" (Oct 2016, CC stable): "Disk drive caches are only explicitly managed by controller firmware when operating in RAID mode."; it changed the check to "if ((scmd->cmnd[0] == SYNCHRONIZE_CACHE) && MEGASAS_IS_LOGICAL(scmd)) {" so JBOD commands fall through to build_and_issue_cmd(). The original 2007 commit 02b01e010afe said: "FW does not support SYNCHRONIZE_CACHE cmd. FW flush cache on its own. So, we just return success from the megasas_queue_command."
6. v6.12 megaraid_sas_base.c megasas_flush_cache() ("Requests FW to flush all its caches"): "dcmd->opcode = cpu_to_le32(MR_DCMD_CTRL_CACHE_FLUSH);" "dcmd->mbox.b[0] = MR_FLUSH_CTRL_CACHE | MR_FLUSH_DISK_CACHE;" — called only from megasas_shutdown, megasas_suspend and megasas_detach_one (skipped if the adapter is not operational). This is the driver's only disk-cache flush and it is never issued per I/O.
7. v6.12 megaraid_sas_fusion.c megasas_build_ld_nonrw_fusion(): a forwarded non-read/write LD command (SYNCHRONIZE_CACHE included) goes as "MEGASAS_MPI2_FUNCTION_LD_IO_REQUEST" to firmware unless fast path applies ("if (!(raid->capability.fpNonRWCapable)) fp_possible = 0;"); when fp_possible it is sent as "MPI2_FUNCTION_SCSI_IO_REQUEST" to "span = physArm = 0; ... devHandle = MR_PdDevHandleGet(pd, local_map_ptr);" i.e. straight to one physical drive (span 0, arm 0), bypassing firmware RAID logic. Which LDs get fpNonRWCapable is decided by firmware's RAID map and cannot be verified from kernel source.
8. v6.12 drivers/scsi/sd.c sd_set_flush_flag(): "if (sdkp->WCE) { lim->features |= BLK_FEAT_WRITE_CACHE; ... } else { lim->features &= ~(BLK_FEAT_WRITE_CACHE | BLK_FEAT_FUA); }"; sd_read_cache_type(): "sdkp->WCE = ((buffer[offset + 2] & 0x04) != 0);". If a VD reports WCE=0, Linux never issues SYNCHRONIZE_CACHE to it and block-layer flushes are no-ops.
- Corrected claim: In Linux 6.12 (and Debian trixie's 6.12.y), megaraid_sas handles SYNCHRONIZE CACHE (10) as follows (megasas_queue_command): for a RAID virtual disk (MEGASAS_IS_LOGICAL), the driver completes the command itself with DID_OK and never sends it to the controller unless the firmware advertised canHandleSyncCache (MR_CAN_HANDLE_SYNC_CACHE_OFFSET, bit 0x01000000 of outbound scratch pad 1, read in megasas_ioc_init_fusion and logged as "FW supports sync cache : Yes/No"); if that bit is set, the VD SYNCHRONIZE CACHE is forwarded to the firmware, which per the introducing commit (d0fc91d67c59, v4.10) acknowledges it with SUCCESS without issuing SYNCHRONIZE CACHE to the member drives (or, if the firmware marks the LD fpNonRWCapable, the driver sends it fast-path to the single physical drive at span 0/arm 0). For JBOD/passthrough drives the command is always forwarded and the firmware relays it to the drive and returns the drive's status (1e793f6fc0db, v4.9, stable). The flag is only ever set on Fusion-class controllers; legacy MFI (Gen2/Gen2.5) adapters always take the in-driver completion path. There is no module parameter to change this. The only disk-cache flush the driver ever requests is DCMD MR_DCMD_CTRL_CACHE_FLUSH with MR_FLUSH_CTRL_CACHE|MR_FLUSH_DISK_CACHE, issued solely at shutdown/suspend/detach. Consequently a host-issued flush never guarantees that the volatile write caches of the physical disks behind a VD have been emptied, in either driver branch.
- Design impact: The design's premise survives and should be stated more strongly: on MegaRAID virtual disks, FLUSH/SYNCHRONIZE CACHE success from the host carries no information about physical-disk cache state in any 6.12 configuration (in-driver completion on legacy or non-advertising firmware; firmware-acknowledged-without-drive-flush on canHandleSyncCache firmware; and for a VD reporting WCE=0, sd.c sets no BLK_FEAT_WRITE_CACHE so Linux emits no flush at all). Therefore: (1) the torn-CP fallback rule must not assume CP N-1 is intact behind a VD unless the physical-disk cache policy is attested; (2) the attestation for MegaRAID VDs must record, per VD, the controller cache mode (write-back with BBU/CacheVault vs write-through) AND the member drives' disk cache policy (write cache disabled, or PLP-rated drives), taken from the controller management tool, not from dmesg; (3) the dmesg line "FW supports sync cache : Yes" must be treated as informational only and never as a durability signal; (4) because megasas_flush_cache's MR_FLUSH_DISK_CACHE runs only on orderly shutdown/suspend/detach, orderly-shutdown testing cannot validate the power-loss case; (5) if the policy cannot be attested, classify the VD as flush-opaque and apply the stronger torn-CP handling (assume both CP N and CP N-1 may be torn, e.g. keep additional checksummed CP generations or require PLP/BBU before allowing CP commit). JBOD/passthrough drives behind the same HBA are different: the flush is relayed to the drive, so the standard rule applies to them.
- Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/scsi/megaraid/megaraid_sas_base.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/scsi/megaraid/megaraid_sas_fusion.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/scsi/megaraid/megaraid_sas.h ; https://github.com/torvalds/linux/commit/d0fc91d67c59068ce6d42e41ce66a4c471e5bc74 ; https://github.com/torvalds/linux/commit/1e793f6fc0db920400574211c48f9157a37e3945 ; https://github.com/torvalds/linux/commits/v4.10/drivers/scsi/megaraid/megaraid_sas_base.c?since=2016-10-01&until=2016-12-31 ; https://android-kvm.googlesource.com/linux/+/02b01e010afeeb49328d35650d70721d2ca3fd59 ; https://sources.debian.org/data/main/l/linux/6.12.94-1/drivers/scsi/megaraid/megaraid_sas_base.c ; https://sources.debian.org/data/main/l/linux/6.12.107-1/drivers/scsi/megaraid/megaraid_sas_base.c ; https://sources.debian.org/api/src/linux/ ; https://tracker.debian.org/pkg/linux ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/scsi/sd.c

### [C08] PARTIALLY-CORRECT
- Claim: On LSI/Avago/Broadcom MegaRAID and Dell PERC controllers with a conventional BBU (e.g. iBBU08 on ServeRAID M5014/M5015, PERC H700 and earlier) the default learn cycle switches 'WriteBack with BBU' virtual drives to write-through for the duration of the learn cycle (hours, roughly every 30 to 90 days) unless the policy is 'Always Write Back'; PERC 8 (H310-H710) and later with CacheVault/transparent learn do not switch during learn but still switch to write-through when the battery is absent, degraded, failed or charging under 'No Write Cache if Bad BBU'.
- Raised by: Opus-Fabrics, Opus-Consensus, Opus-Storage
- Why it matters: A scheduled write-through window turns the sequential CP flusher drain (sized at 1.2 GB/s) into read-modify-write at 150 to 300 MB/s and can trip the 2 s throttle and ALUA Transitioning with no fault present, so the installer attestation and alerting must cover learn-cycle mode and the policy name.
- Summary: The core mechanism is confirmed by Dell, IBM, Intel (LSI OEM) and Oracle documentation: with a conventional Li-ion BBU and a non-transparent (default) learn cycle, 'Write Back with BBU' virtual drives are switched to write-through while the battery charge is below the retention threshold (most of a roughly 7-hour cycle; Oracle says 1 to 12 h) on a 30-day (LSI default Auto Learn Period) to 90-day (Dell) cadence, and 'Always Write Back' / Dell 'Force Write-Back' drives are exempt; Dell PERC 8 (H710/H710P/H810, Shared PERC 8) and later battery-equipped PERCs run a Transparent Learn Cycle every 90 days during which 'Virtual disks stay in Write Back mode', while still dropping to write-through when the battery is absent, failed, degraded or in a low-charge state. Corrections: the switch is a property of the non-transparent learn mode, not of learn cycles as such (LSI iBBU08 has transparent 12 h/24 h modes; its 48 h default is non-transparent); the H310 has no cache or battery; PERC 8+ transparent learn is a battery feature, not CacheVault; and although CacheVault modules do run learn cycles and do force write-through while 'charged, missing, or bad', no primary source read states whether a CacheVault learn cycle itself forces write-through.
- Evidence: 1. Conventional BBU, learn cycle forces write-through (confirmed). Dell PERC H700/H800 User's Guide (ManualsLib mirror, p.38 'Battery Learn Cycle'): "Virtual disks automatically switch to Write-Through mode when the battery charge is low because of a learn cycle"; the cycle runs "periodically", "cannot be disabled", and "the expected time frame for completion of a learn cycle is approximately seven hours" (about 3 h discharge + 4 h charge). Dell KB 000141687: "In PERC H700 and previous, virtual disks automatically switch to Write-Through mode when the battery charge is low ... Once the battery charge is sufficient, Write-Back mode is re-enabled"; "Learn cycle discharge cycle: Approximately three hours", "Learn cycle charge cycle: Approximately four hours". IBM 'Battery mode changes for IBBU08' (ServeRAID M5014/M5015/M5025): "mode_4 (Default): 48 hours retention with a non-transparent learn cycle"; "the controller will change the cache mode to write-through during the calibration cycle"; modes 1 and 3 (12 h / 24 h retention) have "a transparent learn cycle" where "RAID volumes do not change to write-through cache mode during the learn cycles". Intel (LSI OEM) article 000007712: when the policy is Write Back, "Cache Write Policy will be temporarily set to Write Through during a battery recharge ... and then automatically returned to write back when the battery is fully charged." Oracle Exadata/SuperCluster: "During the operation, the write cache policy changes from write-back caching to write-through caching"; alert text: "runs for approximately 1 to 12 hours"; "The disk controller cache might go into WriteThrough caching mode during the learn cycle." Oracle/Sun Exalogic 1437353.1: "the controller switches to Write Through mode ... This results in a reduction in performance". Field capture (Wikimedia T166344, MegaCli): "Default Cache Policy: WriteBack, ReadAdaptive, Direct, No Write Cache if Bad BBU" with "Current Cache Policy: WriteThrough, ..., No Write Cache if Bad BBU" while "Battery State: Learning", "Charging Status : Discharging", "Learn Cycle Active : Yes". Percona (Dell PERC/LSI, 2010): servers in "write-through mode instead of write-back mode" during auto-learn, "Queries were taking multiple seconds".
2. Cadence 30 to 90 days (confirmed). IBM MSM note example: "Auto Learn Period: 2592000 Sec" (= 30 days). Oracle: "earlier than release 11.2.1.3, the operation occurs every month"; later "every three months". Dell KB 000141687 and H710 guide: TLC "once every 90 days". Wikimedia T167809 MegaCli: "Auto Learn Period: 90 Days ... Auto-Learn Mode: Transparent".
3. 'Always Write Back' exempt (confirmed). Intel 000007712: "force a logical drive to stay in write back mode at all time by setting the Cache Write Policy to Always Write Back", but "the data in the cache memory will not be protected when the BBU is not available and functioning". Intel 000023752: options changed from "Write Back with BBU" to "Always Write Back"; "Write Back means write back, only when there is a RAID maintenance free backup unit (RMFBU) installed"; "Always Write Back means write back, regardless of the presence or absence of a RMFBU." Dell H700 and H710 guides: "When Forced Write-Back mode is selected, the virtual disk is in Write-Back mode even if the battery is not present." Dell community capture: omreport "Write Policy : Force Write Back" shows in MegaCli as "Current Cache Policy: WriteBack, ..., Write Cache OK if Bad BBU" with the battery "Degraded"; after reverting, "No Write Cache if Bad BBU". MegaCLI usage text (Thomas-Krenn / TRIUMF mirrors of the built-in help): "-LDSetProp ... WT|WB|ForcedWB ... CachedBadBBU|NoCachedBadBBU".
4. PERC 8 and later: transparent learn, still WT on bad battery (confirmed with corrections). Dell H310/H710/H710P/H810 guide (p.23): TLC "once every 90 days", "causes no impact to the system or controller performance", "Virtual disks stay in Write Back mode, if enabled, during transparent learn cycle", about seven hours; p.17: "The PERC H310 supports only Write-Through" and "Write-Back caching is used under all conditions in which the battery is present and in good condition." Dell KB 000141687: TLC "was first introduced with the PERC 8 (H310 - H710)"; "All newer generation PERC with cache protection in the form of a battery have this feature"; PERC 9/10/11 "operate the battery unit and learn cycles in automatic mode". Dell Shared PERC 8 HTML guide: "Write-through caching is used under conditions in which the battery fails or is not present"; TLC "Virtual disks stay in Write-Back mode, if enabled, during transparent learn cycle"; "approximately seven hours". Dell KB 000038067 (PERC H730P, PERC 9): "If the battery becomes degraded or fails, the controller automatically switches its write policy from Write-Back to Write-Through"; alert "Write policy on Integrated RAID Controller 1 was changed to Write Through"; "A 'Battery failed' alert during the learn cycle is normal". Dell H700 guide p.30: "Low-charge state is when the battery is not capable of maintaining data for at least 24 hours". Dell KB 000141687 also: learn can be delayed "up to 168 hours (7 days)"; a "Battery failed" message during the learn cycle "is considered normal".
5. CacheVault (partly unverified). Supermicro FAQ 23107 quotes the MegaRAID warning: "Your VDs that are configured for write-back are temporally running in write-through mode. This is caused by the battery or super capacitor being charged, missing, or bad"; Supermicro: policy "write back with BBU" changes to "write through" while charging. Supermicro FAQ 35163: "The CacheVault may be incorrectly marked as BAD ... during the initial learn cycle" (MR7.14), fix includes "storcli /cX/cv start learn". Dell Avamar KB 000041546 (CVPM02): "Learn Cycle Requested : No", "Learn Cycle Active : No", "Learn Cycle Status : Failed", log "Battery relearn will start in 4 days", "Battery relearn pending: Battery is under charge". So CacheVault modules do run periodic learn cycles, but no primary source read states whether VDs stay write-back during a CacheVault learn.
6. Not readable here: Broadcom iBBU08 brief (docs.broadcom.com/doc/12352144, 404; a search snippet of it says 48-hour modes are "forced to a write-through cache policy for the duration of the discharge/recharge process"), MegaRAID SAS Software User Guide 12353339 (>10 MB), StorCLI reference 12352476 and CacheVault briefs BC-0497EN/12353174 (compressed PDF streams), all dl.dell.com PDFs (403), Dell KB 000136726 (404), Oracle Exadata BBU-replacement pages (404). Broadcom's own wording for StorCLI wrcache=WT|WB|AWB therefore rests on Intel's OEM articles and field captures.
- Corrected claim: On MegaRAID (LSI/Avago/Broadcom) and Dell PERC controllers whose write cache is protected by a conventional Li-ion BBU (e.g. iBBU07/iBBU08 on ServeRAID M5014/M5015, PERC 6/H700/H800), a non-transparent battery learn cycle switches every virtual drive whose policy is 'Write Back with BBU' (StorCLI/PERCCLI wrcache=WB; MegaCLI -NoCachedBadBBU, displayed as 'No Write Cache if Bad BBU'; Dell 'Write-Back') to write-through while the battery charge is below the retention threshold, which covers most of a cycle of roughly 7 hours (Dell: about 3 h discharge plus 4 h charge; Oracle: 1 to 12 h), on an automatic cadence of 30 days (LSI default Auto Learn Period 2592000 s; Oracle monthly) to 90 days (Dell; iBBU08 transparent mode); write-back is restored automatically once the charge is sufficient, and the cycle can be delayed or scheduled but not disabled on these cards. Virtual drives set to 'Always Write Back' (StorCLI AWB; MegaCLI -CachedBadBBU, displayed as 'Write Cache OK if Bad BBU'; Dell 'Force Write-Back') stay write-back throughout, including with a missing, degraded or failed battery, at the cost of unprotected cache. Whether a learn cycle forces write-through is a property of the battery's learn mode, not of learn cycles as such: LSI iBBU08 can be set to a transparent 12 h or 24 h retention mode in which volumes stay write-back during learn (the 48 h default mode is non-transparent), so the attestation must read the controller's Auto-Learn Mode / 'Transparent Learn' flag rather than assume. Dell PERC 8 (H710/H710P/H810 and Shared PERC 8; the H310 has no cache or battery and is write-through only) and all later battery-equipped PERCs (9/10/11) run a Transparent Learn Cycle about every 90 days (about 7 h) during which 'Virtual disks stay in Write Back mode, if enabled'; these controllers still switch 'Write-Back' drives to write-through whenever the battery is absent, failed, degraded, or in a low-charge state (unable to hold cache for 24 h, e.g. while recharging after depletion) and log 'Write policy ... was changed to Write Through'. Broadcom CacheVault supercapacitor modules likewise force write-through on WB-with-BBU drives while the module is 'charged, missing, or bad'; CacheVault modules do run learn cycles (storcli /cX/cv start learn), but whether a CacheVault learn cycle itself forces write-through is not documented in any primary source found and must be measured on the test controller.
- Design impact: 1. Keep the risk in the design but reword it: the trigger is a non-transparent learn cycle on a conventional-BBU card (or any battery/CacheVault absent, failed, degraded, charging or low-charge state), not 'learn cycles' generically; correct 'PERC 8 (H310-H710)' to 'PERC 8 H710/H710P/H810 and later battery-equipped PERCs' and stop describing PERC 8+ transparent learn as a CacheVault feature. 2. Installer attestation must capture, per controller: cache-protection type and model (BBU vs CacheVault vs none), battery/learn mode (StorCLI /cX/bbu show properties and show all: Auto Learn Period, Next Learn time, Auto-Learn Mode, 'Transparent Learn'; /cX/cv show all for CacheVault; iBBU08 retention mode), and per VD both the configured and current write policy (StorCLI /cX/vX show all Cache column WB/AWB/WT; MegaCLI 'Default Cache Policy' vs 'Current Cache Policy' with 'No Write Cache if Bad BBU' / 'Write Cache OK if Bad BBU'; Dell omreport/perccli 'Write Back' vs 'Force Write Back'). 3. Alerting must poll current-vs-default write policy per VD plus BBU 'Learn Cycle Active' / 'Battery State: Learning' / 'Charging Status', and the Dell/iDRAC event 'Write policy ... was changed to Write Through'; emit an expected-degradation notice for the learn window (so the 2 s throttle and ALUA Transitioning can be attributed to a known write-through window rather than a fault), suppress 'Battery failed' during an active learn (Dell says it is normal), and alert on write-through outside a learn window. 4. Add a policy decision for the hardware guidance: either require AWB/Force Write-Back on validated hosts (stable throughput, cache unprotected if the BBU dies, so pair with UPS and the CP flusher's ordering guarantees), or keep WB-with-BBU and size the throttle/ALUA logic to tolerate a multi-hour write-through window every 30 to 90 days; for iBBU08-class LSI cards prefer the transparent 12 h/24 h learn mode; for H700-and-earlier, schedule learn cycles into maintenance windows (Dell delay up to 168 h; MegaCLI -AdpBbuCmd -ScheduleLearn / -SetBbuProperties), noting IBM's warning that disabling automatic learn in MSM triggers an immediate learn. 5. Add a validation test: on each test controller run storcli /cX/bbu start learn (or /cX/cv start learn for CacheVault) and sample /cX/vX show all through the cycle to measure whether and for how long VDs flip to WT, since Broadcom's own StorCLI/CacheVault documents could not be read and CacheVault learn behaviour is unverified.
- Sources: https://www.dell.com/support/kbdoc/en-us/000141687/dell-perc-controller-learn-cycle-mode ; https://www.ibm.com/support/pages/battery-mode-changes-ibbu08-ibm-system-x ; https://www.ibm.com/support/pages/node/860080 ; https://www.ibm.com/support/pages/additional-information-autolearnmode-and-delay-next-learn-cycle-properties-msm-ibm-serveraid ; https://docs.oracle.com/cd/E40166_01/html/E40167/z4001567134162202.html ; https://www.manualslib.com/manual/667556/Dell-Poweredge-Raid-H700.html?page=29 ; https://www.manualslib.com/manual/667556/Dell-Poweredge-Raid-H700.html?page=30 ; https://www.manualslib.com/manual/667556/Dell-Poweredge-Raid-H700.html?page=38 ; https://www.manualslib.com/manual/3821366/Dell-H710p.html?page=17 ; https://www.manualslib.com/manual/3821366/Dell-H710p.html?page=23 ; https://www.dell.com/support/manuals/en-us/poweredge-vrtx/sperc8ha_ug-v4/battery-transparent-learn-cycle?guid=guid-e23f0bc1-4a64-41b9-9cce-8e28f3eb6143&lang=en-us ; ### [C09] CONFIRMED
- Claim: On Linux 6.12, writing 1 to attrib/emulate_write_cache of a LIO iblock backstore returns EINVAL because iblock implements the get_write_cache backend op, and the WCE bit reported to initiators is derived from bdev_write_cache() of the backing ublk device, which is set only when the ublk daemon passes UBLK_ATTR_VOLATILE_CACHE (and UBLK_ATTR_FUA for FUA support) in the basic params before START_DEV.
- Raised by: Opus-Protocols, Opus-Fabrics
- Why it matters: The configfs tree nbladed writes (emulate_write_cache=1 on iblock) and the round-2 ruling that OpenTAP advertises WCE=1 with FLUSH as an ordering barrier silently fail unless dbladed sets the ublk attribute.
- Summary: Every assertion in C09 is true on Linux 6.12, verified in the v6.12 tree and (for the two load-bearing pieces) in Debian trixie's linux 6.12.107-1 source. emulate_write_cache_store returns -EINVAL for a true value whenever the backend has a get_write_cache op, iblock sets that op to iblock_get_write_cache() which is just bdev_write_cache() on the backing bdev, the MODE SENSE caching page sets WCE from target_check_wce() which prefers get_write_cache over the attribute, and for ublk BLK_FEAT_WRITE_CACHE (and BLK_FEAT_FUA, only together with it) is set solely from UBLK_ATTR_VOLATILE_CACHE / UBLK_ATTR_FUA in the basic params, which cannot be changed once the device is started. The only stale detail is in the suggested source list: in 6.12 the cache/FUA attrs are applied in ublk_ctrl_start_dev() via struct queue_limits, not in ublk_dev_param_basic_apply(), which now only handles READ_ONLY and capacity.
- Evidence: 1) LIO configfs (drivers/target/target_core_configfs.c, v6.12 and Debian 6.12.107-1 identical): emulate_write_cache_store() does `ret = kstrtobool(page, &flag)` then `if (flag && da->da_dev->transport->get_write_cache) { pr_err("emulate_write_cache not supported for this device\n"); return -EINVAL; }`; otherwise `da->emulate_write_cache = flag; ... return count;`. So writing 1 fails with EINVAL on any backend with get_write_cache; writing 0 succeeds. The show side is macro DEF_CONFIGFS_ATTRIB_SHOW and prints the stored attribute (`to_attrib(item)->emulate_write_cache`), whose default is `#define DA_EMULATE_WRITE_CACHE 0` (include/target/target_core_base.h), i.e. it reads 0 on iblock regardless of the effective WCE. emulate_fua_write_store is the plain DEF_CONFIGFS_ATTRIB_STORE_BOOL macro (no get_write_cache check); target_alloc_device() defaults `emulate_fua_write = 1`, `emulate_dpo = 1`, `emulate_fua_read = 1` (target_core_device.c).
2) iblock (drivers/target/target_core_iblock.c v6.12): `static bool iblock_get_write_cache(struct se_device *dev) { return bdev_write_cache(IBLOCK_DEV(dev)->ibd_bd); }` and iblock_ops contains `.get_write_cache = iblock_get_write_cache,`. The op is declared as `bool (*get_write_cache)(struct se_device *);` in include/target/target_core_backend.h. iblock_configure_device() does not touch the write cache at all. iblock_execute_sync_cache() submits `bio_alloc(ib_dev->ibd_bd, 0, REQ_OP_WRITE | REQ_PREFLUSH, GFP_KERNEL)`. In iblock_execute_rw() for writes: `if (bdev_fua(ib_dev->ibd_bd)) { if (cmd->se_cmd_flags & SCF_FUA) opf |= REQ_FUA; else if (!bdev_write_cache(ib_dev->ibd_bd)) opf |= REQ_FUA; }` -- REQ_FUA is never set when the bdev lacks FUA.
3) WCE derivation (drivers/target/target_core_transport.c v6.12): target_check_wce(): `if (dev->transport->get_write_cache) wce = dev->transport->get_write_cache(dev); else if (dev->dev_attrib.emulate_write_cache > 0) wce = true; return wce;` and `target_check_fua(dev) { return target_check_wce(dev) && dev->dev_attrib.emulate_fua_write > 0; }`. target_core_spc.c spc_modesense_caching(): `p[0] = 0x08; p[1] = 0x12; /* No changeable values for now */ if (pc == 1) goto out; if (target_check_wce(dev)) p[2] = 0x04; /* Write Cache Enable */`. Also VPD 86h: `/* If WriteCache emulation is enabled, set V_SUP */ if (target_check_wce(dev)) buf[6] = 0x01;` and MODE SENSE header DPOFUA from `if (target_check_fua(dev)) spc_modesense_dpofua(...)`. spc_emulate_modeselect() rebuilds the current page and `if (memcmp(buf + off, tbuf, length)) ret = TCM_INVALID_PARAMETER_LIST;` so initiators cannot change WCE. target_core_sbc.c sbc_check_dpofua(): `if (cdb[1] & 0x8) { if (!target_check_fua(dev)) { pr_err("Got CDB: 0x%02x with FUA bit set, but device does not advertise support for FUA write\n", ...); return -EINVAL; } cmd->se_cmd_flags |= SCF_FUA; }` (caller returns TCM_INVALID_CDB_FIELD).
4) bdev_write_cache (include/linux/blkdev.h v6.12): `static inline bool bdev_write_cache(struct block_device *bdev) { return blk_queue_write_cache(bdev_get_queue(bdev)); }` with `blk_queue_write_cache(q) = (q->limits.features & BLK_FEAT_WRITE_CACHE) && !(q->limits.flags & BLK_FLAG_WRITE_CACHE_DISABLED)`; `bdev_fua()` = `limits.features & BLK_FEAT_FUA`. BLK_FEAT_WRITE_CACHE is commented "supports a volatile write cache", BLK_FEAT_FUA "supports passing on the FUA bit", BLK_FLAG_WRITE_CACHE_DISABLED "do not send FLUSH/FUA commands despite advertising a write cache". block/blk-sysfs.c: queue_wc_store accepts "write back" (clears the flag) and "write through"/"none" (`lim.flags |= BLK_FLAG_WRITE_CACHE_DISABLED`); queue_wc_show prints "write back" iff blk_queue_write_cache(q); queue/fua is read-only (`QUEUE_RO_ENTRY(queue_fua, "fua")`). block/blk-settings.c blk_validate_limits(): `if (!(lim->features & BLK_FEAT_WRITE_CACHE)) lim->features &= ~BLK_FEAT_FUA;`.
5) ublk (drivers/block/ublk_drv.c, v6.12 and Debian 6.12.107-1): in ublk_ctrl_start_dev(), `struct queue_limits lim = { .logical_block_size = 1 << p->logical_bs_shift, ... }` then `if (ub->params.basic.attrs & UBLK_ATTR_VOLATILE_CACHE) { lim.features |= BLK_FEAT_WRITE_CACHE; if (ub->params.basic.attrs & UBLK_ATTR_FUA) lim.features |= BLK_FEAT_FUA; }` and `disk = blk_mq_alloc_disk(&ub->tag_set, &lim, NULL);`. No other code path sets BLK_FEAT_WRITE_CACHE for ublk (the file has no blk_queue_write_cache call). ublk_dev_param_basic_apply() in 6.12 is only `if (p->attrs & UBLK_ATTR_READ_ONLY) set_disk_ro(ub->ub_disk, true); set_capacity(ub->ub_disk, p->dev_sectors);`. ublk_ctrl_set_params(): v6.12 `/* parameters can only be changed when device isn't live */ ... if (ub->dev_info.state == UBLK_S_DEV_LIVE) { ret = -EACCES;`; Debian 6.12.107-1 carries a stable change testing `test_bit(UB_STATE_USED, &ub->state)` with comment "Parameters can only be changed when device hasn't been started yet" (same -EACCES). include/uapi/linux/ublk_cmd.h: in struct ublk_param_basic, `#define UBLK_ATTR_VOLATILE_CACHE (1 << 2)`, `#define UBLK_ATTR_FUA (1 << 3)` on the `__u32 attrs` field; `#define UBLK_PARAM_TYPE_BASIC (1 << 0)`; `#define UBLK_IO_OP_FLUSH 2`. Documentation/block/ublk.rst: SET_PARAMS "This command has to be sent before sending UBLK_CMD_START_DEV."; START_DEV: "Parameters set via UBLK_CMD_SET_PARAMS are applied for creating the device."
6) Flush short-circuit (block/blk-flush.c v6.12 blk_insert_flush): PREFLUSH/POSTFLUSH policy bits are only computed `if (blk_queue_write_cache(q))`; then `rq->cmd_flags &= ~REQ_PREFLUSH;` always and `if (!supports_fua) rq->cmd_flags &= ~REQ_FUA;`; with policy 0 the request is finished by `blk_mq_end_request(rq, 0)` ("An empty flush handed down from a stacking driver may translate into nothing if the underlying device does not advertise a write-back cache"). So without BLK_FEAT_WRITE_CACHE a SYNCHRONIZE CACHE never reaches the ublk daemon as UBLK_IO_OP_FLUSH.
7) Debian version: sources.debian.org lists linux 6.12.107-1 in trixie (6.12.111-1 in trixie-proposed-updates); the configfs and ublk code quoted above was read from the 6.12.107-1 tree.
- Corrected claim: On Linux 6.12 (verified at v6.12 and Debian trixie linux 6.12.107-1), writing a true value to attrib/emulate_write_cache of a LIO iblock backstore fails with EINVAL ("emulate_write_cache not supported for this device") because iblock_ops sets .get_write_cache = iblock_get_write_cache; writing 0 is accepted but has no effect, and the attribute reads back its stored default 0 regardless of the effective WCE. The WCE bit in the MODE SENSE caching page (and V_SUP in VPD 86h) comes from target_check_wce(), which for iblock is bdev_write_cache() of the backing block device, evaluated at command time: BLK_FEAT_WRITE_CACHE set AND BLK_FLAG_WRITE_CACHE_DISABLED clear (the latter is toggled by /sys/block/<dev>/queue/write_cache). For a ublk backing device BLK_FEAT_WRITE_CACHE is set only when the daemon's UBLK_PARAM_TYPE_BASIC params carry UBLK_ATTR_VOLATILE_CACHE, and BLK_FEAT_FUA only when UBLK_ATTR_FUA is additionally set; ublk_ctrl_start_dev() turns these into queue_limits.features for blk_mq_alloc_disk(), and SET_PARAMS is refused (-EACCES) once the device is started, so both attrs must be in the params sent before START_DEV. Initiators cannot change WCE via MODE SELECT. Without BLK_FEAT_WRITE_CACHE the block layer completes SYNCHRONIZE CACHE flushes itself and the ublk daemon never receives UBLK_IO_OP_FLUSH; with VOLATILE_CACHE but without FUA, LIO still advertises DPOFUA (emulate_fua_write defaults to 1) and accepts FUA writes but iblock never sets REQ_FUA because bdev_fua() is false.
- Design impact: 1) nbladed's configfs tree must not write emulate_write_cache=1 on iblock backstores; the write fails with EINVAL and would abort or be silently skipped by the configfs applier. Remove the attribute for iblock (it is only meaningful for backends without get_write_cache); emulate_fua_write may stay (it is accepted on iblock and defaults to 1). 2) The round-2 ruling (WCE=1, FLUSH as ordering barrier) is implemented entirely on the dbladed side: dbladed must set attrs |= UBLK_ATTR_VOLATILE_CACHE | UBLK_ATTR_FUA in UBLK_PARAM_TYPE_BASIC via UBLK_U_CMD_SET_PARAMS before UBLK_U_CMD_START_DEV, implement UBLK_IO_OP_FLUSH, and honour the FUA flag on writes. 3) Without VOLATILE_CACHE the failure is worse than a wrong bit: LIO reports WCE=0/DPOFUA=0 (write-through semantics), blk_insert_flush() completes initiator SYNCHRONIZE CACHE requests without ever delivering a flush to dbladed, and initiator WRITEs with FUA=1 are rejected with ILLEGAL REQUEST (TCM_INVALID_CDB_FIELD) -- i.e. if dbladed buffers writes there are no barriers at all. 4) VOLATILE_CACHE without FUA is a data-integrity hole: the target advertises DPOFUA and accepts FUA writes, but iblock_execute_rw() issues them as ordinary cached writes with no post-flush. The design must mandate both attrs together. 5) Health checks and integration tests must verify the effective state from /sys/block/ublkbN/queue/write_cache == "write back" and queue/fua == 1 (or MODE SENSE page 08h / sg_modes from an initiator), never from attrib/emulate_write_cache, which reads 0 on iblock. 6) Document an operational guard: no OpenTAP udev rule, tuning script or admin action may write "write through"/"none" to /sys/block/ublkb*/queue/write_cache, since that clears the advertised WCE and stops FLUSH/FUA forwarding while dbladed still buffers. 7) Update the design's source citations: in 6.12 the cache/FUA features are applied in ublk_ctrl_start_dev() via struct queue_limits (ublk_dev_param_basic_apply() now only handles READ_ONLY and capacity); Debian 6.12.107-1 additionally refuses SET_PARAMS on any device that has ever been started (UB_STATE_USED), so a ublk device needing different attrs must be deleted and re-added.
- Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/target/target_core_configfs.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/target/target_core_iblock.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/target/target_core_transport.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/target/target_core_device.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/target/target_core_spc.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/target/target_core_sbc.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/include/target/target_core_backend.h ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/include/target/target_core_base.h ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/block/ublk_drv.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/include/uapi/linux/ublk_cmd.h ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/Documentation/block/ublk.rst ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/include/linux/blkdev.h ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/block/blk-flush.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/block/blk-settings.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/block/blk-sysfs.c ; https://sources.debian.org/api/src/linux/ ; https://sources.debian.org/src/linux/6.12.107-1/drivers/target/target_core_configfs.c/ ; https://sources.debian.org/src/linux/6.12.107-1/drivers/block/ublk_drv.c/

### [C10] PARTIALLY-CORRECT
- Claim: In Linux 6.12 ublk_drv the module parameter ublks_max defaults to 64, can be raised at runtime, is clamped at UBLK_MAX_UBLKS = UBLK_MINORS = 1 << MINORBITS (1,048,576), and ublk_ctrl_add_dev returns -EACCES once ublks_added >= ublks_max; a device's capacity is fixed at START_DEV (set_capacity in ublk_dev_param_basic_apply), UBLK_CMD_SET_PARAMS returns -EACCES while the device is live, UBLK_U_CMD_UPDATE_SIZE does not exist before 6.16, and STOP_DEV/START_DEV deletes and re-creates the gendisk underneath an open LIO iblock handle.
- Raised by: Opus-Storage, Opus-Protocols, Opus-Consensus, Opus-Fabrics
- Why it matters: 64 volumes times 8 snapshot clone LUNs plus the partner's warm-standby devices exceed the default, so the platform profile must set ublk_drv.ublks_max; and online volume growth must be a logical-size change on pre-sized ublk devices rather than a re-create, which would fail the active LUN rather than only the standby.
- Summary: Every numeric and state-machine fact checks out against the v6.12 source: ublks_max defaults to 64, is a 0644 module parameter writable at runtime, is bounded by UBLK_MAX_UBLKS = UBLK_MINORS = 1U << MINORBITS (MINORBITS = 20, so 1,048,576), ADD_DEV returns -EACCES once ublks_added >= ublks_max (unconditionally in 6.12, including CAP_SYS_ADMIN callers), the only set_capacity() call in the driver is in ublk_dev_param_basic_apply() reached from ublk_ctrl_start_dev(), SET_PARAMS returns -EACCES while UBLK_S_DEV_LIVE, and UBLK_U_CMD_UPDATE_SIZE is absent from 6.12, 6.15 and Debian trixie's 6.12.107-1 header but present in 6.16 (commit 98b995660bff). Two corrections: out-of-range writes to ublks_max are rejected with -EINVAL by param_set_uint_minmax(), not clamped; and while STOP_DEV does del_gendisk() underneath an open LIO iblock handle (the handle goes dead: capacity 0, every bio fails), START_DEV on the same device cannot re-create the gendisk underneath that handle, because it returns -EEXIST while UB_STATE_USED is set and that bit is only cleared in ublk_free_disk(), which runs only after LIO's open file drops its reference on the old gendisk.
- Evidence: Note on sources: git.kernel.org returned HTTP 403 and elixir.bootlin.com served only its navigation page to the fetcher, so the kernel files were read from the GitHub mirror of Linus's tree at the exact tags v6.12, v6.15 and v6.16 (identical content to the upstream tags).

1. Limit (drivers/block/ublk_drv.c, v6.12): "static unsigned int ublks_max = 64;" / "static unsigned int ublks_added;	/* protected by ublk_ctl_mutex */"; "module_param_cb(ublks_max, &ublk_max_ublks_ops, &ublks_max, 0644);" / MODULE_PARM_DESC "max number of ublk devices allowed to add(default: 64)". Setter: "return param_set_uint_minmax(buf, kp, 0, UBLK_MAX_UBLKS);" with "#define UBLK_MAX_UBLKS UBLK_MINORS" and "#define UBLK_MINORS (1U << MINORBITS)"; include/linux/kdev_t.h v6.12: "#define MINORBITS 20" (so 1,048,576). kernel/params.c v6.12 param_set_uint_minmax: "if (num < min || num > max)" -> "return -EINVAL;" i.e. out-of-range values are rejected, not clamped. ublk_ctrl_add_dev: "ret = -EACCES; if (ublks_added >= ublks_max) goto out_unlock;" with no capability exemption. ublks_added is incremented in ublk_add_chdev() after cdev_device_add() succeeds (ADD_DEV) and decremented in ublk_remove() (DEL_DEV), so added-but-never-started devices count. For contrast, v6.16 has "static unsigned int unprivileged_ublks_max = 64;" and checks "(info.flags & UBLK_F_UNPRIVILEGED_DEV) && unprivileged_ublks_added >= unprivileged_ublks_max" only; CAP_SYS_ADMIN devices are not limited there. Debian 6.12.107-1 debian/config/config: "CONFIG_BLK_DEV_UBLK=m"; drivers/block/Makefile: "obj-$(CONFIG_BLK_DEV_UBLK) += ublk_drv.o" (module name ublk_drv).

2. Capacity fixed at START_DEV (v6.12): the file's only set_capacity call is in ublk_dev_param_basic_apply(): "set_capacity(ub->ub_disk, p->dev_sectors);" (no set_capacity_and_notify anywhere); ublk_apply_params() calls it and is invoked from ublk_ctrl_start_dev() after blk_mq_alloc_disk() and before "ret = add_disk(disk);". ublk_ctrl_end_recovery() does not call ublk_apply_params or set_capacity (it sets ublksrv_pid, blk_mq_unquiesce_queue, state = UBLK_S_DEV_LIVE), so the recovery path cannot resize either. ublk_ctrl_set_params: "/* parameters can only be changed when device isn't live */ ... if (ub->dev_info.state == UBLK_S_DEV_LIVE) { ret = -EACCES; }". Documentation/block/ublk.rst v6.12 on SET_PARAMS: "This command has to be sent before sending UBLK_CMD_START_DEV."; on START_DEV: "Parameters set via UBLK_CMD_SET_PARAMS are applied for creating the device."; on STOP_DEV: "Halt IO on /dev/ublkb* and remove the device."; the doc mentions neither resizing nor ublks_max.

3. UPDATE_SIZE: include/uapi/linux/ublk_cmd.h v6.12 defines control commands up to UBLK_U_CMD_GET_FEATURES (0x13) and UBLK_U_CMD_DEL_DEV_ASYNC (0x14); UBLK_U_CMD_UPDATE_SIZE / UBLK_F_UPDATE_SIZE do not appear. Same in v6.15 (flags end at UBLK_F_USER_RECOVERY_FAIL_IO, bit 9). The Debian trixie source (sources.debian.org, linux 6.12.107-1) header likewise lacks both. v6.16 adds "#define UBLK_U_CMD_UPDATE_SIZE _IOWR('u', 0x15, struct ublksrv_ctrl_cmd)" and "/* Resizing a block device is possible with UBLK_U_CMD_UPDATE_SIZE * New size is passed in cmd->data[0] and is in units of sectors */ #define UBLK_F_UPDATE_SIZE (1ULL << 10)". Commit 98b995660bff "ublk: Add UBLK_U_CMD_UPDATE_SIZE" (Omri Mann, reviewed by Ming Lei, committed by Jens Axboe): "Currently ublk only allows the size of the ublkb block device to be set via UBLK_CMD_SET_PARAMS before UBLK_CMD_START_DEV is triggered. This does not provide support for extendable user-space block devices without having to stop and restart the underlying ublkb block device causing IO interruption." Its handler ublk_ctrl_set_size() does "p->dev_sectors = new_size; set_capacity_and_notify(ub->ub_disk, p->dev_sectors);" under ub->mutex with no state check. kernelnewbies lists it under Linux 6.16 (released 27 July 2025). LKML 2026-03-05 "[PATCH] ublk: fix NULL pointer dereference in ublk_ctrl_set_size()" (Mehul Rao, Fixes: 98b995660bff): "a user can trigger a NULL pointer dereference by sending UPDATE_SIZE to a device that has been added but not yet started, or one that has been stopped"; proposed fix returns -ENODEV. Debian tracker lists stable (trixie) linux at 6.12.94-1 / 6.12.111-1 (security, proposed-updates) and sources.debian.org serves 6.12.107-1 for "trixie": all 6.12.y.

4. STOP_DEV / START_DEV versus an open LIO handle. ublk_stop_dev() (v6.12): "del_gendisk(ub->ub_disk);" "ub->dev_info.state = UBLK_S_DEV_DEAD;" "put_disk(disk);" "ub->ub_disk = NULL;". block/genhd.c v6.12 del_gendisk: comment "Prevent new openers by unlinked the bdev inode." then bdev_unhash(), "blk_report_disk_dead(disk, false);" and "__blk_mark_disk_dead(disk);", whose body is "/* Fail any new I/O. */ if (test_and_set_bit(GD_DEAD, &disk->state))", "/* Stop buffered writers from dirtying pages that can't be written out. */ set_capacity(disk, 0);", "/* Prevent new I/O from crossing bio_queue_enter(). */ blk_queue_start_drain(disk->queue);". block/blk-core.c __bio_queue_enter: "if (test_bit(GD_DEAD, &disk->state))" -> "dead: bio_io_error(bio); return -ENODEV;". block/bdev.c bdev_mark_dead: calls bd_holder_ops->mark_dead only "if (bdev->bd_holder_ops && bdev->bd_holder_ops->mark_dead)", otherwise sync_blockdev() + invalidate_bdev(). drivers/target/target_core_iblock.c v6.12 iblock_configure_device: "blk_mode_t mode = BLK_OPEN_READ;" "if (!ib_dev->ibd_readonly) mode |= BLK_OPEN_WRITE;" "bdev_file = bdev_file_open_by_path(ib_dev->ibd_udev_path, mode, ib_dev, NULL);" "ib_dev->ibd_bd = bd = file_bdev(bdev_file);" (holder ib_dev, so exclusive per bdev_open's "if (holder) { mode |= BLK_OPEN_EXCL; ... bd_prepare_to_claim", holder ops NULL so no mark_dead notification); iblock_get_blocks computes "div_u64(bdev_nr_bytes(ib_dev->ibd_bd), block_size) - 1" at call time; bio errors are counted in iblock_bio_done and iblock_complete_cmd maps them to "status = SAM_STAT_CHECK_CONDITION"; the only release is fput() in iblock_destroy_device(). So after STOP_DEV the LIO handle stays open but the disk is dead: every I/O fails and READ CAPACITY is computed from a zero-length bdev. Re-start: ublk_ctrl_start_dev: "if (ub->dev_info.state == UBLK_S_DEV_LIVE || test_bit(UB_STATE_USED, &ub->state)) { ret = -EEXIST;"; UB_STATE_USED is set after add_disk() succeeds and "UB_STATE_USED is cleared only in ublk_free_disk" ("clear_bit(UB_STATE_USED, &ub->state); ublk_put_device(ub);"), wired as ub_fops ".free_disk = ublk_free_disk,". genhd.c disk_release(): "if (test_bit(GD_ADDED, &disk->state) && disk->fops->free_disk) disk->fops->free_disk(disk);" then "bdev_drop(disk->part0); /* frees the disk */"; put_disk() is "put_device(disk_to_dev(disk));" and blkdev.h "#define disk_to_dev(disk) (&((disk)->part0->bd_device))". bdev.c blkdev_get_no_open takes "kobject_get_unless_zero(&bdev->bd_device.kobj)" and bdev_release ends with blkdev_put_no_open -> "put_device(&bdev->bd_device);". Hence LIO's open file pins the old gendisk's refcount, ublk_free_disk cannot run, UB_STATE_USED stays set, and START_DEV returns -EEXIST until the iblock backstore is destroyed. The gendisk also holds a ub reference (ublk_get_device() in start_dev), and ublk_ctrl_del_dev waits with "wait_event_interruptible(ublk_idr_wq, ublk_idr_freed(idx))" for the number, freed only in ublk_cdev_rel() -> ublk_free_dev_number(), so a synchronous DEL_DEV also blocks until LIO lets go. When START_DEV does succeed it allocates a fresh gendisk via blk_mq_alloc_disk(); ublk never sets disk->major/first_minor, so device_add_disk takes the "blk_alloc_ext_minor(); disk->major = BLOCK_EXT_MAJOR; disk->first_minor = ret;" path: a new dev_t that LIO must re-open by path. Also: bdev_open fails new opens of a dead disk with "ret = -ENXIO; if (!disk_live(disk))".
- Corrected claim: In Linux 6.12 ublk_drv (Debian trixie ships 6.12.y, CONFIG_BLK_DEV_UBLK=m, module name ublk_drv), the module parameter ublks_max defaults to 64, is exposed read-write (0644) at /sys/module/ublk_drv/parameters/ublks_max so it can be raised at runtime, and accepts only values in [0, UBLK_MAX_UBLKS] where UBLK_MAX_UBLKS = UBLK_MINORS = 1U << MINORBITS = 1,048,576; a write outside that range is rejected with -EINVAL rather than clamped. ublk_ctrl_add_dev() returns -EACCES once ublks_added >= ublks_max; the counter is incremented at ADD_DEV and decremented at DEL_DEV, so devices that were added but never started count, and in 6.12 the limit applies to every device including CAP_SYS_ADMIN callers (only from 6.16 is it restricted to UBLK_F_UNPRIVILEGED_DEV devices). A device's capacity is set once, at START_DEV, by set_capacity(ub->ub_disk, p->dev_sectors) in ublk_dev_param_basic_apply() before add_disk(); UBLK_CMD_SET_PARAMS returns -EACCES while the device is UBLK_S_DEV_LIVE, the END_USER_RECOVERY path does not re-apply params, and UBLK_U_CMD_UPDATE_SIZE / UBLK_F_UPDATE_SIZE (commit 98b995660bff, ioctl 0x15, flag bit 10) exist only from Linux 6.16; they are absent from 6.12, 6.15 and the Debian trixie 6.12.107-1 header. STOP_DEV calls del_gendisk() + put_disk() underneath LIO's open iblock handle (opened via bdev_file_open_by_path with holder ib_dev and no holder ops, i.e. exclusive and with no mark_dead notification): the handle stays open but the disk is marked GD_DEAD with capacity 0, so every subsequent bio fails (bio_io_error, surfaced by iblock as CHECK CONDITION) and READ CAPACITY is computed from a zero-length bdev. START_DEV cannot then re-create the gendisk underneath that handle: it returns -EEXIST while UB_STATE_USED is set, and that bit is cleared only in ublk_free_disk() (the gendisk release callback), which cannot run while LIO's open file still holds a reference on the old gendisk; a synchronous DEL_DEV likewise waits for that release before the device number is freed. Only after the iblock backstore is destroyed can START_DEV allocate a brand-new gendisk with a newly allocated extended (major 259) dev_t, which LIO must re-open by path as a new backstore.
- Design impact: 1) Keep the platform-profile requirement: set ublks_max (options ublk_drv ublks_max=N in modprobe.d or ublk_drv.ublks_max=N on the kernel command line, since it is a module; or write /sys/module/ublk_drv/parameters/ublks_max before the ADD_DEV that would hit the limit) and size N for every device the node will ADD_DEV, including warm-standby devices that are added but not started and clone LUN devices; any value up to 1,048,576 is accepted, larger values fail with -EINVAL. Monitor ublks_added-vs-ublks_max and treat -EACCES from ADD_DEV as a capacity-planning fault. 2) Online volume growth on 6.12 cannot be done at the ublk layer at all: not via SET_PARAMS (live -EACCES), not via the user-recovery path, and not via UPDATE_SIZE (absent). So the design must either pre-size ublk dev_sectors to the volume's maximum and manage the logical size in the OpenTAP control plane/daemon, or accept a planned failover-and-re-create. 3) Rewrite the re-create path: it is not "STOP_DEV then START_DEV". Stopping the active device immediately fails every in-flight and new I/O on its LUN and corrupts READ CAPACITY, and restarting is impossible until the LIO iblock backstore holding the device is destroyed (START_DEV -EEXIST, synchronous DEL_DEV blocks); after the restart the device has a new gendisk/dev_t and LIO needs a new backstore and LUN mapping. Therefore re-create may only ever be applied to a device that LIO is not exporting (the standby), with the standby's backstore torn down first, never to the active LUN. 4) Record the forward path: on kernels >= 6.16 UBLK_U_CMD_UPDATE_SIZE resizes a live device with set_capacity_and_notify(), and because LIO iblock computes capacity from bdev_nr_bytes() on each READ CAPACITY the new size would be visible to LIO without reconfiguration; the daemon must send UPDATE_SIZE only to a LIVE device (a reported NULL-deref when sent to an added-but-not-started or stopped device, fix proposed March 2026). Initiator-side detection of the size change was not verified here and needs its own check.
- Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/block/ublk_drv.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/include/uapi/linux/ublk_cmd.h ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.15/include/uapi/linux/ublk_cmd.h ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.16/include/uapi/linux/ublk_cmd.h ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.16/drivers/block/ublk_drv.c ; https://github.com/torvalds/linux/commit/98b995660bff ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/include/linux/kdev_t.h ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/kernel/params.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/block/Makefile ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/Documentation/block/ublk.rst ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/target/target_core_iblock.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/block/genhd.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/block/bdev.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/block/blk-core.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/include/linux/blkdev.h ; https://sources.debian.org/src/linux/trixie/include/uapi/linux/ublk_cmd.h/ ; https://sources.debian.org/data/main/l/linux/6.12.107-1/debian/config/config ; https://tracker.debian.org/pkg/linux ; https://kernelnewbies.org/Linux_6.16 ; https://lkml.iu.edu/hypermail/linux/kernel/2603.0/09727.html

### [C11] CONFIRMED
- Claim: In Linux 6.12, iscsit_setup_np() in drivers/target/iscsi/iscsi_target_login.c creates the portal's listening socket with sock_create() (kern=0), which uses current->nsproxy->net_ns, so a portal created from a configfs write inside an SVM network namespace listens in that namespace; iscsit_get_np() in drivers/target/iscsi/iscsi_target.c walks the single global g_np_list and matches on IP address, port and transport only, with no namespace in the comparison, and iscsit_add_np() returns the existing portal with np_exports incremented; a kern=0 socket takes a tracked reference on its network namespace (sk_net_refcnt = 1), so a leftover portal keeps a stopped SVM's namespace alive after its pins are removed. Likewise nvmet_tcp_add_port() in drivers/nvme/target/tcp.c creates its socket with sock_create(port->addr.ss_family, SOCK_STREAM, IPPROTO_TCP, &port->sock) in the caller's netns but resolves the address with inet_pton_with_scope(&init_net, ...).
- Raised by: Opus-Protocols, Opus-Storage, Opus-Consensus
- Why it matters: Decides that iSCSI and NVMe/TCP targets live inside SVM namespaces with SVM LIFs, forces the cluster-wide uniqueness rule for block LIF ip:port even across IPspaces, fixes the stop-ladder order (delete portals before unpinning the namespace), and defers IPv6 link-local NVMe/TCP port addresses.
- Summary: Every element of C11 is true as stated in Linux v6.12 and is byte-identical in linux-6.12.y (6.12.112); Debian trixie ships linux 6.12.111-1 and its debian/patches/series names nothing touching iscsi, nvme, target or netns. iscsit_setup_np() calls sock_create() (kern=0, current->nsproxy->net_ns) synchronously in the configfs mkdir context; iscsit_get_np() walks the global g_np_list matching address, port and transport only (np_exports++ on a hit, returned by iscsit_add_np()); sk_alloc() gives a kern=0 socket sk_net_refcnt=1 and a tracked get_net_track() reference released only in __sk_destruct(); nvmet_tcp_add_port() parses with inet_pton_with_scope(&init_net, ...) and then sock_create()s in the caller's namespace. Two additions matter for the design: the iSCSI configfs name parser also uses inet_pton_with_scope(&init_net, AF_UNSPEC, ...), and LIO only rejects a duplicate ip:port within the same IQN (-EEXIST); across IQNs/namespaces it silently coalesces onto the first listener.
- Evidence: All line numbers are Linux v6.12 (git.kernel.org stable tree, tag v6.12); the same functions were extracted from linux-6.12.y (Makefile: 6.12.112) and compared: iscsit_setup_np, iscsit_get_np, iscsit_add_np, iscsit_check_np_match and nvmet_tcp_add_port are identical; sk_alloc differs only by an added "net_passive_inc(net);" in the kernel-socket (kern=1) else-branch, which does not affect kern=0 sockets.

1. Listener creation, drivers/target/iscsi/iscsi_target_login.c, iscsit_setup_np() lines 814-883: "ret = sock_create(sockaddr->ss_family, np->np_sock_type, np->np_ip_proto, &sock);" (840-841), then "tcp_sock_set_nodelay(sock->sk); sock_set_reuseaddr(sock->sk); ip_sock_set_freebind(sock->sk);" (862-864), "kernel_bind(...)" (866), "kernel_listen(sock, backlog)" (872). It is the ISCSI_TCP transport op: iscsi_target.c 661-668 "static struct iscsit_transport iscsi_target_transport = { ... .iscsit_setup_np = iscsit_setup_np, ... .iscsit_free_np = iscsit_free_np,".

2. net/socket.c line 1630-1633: "int sock_create(int family, int type, int protocol, struct socket **res) { return __sock_create(current->nsproxy->net_ns, family, type, protocol, res, 0); }" versus line 1648-1651 "sock_create_kern(struct net *net, ...) { return __sock_create(net, family, type, protocol, res, 1); }". __sock_create() (1505) passes kern through: "err = pf->create(net, sock, protocol, kern);" (1576). net/ipv4/af_inet.c 326: "sk = sk_alloc(net, PF_INET, GFP_KERNEL, answer_prot, kern);" (inet6_create likewise, net/ipv6/af_inet6.c 193).

3. Synchronous configfs context: fs/configfs/dir.c configfs_mkdir() (1264) calls "group = type->ct_group_ops->make_group(to_config_group(parent_item), name);" (1338-1339); drivers/target/target_core_fabric_configfs.c 502-503 "target_fabric_np_group_ops = { .make_group = &target_fabric_make_np," which calls "tf->tf_ops->fabric_make_np(se_tpg, group, name)" (481); iscsi_target_configfs.c 1576 ".fabric_make_np = lio_target_call_addnptotpg,". lio_target_call_addnptotpg() (154-245) calls "iscsit_tpg_add_network_portal(tpg, &sockaddr, NULL, ISCSI_TCP)" (235-236) -> iscsi_target_tpg.c 479 "np = iscsit_add_np(sockaddr, network_transport);" -> iscsi_target.c 367 "iscsi_target_setup_login_socket(np, sockaddr)" -> iscsi_target_login.c 896 "rc = t->iscsit_setup_np(np, sockaddr);". No workqueue in the chain, so current is the process that did the mkdir.

4. Global list and match, drivers/target/iscsi/iscsi_target.c: line 48 "static LIST_HEAD(g_np_list);", line 50 "static DEFINE_MUTEX(np_lock);". iscsit_get_np() (304-335): "list_for_each_entry(np, &g_np_list, np_list) { ... if (np->np_thread_state != ISCSI_NP_THREAD_ACTIVE) ... continue; match = iscsit_check_np_match(sockaddr, np, network_transport); if (match) { ... np->np_exports++; ... return np; }". iscsit_check_np_match() (265-302): IPv6 "if (!memcmp(&sock_in6->sin6_addr.in6_u, &sock_in6_e->sin6_addr.in6_u, sizeof(struct in6_addr))) ip_match = true;" (sin6_scope_id is not compared), IPv4 "if (sock_in->sin_addr.s_addr == sock_in_e->sin_addr.s_addr) ip_match = true;", result "if (ip_match && (port_e == port) && (np->np_network_transport == network_transport)) return true;". No identifier net_ns/netns/sock_net/struct net appears in any drivers/target/iscsi/*.c or include/target/iscsi/iscsi_target_core.h except the init_net use in item 8; struct iscsi_np (iscsi_target_core.h) has no namespace field. iscsit_add_np() (337-399): "np = iscsit_get_np(sockaddr, network_transport); if (np) { mutex_unlock(&np_lock); return np; }" (349-353); for a new portal "np->np_exports = 1; np->np_thread_state = ISCSI_NP_THREAD_ACTIVE; list_add_tail(&np->np_list, &g_np_list);" (389-392). Precision: the increment for an existing portal is inside iscsit_get_np() (327), which iscsit_add_np() calls.

5. Same-IQN pre-check only: iscsi_target_tpg.c iscsit_tpg_add_network_portal() 462-469 "if (iscsit_tpg_check_network_portal(tpg->tpg_tiqn, sockaddr, network_transport)) { pr_err("Network Portal: %pISc already exists on a different TPG on %s\n" ...); return ERR_PTR(-EEXIST); }" and iscsit_tpg_check_network_portal() (421-451) walks only tiqn->tiqn_tpg_list. Across different IQNs the duplicate is silently coalesced by iscsit_get_np().

6. Namespace reference, net/core/sock.c sk_alloc() 2218-2253: "sk->sk_kern_sock = kern; ... sk->sk_net_refcnt = kern ? 0 : 1; if (likely(sk->sk_net_refcnt)) { get_net_track(net, &sk->ns_tracker, priority); sock_inuse_add(net, 1); } else { __netns_tracker_alloc(net, &sk->ns_tracker, false, priority); } sock_net_set(sk, net);" (2231-2242). Release in __sk_destruct() 2293-2294: "if (likely(sk->sk_net_refcnt)) put_net_track(sock_net(sk), &sk->ns_tracker);". include/net/net_namespace.h: get_net_track() 353-359 calls get_net() which is "refcount_inc(&net->ns.count);" (256-260); put_net() "if (refcount_dec_and_test(&net->ns.count)) __put_net(net);" (276-280). include/net/sock.h 120 "@skc_net_refcnt: socket is using net ref counting". Accepted connection sockets inherit the flag and take their own reference, sock.c sk_clone_lock() 2388-2390 "if (likely(newsk->sk_net_refcnt)) { get_net_track(sock_net(newsk), &newsk->ns_tracker, priority);". Portal teardown releases it: iscsi_target.c iscsit_del_np() 438-472 "np->np_exports--; if (np->np_exports) { ... return 0; } ... np->np_transport->iscsit_free_np(np);" and iscsit_free_np() 432-436 "if (np->np_socket) sock_release(np->np_socket);".

7. NVMe/TCP, drivers/nvme/target/tcp.c nvmet_tcp_add_port() 2008-2084: "ret = inet_pton_with_scope(&init_net, af, nport->disc_addr.traddr, nport->disc_addr.trsvcid, &port->addr);" (2032-2033) then "ret = sock_create(port->addr.ss_family, SOCK_STREAM, IPPROTO_TCP, &port->sock);" (2045-2046), "sock_set_reuseaddr(port->sock->sk); tcp_sock_set_nodelay(port->sock->sk);" (2055-2056; no freebind), "kernel_bind(...)" (2060), "kernel_listen(port->sock, NVMET_TCP_BACKLOG)" (2067); nvmet_tcp_remove_port() 2097-2114 ends with "sock_release(port->sock);". Call context: drivers/nvme/target/configfs.c nvmet_port_subsys_allow_link() "if (list_empty(&port->subsystems)) { ret = nvmet_enable_port(port);" (1037-1038) -> drivers/nvme/target/core.c nvmet_enable_port() 320-381 "ret = ops->add_port(port);" (354), i.e. the listener is created in the namespace of the process that links the first subsystem into the port.

8. Scope resolution, net/core/utils.c inet6_pton() 320-357: "if (ipv6_addr_type(&addr6->sin6_addr) & IPV6_ADDR_LINKLOCAL && src + srclen != scope_delim && *scope_delim == '%') { ... dev = dev_get_by_name(net, scope_id); if (dev) { addr6->sin6_scope_id = dev->ifindex; dev_put(dev); } else if (kstrtouint(scope_id, 0, &addr6->sin6_scope_id)) { return -EINVAL; } }"; inet_pton_with_scope() 369-399 dispatches AF_INET6/AF_UNSPEC to inet6_pton(net, ...). The iSCSI configfs parser uses the same helper with init_net: iscsi_target_configfs.c 206-207 "ret = inet_pton_with_scope(&init_net, AF_UNSPEC, ip_str, port_str, &sockaddr);". bind() interprets a numeric scope id in the socket's own namespace: net/ipv6/af_inet6.c __inet6_bind() 288 "struct net *net = sock_net(sk);", 354-367 "if (__ipv6_addr_needs_scope_id(addr_type)) { if (... addr->sin6_scope_id) sk->sk_bound_dev_if = addr->sin6_scope_id; /* Binding to link-local address requires an interface */ if (!sk->sk_bound_dev_if) { err = -EINVAL; ...", 371 "dev = dev_get_by_index_rcu(net, sk->sk_bound_dev_if);".

9. Platform: packages.debian.org/trixie/linux-image-amd64 shows version "6.12.111-1" depending on "linux-image-6.12.111+deb13-amd64 (= 6.12.111-1)"; sources.debian.org linux 6.12.111-1 debian/patches/series (115 entries) contains no patch name matching iscsi, nvme, target, netns, namespace or socket (name-based check only). WebSearch for LIO iSCSI network-namespace support found only the 2014 "target/iscsi: Fix network portal creation race" commit (ee291e63) that introduced the np_lock mutex and ACTIVE-before-list-add ordering, nothing adding namespace awareness. Note: elixir.bootlin.com pages were fetched but the fetcher returned only their navigation markup, so the kernel.org raw files (curl) and the GitHub raw v6.12 files (WebFetch, which returned the same lines) are the sources actually read.
- Corrected claim: In Linux 6.12 (verified at v6.12 and linux-6.12.y 6.12.112; Debian trixie ships 6.12.111-1 with no patches in this area) an iSCSI/TCP portal's listening socket is created synchronously in the configfs mkdir context: configfs_mkdir() -> target_fabric_make_np() -> lio_target_call_addnptotpg() -> iscsit_tpg_add_network_portal() -> iscsit_add_np() -> iscsi_target_setup_login_socket() -> iscsit_setup_np() (drivers/target/iscsi/iscsi_target_login.c), which calls sock_create(sockaddr->ss_family, np->np_sock_type, np->np_ip_proto, &sock); sock_create() is __sock_create(current->nsproxy->net_ns, ..., kern = 0), so a portal created from inside an SVM network namespace listens in that namespace (iscsit_setup_np() also sets ip_sock_set_freebind, so the bind succeeds even if the address is not yet present there). iscsit_add_np() (drivers/target/iscsi/iscsi_target.c) first calls iscsit_get_np(), which walks the single global g_np_list and matches via iscsit_check_np_match() on the address bytes (IPv4 s_addr, or the 16 IPv6 address bytes with sin6_scope_id ignored), port and np_network_transport only, with no namespace in the comparison; on a match iscsit_get_np() increments np->np_exports and iscsit_add_np() returns that existing portal (a newly created portal gets np_exports = 1). LIO itself only rejects a duplicate ip:port on another TPG of the same IQN (-EEXIST via iscsit_tpg_check_network_portal()); across different IQNs, and therefore across SVM namespaces, the second portal silently reuses the first namespace's listener. A kern = 0 socket gets sk->sk_net_refcnt = 1 in sk_alloc() (net/core/sock.c) and takes a tracked reference on its namespace (get_net_track() -> refcount_inc(&net->ns.count)) that is dropped only in __sk_destruct() when the socket is released (iscsit_del_np() -> iscsit_free_np() -> sock_release()); accepted connection sockets inherit the flag and take their own reference in sk_clone_lock(). Hence a leftover portal, or a live session on it, keeps a stopped SVM's namespace alive after its pins are removed. Likewise nvmet_tcp_add_port() (drivers/nvme/target/tcp.c), invoked from nvmet_enable_port() -> ops->add_port when the first subsystem is linked into the port, resolves the address with inet_pton_with_scope(&init_net, af, nport->disc_addr.traddr, nport->disc_addr.trsvcid, &port->addr) and then creates its listener with sock_create(port->addr.ss_family, SOCK_STREAM, IPPROTO_TCP, &port->sock) in the linking process's namespace, without freebind. The iSCSI configfs portal-name parser also calls inet_pton_with_scope(&init_net, AF_UNSPEC, ...), so for both protocols an IPv6 "%ifname" scope is looked up in init_net; a numeric scope id is stored as given and interpreted by bind() in the socket's own namespace, and a link-local address with no scope fails bind() with -EINVAL.
- Design impact: The four decisions stand (targets inside SVM namespaces with SVM LIFs; cluster-wide ip:port uniqueness for block LIFs even across IPspaces; portals/ports deleted before the namespace is unpinned; IPv6 link-local deferred), with these adjustments: (1) Make the uniqueness rule a control-plane invariant and say why: the kernel will not report a cross-SVM collision (only a same-IQN one), it silently coalesces onto whichever namespace bound first, so forbid wildcard portals (0.0.0.0/[::]) in SVM-scoped targets and treat IPv6 addresses as duplicates regardless of scope id, since LIO's match ignores sin6_scope_id. (2) In the stop ladder, tear down sessions and delete every iSCSI portal and NVMe/TCP port of the SVM, and wait for the np_exports count to reach zero so the listener is actually sock_release()d, before removing namespace pins; otherwise the namespace (and its interfaces/routes) lingers invisibly. (3) For NVMe/TCP the namespace is captured when the first subsystem is linked into the port (nvmet_enable_port), not when traddr is written, so the setns wrapper must cover that symlink step; and because nvmet has no freebind, the LIF address must already be configured in the namespace or kernel_bind fails, whereas iSCSI (freebind) will bind an absent or wrong-namespace address without error, so add a post-create health check that the listener is visible inside the SVM namespace. (4) Extend the IPv6 link-local deferral to iSCSI portals as well, since the same init_net scope lookup is used; a possible later path is passing a numeric scope id (the ifindex as seen inside the SVM namespace), which the kernel code path suggests would bind correctly, but this was not tested.
