### [C12] PARTIALLY-CORRECT
- Claim: In Linux 6.12, fs/nfsd/nfsctl.c mounts the nfsd filesystem per network namespace (nfsd_fs_get_tree uses get_tree_keyed(fc, nfsd_fill_super, get_net(fc->net_ns))) exposing threads, portlist, versions, nfsv4leasetime, nfsv4gracetime, v4_end_grace, unlock_ip and unlock_filesystem; writing Y to v4_end_grace calls nfsd4_end_grace for that namespace and returns -EBUSY if no server runs there; and the file defines the genetlink handlers nfsd_nl_threads_set_doit, nfsd_nl_version_set_doit and nfsd_nl_listener_set_doit.
- Raised by: Opus-Protocols, Opus-Consensus
- Why it matters: Each SVM gets its own knfsd instance, lease, grace and controller-written early grace end after migration, which requires a per-SVM mount namespace to mount /proc/fs/nfsd per netns.
- Summary: Every structural part of the claim is confirmed against the v6.12 tag and Debian's 6.12.107-1 source: nfsd_fs_get_tree is exactly get_tree_keyed(fc, nfsd_fill_super, get_net(fc->net_ns)), the nfsd_files[] table exposes threads, portlist, versions, unlock_ip, unlock_filesystem and (under CONFIG_NFSD_V4, which Debian sets =y) nfsv4leasetime, nfsv4gracetime and v4_end_grace, and nfsctl.c defines nfsd_nl_threads_set_doit, nfsd_nl_version_set_doit and nfsd_nl_listener_set_doit (plus six other nfsd_nl_* handlers), all resolving the namespace via genl_info_net(info). The v4_end_grace sentence is only true of 6.12.0 through 6.12.65: the kernel Debian 13 actually ships (6.12.69-1 and later, currently 6.12.107-1) carries the CVE-2026-22980 fix from stable 6.12.66, which replaces the direct nfsd4_end_grace() call with nfsd4_force_end_grace(), returns -EBUSY also when the grace period has already ended or client tracking is inactive, and ends grace asynchronously via the laundromat rather than before the write returns.
- Evidence: 1) Per-netns keying (v6.12 tag, GitHub mirror of torvalds/linux; identical in Debian 6.12.107-1): nfsd_fs_get_tree body is "return get_tree_keyed(fc, nfsd_fill_super, get_net(fc->net_ns));"; nfsd_fs_context_ops has ".get_tree = nfsd_fs_get_tree," and nfsd_fs_type has ".name = "nfsd"" / ".kill_sb = nfsd_umount,"; nfsd_umount does "struct net *net = sb->s_fs_info;" ... "put_net(net);". The helper used by every write handler is "static inline struct net *netns(struct file *file)" -> "return file_inode(file)->i_sb->s_fs_info;". fs/fs_context.c alloc_fs_context sets "fc->net_ns = get_net(current->nsproxy->net_ns);" and fs/super.c get_tree_keyed does "fc->s_fs_info = key;" with test_keyed_super "return sb->s_fs_info == fc->s_fs_info;" and sget_fc "s->s_fs_info = fc->s_fs_info;" -- so one superblock per network namespace, selected by the netns of the process that creates the fs_context, and any mount path works. Per-netns state comes from pernet ops ".init = nfsd_net_init," ".exit = nfsd_net_exit," ".id = &nfsd_net_id," ".size = sizeof(struct nfsd_net),". Minor nit: nfsd_fill_super looks up nn with "net_generic(current->nsproxy->net_ns, nfsd_net_id)" (current's netns, not sb->s_fs_info) when creating the per-instance "clients" directory.

2) File table (nfsd_files[] in nfsd_fill_super, "simple_fill_super(sb, 0x6e667364, nfsd_files)"): exports, export_stats, export_features, unlock_ip, unlock_filesystem, filehandle, threads, pool_threads, pool_stats, reply_cache_stats, versions, portlist, max_block_size, max_connections, filecache; "#ifdef CONFIG_NFSD_V4": nfsv4leasetime, nfsv4gracetime, (nested "#ifdef CONFIG_NFSD_LEGACY_CLIENT_TRACKING": nfsv4recoverydir), v4_end_grace. The supported_krb5_enctypes symlink and the per-instance "clients" directory are created separately. Debian 6.12.107-1 debian/config/config: "CONFIG_NFSD=m", "CONFIG_NFSD_V4=y", "CONFIG_NFSD_V3_ACL=y", "CONFIG_NFSD_BLOCKLAYOUT=y", "CONFIG_NFSD_SCSILAYOUT=y", "CONFIG_NFSD_V4_SECURITY_LABEL=y" (no CONFIG_NFSD_LEGACY_CLIENT_TRACKING line found, so nfsv4recoverydir is likely absent -- not part of the claim).

3) write_v4_end_grace at the v6.12 tag (also still in Debian 6.12.38-1): "struct nfsd_net *nn = net_generic(netns(file), nfsd_net_id);" "switch(buf[0]) {" "case 'Y':" "case 'y':" "case '1':" "if (!nn->nfsd_serv)" "return -EBUSY;" "trace_nfsd_end_grace(netns(file));" "nfsd4_end_grace(nn);" "default:" "return -EINVAL;" then readback "return scnprintf(buf, SIMPLE_TRANSACTION_LIMIT, "%c\n"," "nn->grace_ended ? 'Y' : 'N');". nfsd4_end_grace (nfs4state.c v6.12): "if (nn->grace_ended)" "return;" "trace_nfsd_grace_complete(nn);" "nn->grace_ended = true;" "nfsd4_record_grace_done(nn);" "locks_end_grace(&nn->nfsd4_manager);". So at 6.12.0 the claim is exact.

4) What changed: upstream commit 2857bd59feb63fcf40fe4baf55401baea6b4feb4 "nfsd: provide locking for v4_end_grace" (NeilBrown, Fixes: 7f5ef2e ("nfsd: add a v4_end_grace file to /proc/fs/nfsd"), Cc: stable, CVE-2026-22980, 4 files +44 -5): "Writing to v4_end_grace can race with server shutdown and result in memory being accessed after it was freed"; nfsd_mutex cannot be held because "client_tracking_op->init() is called and that can wait for an upcall to nfsdcltrack"; "So this patch adds a nfsd_net field "client_tracking_active""; "Another field "grace_end_forced", is set when v4_end_grace is written."; "This "grace_end_forced" field bypasses other checks for whether the grace period has finished." The nfsctl.c hunk: "-	if (!nn->nfsd_serv)" "+	if (!nfsd4_force_end_grace(nn))" "return -EBUSY;" and "-	nfsd4_end_grace(nn);" removed. CVE record (cveawg.mitre.org): 6.12.* unaffected from "6.12.66"; ChangeLog-6.12.66 ("Linux 6.12.66", Sat Jan 17 2026) contains "commit ba4811c8b433bfa681729ca42cc62b6034f223b0 ... nfsd: provide locking for v4_end_grace ... commit 2857bd59feb63fcf40fe4baf55401baea6b4feb4 upstream." Debian: DSA-6126-1 (Feb 09 2026) "For the stable distribution (trixie), these problems have been fixed in version 6.12.69-1." listing CVE-2026-22980; security-tracker shows trixie 6.12.107-1 / trixie-security 6.12.111-1 fixed; sources.debian.org lists 6.12.107-1 in trixie. Debian 6.12.94-1 and 6.12.107-1 nfsctl.c confirmed: "if (!nfsd4_force_end_grace(nn))" "return -EBUSY;" "trace_nfsd_end_grace(netns(file));" with no direct nfsd4_end_grace call. Debian 6.12.107-1 nfs4state.c: "bool nfsd4_force_end_grace(struct nfsd_net *nn)" -> "if (!nn->client_tracking_ops)" "return false;" "spin_lock(&nn->client_lock);" "if (nn->grace_ended || !nn->client_tracking_active) {" (unlock, return false) "WRITE_ONCE(nn->grace_end_forced, true);" "mod_delayed_work(laundry_wq, &nn->laundromat_work, 0);" return true; kerneldoc: "Forces bypass of normal grace period completion, then schedules the laundromat to end the grace period immediately. Does not wait for the grace period to fully terminate before returning." "Return values: %true: Grace termination schedule %false: No action was taken". clients_still_reclaiming begins "if (READ_ONCE(nn->grace_end_forced))" "return false;" after which nfs4_laundromat calls the now-"static void nfsd4_end_grace". client_tracking_active is set under client_lock in nfs4_state_start_net ("nn->client_tracking_active = true;") and cleared in nfs4_state_shutdown_net ("nn->client_tracking_active = false;" then "cancel_delayed_work_sync(&nn->laundromat_work);"); client_tracking_ops is set in nfsd4_client_tracking_init and NULLed in nfsd4_client_tracking_exit (nfs4recover.c).

5) Genetlink: nfsctl.c (v6.12 and Debian 6.12.107-1) defines nfsd_nl_rpc_status_get_dumpit, nfsd_nl_threads_set_doit, nfsd_nl_threads_get_doit, nfsd_nl_version_set_doit, nfsd_nl_version_get_doit, nfsd_nl_listener_set_doit, nfsd_nl_listener_get_doit, nfsd_nl_pool_mode_set_doit, nfsd_nl_pool_mode_get_doit. nfsd_nl_threads_set_doit: "struct net *net = genl_info_net(info);" "ret = nfsd_svc(nrpools, nthreads, net, get_current_cred(), scope);" and "nn->nfsd4_grace = gracetime;" "nn->nfsd4_lease = leasetime;"; nfsd_nl_version_set_doit: "nn = net_generic(genl_info_net(info), nfsd_net_id);"; nfsd_nl_listener_set_doit: "struct net *net = genl_info_net(info);". Documentation/netlink/specs/nfsd.yaml (v6.12): "name: nfsd", "protocol: genetlink", ops rpc-status-get, threads-set (request: threads, gracetime, leasetime, scope; admin-perm), threads-get, version-set, version-get, listener-set, listener-get, pool-mode-set, pool-mode-get.

6) Userspace in trixie (nfs-utils 1:2.8.3-1, nfs-kernel-server depends on libnl-genl-3-200): rpc.nfsd's utils/nfsd/nfssvc.c hardcodes "#define NFSD_FS_DIR "/proc/fs/nfsd"" with NFSD_PORTS_FILE/NFSD_VERS_FILE/NFSD_THREAD_FILE under it and nfssvc_mount_nfsdfs() runs "mount -t nfsd nfsd /proc/fs/nfsd" if the threads file is missing; main() calls nfssvc_mount_nfsdfs, nfssvc_setvers, nfssvc_set_time("grace"/"lease"), nfssvc_set_sockets, nfssvc_threads (no netlink). utils/nfsdctl/nfsdctl.c talks only generic netlink ("genl_ctrl_resolve(sock, family)" with NFSD_FAMILY_NAME; NFSD_CMD_THREADS_SET with NFSD_A_SERVER_GRACETIME/LEASETIME/SCOPE/THREADS, NFSD_CMD_VERSION_SET, NFSD_CMD_LISTENER_SET, NFSD_CMD_POOL_MODE_SET; no /proc/fs/nfsd), and its man page NOTES say "nfsdctl instead uses a netlink(7) interface to achieve the same goals."
- Corrected claim: In Linux 6.12 (verified at the v6.12 tag and in Debian trixie's 6.12.107-1), fs/nfsd/nfsctl.c instantiates one nfsd filesystem superblock per network namespace: nfsd_fs_get_tree is "return get_tree_keyed(fc, nfsd_fill_super, get_net(fc->net_ns));", where fc->net_ns is the netns of the process that created the fs_context (fs/fs_context.c: fc->net_ns = get_net(current->nsproxy->net_ns)), superblocks are matched on that net pointer (s_fs_info), and every control file resolves its namespace through netns(file) = file_inode(file)->i_sb->s_fs_info. The instance exposes exports, export_stats, export_features, unlock_ip, unlock_filesystem, filehandle, threads, pool_threads, pool_stats, reply_cache_stats, versions, portlist, max_block_size, max_connections, filecache and, under CONFIG_NFSD_V4 (=y in Debian's config), nfsv4leasetime, nfsv4gracetime and v4_end_grace, plus a per-instance clients/ directory. Writing Y/y/1 to v4_end_grace acts on that namespace only, but its semantics depend on the point release: in 6.12.0-6.12.65 it returns -EBUSY if nn->nfsd_serv is NULL and otherwise calls nfsd4_end_grace(nn) synchronously (idempotent if grace already ended); from stable 6.12.66 (commit ba4811c8b433, upstream 2857bd59feb6 "nfsd: provide locking for v4_end_grace", CVE-2026-22980; Debian trixie since 6.12.69-1 per DSA-6126-1) it calls nfsd4_force_end_grace(nn), which returns false (so the write returns -EBUSY) when client tracking is not initialised (no server/NFSv4 state in that netns), when the grace period has already ended, or when the server is shutting down (client_tracking_active false); otherwise it sets grace_end_forced and schedules the laundromat to end the grace period, without waiting for it. Any other first character returns -EINVAL; reading the file (and the write's read-back) reports Y/N from nn->grace_ended. The same file defines the generic-netlink handlers nfsd_nl_rpc_status_get_dumpit, nfsd_nl_threads_set_doit/get_doit (threads-set also sets nn->nfsd4_grace and nn->nfsd4_lease and takes a scope), nfsd_nl_version_set_doit/get_doit, nfsd_nl_listener_set_doit/get_doit and nfsd_nl_pool_mode_set_doit/get_doit, each operating on the netns of the netlink socket (genl_info_net(info)), as specified in Documentation/netlink/specs/nfsd.yaml.
- Design impact: 1) Per-SVM knfsd instances with independent lease/grace are supported as the design assumes: no kernel change is needed, and CONFIG_NFSD_V4=y in Debian's config so nfsv4leasetime/nfsv4gracetime/v4_end_grace exist. 2) The design must not assume that a write of Y to v4_end_grace ends the grace period before the write returns or that -EBUSY means only "no server here". On the trixie kernel (>= 6.12.69-1, currently 6.12.107-1) -EBUSY is also returned when grace has already ended or the server is mid-shutdown, and success only schedules the laundromat. The controller's post-migration early-grace-end step should therefore: read v4_end_grace first (N means still in grace), treat -EBUSY as "nothing to do or server not running" and distinguish those by re-reading the file / checking threads, and poll v4_end_grace until Y (or wait for the nfsd_grace_complete tracepoint) before signalling clients that reclaim is closed. The design should also note both code paths if it ever has to run on a 6.12.0-6.12.65 kernel. 3) The "requires a per-SVM mount namespace" rationale is stronger than the kernel requires. The superblock is keyed by the netns of the mounting process, not by the mount path, so the controller can mount one nfsd instance per SVM at a per-SVM path (e.g. /run/opentap/svm/<id>/nfsd) by entering the SVM's netns (setns) in a single mount namespace; mount(2) from the same netns reuses the superblock. A per-SVM mount namespace is needed only if the SVM runs stock nfs-utils daemons, because rpc.nfsd in trixie's nfs-utils 2.8.3 hardcodes /proc/fs/nfsd (and tries to mount it there). 4) Threads, enabled versions, listeners, pool mode and the lease/grace times can be set per SVM over generic netlink from any process inside the SVM netns without mounting the nfsd fs at all (nfsd.yaml threads-set carries threads/gracetime/leasetime/scope; trixie's nfsdctl already does this and the scope attribute is the per-SVM server-scope the design needs for migration); only v4_end_grace, unlock_ip, unlock_filesystem, exports/filehandle and the clients/ directory still require the per-netns nfsd mount, so the controller must still mount it per SVM, but for fewer operations than the design implies.
- Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/fs/nfsd/nfsctl.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/fs/nfsd/nfs4state.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/Documentation/netlink/specs/nfsd.yaml ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/fs/fs_context.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/fs/super.c ; https://sources.debian.org/data/main/l/linux/6.12.107-1/fs/nfsd/nfsctl.c ; https://sources.debian.org/data/main/l/linux/6.12.107-1/fs/nfsd/nfs4state.c ; https://sources.debian.org/data/main/l/linux/6.12.107-1/fs/nfsd/nfs4recover.c ; https://sources.debian.org/data/main/l/linux/6.12.107-1/debian/config/config ; https://sources.debian.org/data/main/l/linux/6.12.38-1/fs/nfsd/nfsctl.c ; https://sources.debian.org/data/main/l/linux/6.12.94-1/fs/nfsd/nfsctl.c ; https://sources.debian.org/api/src/linux/ ; https://github.com/torvalds/linux/commit/2857bd59feb63fcf40fe4baf55401baea6b4feb4 ; https://cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/CVE-2026-22980 ; https://cdn.kernel.org/pub/linux/kernel/v6.x/ChangeLog-6.12.66 ; https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-22980 ; https://lists.debian.org/debian-security-announce/2026/msg00035.html ; https://www.suse.com/security/cve/CVE-2026-22980.html ; https://mailweb.openeuler.org/archives/list/kernel@openeuler.org/thread/22B3DX67QBXEUNPIN4CSGWK55OTX35OM/ ; https://packages.debian.org/trixie/nfs-kernel-server ; https://sources.debian.org/api/src/nfs-utils/ ; https://sources.debian.org/data/main/n/nfs-utils/1:2.8.3-1/utils/nfsd/nfssvc.c ; https://sources.debian.org/data/main/n/nfs-utils/1:2.8.3-1/utils/nfsd/nfsd.c ; https://sources.debian.org/data/main/n/nfs-utils/1:2.8.3-1/utils/nfsdctl/nfsdctl.adoc ; https://sources.debian.org/data/main/n/nfs-utils/1:2.8.3-1/utils/nfsdctl/nfsdctl.c

### [C13] PARTIALLY-CORRECT
- Claim: In Linux 6.12, lockd (NLM) is a single global svc_serv with exactly one kernel thread (svc_set_num_threads(nlmsvc_serv, NULL, 1) in lockd_get() in fs/lockd/svc.c) shared by every network namespace; lockd_up_net() only adds per-net sockets and arms a per-net grace timer via set_grace_period(net); nlm_grace_period and nlm_tcpport/nlm_udpport (sysctl fs.nfs.*) are file-scope globals; and an NLM_LOCK on a cold inode performs the VFS/XFS inode read (nlm_fopen -> nfsd_open -> fh_verify -> xfs_iget) on that single thread.
- Raised by: Opus-Protocols, Opus-Consensus
- Why it matters: Per-SVM NLM isolation and the per-SVM 20 s grace window on a shared port depend on this; if one thread serves all SVMs, a stalled volume in one datastore SVM blocks NLM lock operations (Proxmox qemu lock=on reclaims) for every SVM on the node.
- Summary: Every load-bearing assertion is confirmed from the 6.12 source (and identical in Debian's 6.12.111-1 svc.c): one file-static `nlmsvc_serv`, created by lockd_get() with svc_create() (one pool) and `svc_set_num_threads(serv, NULL, 1)`, is shared by every network namespace; lockd_up_net() creates no threads; nlm_grace_period/nlm_udpport/nlm_tcpport are file-static globals under register_sysctl("fs/nfs"); and NLM_LOCK runs nlm_fopen -> nfsd_open -> fh_verify -> exportfs_decode_fh_raw -> xfs_fs_fh_to_dentry -> xfs_iget on that single thread. Corrections: the per-net grace end is a `struct delayed_work` (grace_period_end), not a timer; lockd_up_net() also calls svc_bind(serv, net) (per-net rpcbind) before make_socks(); the grace check in nlmsvc_lock() runs after the file has already been opened; and the per-net locks_in_grace() list is shared with nfsd's NFSv4 grace (default 90 s), which conditions the "per-SVM 20 s grace window" assumption.
- Evidence: 1. Single global service and thread (fs/lockd/svc.c, v6.12 and Debian 6.12.111-1 identical): "static struct svc_serv *nlmsvc_serv;", "static unsigned int nlmsvc_users;". lockd_get(): "serv = svc_create(&nlmsvc_program, LOCKD_BUFSIZE, lockd);" then "error = svc_set_num_threads(serv, NULL, 1);" then stores nlmsvc_serv = serv, registers inetaddr notifiers, nlmsvc_users++. The only other svc_set_num_threads call in the file is lockd_put(): "svc_set_num_threads(nlmsvc_serv, NULL, 0);" followed by "svc_destroy(&nlmsvc_serv);". No sysctl/module parameter changes the lockd thread count. lockd_up(): "error = lockd_get();" then "error = lockd_up_net(nlmsvc_serv, net, cred);".
   net/sunrpc/svc.c: svc_create() is "return __svc_create(prog, 1, NULL, bufsize, 1, threadfn);" (npools = 1); svc_set_num_threads() with NULL pool: "if (!pool)" "nrservs -= serv->sv_nrthreads;" then svc_start_kthreads(); threads are created with kthread_create_on_node(serv->sv_threadfn, rqstp, node, "%s", serv->sv_name). svc_pool_for_cpu(): "if (serv->sv_nrpools <= 1)" "return serv->sv_pools;". net/sunrpc/svc_xprt.c svc_xprt_enqueue(): "pool = svc_pool_for_cpu(xprt->xpt_server);" so every transport in every net lands in the one pool; svc_recv() ("Receive and process the next request on any transport") does "rqstp->rq_xprt = svc_xprt_dequeue(pool);" then svc_handle_xprt() -> svc_process() ("svc_process - Execute one RPC transaction"). lockd() main loop: while (!svc_thread_should_stop(rqstp)) { rqstp->rq_server->sv_maxconn = nlm_max_connections; nlmsvc_retry_blocked(rqstp); svc_recv(rqstp); }. fs/lockd/svclock.c comment in nlmdbg_cookie2a(): "We can get away with a static buffer because this is only called from lockd, which is single-threaded."

2. lockd_up_net() (svc.c): runs only when "ln->nlmsvc_users++" was 0; "error = svc_bind(serv, net);" (net/sunrpc/svc.c svc_bind -> svc_rpcb_setup: "err = rpcb_create_local(net);" and "svc_unregister(serv, net);" under "/* Remove any stale portmap registrations */"); "error = make_socks(serv, net, cred);" (make_socks -> create_lockd_family(serv, net, PF_INET/PF_INET6, cred) -> create_lockd_listener -> "return svc_xprt_create(serv, name, net, family, port," "SVC_SOCK_DEFAULTS, cred);"); "set_grace_period(net);"; "dprintk("%s: per-net data created; net=%x\n", __func__, net->ns.inum);". No thread creation. lockd_down_net(): on last user, nlm_shutdown_hosts_net(net), cancel_delayed_work_sync(&ln->grace_period_end), locks_end_grace(&ln->lockd_manager), svc_xprt_destroy_all(serv, net), svc_rpcb_cleanup(serv, net).
   Grace mechanism: fs/lockd/netns.h struct lockd_net { unsigned int nlmsvc_users; unsigned long next_gc; unsigned long nrhosts; struct delayed_work grace_period_end; struct lock_manager lockd_manager; struct list_head nsm_handles; } -- there is no grace_timer field. lockd_init_net(): INIT_DELAYED_WORK(&ln->grace_period_end, grace_ender). set_grace_period(net): "locks_start_grace(net, &ln->lockd_manager);", cancel_delayed_work_sync(), schedule_delayed_work(&ln->grace_period_end, grace_period); grace_ender() -> locks_end_grace(). get_lockd_grace_period(): "return roundup(nlm_grace_period, nlm_timeout) * HZ;" else nlm_timeout * 5 * HZ -- a single global duration.

3. Globals/sysctls (svc.c): "static unsigned long nlm_grace_period;" (comment: "These can be set at insmod time (useful for NFS as root filesystem),"), "static int nlm_udpport, nlm_tcpport;", "unsigned long nlm_timeout = LOCKD_DFLT_TIMEO;", "static unsigned int nlm_max_connections = 1024;". nlm_sysctls entries nlm_grace_period (&nlm_grace_period, proc_doulongvec_minmax), nlm_timeout, nlm_udpport, nlm_tcpport (&nlm_udpport/&nlm_tcpport, proc_dointvec_minmax), nsm_use_hostnames, nsm_local_state, all mode 0644; registered once in init_nlm(): "nlm_sysctl_table = register_sysctl("fs/nfs", nlm_sysctls);" (global, not register_net_sysctl). Also module_param_call(nlm_grace_period, ...), module_param_call(nlm_udpport, ...), module_param_call(nlm_tcpport, ...).

4. NLM_LOCK cold-inode path, all on the lockd thread: fs/lockd/svc4proc.c "[NLMPROC_LOCK] = {" ".pc_func = nlm4svc_proc_lock," -> __nlm4svc_proc_lock() -> nlm4svc_retrieve_args(): "if (!(host = nlmsvc_lookup_host(rqstp, lock->caller, lock->len))" "|| (argp->monitor && nsm_monitor(host) < 0))" "goto no_locks;" then "error = nlm_lookup_file(rqstp, &file, lock);" (svcproc.c for NLM v1/v3 is the same shape with cast_status()). fs/lockd/svcsubs.c nlm_lookup_file() ("Lookup file info. If it doesn't exist, create a file info struct" "and open a (VFS) file for the given inode."): mutex_lock(&nlm_file_mutex); hlist walk of global "static struct hlist_head nlm_files[FILE_NRHASH];" matched by file handle only; nlm_do_fopen() returns 0 if file->f_file[mode] is already open, else "nlmsvc_ops->fopen(rqstp, &file->f_handle, fp, mode)". fs/nfsd/lockd.c: nfsd_lockd_init() sets nlmsvc_ops = &nfsd_nlm_ops (.fopen = nlm_fopen); nlm_fopen() builds an svc_fh by hand (fh_init, copies the handle, fh_export = NULL, access NFSD_MAY_READ/WRITE | NFSD_MAY_LOCK) and calls "nfsd_open(rqstp, &fh, S_IFREG, access, filp)"; nfserr_dropit -> nlm_drop_reply, nfserr_stale -> nlm_stale_fh. fs/nfsd/vfs.c nfsd_open(): calls fh_verify() then __nfsd_open() (dentry_open). fs/nfsd/nfsfh.c fh_verify ("Look up a dentry from the on-the-wire filehandle, check the client's" "access to the export") -> __fh_verify -> nfsd_set_fh_dentry: "exp = rqst_exp_find(rqstp ? &rqstp->rq_chandle : NULL," "net, client, gssclient," ...) then "/* Look up the dentry using the NFS file handle. */" "dentry = exportfs_decode_fh_raw(exp->ex_path.mnt, fid," ... "nfsd_acceptable, exp);". fs/exportfs/expfs.c: "result = nop->fh_to_dentry(mnt->mnt_sb, fid, fh_len, fileid_type);". fs/xfs/xfs_export.c: ".fh_to_dentry = xfs_fs_fh_to_dentry," -> xfs_nfs_get_inode(): "error = xfs_iget(mp, NULL, ino, XFS_IGET_UNTRUSTED, 0, &ip);" (comments: "clients can" "send invalid file handles and we have to handle it gracefully.."). Export lookup side-path: fs/nfsd/export.c exp_find_key()/exp_get_by_name() call "err = cache_check(cd, &ek->h, reqp);"; net/sunrpc/cache.c cache_check(): "-EAGAIN if upcall is pending and request has been queued", cache_wait_req() waits "wait_for_completion_interruptible_timeout(" "&sleeper.completion, req->thread_wait)"; svc_recv() sets "rqstp->rq_chandle.thread_wait = 5 * HZ;" or "= 1 * HZ;" ("When there are no" "idle threads, we reduce the wait time"). fs/lockd/mon.c nsm_mon_unmon(): "status = rpc_call_sync(clnt, &msg, RPC_TASK_SOFTCONN);" to a client created by nsm_create() with ".net = net," ".servername = "rpc.statd"," and "sin_addr.s_addr = htonl(INADDR_LOOPBACK),".
   Ordering: fs/lockd/svclock.c nlmsvc_lock() does nlmsvc_lookup_block()/nlmsvc_create_block(), then "if (locks_in_grace(SVC_NET(rqstp)) && !reclaim) {" "ret = nlm_lck_denied_grace_period;" and "if (reclaim && !locks_in_grace(SVC_NET(rqstp))) {", then "error = vfs_lock_file(file->f_file[mode], F_SETLK, &lock->fl, NULL);" -- i.e. the grace check comes after nlm_lookup_file() has opened the inode.

5. Per-net grace is unioned with NFSv4 grace: fs/nfs_common/grace.c keeps one list per net ("net_generic(net, grace_net_id)"); locks_start_grace() adds any lock_manager; locks_in_grace() "Lock managers call this function to determine when it is OK for them to answer ordinary lock requests" and is true while the net's list is non-empty; header comment: grace is "only enforced by the two lock managers (lockd and nfsd)". fs/nfsd/nfs4state.c nfs4_state_start_net(): "locks_start_grace(net, &nn->nfsd4_manager);", printk "NFSD: starting %lld-second grace period (net %x)" with nn->nfsd4_grace, "queue_delayed_work(laundry_wq, &nn->laundromat_work, nn->nfsd4_grace * HZ);", or skip when "nn->track_reclaim_completes && nn->reclaim_str_hashtbl_size == 0" ("NFSD: no clients to reclaim, skipping NFSv4 grace period (net %x)"); nfsd4_init_leases_net(): "nn->nfsd4_lease = 90; /* default lease time */" "nn->nfsd4_grace = 90;". fs/nfsd/nfsctl.c: nfsv4gracetime writes accept 10 to 3600 seconds; the nfsd filesystem is keyed per net ("get_tree_keyed(fc, nfsd_fill_super, get_net(fc->net_ns))").

6. Who starts lockd per net: fs/nfsd/nfssvc.c nfsd_needs_lockd(): "return nfsd_vers(nn, 2, NFSD_TEST) || nfsd_vers(nn, 3, NFSD_TEST);"; nfsd_startup_net(): "if (nfsd_needs_lockd(nn) && !nn->lockd_up) {" "ret = lockd_up(net, cred);" "nn->lockd_up = true;"; nfsd_shutdown_net(): "lockd_down(net);". By contrast nfsd's own service is per net (nn->nfsd_serv; nfsd_set_nrthreads "alters the number of running threads for the given network", "svc_set_num_threads(nn->nfsd_serv, NULL, nthreads[0])"). fs/lockd/host.c: host tables are global ("static struct hlist_head nlm_server_hosts[NLM_HOST_NRHASH];") but matched per net ("struct net *net = SVC_NET(rqstp);", "if (host->net != net)" "continue;"); nlm_files and nlm_blocked are global with no net key.

7. Platform pin: packages.debian.org/trixie/linux-image-amd64 lists "6.12.111-1" depending on "linux-image-6.12.111+deb13-amd64 (= 6.12.111-1)"; sources.debian.org linux 6.12.111-1 fs/lockd/svc.c contains the same "svc_create(&nlmsvc_program, LOCKD_BUFSIZE, lockd)", "svc_set_num_threads(serv, NULL, 1)", "svc_bind(serv, net)", "make_socks(serv, net, cred)", "set_grace_period(net)" and "register_sysctl("fs/nfs", nlm_sysctls)" lines.

Note on sources: git.kernel.org/plain and elixir.bootlin.com returned HTTP 403 / navigation-only pages, so the v6.12 tag was read from the official torvalds/linux GitHub mirror and cross-checked against Debian's 6.12.111-1 source.
- Corrected claim: In Linux 6.12 (verified at tag v6.12 and in Debian 13's linux 6.12.111-1), NLM is served by one global SUNRPC service: fs/lockd/svc.c holds `static struct svc_serv *nlmsvc_serv`; lockd_get() creates it with svc_create(&nlmsvc_program, LOCKD_BUFSIZE, lockd) (a single pool) and calls svc_set_num_threads(serv, NULL, 1), so exactly one kernel thread ("lockd") exists system-wide; the count is only ever set to 1 (lockd_get) or 0 (lockd_put) and is not tunable. Every network namespace that calls lockd_up(net, cred) -- each per-net nfsd via nfsd_startup_net() when NFSv2/v3 is enabled, or an NFS client mount -- shares that service and thread. lockd_up_net(serv, net, cred) runs only when the per-net lockd_net.nlmsvc_users count goes 0 -> 1 and does three per-net things, none of which creates a thread: svc_bind(serv, net) (per-net rpcbind client and stale-registration cleanup), make_socks(serv, net, cred) (per-net PF_INET/PF_INET6 UDP and TCP listeners on nlm_udpport/nlm_tcpport via svc_xprt_create(serv, ..., net, ...)), and set_grace_period(net), which calls locks_start_grace(net, &ln->lockd_manager) and schedules the per-net `struct delayed_work grace_period_end` (grace_ender -> locks_end_grace); there is no timer field. With one pool, svc_pool_for_cpu() returns that pool for every transport in every namespace, so the one thread executes all namespaces' NLM RPCs one at a time (lockd() loop: nlmsvc_retry_blocked(rqstp); svc_recv(rqstp) -> svc_handle_xprt -> svc_process). nlm_grace_period (static unsigned long), nlm_udpport/nlm_tcpport (static int), nlm_timeout and nlm_max_connections are file-scope globals exposed as module parameters and through register_sysctl("fs/nfs", nlm_sysctls) (/proc/sys/fs/nfs/nlm_grace_period, nlm_tcpport, nlm_udpport), i.e. one value for all namespaces; the NLM grace length is roundup(nlm_grace_period, nlm_timeout) seconds, or 5 * nlm_timeout when unset. For NLM_LOCK (nlm4svc_proc_lock / nlmsvc_proc_lock -> nlm[4]svc_retrieve_args) the thread first resolves the host (nlmsvc_lookup_host, matched by SVC_NET(rqstp)), performs a synchronous nsm_monitor() RPC (rpc_call_sync, RPC_TASK_SOFTCONN) to the loopback rpc.statd inside that namespace if the peer is not yet monitored, then, when the handle is not already open in the global nlm_files hash, runs nlm_lookup_file -> nlm_do_fopen -> nlmsvc_ops->fopen = nlm_fopen (fs/nfsd/lockd.c) -> nfsd_open -> fh_verify -> __fh_verify -> nfsd_set_fh_dentry -> rqst_exp_find (export cache; a missing entry waits on the mountd upcall for rq_chandle.thread_wait, 1 s when the pool has no idle thread, else 5 s, before the request is dropped) -> exportfs_decode_fh_raw -> xfs_fs_fh_to_dentry -> xfs_nfs_get_inode -> xfs_iget(mp, NULL, ino, XFS_IGET_UNTRUSTED, 0, &ip) -> __nfsd_open -> dentry_open. All of this runs on the single lockd thread and completes before nlmsvc_lock() evaluates locks_in_grace(SVC_NET(rqstp)) and vfs_lock_file(). The per-net grace state (fs/nfs_common/grace.c) is a single per-namespace list shared by lockd's lockd_manager and nfsd's nfsd4_manager, so NLM in a namespace is in grace while either lockd's grace or that namespace's NFSv4 grace (nn->nfsd4_grace, default 90 s, settable per namespace from 10 to 3600 s, or skipped when reclaim tracking shows no clients) is active.
- Design impact: 1. Per-SVM NLM isolation does not exist at the execution level on a 6.12 node: one lockd thread serves every SVM network namespace, and it processes one RPC at a time. Any NLM request that blocks -- a cold-inode xfs_iget on a stalled or hung volume, a dentry_open/lease break, an export-cache upcall waiting on rpc.mountd, a slow loopback rpc.statd -- stalls NLM_LOCK/UNLOCK/CANCEL/TEST, GRANTED retries and blocked-lock retries for all SVMs on the node (including Proxmox qemu lock=on reclaims). The design must either document node-wide NLM head-of-line blocking as an accepted failure mode, push datastore clients to NFSv4.1/4.2 (NFSv4 locking is handled by nfsd's per-net nn->nfsd_serv threads, not lockd, so it does keep per-SVM isolation), make the node rather than the SVM the NLM blast-radius unit, or carry a kernel change for per-net lockd threads (not present in 6.12 and not tunable). Note also that NLM server state is not partitioned per net: nlm_files (keyed by file handle only) and nlm_blocked are global; only the host table is matched per net.
2. The "per-SVM 20 s grace window" needs restating. The grace flag is per net and starts when that net's lockd user count goes 0 -> 1 (first nfsd start in the SVM namespace), but its length is a single global sysctl (fs.nfs.nlm_grace_period, rounded up to a multiple of fs.nfs.nlm_timeout, default 5 x nlm_timeout) shared by all SVMs; it cannot differ per SVM. Because locks_in_grace() is a union over lockd and nfsd managers in the same net, an SVM's NLM clients are also denied with nlm_lck_denied_grace_period for the whole NFSv4 grace of that namespace (90 s default); to get a 20 s window the design must set nfsv4gracetime per SVM namespace to <= 20 s (minimum accepted is 10 s) or ensure NFSv4 grace is skipped, otherwise Proxmox lock=on VM starts after an SVM move stall for up to 90 s. Also, the grace check runs after the file open, so NLM_LOCK during grace still performs the cold-inode read on the shared thread before being denied.
3. Ports and statd: nlm_tcpport/nlm_udpport are global, so every SVM namespace listens on the same port number (in its own port space); the port cannot vary per SVM. Each SVM namespace must run its own rpc.statd reachable on 127.0.0.1 inside that namespace (nsm_create uses INADDR_LOOPBACK with .net = net); if it is absent, nsm_monitor() fails and monitored LOCK requests are refused with nlm_lck_denied_nolocks.
- Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/fs/lockd/svc.c ; https://sources.debian.org/data/main/l/linux/6.12.111-1/fs/lockd/svc.c ; https://packages.debian.org/trixie/linux-image-amd64 ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/fs/lockd/netns.h ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/fs/lockd/svc4proc.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/fs/lockd/svcproc.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/fs/lockd/svcsubs.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/fs/lockd/svclock.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/fs/lockd/host.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/fs/lockd/mon.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/fs/nfsd/lockd.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/fs/nfsd/vfs.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/fs/nfsd/nfsfh.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/fs/nfsd/export.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/fs/nfsd/nfssvc.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/fs/nfsd/nfs4state.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/fs/nfsd/nfsctl.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/fs/nfs_common/grace.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/fs/exportfs/expfs.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/fs/xfs/xfs_export.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/net/sunrpc/svc.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/net/sunrpc/svc_xprt.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/net/sunrpc/cache.c

### [C14] PARTIALLY-CORRECT
- Claim: nfs-utils 1:2.8.3-1 (Debian trixie): rpc.nfsd --scope is implemented as unshare(CLONE_NEWUTS) followed by sethostname(scope); nfsdctl's threads subcommand has no scope option, and the remaining ways to set a per-namespace NFSv4 server scope are nfsdctl autostart via a [nfsd] scope= option in nfs.conf or the NFSD_A_SERVER_SCOPE attribute of the nfsd generic-netlink THREADS_SET command; sm-notify accepts -P <state directory>, -v <name> and -f and without -v uses the mon_name recorded at monitor time; rpc.statd's no-notify flag is -L (while -N runs sm-notify and exits); nfsdcld accepts -p <pipefs dir> and -s <storage dir> and stores main.sqlite there.
- Raised by: Opus-Protocols, Opus-Consensus
- Why it matters: The per-SVM NFSv4.1 server scope (which must survive migration to avoid no-grace recovery and silent lock loss), NFSv3 lock recovery after an SVM move, and the NFSv4 client-reclaim database redirected to the SVM root volume all depend on these exact flags and mechanisms.
- Summary: Almost everything in C14 is confirmed from the nfs-utils 1:2.8.3-1 sources and man pages and from the 6.12 kernel (v6.12 tag and Debian's 6.12.107-1): rpc.nfsd --scope is unshare(CLONE_NEWUTS)+sethostname(), nfsdctl threads has only -h, autostart reads [nfsd] scope= and sends NFSD_A_SERVER_SCOPE on THREADS_SET, statd -L/-N, sm-notify -P/-v/-f and nfsdcld -p/-s with main.sqlite are all exactly as stated. Two corrections matter: without -v sm-notify sends the record's my_name field (not its mon_name, which is the destination peer) as the SM_NOTIFY mon_name, and on a Linux server that my_name is lockd's copy of the node's UTS nodename, so after an SVM move it is the wrong name; and the kernel copies the scope into nn->nfsd_name unconditionally on every nfsd_svc() call, so the scope can only be set while no threads run (-EBUSY otherwise) and any later thread-count change made without a scope silently resets it to the caller's UTS nodename.
- Evidence: VERSION: tracker.debian.org lists nfs-utils "stable: 1:2.8.3-1" (testing/unstable 1:3.1.1-1); packages.debian.org/trixie/nfs-kernel-server shows "Package: nfs-kernel-server (1:2.8.3-1)", source nfs-utils; sources.debian.org maps "1:2.8.3-1" to trixie. Trixie's nfs-kernel-server file list contains /usr/sbin/rpc.nfsd, /usr/sbin/nfsdctl, /usr/sbin/nfsdcld, /usr/sbin/nfsdclddb; nfs-common contains /usr/sbin/rpc.statd and /usr/sbin/sm-notify. Trixie's kernel source is linux 6.12.107-1 (6.12.111-1 in trixie-proposed-updates).

RPC.NFSD --scope (utils/nfsd/nfsd.c, 2.8.3-1): longopt `{ "scope", 1, 0, 'S'}`, getopt string "dH:S:hN:V:p:P:stTuUrG:L:", `case 'S': scope = optarg;`, config `scope = conf_get_str("nfsd", "scope");`, then after nfssvc_set_time(): `if (scope) { if (unshare(CLONE_NEWUTS) < 0 || sethostname(scope, strlen(scope)) < 0) { xlog(L_ERROR, "Unable to set server scope: %m"); error = -1; goto out; }` followed by nfssvc_set_sockets() and nfssvc_threads(count). Conditions found: (a) if `nfssvc_inuse()` is true rpc.nfsd does `goto set_threads`, skipping the scope block, so --scope only acts on a cold start; (b) the usage() text omits --scope but nfsd.man documents it ("By default Linux NFSD uses the host name as the scope ... important for high-availablity configurations to ensure that all potential server nodes report the same server scope"); (c) nfsd.c contains no netlink code, it writes /proc/fs/nfsd/threads, and the kernel's write_threads does `rv = nfsd_svc(1, &newthreads, net, file->f_cred, NULL);`, which is why the UTS trick works.

KERNEL 6.12: fs/nfsd/nfssvc.c nfsd_svc(int n, int *nthreads, struct net *net, const struct cred *cred, const char *scope) does, unconditionally and before nfsd_create_serv(): `strscpy(nn->nfsd_name, scope ? scope : utsname()->nodename, sizeof(nn->nfsd_name));` with kernel-doc "@scope: server scope value (defaults to nodename)". Identical in Debian 6.12.107-1 and in current mainline. netns.h: `/* utsname taken from the process that starts the server */ char nfsd_name[UNX_MAXNODENAME+1];`. nfs4xdr.c: `/* eir_server_scope */ nfserr = nfsd4_encode_opaque(xdr, nn->nfsd_name, strlen(nn->nfsd_name));` and `/* so_major_id */ return nfsd4_encode_opaque(xdr, nn->nfsd_name, strlen(nn->nfsd_name));` (scope and server-owner major_id are the same string). Documentation/netlink/specs/nfsd.yaml: attribute-set "server" = threads (u32, multi-attr), gracetime (u32), leasetime (u32), scope (string); operation threads-set (flags admin-perm) request attributes threads, gracetime, leasetime, scope; threads-get reply has the same four. fs/nfsd/netlink.c policy `[NFSD_A_SERVER_SCOPE] = { .type = NLA_NUL_STRING, }` (no maxlen; strscpy truncates to the nfsd_name buffer), op flags `GENL_ADMIN_PERM | GENL_CMD_CAP_DO`. fs/nfsd/nfsctl.c nfsd_nl_threads_set_doit: `if (info->attrs[NFSD_A_SERVER_GRACETIME] || info->attrs[NFSD_A_SERVER_LEASETIME] || info->attrs[NFSD_A_SERVER_SCOPE]) {` ... `if (nn->nfsd_serv && nn->nfsd_serv->sv_nrthreads) ret = -EBUSY;` ... `scope = nla_data(attr);` ... `ret = nfsd_svc(nrpools, nthreads, net, get_current_cred(), scope);`; threads_get puts `nla_put_string(skb, NFSD_A_SERVER_SCOPE, nn->nfsd_name)`. Debian 6.12.107-1 include/uapi/linux/nfsd_netlink.h has NFSD_A_SERVER_SCOPE and NFSD_CMD_THREADS_SET. Commit 9077d598 ("NFSD: allow callers to pass in scope string to nfsd_svc"): "Currently admins set this by using unshare to create a new uts namespace, and then resetting the hostname. With the new netlink interface we can just pass this in directly."

NFSDCTL (utils/nfsdctl/nfsdctl.c, 2.8.3-1): threads subcommand parses `getopt_long(argc, argv, "h", help_only_options, NULL)`, usage "Usage: %s threads [ pool0_count ] [ pool1_count ] ..."; threads_func: `return threads_doit(sock, cmd, 0, 0, pools, pool_threads, NULL);` (scope NULL). threads_doit(..., char *scope): `if (scope) nla_put_string(msg, NFSD_A_SERVER_SCOPE, scope);`. autostart_func: `conf_get_num("nfsd", "grace-time", 0)`, `conf_get_num("nfsd", "lease-time", 0)`, `scope = conf_get_str("nfsd", "scope");`, `conf_get_list("nfsd", "threads")` (default 16) then `threads_doit(sock, NFSD_CMD_THREADS_SET, grace, lease, pools, threads, scope);`. nfsdctl.adoc: autostart "Start the server using the settings in the [nfsd] section of /etc/nfs.conf. This subcommand takes no arguments." Kernel errors are reported generically as `xlog(L_ERROR, "Error: %s", strerror(-ret))`. threads (get) prints "gracetime: %u", "leasetime: %u", "scope: %s". nfs.conf(5) (systemd/nfs.conf.man) [nfsd] values: "threads, host, scope, port, grace-time, lease-time, udp, tcp, vers3, vers4, vers4.0, vers4.1, vers4.2, rdma".

SM-NOTIFY (utils/statd/sm-notify.c + sm-notify.man): getopt "dm:np:v:P:f"; SYNOPSIS "/usr/sbin/sm-notify [-dfn] [-m minutes] [-v name] [-p notify-port] [-P path]"; `case 'P': if (!nsm_setup_pathnames(argv[0], optarg)) exit(1);`; -f sets force=1 and the guard is `if (nsm_is_default_parentdir()) { if (record_pid() == 0 && force == 0 && opt_update_state) { xlog(L_NOTICE, "Already notifying clients; Exiting!");` (so with a non-default -P the guard never applies); -n clears opt_update_state (no NSM state bump). Name selection: smn_get_host passes `m->mon_id.mon_name, m->mon_id.my_id.my_name` and smn_alloc_host sets `host->notify_arg = strdup(opt_srcaddr != NULL ? nsm_hostname : my_name);`, sent via `nsm_xmit_notify(sock, sap, salen, SM_PROG, host->notify_arg, nsm_state)`. Man page: "If this option is not specified, sm-notify uses a wildcard address as the transport bind address, and uses the my_name recorded when the remote was monitored as the mon_name argument when sending SM_NOTIFY requests." and -v "Specifies the network address from which to send reboot notifications, and the mon_name argument"; with an IP, smn_verify_my_name -> smn_get_hostname uses `getnameinfo(..., NI_NAMEREQD)` and fails with "my_name '%s' is unusable: %s"; a non-address name is used as-is (EAI_NONAME -> strdup). What my_name holds: utils/statd/monitor.c stores `my_name = argp->mon_id.my_id.my_name` as received (only whitespace replaced), and the Linux lockd fills it from fs/lockd/host.c nlm_alloc_host `strscpy(host->nodename, utsname()->nodename, sizeof(host->nodename));` passed as `.nodename = host->nodename` in fs/lockd/mon.c nsm_mon_unmon and encoded by encode_my_id. Client side (utils/statd/callback.c sm_notify_1_svc) matches `NL_STATE(lp) != argp->state && (statd_matchhostname(argp->mon_name, lp->dns_name) || statd_matchhostname(ip_addr, lp->dns_name))`, i.e. the mon_name argument or the sender's IP must match the canonical name of the server the client monitored.

RPC.STATD (utils/statd/statd.c + statd.man): getopt "h?vVFNH:dn:p:o:P:LT:U:", longopts `{ "no-notify", 0, 0, 'L' }`, `{ "notify-mode", 0, 0, 'N' }`; `case 'L': /* Listen only */ run_mode |= MODE_NO_NOTIFY;`; -N sets MODE_NOTIFY_ONLY, prints "-N deprecated, consider using /usr/sbin/sm-notify directly" and run_sm_notify() execv's "/usr/sbin/sm-notify". Man: "-L, --no-notify: Prevents rpc.statd from running the sm-notify command when it starts up, preserving the existing NSM state number and monitor list."; "-N: Causes rpc.statd to run the sm-notify command, and then exit ... deprecated". Also `conf_get_bool("statd", "no-notify", false)` and env RPC_STATD_NO_NOTIFY set the same mode.

NFSDCLD (utils/nfsdcld/nfsdcld.c, sqlite.c, nfsdcld.man): getopt "hdFp:s:", longopts pipefsdir/'p', storagedir/'s'; usage "%s [ -hFd ] [ -p pipefsdir ] [ -s storagedir ]"; defaults `DEFAULT_PIPEFS_DIR NFS_STATEDIR "/rpc_pipefs"`, `CLD_DEFAULT_STORAGEDIR NFS_STATEDIR "/nfsdcld"` (man: /var/lib/nfs/rpc_pipefs, /var/lib/nfs/nfsdcld), pipe `DEFAULT_CLD_PATH "/nfsd/cld"`; config `conf_get_str("general", "pipefs-directory")`, `conf_get_str("nfsdcld", "storagedir")`; `rc = sqlite_prepare_dbh(storagedir);` which does `snprintf(buf, PATH_MAX - 1, "%s/main.sqlite", topdir); ... sqlite3_open(buf, &dbh)` and `mkdir_if_not_exist(topdir)` on failure; man FILES "/var/lib/nfs/nfsdcld/main.sqlite", "the storagedir should be owned by root, and be readable and writable by owner". Not verified here: which UTS namespace lockd kernel threads run in (assumed the initial one, hence the physical host name) and the numeric value of UNX_MAXNODENAME.
- Corrected claim: nfs-utils 1:2.8.3-1 is the trixie version (nfs-kernel-server ships rpc.nfsd, nfsdctl, nfsdcld; nfs-common ships rpc.statd and sm-notify); trixie's kernel is linux 6.12.107-1. rpc.nfsd -S/--scope <name> (or [nfsd] scope= in nfs.conf) is implemented as unshare(CLONE_NEWUTS) followed by sethostname(scope, strlen(scope)), executed before sockets and threads are set up and only on a cold start (when nfsd is already running, rpc.nfsd jumps straight to the thread write and skips it); rpc.nfsd still uses /proc/fs/nfsd, whose write_threads path calls nfsd_svc(..., scope=NULL) so the kernel takes utsname()->nodename of the writing process. nfsdctl's threads subcommand accepts only -h/--help and always sends scope=NULL; the explicit ways to set the per-net-namespace scope are nfsdctl autostart (reads [nfsd] scope=, grace-time, lease-time, threads from /etc/nfs.conf and adds NFSD_A_SERVER_SCOPE) or a direct nfsd generic-netlink THREADS_SET carrying NFSD_A_SERVER_SCOPE (NLA_NUL_STRING, GENL_ADMIN_PERM, sent from inside the target net namespace); implicitly, any thread write (proc or netlink) made without a scope uses the caller's UTS nodename. Kernel 6.12 (v6.12 and Debian 6.12.107-1): nfsd_nl_threads_set_doit returns -EBUSY if gracetime, leasetime or scope is supplied while the server already has running threads, and nfsd_svc() unconditionally executes strscpy(nn->nfsd_name, scope ? scope : utsname()->nodename) on every call, so each later thread-count change made without a scope (rpc.nfsd N, nfsdctl threads N, any write to /proc/fs/nfsd/threads) rewrites the scope to the caller's UTS nodename; nfsd_name[UNX_MAXNODENAME+1] bounds the string and is encoded as both eir_server_scope and so_major_id in EXCHANGE_ID; `nfsdctl threads` (no arguments) prints the effective "scope:". sm-notify accepts -P <parent state directory> (nsm_setup_pathnames), -v <ipaddr|hostname> (bind address and SM_NOTIFY mon_name argument; an IP must reverse-resolve or sm-notify exits with "my_name ... is unusable"), -f (bypass the "Already notifying clients" guard, which only applies for the default state directory) and -n (do not bump the NSM state number). Without -v it sends, as the SM_NOTIFY mon_name argument, the my_name field recorded in each monitor record (notify_arg = my_name), not the record's mon_name (which is the destination peer); for a Linux server that my_name is lockd's copy of utsname()->nodename taken when the client was first monitored, i.e. the node's hostname, not an SVM name, and a Linux client statd accepts the notification only if that mon_name or the sender's IP address matches the canonical name of the server it monitored. rpc.statd's no-notify flag is -L/--no-notify (also [statd] no-notify= and env RPC_STATD_NO_NOTIFY), which skips running sm-notify at startup and preserves the NSM state number and monitor list; -N (deprecated) execs /usr/sbin/sm-notify and exits. nfsdcld accepts -p/--pipefsdir (default /var/lib/nfs/rpc_pipefs, [general] pipefs-directory; it opens <pipefs>/nfsd/cld) and -s/--storagedir (default /var/lib/nfs/nfsdcld, [nfsdcld] storagedir, must be root-owned) and sqlite_prepare_dbh() opens "<storagedir>/main.sqlite", creating the directory if needed.
- Design impact: 1) Scope lifecycle: the design must set the SVM scope exactly once per nfsd start, before any threads exist, and must treat the scope as volatile thereafter: because nfsd_svc() rewrites nn->nfsd_name from the caller's UTS nodename on every scope-less thread write, OpenTAP must never adjust a running SVM's thread count via rpc.nfsd, nfsdctl threads or /proc/fs/nfsd/threads from the host UTS namespace. Either run every nfsd control operation for an SVM inside a per-SVM UTS namespace whose hostname equals the scope (then even scope-less writes preserve it), or change thread counts only by stopping and restarting that SVM's nfsd with the scope, and have the control plane read back "scope:" via THREADS_GET / nfsdctl threads as a post-condition. Changing the scope on a live server is impossible (-EBUSY); keep it <= the UNX_MAXNODENAME buffer and byte-identical on every node, noting it also becomes so_major_id. 2) Prefer sending THREADS_SET with NFSD_A_SERVER_SCOPE directly from the Rust control plane inside the SVM's network namespace (GENL_ADMIN_PERM) rather than nfsdctl autostart, which only reads the global /etc/nfs.conf (per-SVM use would need a private mount namespace); if rpc.nfsd is used, document that --scope is honoured only on a cold start. 3) NFSv3 lock recovery after an SVM move: the stored my_name is the old node's hostname, so sm-notify must be invoked as `sm-notify -P <SVM state dir> -v <SVM hostname resolving to the SVM address> [-f]` (not bare `sm-notify -P`), with the SVM name resolvable (reverse DNS or /etc/hosts if an IP is given), so that both the mon_name argument and the source address match what clients monitored; start the SVM's rpc.statd with -L -P <SVM state dir> (plus -n <svm-name>) and run sm-notify explicitly after the state directory has been moved with the volume; do not pass -n so the NSM state number is bumped. 4) nfsdcld per SVM: run it with -s <SVM root volume>/nfsdcld (root-owned, main.sqlite travels with the volume) and -p pointing at an rpc_pipefs mounted inside the SVM's network namespace, started before that namespace's nfsd. 5) The flags themselves (-P/-v/-f, -L/-N, -p/-s) need no change in the document; replace the phrase "uses the mon_name recorded at monitor time" with "uses the recorded my_name (the server-side node's UTS hostname) as the SM_NOTIFY mon_name".

### [C15] CONFIRMED
- Claim: systemd 257.13-1~deb13u1 in Debian trixie provides NetworkNamespacePath= (joins the network namespace referenced by an absolute path to a netns pseudo-file, system services only, overriding PrivateNetwork=) and ProtectHostname= as a boolean only (sets up a new UTS namespace and blocks sethostname; no 'private' value), but offers no unit directive to join an existing mount namespace or UTS namespace by path, so joining all three pinned namespaces requires an ExecStart wrapper such as nsenter --net= --uts= --mount= from util-linux 2.41.5-0+deb13u1.
- Raised by: Opus-Protocols, Opus-Consensus
- Why it matters: Determines how SVM transient units enter their namespaces (nsenter wrapper versus native directives), whether warm-standby skeleton units can pre-join a netns by path, and that ProtectHostname= cannot be used as the UTS namespace for rpc.nfsd --scope (sethostname would fail).
- Summary: Every operative statement checks out against the trixie-shipped systemd 257.13-1~deb13u1 sources and man pages: NetworkNamespacePath= joins a netns by absolute pseudo-file path and makes PrivateNetwork= a no-op; ProtectHostname= is parsed with config_parse_bool, does unshare(CLONE_NEWUTS) plus a seccomp filter returning EPERM for sethostname/setdomainname, and the 'private[:hostname]' value only arrived in v258; the only *NamespacePath= directives in 257.13 are NetworkNamespacePath= and IPCNamespacePath=, and JoinsNamespaceOf= covers only network/IPC/tmp between units, so mount and UTS namespaces can be joined by path only via a wrapper such as nsenter (util-linux 2.41.5-0+deb13u1 in trixie, /usr/bin/nsenter, --mount=/--uts=/--net=file). Two precision points: the directives are available to system services or to user-manager services with implicit PrivateUsers= (not strictly 'system only'), and 2.41.5-0+deb13u1 reached trixie as a security/point update (13.0 shipped 2.41-5, same nsenter syntax). Bonus finding that sharpens the 'why it matters': rpc.nfsd --scope in nfs-utils 2.8.3 does its own unshare(CLONE_NEWUTS)+sethostname(), so it fails under ProtectHostname=yes but also never uses a pre-pinned UTS namespace; nfsdctl (shipped in trixie's nfs-kernel-server) passes the scope via the nfsd netlink NFSD_A_SERVER_SCOPE attribute on 6.12, needing no UTS namespace at all.
- Evidence: VERSIONS. tracker.debian.org/pkg/systemd: stable = "257.13-1~deb13u1" (testing/unstable 262-1; no trixie-backports entry). packages.debian.org/trixie/systemd: "Package: systemd (257.13-1~deb13u1)", suite "trixie (stable)". packages.debian.org/trixie/util-linux: "Package: util-linux (2.41.5-0+deb13u1)", "trixie (stable)"; tracker.debian.org/pkg/util-linux lists stable "2.41-5", stable-sec "2.41.5-0+deb13u1", and "Accepted util-linux 2.41.5-0+deb13u1 (source) into proposed-updates" (2026-08-18), i.e. the 13.0 release shipped 2.41-5 and 2.41.5 came via security/point update. util-linux trixie amd64 filelist contains "/usr/bin/nsenter" and "/usr/share/man/man1/nsenter.1.gz".

NetworkNamespacePath= (systemd.exec.xml at tag v257.13, byte-identical by diff to sources.debian.org systemd/257.13-1~deb13u1/man/systemd.exec.xml): "Takes an absolute file system path referring to a Linux network namespace pseudo-file (i.e. a file like /proc/$PID/ns/net or a bind mount or symlink to one). When set the invoked processes are added to the network namespace referenced by that path. The path has to point to a valid namespace file at the moment the processes are forked off. If this option is used PrivateNetwork= has no effect." ... "When this option is enabled, PrivateMounts= is implied unless it is explicitly disabled, and /sys will be remounted to associate it with the new network namespace." ... "When this option is used on a socket unit any sockets bound on behalf of this unit will be bound within the specified network namespace." Added in version 242. Availability include (man/system-or-user-ns.xml, 'singular'): "This option is only available for system services, or for services running in per-user instances of the service manager in which case PrivateUsers= is implicitly enabled (requires unprivileged user namespaces support ... kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone= sysctl)." NEWS v242: "A new unit setting NetworkNamespacePath= may be used to specify a namespace for service or socket units through a path referring to a Linux network namespace pseudo-file."

ProtectHostname= (same 257.13 man XML): "Takes a boolean argument. When set, sets up a new UTS namespace for the executed processes. In addition, changing hostname or domainname is prevented. Defaults to off." ... "Note that the implementation of this setting might be impossible (for example if UTS namespaces are not available), and the unit should be written in a way that does not solely rely on this setting for security." Added in version 242. Parser, src/core/load-fragment-gperf.gperf.in v257.13 line 183: "{{type}}.ProtectHostname, config_parse_bool, 0, offsetof({{type}}, exec_context.protect_hostname)"; v258 line 195 changes it to "config_parse_protect_hostname". Implementation, src/core/exec-invoke.c v257.13 apply_protect_hostname(): "if (unshare(CLONE_NEWUTS) < 0) { ... log_exec_warning(... "ProtectHostname=yes is configured, but UTS namespace setup is prohibited (container manager?), ignoring namespace setup.")" then "r = seccomp_protect_hostname();". src/shared/seccomp-util.c v257.13 seccomp_protect_hostname(): seccomp_rule_add_exact(seccomp, SCMP_ACT_ERRNO(EPERM), SCMP_SYS(sethostname), 0) and likewise SCMP_SYS(setdomainname). NEWS at tag v258, section "CHANGES WITH 258": "The ProtectHostname= unit setting now accepts a new value "private", which is similar to "yes", but allows the unit's processes to modify the hostname. Since a UTC namespace is allocated for the unit this hostname change remains local to the unit ... Optionally, the "private" string may be suffixed by a colon and a literal hostname specification, which is then used to initialize the hostname of the namespace to."

NO MOUNT/UTS PATH DIRECTIVE. grep -o '[A-Za-z]*NamespacePath=' over the 257.13 systemd.exec.xml (both upstream and Debian copies) yields only NetworkNamespacePath= and IPCNamespacePath=; grep for MountNamespacePath|UTSNamespacePath|PIDNamespacePath|UserNamespacePath|CgroupNamespacePath returns nothing. The gperf directive table in 257.13 has only NetworkNamespacePath and IPCNamespacePath (config_parse_unit_path_printf). manpages.debian.org trixie systemd.unit(5) (footer "systemd 257.13") JoinsNamespaceOf=: "lists one or more other units whose network and/or temporary file namespace to join ... its processes will see the same /tmp/, /var/tmp/, IPC namespace and network namespace as one listed unit" — no mount or UTS namespace, and unit-to-unit only, not by path.

NSENTER. util-linux v2.41 sys-utils/nsenter.1.adoc and manpages.debian.org trixie nsenter(1) (trixie 2.41.5-0+deb13u1): "-m, --mount[=file] Enter the mount namespace. If no file is specified, enter the mount namespace of the target process. If file is specified, enter the mount namespace specified by file." Same wording for "-u, --uts[=file]" and "-n, --net[=file]". file "should be one of the /proc/[pid]/ns/* files described in namespaces(7) or the pathname of a bind mount that was created on one of those files." nsenter.c v2.41: enable_namespace(nstype, path) -> enable_nsfile -> open_target_fd() opens the file at option-parse time; enter_namespaces() later calls setns() per fd in table order user, cgroup, ipc, uts, net, pid, mnt (mount last), so all three paths resolve in the caller's mount namespace before any switch.

RPC.NFSD --scope (why-it-matters check). manpages.debian.org trixie rpc.nfsd(8) (nfs-kernel-server 1:2.8.3-1): "By default Linux NFSD uses the host name as the scope." nfs-utils 1:2.8.3-1 utils/nfsd/nfsd.c lines 396-402: "if (scope) { if (unshare(CLONE_NEWUTS) < 0 || sethostname(scope, strlen(scope)) < 0) { xlog(L_ERROR, "Unable to set server scope: %m"); error = -1; goto out; } }" — under ProtectHostname=yes sethostname returns EPERM and rpc.nfsd aborts. Kernel linux-6.12.y (Makefile 6.12.112) fs/nfsd/nfssvc.c nfsd_svc(): "strscpy(nn->nfsd_name, scope ? scope : utsname()->nodename, sizeof(nn->nfsd_name));" with nfsctl.c:434 (the /proc/fs/nfsd/threads path) passing NULL and nfsctl.c:1743-1774 (netlink threads-set) taking scope from info->attrs[NFSD_A_SERVER_SCOPE]; nfs4xdr.c encodes nn->nfsd_name as eir_server_scope and so_major_id. nfs-utils 2.8.3 utils/nfsdctl/nfsdctl.c:541-542: "if (scope) nla_put_string(msg, NFSD_A_SERVER_SCOPE, scope);" and trixie's nfs-kernel-server filelist includes "/usr/sbin/nfsdctl".
- Corrected claim: Debian 13 trixie ships systemd 257.13-1~deb13u1. Its systemd.exec(5) provides NetworkNamespacePath= (an absolute path to a network-namespace pseudo-file, bind mount or symlink to one, which must exist at fork time; the unit's processes are added to that netns; PrivateNetwork= then has no effect; PrivateMounts= is implied and /sys is remounted; it also applies to socket units; available to system services, or to user-manager services with implicitly enabled PrivateUsers=) and ProtectHostname= as a boolean only (config_parse_bool; unshare(CLONE_NEWUTS) into a fresh UTS namespace plus a seccomp filter returning EPERM for sethostname() and setdomainname(); best-effort if UTS namespacing is unavailable). The 'private[:hostname]' value was introduced in systemd 258 and is not in trixie (no trixie-backports build is listed). The only path-joining directives in 257.13 are NetworkNamespacePath= and IPCNamespacePath=; JoinsNamespaceOf= shares only network, IPC and /tmp namespaces between units. There is no directive to join an existing mount or UTS namespace by path, so joining all three pinned namespaces requires an ExecStart wrapper, e.g. nsenter --net=FILE --uts=FILE --mount=FILE from util-linux 2.41.5-0+deb13u1 (/usr/bin/nsenter; trixie 13.0 shipped 2.41-5 with identical nsenter syntax; nsenter opens all namespace files before calling setns() and enters the mount namespace last), or NetworkNamespacePath= for the netns combined with nsenter --uts= --mount= for the other two. Note that rpc.nfsd --scope (nfs-utils 1:2.8.3-1) itself calls unshare(CLONE_NEWUTS) then sethostname(scope); it therefore fails ("Unable to set server scope") under ProtectHostname=yes, and it never uses a pre-existing pinned UTS namespace; the 6.12 kernel copies the scope (or the starting process's UTS nodename) into nn->nfsd_name once at server start, and nfsdctl (also in trixie's nfs-kernel-server) can pass the scope directly via the nfsd netlink NFSD_A_SERVER_SCOPE attribute with no UTS namespace or sethostname at all.
- Design impact: No change to the claim's conclusions: SVM transient units must use an nsenter (or equivalent setns(2)) wrapper for the mount and UTS namespaces; warm-standby skeleton units may declare NetworkNamespacePath= natively as long as the netns pseudo-file exists when the unit is actually started (not when it is loaded); ProtectHostname= must not be set on any unit that runs rpc.nfsd --scope. Refinements the design should absorb: (1) Decide between all-nsenter and the hybrid NetworkNamespacePath= + nsenter --uts= --mount=; the hybrid lets socket units bind inside the SVM netns, but NetworkNamespacePath= implies PrivateMounts=, and any systemd mount-based sandboxing (PrivateMounts=, ProtectSystem=, ReadOnlyPaths=, PrivateTmp=, BindPaths=) is discarded the moment the wrapper does setns into the pinned mount namespace, so sandboxing must be built into the pinned mount namespace itself and /run/systemd/notify must be reachable there for Type=notify. (2) setns() needs CAP_SYS_ADMIN in the owning user namespace, so the unit must run as root or keep CAP_SYS_ADMIN in its bounding/ambient set at exec time; nsenter execs in place (no fork unless a PID namespace is entered), so MainPID remains the real service. (3) The pinned UTS namespace is not what gives rpc.nfsd its scope: rpc.nfsd --scope unshares its own UTS namespace, and the legacy /proc/fs/nfsd/threads path uses the writing process's nodename at start time only. Prefer nfsdctl's netlink scope attribute (6.12 + nfs-utils 2.8.3), which removes the UTS-namespace requirement for NFS scope entirely and is immune to ProtectHostname=; keep the pinned UTS namespace only if something else (e.g. Samba netbios/hostname, ublk or LIO identity strings) needs a per-SVM nodename. (4) Do not plan on ProtectHostname=private[:name] until a systemd >= 258 is available for trixie. (5) Pin the util-linux dependency as >= 2.41 rather than exactly 2.41.5-0+deb13u1, since 13.0 media carry 2.41-5 with the same nsenter behaviour.
