### [C26] REFUTED
- Claim: On Linux 6.12, IORING_OP_SEND_ZC on a socket with the kernel TLS ULP in software mode (tls_sw) does not achieve zero copy: tls_sw_sendmsg copies plaintext into its own encryption scatterlist before transmission, so IORING_CQE_F_NOTIF arrives after that copy and the user buffer is never referenced by the NIC.
- Raised by: Opus-Fabrics, Opus-Storage
- Why it matters: If kTLS software mode copies, 'optional TLS' on the replication transport costs a full copy plus AES-GCM per byte (roughly 0.5 to 1 core per GB/s) and changes the hold-release semantics, which the Phase B CPU budget must reflect.
- Summary: The bottom line (no zero copy, NIC never touches the user buffer) is right, but the described mechanism does not occur on 6.12: IORING_OP_SEND_ZC/SENDMSG_ZC on a kTLS socket fail with -EOPNOTSUPP before any sendmsg, because setsockopt(TCP_ULP,"tls") runs __tcp_set_ulp(), which clears SOCK_SUPPORT_ZC, and io_send_zc() rejects sockets without that bit (tls_sw_sendmsg() would independently reject the MSG_ZEROCOPY flag io_uring always sets). This applies to both software and device-offload kTLS, and the notification CQE that still arrives reports nothing sent. Separately, tls_sw_sendmsg_locked() does not always copy plaintext: for non-kvec writes that complete a record or carry no MSG_MORE (while the AEAD has not gone async) it pins the user pages straight into the AEAD input scatterlist and only the ciphertext lands in kernel pages; the memcpy path is used for partial-record/MSG_MORE/kvec writes or after the AEAD returns -EINPROGRESS.
- Evidence: 1) Gate in io_uring (v6.12 io_uring/net.c): io_send_zc() and io_sendmsg_zc() both do "if (!test_bit(SOCK_SUPPORT_ZC, &sock->flags)) return -EOPNOTSUPP;" immediately after sock_from_file(), before io_send_zc_import() and before "kmsg->msg.msg_ubuf = &io_notif_to_data(zc->notif)->uarg; ret = sock_sendmsg(sock, &kmsg->msg);". io_send_zc_prep() sets "zc->msg_flags = READ_ONCE(sqe->msg_flags) | MSG_NOSIGNAL | MSG_ZEROCOPY;" and allocates the notif ("notif = zc->notif = io_alloc_notif(ctx);"). The stable backport of upstream edf81438799ccead7122948446d7e44b083e788d ("io_uring/net: fail zc send when unsupported by socket") explains the intent: when a protocol lacks zerocopy support the kernel used to silently fall back to copying; the patch makes such requests fail instead.
2) kTLS removes the bit (v6.12 net/ipv4/tcp_ulp.c, __tcp_set_ulp, between the icsk_ulp_ops check and the TCP_LISTEN check): "if (sk->sk_socket) clear_bit(SOCK_SUPPORT_ZC, &sk->sk_socket->flags);" — added by commit e276d62dcfdee6582486e8b8344dd869518e14be "net/ulp: remove SOCK_SUPPORT_ZC from tls sockets" (Pavel Begunkov; Fixes e993ffe3da4b; Cc stable 6.0): "Remove SOCK_SUPPORT_ZC when we're setting ulp as it might not support msghdr::ubuf_info". The bit is set in tcp_init_sock()/udp_init_sock() by commit e993ffe3da4bcddea0536b03be1031bf35cd8d85 ("set_bit(SOCK_SUPPORT_ZC, &sk->sk_socket->flags);") and propagated to accepted sockets in __inet_accept() ("if (test_bit(SOCK_SUPPORT_ZC, &sock->flags)) set_bit(SOCK_SUPPORT_ZC, &newsock->flags);"). tls_main.c: tcp_tls_ulp_ops has .name = "tls", .init = tls_init, and tls_init swaps the protocol via update_sk_prot(); build_protos sets "prot[TLS_SW][TLS_BASE].sendmsg = tls_sw_sendmsg;" and "prot[TLS_HW][TLS_BASE].sendmsg = tls_device_sendmsg;". Because the clear happens at TCP_ULP time, before TLS_TX picks "rc = tls_set_device_offload(sk); conf = TLS_HW" or "rc = tls_set_sw_offload(sk, 1); conf = TLS_SW", SEND_ZC fails in both modes.
3) Second, independent gate (v6.12 net/tls/tls_sw.c, tls_sw_sendmsg): "if (msg->msg_flags & ~(MSG_MORE | MSG_DONTWAIT | MSG_NOSIGNAL | MSG_CMSG_COMPAT | MSG_SPLICE_PAGES | MSG_EOR | MSG_SENDPAGE_NOPOLICY)) return -EOPNOTSUPP;". MSG_ZEROCOPY (0x4000000) is not in that list, and io_uring's mask "msg_flags &= ~MSG_INTERNAL_SENDMSG_FLAGS" only strips "(MSG_SPLICE_PAGES | MSG_SENDPAGE_NOPOLICY | MSG_SENDPAGE_DECRYPTED)" (include/linux/socket.h), so MSG_ZEROCOPY would reach tls_sw_sendmsg and be rejected even if the first gate were absent.
4) What the failed request posts: io_sendrecv_fail() sets "req->cqe.flags |= IORING_CQE_F_MORE" for failed SEND_ZC/SENDMSG_ZC requests that have REQ_F_NEED_CLEANUP (notif allocated at prep), and io_send_zc_cleanup() calls io_notif_flush(zc->notif), so a NOTIF CQE still arrives; with IORING_SEND_ZC_REPORT_USAGE, io_notif_tw_complete() does "if (unlikely(nd->zc_report) && (nd->zc_copied || !nd->zc_used)) notif->cqe.res |= IORING_NOTIF_USAGE_ZC_COPIED;" (zc_used is only set on a successful skb completion), so the suggested empirical check would show res = -EOPNOTSUPP on the first CQE and ZC_COPIED on the notification, not a copy-then-send.
5) The plain (non-ZC) TLS path does not always copy (v6.12 tls_sw_sendmsg_locked): "bool is_kvec = iov_iter_is_kvec(&msg->msg_iter);", "bool eor = !(msg->msg_flags & MSG_MORE);", "bool async_capable = ctx->async_capable;"; "if (!is_kvec && (full_record || eor) && !async_capable) {" -> "ret = sk_msg_zerocopy_from_iter(sk, &msg->msg_iter, msg_pl, try_to_copy);" (net/core/skmsg.c pins pages with "copied = iov_iter_get_pages2(from, pages, bytes, maxpages, ..."); on failure "goto fallback_to_reg_send;". Otherwise "ret = tls_clone_plaintext_msg(sk, required_size);" (which is "return sk_msg_clone(sk, msg_pl, msg_en, skip, len);", i.e. plaintext shares the encryption buffer pages, encrypted in place) followed by "ret = sk_msg_memcopy_from_iter(sk, &msg->msg_iter, msg_pl, try_to_copy);" ("copy_from_iter_nocache"/"copy_from_iter"). TX async_capable is only set lazily: tls_push_record does "ctx->async_capable = 1;" after the AEAD returns -EINPROGRESS; tls_set_sw_offload sets only the RX flag. Encryption always reads msg_pl and writes msg_en: "sg_chain(rec->sg_aead_in, 2, &msg_pl->sg.data[i]);", "sg_chain(rec->sg_aead_out, 2, &msg_en->sg.data[i]);", "aead_request_set_crypt(aead_req, rec->sg_aead_in, rec->sg_aead_out, ...)". Before returning, sendmsg waits for any async encryption: "/* Wait for pending encryptions to get completed */ err = tls_encrypt_async_wait(ctx);". Ciphertext pages are handed to TCP by tls_push_sg() in tls_main.c (".msg_flags = MSG_SPLICE_PAGES | flags,", "bvec_set_page(&bvec, p, size, offset);", "ret = tcp_sendmsg_locked(sk, &msg, size);", then "put_page(p);"), and tls_tx_records() then runs "list_del(&rec->list); sk_msg_free(sk, &rec->msg_plaintext); kfree(rec);". So the NIC only ever sees kernel ciphertext pages, and the user buffer is consumed before sendmsg returns.
6) Documentation/networking/tls.rst (v6.12) matches: "send() data is directly encrypted from the userspace buffer provided to the encrypted kernel send buffer if possible."; "The kernel will need to allocate a buffer for the encrypted data."; TLS_TX_ZEROCOPY_RO is "For device offload only. Allow sendfile() data to be transmitted directly to the NIC without making an in-kernel copy. This allows true zero-copy behavior when device offload is enabled."
7) io_uring_prep_send_zc(3): the NOTIF CQE "tells the application that the memory associated with the send is safe to get reused"; with REPORT_USAGE "the notification CQE res field will report ... IORING_NOTIF_USAGE_ZC_COPIED" when data was copied.
8) Platform: packages.debian.org lists trixie linux-image-amd64 "6.12.111-1" depending on "linux-image-6.12.111+deb13-amd64", so the 6.12 sources above are the shipped kernel. Note: git.kernel.org's plain endpoint returned 403 and elixir's ident page returned only its version index, so the v6.12 files were read from GitHub's mirror of Linus's tree at tag v6.12 and the commits from github.com/torvalds/linux.
- Corrected claim: On Linux 6.12 (Debian 13's 6.12.x kernel), IORING_OP_SEND_ZC and IORING_OP_SENDMSG_ZC cannot be used on a kTLS socket in either software or device-offload mode: setsockopt(TCP_ULP, "tls") runs __tcp_set_ulp(), which clears SOCK_SUPPORT_ZC on the socket, and io_send_zc()/io_sendmsg_zc() fail with -EOPNOTSUPP before calling sendmsg (tls_sw_sendmsg() would independently reject the MSG_ZEROCOPY flag io_uring always sets). The failed request still posts a notification CQE (IORING_CQE_F_NOTIF; with IORING_SEND_ZC_REPORT_USAGE its res carries IORING_NOTIF_USAGE_ZC_COPIED), but nothing is sent. kTLS connections must therefore use plain IORING_OP_SEND/SENDMSG. On that path tls_sw_sendmsg_locked() either pins the user pages directly into the AEAD input scatterlist (iovec/ubuf iterators, when the write completes a 16 KiB record or ends a message without MSG_MORE, and the AEAD has not previously returned -EINPROGRESS) or copies the plaintext into the record's encryption buffer (partial-record/MSG_MORE writes, kvec iterators, or once the socket's AEAD has gone asynchronous); in both cases AES-GCM writes the ciphertext into kernel-allocated pages that are spliced into TCP, so the NIC never references the user buffer. The plaintext is fully consumed (copied, or pinned and encrypted with any asynchronous encryption awaited) before sendmsg returns, so the buffer is reusable at the send CQE with no second notification and no hold period. "True zero-copy" kTLS transmit exists only for device offload with sendfile/splice data under TLS_TX_ZEROCOPY_RO.
- Design impact: 1) The replication transport must select the send opcode per connection: SEND_ZC/SENDMSG_ZC only on plaintext TCP; plain SEND/SENDMSG on kTLS connections. Treat -EOPNOTSUPP from a ZC send as a configuration error, not a transient one; the kernel deliberately refuses rather than falling back to a copy. 2) Buffer-lifetime (hold/release) rules diverge by mode in the opposite direction from the claim: plaintext SEND_ZC = hold the buffer until the NOTIF CQE (NIC may reference it until TCP ACK); kTLS SEND = buffer released at the send CQE, no NOTIF. If the design wants one lifecycle state machine, model the kTLS CQE as "sent and released"; do not wait for a notification that never comes. 3) Phase B CPU budget for the TLS option: one AES-GCM pass over every byte is unavoidable; the extra memcpy is avoidable for writes that complete a TLS record (16 KiB plaintext) or end a message without MSG_MORE from iovec/ubuf buffers, but is incurred for partial-record/MSG_MORE writes and for the whole socket lifetime once the AEAD has gone asynchronous (tls_push_record latches async_capable=1). Size and align replication writes to record boundaries and avoid MSG_MORE if the copy matters. The "0.5 to 1 core per GB/s" figure was not verified here; measure AES-GCM throughput on the target CPUs rather than budgeting from that number. 4) Acceptance test to encode: SEND_ZC with IORING_SEND_ZC_REPORT_USAGE on a kTLS socket must yield a first CQE with res = -EOPNOTSUPP and IORING_CQE_F_MORE, followed by a NOTIF CQE with IORING_NOTIF_USAGE_ZC_COPIED set; plain SEND on the same socket must succeed. 5) Device-offload kTLS does not change any of the above for SEND_ZC; it only matters for sendfile/splice data under TLS_TX_ZEROCOPY_RO.
- Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/io_uring/net.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/net/ipv4/tcp_ulp.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/net/tls/tls_sw.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/net/tls/tls_main.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/net/core/skmsg.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/io_uring/notif.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/include/linux/socket.h ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/include/linux/net.h ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/net/ipv4/af_inet.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/Documentation/networking/tls.rst ; https://github.com/torvalds/linux/commit/e276d62dcfdee6582486e8b8344dd869518e14be ; https://github.com/torvalds/linux/commit/e993ffe3da4bcddea0536b03be1031bf35cd8d85 ; https://lkml.iu.edu/hypermail/linux/kernel/2210.3/00493.html ; https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man3/io_uring_prep_send_zc.3.html ; https://packages.debian.org/trixie/linux-image-amd64

### [C27] PARTIALLY-CORRECT
- Claim: In Linux 6.12 the qla2xxx module parameter qlini_mode accepts exclusive, disabled, enabled (default) and dual (qla_target.c); the per-host sysfs attribute qlini_mode (qla_attr.c, DEVICE_ATTR_RW) is visible only when the module-wide mode is dual; writing it calls qla_set_ini_mode, which refuses with 'Target Mode is active. Unable to change Mode' while target mode is active and otherwise sets ISP_ABORT_NEEDED; qlt_enable_vha performs an ISP abort for a physical port but only qla24xx_disable_vp/qla24xx_enable_vp for a vport; and qlt_lport_register refuses a physical port whose qlini_mode is QLA2XXX_INI_MODE_ENABLED.
- Raised by: Opus-Fabrics
- Why it matters: The Phase C profile (module-wide qlini_mode=disabled), the single-role port arrangement, the rule that physical TPGs are enabled once at boot and never toggled, and the no-reset NPIV create/delete cycle depend on it.
- Summary: Four of the five sub-claims are confirmed verbatim in Linux v6.12 (and byte-identical in Debian trixie's linux 6.12.107-1): the module parameter and its four values with "enabled" as default, the DEVICE_ATTR_RW per-host attribute hidden unless the module-wide mode is dual, qlini_mode_store calling qla_set_ini_mode, and qlt_enable_vha doing a base-port ISP abort for vp_idx 0 but only qla24xx_disable_vp/qla24xx_enable_vp for a vport. Two parts are oversimplified: qla_set_ini_mode refuses with "Target Mode is active. Unable to change Mode." only for a change TO "enabled" while target (or dual) mode is active, accepts other transitions even with target mode active, sets ISP_ABORT_NEEDED only in the MODE_CHANGE_ACCEPT branch (MODE_CHANGE_NO_ACTION/NO_ACTION do not), and the store returns success even when refused; and qlt_lport_register skips any host (physical or NPIV) whose per-host vha->qlini_mode is ENABLED (not a module-wide check), plus a physical registration is also skipped when target mode is already active on that host.
- Evidence: All line numbers are from the v6.12 tag (torvalds/linux mirror); the Debian trixie copies (linux 6.12.107-1, the current trixie version per sources.debian.org; 6.12.111-1 is in trixie-proposed-updates) were diffed function-by-function and are IDENTICAL for qlt_lport_register, qlt_enable_vha, qlt_disable_vha, qlt_set_mode, qlt_clear_mode, qlt_parse_ini_mode, qla_set_ini_mode, qlini_mode_show/store, qla_host_attr_is_visible, tcm_qla2xxx_enable_tpg, tcm_qla2xxx_npiv_enable_tpg and tcm_qla2xxx_lport_register_npiv_cb.

1. Module parameter (qla_target.c:39-49, 58, 7242-7270, 7310-7313). "static char *qlini_mode = QLA2XXX_INI_MODE_STR_ENABLED; module_param(qlini_mode, charp, S_IRUGO);" MODULE_PARM_DESC: "\"exclusive\" - initiator mode will be enabled on load, disabled on enabling target mode and then on disabling target mode enabled back; \"disabled\" - initiator mode will never be enabled; \"dual\" - Initiator Modes will be enabled. Target Mode can be activated when ready \"enabled\" (default) - initiator mode will always stay enabled." qlt_parse_ini_mode uses strcasecmp against QLA2XXX_INI_MODE_STR_EXCLUSIVE/DISABLED/ENABLED/DUAL and "else return false"; qlt_init: "if (!qlt_parse_ini_mode()) { ql_log(ql_log_fatal, NULL, 0xe06b, \"qlt_parse_ini_mode() failed\\n\"); return -EINVAL; }" and ends "Return 1 to signal that initiator-mode is being disabled ... return (ql2x_ini_mode == QLA2XXX_INI_MODE_DISABLED) ? 1 : 0;". S_IRUGO means the module-wide value is read-only after load. qla_target.h: EXCLUSIVE=0, DISABLED=1, ENABLED=2, DUAL=3; "#define QLA_TGT_MODE_ENABLED() (ql2x_ini_mode != QLA2XXX_INI_MODE_ENABLED)".

2. Per-host attribute and visibility (qla_attr.c:2463, 2517, 2523-2537). "static DEVICE_ATTR_RW(qlini_mode);" listed in qla2x00_host_attrs[]; "static umode_t qla_host_attr_is_visible(...) { if (ql2x_ini_mode != QLA2XXX_INI_MODE_DUAL && (attr == &dev_attr_qlini_mode.attr || attr == &dev_attr_ql2xiniexchg.attr || attr == &dev_attr_ql2xexchoffld.attr)) return 0; return attr->mode; }" with ".is_visible = qla_host_attr_is_visible". The driver's own message names the path: "/sys/class/scsi_host/host%ld/qlini_mode" (qla_attr.c:2286). The per-host field is "uint16_t qlini_mode;" in struct scsi_qla_host (qla_def.h:5092), initialised in qla2x00_create_host (qla_os.c:5074) "vha->qlini_mode = ql2x_ini_mode;", which is used for the base host and for NPIV vports (qla_mid.c:502 qla24xx_create_vhost -> qla2x00_create_host).

3. Store path (qla_attr.c:2246-2272). qlini_mode_store matches "exclusive"/"disabled"/"enabled"/"dual" with strncasecmp, "else return -EINVAL;", then "qla_set_ini_mode(vha, ini); return strlen(buf);" - it returns success regardless of what qla_set_ini_mode decided.

4. qla_set_ini_mode (qla_attr.c:1969-2244). Actions enum: NO_ACTION, MODE_CHANGE_ACCEPT, MODE_CHANGE_NO_ACTION, TARGET_STILL_ACTIVE. TARGET_STILL_ACTIVE is assigned in exactly three places, all for op == QLA2XXX_INI_MODE_ENABLED: from DISABLED "if (qla_tgt_mode_enabled(vha)) action = TARGET_STILL_ACTIVE;", from EXCLUSIVE same condition, from DUAL "if (qla_tgt_mode_enabled(vha) || qla_dual_mode_enabled(vha)) { action = TARGET_STILL_ACTIVE; }". Transitions accepted while target mode is active include disabled->dual ("/* active_mode is target only, reset it to dual */ ... set_mode = 1; action = MODE_CHANGE_ACCEPT;"), exclusive->dual, dual->disabled ("/* turning off initiator mode */ set_mode = 1; action = MODE_CHANGE_ACCEPT;"), dual->exclusive, and same-mode rewrites when exchange-offload settings changed. Final switch: MODE_CHANGE_ACCEPT logs "Mode change accepted. From %s to %s ...", then "vha->qlini_mode = op; ... if (set_mode) qlt_set_mode(vha); vha->flags.online = 1; set_bit(ISP_ABORT_NEEDED, &vha->dpc_flags);"; MODE_CHANGE_NO_ACTION logs "Mode is set. No action taken. ..." and updates vha->qlini_mode and exchange counts WITHOUT setting ISP_ABORT_NEEDED; TARGET_STILL_ACTIVE logs "Target Mode is active. Unable to change Mode.\n" and changes nothing; NO_ACTION/default logs "Mode unchange. No action taken. ...". Also exclusive->enabled with target inactive but "vha->hw->flags.fw_started" is MODE_CHANGE_NO_ACTION (no abort).

5. qlt_enable_vha (qla_target.c:6641-6686, comment "host_reset, bring up w/ Target Mode Enabled"). "if (vha->qlini_mode == QLA2XXX_INI_MODE_ENABLED) return;" then under hardware_lock "tgt->tgt_stopped = 0; qlt_set_mode(vha);" then under optrom_mutex: "if (vha->vp_idx) { qla24xx_disable_vp(vha); qla24xx_enable_vp(vha); } else { set_bit(ISP_ABORT_NEEDED, &base_vha->dpc_flags); qla2xxx_wake_dpc(base_vha); WARN_ON_ONCE(qla2x00_wait_for_hba_online(base_vha) != QLA_SUCCESS); }". qlt_set_mode (6604-6620): DISABLED/EXCLUSIVE -> "vha->host->active_mode = MODE_TARGET", ENABLED -> MODE_INITIATOR, DUAL -> MODE_DUAL; qlt_clear_mode (6623-6639): DISABLED -> MODE_UNKNOWN, EXCLUSIVE/ENABLED/DUAL -> MODE_INITIATOR. qla24xx_disable_vp (qla_mid.c:163-204): "if (vha->hw->flags.fw_started) ret = qla24xx_control_vp(vha, VCE_COMMAND_DISABLE_VPS_LOGO_ALL);", marks loop down, waits for session deletion, FC_VPORT_DISABLED. qla24xx_enable_vp (206-245): "Check if physical ha port is Up ... LOOP_DOWN || LOOP_DEAD || !(ha->current_topology & ISP_CFG_F)" -> FC_VPORT_LINKDOWN, "skip enable"; else qla24xx_modify_vp_config. A base-port ISP abort also runs qla2x00_vp_abort_isp(vp) on every vport (qla_init.c:7671 inside qla2x00_abort_isp), which issues VCE_COMMAND_DISABLE_VPS_LOGO_ALL and re-enables the vport ("Physical port will do most of the abort and recovery work").

6. qlt_lport_register (qla_target.c:6515-6580). Loop over qla_tgt_glist (all targets, physical and NPIV): "if (!(host->hostt->supported_mode & MODE_TARGET)) continue; if (vha->qlini_mode == QLA2XXX_INI_MODE_ENABLED) continue;" then "if ((!npiv_wwpn || !npiv_wwnn) && host->active_mode & MODE_TARGET) { pr_debug(\"MODE_TARGET already active on qla2xxx(%d)\\n\", ...); continue; } if (tgt->tgt_stop) { pr_debug(\"MODE_TARGET in shutdown ...\"); continue; }", then WWPN match "memcmp(vha->port_name, b, WWN_SIZE)" and callback; no match -> "return -ENODEV". The check is the per-host field, not ql2x_ini_mode.

7. Call sites (tcm_qla2xxx.c): tcm_qla2xxx_enable_tpg (908-934) and tcm_qla2xxx_npiv_enable_tpg (1051-1077): enable -> "qlt_enable_vha(vha);", disable -> "qlt_stop_phase1(...); qlt_stop_phase2(...);". qlt_stop_phase1 ends with "/* Big hammer */ if (!ha->flags.host_shutting_down && (qla_tgt_mode_enabled(vha) || qla_dual_mode_enabled(vha))) qlt_disable_vha(vha);" and qlt_disable_vha (6692-6718) does qlt_clear_mode then "set_bit(ISP_ABORT_NEEDED, &vha->dpc_flags); qla2xxx_wake_dpc(vha);" and waits for HBA online. tcm_qla2xxx_lport_register_npiv_cb (1660-1686) requires "!qla_ini_mode_enabled(base_vha)" and "base_lport->tpg_1 ... lport_tpg_enabled" before fc_vport_create. qla_os.c:3586-3591: scsi_scan_host only "if (qla_ini_mode_enabled(base_vha) || qla_dual_mode_enabled(base_vha))", otherwise "skipping scsi_scan_host() for non-initiator port"; qla2x00_do_dpc (7036-7057) services ISP_ABORT_NEEDED only on base_vha->dpc_flags, and for base qlini_mode DISABLED "if (!qla_tgt_mode_enabled(base_vha) && !ha->flags.fw_started) do_reset = false;". qla2x00_do_dpc_vp (qla_mid.c:359-420) never tests ISP_ABORT_NEEDED.

Not reachable: git.kernel.org returned 403 to WebFetch and a bot-check page to curl; elixir.bootlin.com served only navigation in the first 100k characters. The GitHub mirror of the v6.12 tag and Debian's sources.debian.org copies were used instead.
- Corrected claim: In Linux 6.12 (identical in Debian trixie linux 6.12.107-1) the qla2xxx module parameter qlini_mode (qla_target.c, charp, S_IRUGO, i.e. load-time only) accepts, case-insensitively, "exclusive", "disabled", "enabled" (default) and "dual"; any other value makes qlt_init fail with -EINVAL. Every qla2xxx Scsi_Host, physical or NPIV, gets a per-host copy vha->qlini_mode initialised from the module value in qla2x00_create_host. The per-host sysfs attribute /sys/class/scsi_host/hostN/qlini_mode (qla_attr.c, DEVICE_ATTR_RW) is hidden by qla_host_attr_is_visible unless the module-wide mode is dual, so in disabled/exclusive/enabled mode the per-host mode can never change at run time. Writing it calls qla_set_ini_mode(vha, op): the "Target Mode is active. Unable to change Mode." refusal occurs only when the requested mode is "enabled" and target mode (from disabled/exclusive) or target-or-dual mode (from dual) is active; other transitions are accepted even with target mode active (e.g. disabled<->dual, exclusive->dual, dual->disabled/exclusive), and only the MODE_CHANGE_ACCEPT outcome updates vha->qlini_mode, optionally changes host->active_mode via qlt_set_mode, and sets ISP_ABORT_NEEDED on that host's dpc_flags; MODE_CHANGE_NO_ACTION records the new mode without an abort and NO_ACTION changes nothing. The sysfs write returns success in every case, so a refusal is visible only in the kernel log or by re-reading the attribute. qlt_enable_vha (the TPG-enable path from tcm_qla2xxx_enable_tpg/tcm_qla2xxx_npiv_enable_tpg) is a no-op when the host's qlini_mode is ENABLED; otherwise it sets active_mode via qlt_set_mode and then, for a physical port (vp_idx 0), sets ISP_ABORT_NEEDED on the base host, wakes the dpc and waits for the HBA to come back online (a full ISP abort, which also logs out and re-enables every NPIV vport via qla2x00_vp_abort_isp), while for an NPIV vport it only calls qla24xx_disable_vp (DISABLE_VPS_LOGO_ALL mailbox, logs out that vport's sessions) and qla24xx_enable_vp (requires the base port's link up and fabric topology). qlt_lport_register walks all registered targets and skips any host, physical or NPIV, whose per-host vha->qlini_mode is QLA2XXX_INI_MODE_ENABLED, skips a physical (non-NPIV) registration when target mode is already active on that host, skips hosts being stopped, and returns -ENODEV if no host with the requested physical WWPN remains.
- Design impact: (1) The Phase C profile (module-wide qlini_mode=disabled) is sound and should be stated as load-time only: the parameter is S_IRUGO, so it must be set in modprobe.d/initramfs before qla2xxx loads, and a misspelling makes the module fail to load. With "disabled", every host (physical and NPIV) starts as MODE_UNKNOWN with no initiator scan, the sysfs qlini_mode attribute is hidden, and qlt_lport_register accepts the ports; the sentence about qla_set_ini_mode refusals should either be dropped from Phase C (it is unreachable when the attribute is hidden) or rewritten as corrected above if the design also describes a dual-mode profile. (2) The single-role port arrangement should be justified by the hidden attribute (no run-time mode flips are possible at all in disabled mode), not by the refusal text; and the design must not rely on an error return from the sysfs write to detect a refused change. (3) "Physical TPGs enabled once at boot and never toggled" is confirmed and should be strengthened: enabling the physical TPG is a full ISP abort of the HBA that also logs out and re-enables every existing NPIV vport, and disabling it (qlt_stop_phase1 -> qlt_disable_vha) likewise schedules ISP_ABORT_NEEDED and waits for the HBA, so the physical TPG must be enabled before any NPIV TPG and never disabled while vports are in service. (4) The no-reset NPIV create/delete cycle is confirmed for the enable step (qla24xx_disable_vp + qla24xx_enable_vp, no chip reset), with two conditions to record: the base port must be link-up in a fabric topology (ISP_CFG_F) or qla24xx_enable_vp fails with FC_VPORT_LINKDOWN, and the base lport's tpg_1 must already be enabled (tcm_qla2xxx_lport_register_npiv_cb). The delete side is outside this claim: disabling an NPIV TPG sets ISP_ABORT_NEEDED on the vport's own dpc_flags, and the consumers found (qla2x00_do_dpc tests only the base host's bit; qla2x00_do_dpc_vp never tests it) suggest no chip reset results, but this was not verified end-to-end and should be a separate claim tested on hardware. (5) Note that qlt_lport_register's ENABLED check is per host, so if a dual-mode profile is ever used, a host whose per-host mode was switched to "enabled" via sysfs cannot be registered as a target until it is switched back.
- Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/qla_target.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/qla_attr.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/qla_target.h ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/qla_os.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/qla_mid.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/tcm_qla2xxx.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/qla_init.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/qla_def.h ; https://sources.debian.org/api/src/linux/ ; https://sources.debian.org/data/main/l/linux/6.12.107-1/drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/qla_target.c ; https://sources.debian.org/data/main/l/linux/6.12.107-1/drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/qla_attr.c ; https://sources.debian.org/data/main/l/linux/6.12.107-1/drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/qla_os.c ; https://sources.debian.org/data/main/l/linux/6.12.107-1/drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/tcm_qla2xxx.c

### [C28] CONFIRMED
- Claim: In Linux 6.12 drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/tcm_qla2xxx.c registers two fabrics, 'qla2xxx' (rejects any tpgt other than 1) and 'qla2xxx_npiv' (any tpgt), with the NPIV lport configfs directory named <physical wwpn>@<npiv wwpn>:<npiv wwnn> where the part after '@' is exactly 16 hex digits, a colon and 16 hex digits; and in qla_mid.c qla24xx_vport_create_req_sanity_check returns VPCERR_NO_FABRIC_SUPP unless ha->switch_cap has FLOGI_MID_SUPPORT, also requires ha->flags.npiv_supported and a unique WWPN under max_npiv_vports, while qla24xx_enable_vp keeps a vport down unless ha->current_topology & ISP_CFG_F.
- Raised by: Opus-Fabrics
- Why it matters: The configfs tree nbladed writes for per-SVM NPIV FC LIFs, and the position that NPIV FC LIFs exist only on a switched fabric while direct-attached ports must use the physical WWPN as the SVM's target, depend on it.
- Summary: Every element of C28 matches the Linux v6.12 source: tcm_qla2xxx.c registers fabric templates named "qla2xxx" (make_tpg returns -ENOSYS for any tpgt != 1) and "qla2xxx_npiv" (make_tpg accepts any "tpgt_<0..65535>"), the NPIV lport name is split at '@' with the tail required to be exactly 16 hex digits, ':', 16 hex digits, and qla_mid.c's qla24xx_vport_create_req_sanity_check returns VPCERR_NO_FABRIC_SUPP unless ha->switch_cap & FLOGI_MID_SUPPORT, VPCERR_UNSUPPORTED unless ha->flags.npiv_supported (and when num_vhosts > max_npiv_vports), VPCERR_BAD_WWN for a duplicate WWPN, while qla24xx_enable_vp sets FC_VPORT_LINKDOWN unless ha->current_topology & ISP_CFG_F. The surrounding code adds conditions the design should state: the physical port must be in target/dual mode with its qla2xxx/<wwpn>/tpgt_1 created and enabled first, the physical-WWPN half of the name must be strict lowercase xx:xx:...:xx, direct-attach (N_Port-to-N_Port) and loop topologies force switch_cap=0 so the NPIV mkdir itself fails with ENODEV, and FL_Port (public loop) passes the sanity check but never enables because ISP_CFG_FL (4) is not ISP_CFG_F (8).
- Evidence: Note on sources: git.kernel.org "plain" URLs returned HTTP 403 to the fetcher and elixir returned only its navigation header, so the files were read from the torvalds/linux GitHub mirror at tag v6.12 (identical tree). Line numbers below are v6.12.

tcm_qla2xxx.c:
- L1783 `.fabric_name = "qla2xxx",` and L1832 `.fabric_name = "qla2xxx_npiv",`; tcm_qla2xxx_register_configfs: `ret = target_register_template(&tcm_qla2xxx_ops);` (L1878) then `ret = target_register_template(&tcm_qla2xxx_npiv_ops);` (L1882). - Corrected claim: In Linux 6.12, drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/tcm_qla2xxx.c registers two target fabric templates: "qla2xxx", whose make_tpg accepts only "tpgt_1" (any other value logs "In non NPIV mode, a single TPG=1 is used for HW port mappings" and returns -ENOSYS), and "qla2xxx_npiv", whose make_tpg accepts any "tpgt_<N>" with N a decimal 0..65535 (the lport keeps a single tpg_1 pointer, so exactly one TPG per lport is used; OpenTAP standardizes on tpgt_1 in both fabrics). An NPIV lport directory is "<physical wwpn>@<npiv wwpn>:<npiv wwnn>": the part before '@' must be the physical port's WWPN in strict lowercase "xx:xx:xx:xx:xx:xx:xx:xx" form, and the part after '@' must be exactly 16 hex digits, a colon and 16 hex digits (33 characters, case-insensitive). The mkdir succeeds only if the physical port is in target or dual (not initiator) mode and its "qla2xxx/<wwpn>/tpgt_1" already exists and is enabled; it then calls fc_vport_create (roles FCP_INITIATOR, type NPIV). In qla_mid.c, qla24xx_vport_create_req_sanity_check returns VPCERR_UNSUPPORTED (-ENOSYS) unless ha->flags.npiv_supported (firmware attribute BIT_2 on mid-type ISPs), VPCERR_NO_FABRIC_SUPP (-EOPNOTSUPP) unless ha->switch_cap & FLOGI_MID_SUPPORT (BIT_10; switch_cap is forced to 0 in NL private-loop and N_Port-to-N_Port direct-attach topologies, so no NPIV vport can be created there), VPCERR_BAD_WWN (-ENOTUNIQ) if the WWPN equals the physical port's or an existing vport's, and VPCERR_UNSUPPORTED if num_vhosts > max_npiv_vports (firmware value, defaulted to 63); any such failure makes the configfs mkdir fail with ENODEV. qla24xx_enable_vp leaves a created vport in FC_VPORT_LINKDOWN unless the base port's loop_state is up and ha->current_topology & ISP_CFG_F (value 8; FL=4, N=2 and NL=1 never qualify), and that check is re-run from qla2x00_vp_abort_isp on later link/ISP-abort events.
- Design impact: The design position stands: NPIV FC LIFs exist only on a port logged into an NPIV-capable switch as an F_Port, and a direct-attached (N_Port-to-N_Port) or loop-attached port must expose the SVM's LUNs under the physical "qla2xxx/<wwpn>/tpgt_1" lport. Make these consequences explicit in the configfs section: (1) ordering: nbladed must set the physical port to target or dual mode (qlini_mode), create and enable qla2xxx/<phys wwpn>/tpgt_1 first, and only then mkdir qla2xxx_npiv/<phys>@<npiv wwpn>:<npiv wwnn>/tpgt_1, otherwise mkdir fails with EPERM; (2) name formatting: physical half strict lowercase colon-separated (e.g. 21:00:00:24:ff:12:34:56), NPIV half two bare 16-hex-digit strings joined by ':' (e.g. @2100001b32a90002:2000001b32a90002); the NPIV WWPN must differ from the physical WWPN and from every existing vport; (3) error mapping for the control plane: EINVAL = malformed name, EPERM = initiator mode or base tpgt_1 missing/disabled, ENODEV = no physical port with that WWPN in target/dual mode, or vport refused (no NPIV firmware support, fabric does not support NPIV / direct-attach or loop, duplicate WWPN, vport count over max_npiv_vports); (4) state tracking: a successful mkdir does not mean the LIF is up — if the base link is down or the topology is not F_Port the vport sits in FC_VPORT_LINKDOWN, so nbladed should treat /sys/class/fc_vports/*/vport_state as the LIF's operational state and expect the driver to re-enable automatically on link recovery; (5) capacity: per physical port vports are limited to max_npiv_vports (typically 63), which bounds SVM FC LIFs per port; (6) public loop (FL_Port) is not a supported NPIV topology even if the switch advertises NPIV, so the design should say "F_Port point-to-point fabric login", not merely "switched"; (7) one TPG per NPIV lport, conventionally tpgt_1 in both fabrics.
- Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/tcm_qla2xxx.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/qla_mid.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/qla_def.h ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/qla_init.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/qla_attr.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/qla_target.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/qla_target.h ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/qla_fw.h ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/tcm_qla2xxx.h ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/include/scsi/scsi_transport_fc.h ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/scsi/scsi_transport_fc.c

### [C29] CONFIRMED
- Claim: In Linux 6.12, drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/qla_nvme.c registers only an NVMe-FC host local port (nvme_fc_register_localport with a struct nvme_fc_port_template) and contains no nvmet_fc_register_targetport or nvmet_fc_target_template; qla2xxx has no NVMe-over-FC target mode.
- Raised by: Opus-Fabrics
- Why it matters: The conclusion that FC-NVMe is unavailable both as a replication transport and as a client protocol on QLogic HBAs, leaving FCP via tcm_qla2xxx as the only FC path, depends on it.
- Summary: Every part of the claim checks out against the v6.12 source and against Debian trixie's actual kernel source (linux 6.12.107-1). qla_nvme.c registers a single NVMe-FC local port via nvme_fc_register_localport() with pinfo.port_role = FC_PORT_ROLE_NVME_INITIATOR and a static struct nvme_fc_port_template (qla_nvme_fc_transport); the strings "nvmet" and "targetport" do not occur in qla_nvme.c or qla_nvme.h, no qla_nvmet.o exists in the Makefile, and Elixir's v6.12 cross-reference shows nvmet_fc_register_targetport/nvmet_fc_target_template referenced only by drivers/nvme/target/fc.c, the fcloop test driver and drivers/scsi/lpfc/lpfc_nvmet.c. A Marvell/Cavium "qla2xxx: Add FC-NVMe Target support" series (qla_nvmet.c/.h) was posted repeatedly in 2017-2018 and never merged, and in April 2025 Hannes Reinecke stated on linux-nvme that "Driver support for nvmet on qla2xxx is missing, and Marvell has no intention of bringing it back."
- Evidence: 1. Linux v6.12 drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/qla_nvme.c (torvalds/linux tag v6.12, raw mirror; git.kernel.org's plain endpoint returned HTTP 403): the only transport registration is in qla_nvme_register_hba(): "pinfo.port_role = FC_PORT_ROLE_NVME_INITIATOR;" ... "ret = nvme_fc_register_localport(&pinfo, tmpl, get_device(&ha->pdev->dev), &vha->nvme_local_port);" where "tmpl = &qla_nvme_fc_transport;" and "static struct nvme_fc_port_template qla_nvme_fc_transport = { .localport_delete = qla_nvme_localport_delete, .remoteport_delete = qla_nvme_remoteport_delete, .create_queue = qla_nvme_alloc_queue, ... .fcp_io = qla_nvme_post_cmd, .fcp_abort = qla_nvme_fcp_abort, .xmt_ls_rsp = qla_nvme_xmt_ls_rsp, .map_queues = qla_nvme_map_queues, ... };". The function also begins "if (!IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_NVME_FC)) return ret;". Strings 'nvmet_fc_register_targetport', 'nvmet_fc_target_template', 'nvmet_fc', 'nvmet', 'targetport': all absent. Includes are qla_nvme.h, <linux/nvme.h>, <linux/nvme-fc.h>, blk-mq headers only.
2. Linux v6.12 drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/qla_nvme.h: includes "<linux/nvme-fc-driver.h>"; 'nvmet', 'nvmet_fc', 'targetport', 'nvme_fc_target', 'target_template' all absent; the only prototypes are qla_nvme_register_hba, qla_nvme_register_remote, qla_nvme_delete, qla24xx_nvme_ls4_iocb, qla24xx_async_gffid_sp_done.
3. Linux v6.12 drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/Makefile: "qla2xxx-y := qla_os.o ... qla_target.o qla_tmpl.o qla_nvme.o qla_edif.o" / "obj-$(CONFIG_TCM_QLA2XXX) += tcm_qla2xxx.o" — no qla_nvmet.o. Kconfig: SCSI_QLA_FC "depends on NVME_FC || !NVME_FC"; nothing references NVME_TARGET_FC.
4. Elixir JSON API, v6.12 (the HTML ident pages were unreadable past the version list): nvmet_fc_register_targetport — defined include/linux/nvme-fc-driver.h:996 and drivers/nvme/target/fc.c:1380; referenced drivers/nvme/target/fc.c:1463, drivers/nvme/target/fcloop.c:1433, drivers/scsi/lpfc/lpfc_nvmet.c:1679; no drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/ path. nvmet_fc_target_template — defined nvme-fc-driver.h:963; referenced fc.c:101,1381, fcloop.c:1077, lpfc_nvmet.c:1415, nvme-fc-driver.h:997; no qla2xxx path. nvme_fc_register_localport — referenced drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/qla_nvme.c:987, drivers/scsi/lpfc/lpfc_nvme.c:2175, fcloop.c:1135. So in drivers/scsi/ only lpfc calls the target-side registration.
5. Linux v6.12 include/linux/nvme-fc-driver.h: "struct nvme_fc_port_template - structure containing static entrypoints and operational parameters for an LLDD that supports NVME host behavior" (banner "LLDD FC-NVME Host API ... For FC LLDD's that are the NVME Host role.") versus "struct nvmet_fc_target_template - structure containing static entrypoints and operational parameters for an LLDD that supports NVME subsystem behavior" (banner "LLDD FC-NVME Target/Subsystem API ... For FC LLDD's that are the NVME Subsystem role"); "int nvmet_fc_register_targetport(struct nvmet_fc_port_info *portinfo, struct nvmet_fc_target_template *template, struct device *dev, struct nvmet_fc_target_port **tgtport_p);". drivers/nvme/target/fc.c v6.12: "nvmet_fc_register_targetport - transport entry point called by an LLDD to register the existence of a local NVME subystem FC port." and "EXPORT_SYMBOL_GPL(nvmet_fc_register_targetport);" — it returns -EINVAL unless the template supplies xmt_ls_rsp, fcp_op, fcp_abort, fcp_req_release, targetport_delete etc.
6. Debian trixie: sources.debian.org lists linux 6.12.107-1 in suites ["trixie","forky","sid"] (6.12.111-1 in trixie-proposed-updates). Its drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/ directory has 41 files including qla_nvme.c, qla_nvme.h, qla_target.c, tcm_qla2xxx.c and no file containing "nvmet". Its qla_nvme.c has the same qla_nvme_register_hba() call with "pinfo.port_role = FC_PORT_ROLE_NVME_INITIATOR;" and "nvmet"/"targetport" absent. debian/config/config for 6.12.107-1: "CONFIG_NVME_FC=m", "CONFIG_NVME_TARGET=m", "CONFIG_NVME_TARGET_FC=m", "CONFIG_NVME_TARGET_FCLOOP=m", "CONFIG_SCSI_QLA_FC=m", "CONFIG_TCM_QLA2XXX=m", "CONFIG_SCSI_LPFC=m", "CONFIG_TARGET_CORE=m" — so nvmet-fc and tcm_qla2xxx modules ship, but no LLDD other than lpfc can bind nvmet-fc to hardware.
7. History (marc.info linux-scsi archive): "[PATCH 0/4] qla2xxx: Add FC-NVMe Target support" and v2 (Nov 2017), "[PATCH 0/6]" (Sep 2018), v2 0/5, v3 0/5 and "[PATCH v4 0/5] qla2xxx: Add FC-NVMe Target support" (Himanshu Madhani, 2018-10-31: "This series adds support for FC-NVMe Target." adding drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/qla_nvmet.c (831 lines) and qla_nvmet.h (129 lines)). The last message in the v4 thread is James Smart, 2018-11-08: "I'll be looking through it over the weekend." No later version exists in the archive and no qla_nvmet files exist in v6.12, so the series was never merged.
8. Maintainer status, linux-nvme April 2025 ("nvmetcli restore fails in add_subsystem"): Daniel Wagner: "As far I can tell, the qla2xxx driver or/and the HBA firmware do not support the target mode anymore." ... "Though he was able to get the target mode running with a Emulex HBA (lpfc driver)." Hannes Reinecke (2025-04-09): "Driver support for nvmet on qla2xxx is missing, and Marvell has no intention of bringing it back. (Which really is a bit ironic, seeing that the have target mode support for SCSI...)".
9. Potential confusion pre-empted: upstream commit 84ed362ac40ca44dbbbebf767301463aa72bc797 "scsi: qla2xxx: Dual FCP-NVMe target port support" is initiator-side only: "Some storage arrays advertise FCP LUNs and NVMe namespaces behind the same WWN. The driver now offers a user option by way of NVRAM parameter to allow users to choose, on a per port basis, the kind of FC-4 type they would like to prioritize for login." It does not add target mode.
- Corrected claim: In Linux 6.12 (and in Debian trixie's linux 6.12.107-1), drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/qla_nvme.c implements only the NVMe-FC host (initiator) role: qla_nvme_register_hba() calls nvme_fc_register_localport() with port_role = FC_PORT_ROLE_NVME_INITIATOR and a static struct nvme_fc_port_template (qla_nvme_fc_transport). Neither qla_nvme.c nor qla_nvme.h references nvmet_fc_register_targetport or nvmet_fc_target_template, no qla_nvmet.* file is built, and the only in-tree hardware LLDD that registers an NVMe-FC target port (nvmet_fc_register_targetport, lpfc_nvmet.c) is Emulex/Broadcom lpfc (plus the fcloop software test driver). qla2xxx therefore has no NVMe-over-FC target (subsystem) mode; a Marvell "qla2xxx: Add FC-NVMe Target support" series (2017-2018, v4 posted 2018-10-31) was never merged, and in April 2025 the nvme-fc maintainers stated that nvmet support on qla2xxx is missing and Marvell has no intention of bringing it back. On QLogic HBAs the only FC target path is FCP via tcm_qla2xxx/LIO (CONFIG_TCM_QLA2XXX=m in trixie); qla2xxx can still act as an FC-NVMe initiator (CONFIG_NVME_FC=m).
- Design impact: No change to the conclusion: with QLogic HBAs, OpenTAP cannot serve FC-NVMe to ESXi/Proxmox/Windows clients and cannot terminate an FC-NVMe replication link, so FCP via tcm_qla2xxx remains the only FC target path. Three precisions are worth adding to the design document: (1) state the limitation as "no NVMe-FC target/subsystem role" rather than "no FC-NVMe", because qla2xxx does provide the initiator role — OpenTAP could consume an external FC-NVMe array or act as the initiator half of a replication link if the peer were an lpfc-based target; (2) if FC-NVMe target service ever becomes a requirement, it is a hardware decision, not a software one: Debian trixie already ships nvmet-fc (CONFIG_NVME_TARGET_FC=m) and lpfc (CONFIG_SCSI_LPFC=m), and lpfc_nvmet.c is the only in-tree LLDD that binds to it, so Emulex/Broadcom HBAs would be needed; (3) footnote the unmerged 2017-2018 qla2xxx_nvmet series and the April 2025 maintainer statement so reviewers do not expect a future kernel bump to change this, and note that the commit titled "scsi: qla2xxx: Dual FCP-NVMe target port support" (84ed362ac40c) is initiator-side login-preference logic and does not indicate target mode.
- Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/qla_nvme.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/qla_nvme.h ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/Makefile ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/Kconfig ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/include/linux/nvme-fc-driver.h ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/nvme/target/fc.c ; https://elixir.bootlin.com/api/ident/linux/nvmet_fc_register_targetport?version=v6.12 ; https://elixir.bootlin.com/api/ident/linux/nvmet_fc_target_template?version=v6.12 ; https://elixir.bootlin.com/api/ident/linux/nvme_fc_register_localport?version=v6.12 ; https://sources.debian.org/api/src/linux/ ; https://sources.debian.org/api/src/linux/trixie/drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/ ; https://sources.debian.org/data/main/l/linux/6.12.107-1/drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/qla_nvme.c ; https://sources.debian.org/data/main/l/linux/6.12.107-1/debian/config/config ; https://lists.infradead.org/pipermail/linux-nvme/2025-April/055140.html ; https://lists.infradead.org/pipermail/linux-nvme/2025-April/055131.html ; https://lkml.iu.edu/hypermail/linux/kernel/2104.2/02790.html ; https://marc.info/?l=linux-scsi&w=2&r=1&s=FC-NVMe+Target&q=t ; https://marc.info/?t=154102922500052&r=1&w=2 ; https://marc.info/?l=linux-scsi&m=154102084405195&w=2 ; https://marc.info/?l=linux-scsi&m=154169748107834&w=2

### [C30] CONFIRMED
- Claim: VMware ESXi 8: Disk.MaxLUN defaults to 1024, is an exclusive upper bound on scanned LUN IDs and can be raised to 16384; the default PSP for devices claimed by VMW_SATP_ALUA is VMW_PSP_MRU; and Broadcom KB 323068 states that qlnativefc 5.2.46.0, 5.3.1.0 and 5.3.2.0 on ESXi 8.0.x cannot log into direct-attached (N2N/point-to-point) targets and that 5.4.80 fixes it (on ESXi 7.0: 4.1.37.0 and later broken, 5.3.80 fixed).
- Raised by: Opus-Fabrics
- Why it matters: The LUN-ID policy (0 to 255, LUN 0 always mapped), the shipped SATP round-robin claim rule, and the direct-attach client matrix's driver pin depend on it.
- Summary: All three assertions check out against Broadcom primary pages. The vSphere 8.0 Storage guide and Host Client guide state Disk.MaxLUN "has a default value of 1024", that "the SCSI scan code does not scan the LUNs with IDs greater than or equal to the value you enter" (exclusive bound), and that the scannable range is "0 to 16,383" (so 16384 is the maximum useful value; the literal "maximum of 16384" is stated by Dell's PowerStore KB rather than by VMware, and Broadcom KB 398604 loosely says "less than or equal to 16383"). The vSphere 8.0 Multipathing Considerations page says verbatim "The default PSP for all devices claimed by VMW_SATP_ALUA is VMW_PSP_MRU", and Broadcom KB 323068 states exactly the qlnativefc versions in the claim (ESXi 7.0: 4.1.37.0 onward broken, fixed 5.3.80; ESXi 8.0: 5.2.46.0/5.3.1.0/5.3.2.0 broken, fixed 5.4.80), describing the topology as "Direct Connect/DAS/N2N" (it never uses the words "point-to-point").
- Evidence: 1) Disk.MaxLUN (vSphere 8.0 Storage guide, "Change the Number of Scanned Storage Devices"): "The range of scanned LUN IDs for an ESXi host can be from 0 to 16,383." "ESXi ignores LUN IDs greater than 16,383." "The configurable Disk.MaxLUN parameter controls the range of scanned LUN ID range." "The parameter has a default value of 1024." "For example, to discover LUN IDs from 1 through 100, set Disk.MaxLUN to 101." "In other cases, you might need to increase the value if your environment uses LUN IDs that are greater than 1023." The page also says Disk.MaxLUN "also determines how many LUNs the SCSI scan code attempts to discover" by individual INQUIRY when a target does not support REPORT_LUNS. The vSphere 8.0 Host Client guide adds the explicit exclusive rule: "The SCSI scan code does not scan the LUNs with IDs greater than or equal to the value you enter." and "For example, to discover LUN IDs from 0 to 100, set Disk.MaxLUN to 101." Broadcom KB 342823 (Environment: ESXi 7.x, 8.x): default "was increased from 256 to 1024 by default in vSphere 6.0"; "The value you enter specifies the highest LUN to be recognized and used by the system" with the 101-for-0..100 example. Broadcom KB 398604 (vSphere 7.0/8.0): "In ESXi 7.0.x and 8.0.x default value of Disk.MaxLUN is set at 1024." and config maximum "Maximum number of fiber Channel - SCSI LUN ID = 0 to 16383", but its resolution says "change the Disk.MaxLUN value to a desired value less than or equal to 16383" (loose wording given the exclusive semantics). The literal maximum value 16384 is stated by Dell KB 000199943: "The default value is 1024, allowing the host to discover the LUN IDs 0-1023." "This can be increased to a maximum of 16384 (LUN ID 0-16383)". I could not find esxcli "Max Value" output for /Disk/MaxLUN in any VMware/Broadcom page.

2) Default PSP for VMW_SATP_ALUA (vSphere 8.0 Storage guide, "Multipathing Considerations"): "The default PSP for all devices claimed by VMW_SATP_ALUA is VMW_PSP_MRU." "The VMW_PSP_MRU selects an active/optimized path as reported by the VMW_SATP_ALUA" (or an active/unoptimized path if none). Caveat on the same page: "certain ALUA storage arrays need to use VMW_PSP_FIXED." vSphere 8.0 "VMware Path Selection Plug-Ins and Policies": MRU "is default for most active-passive storage devices", "Fixed is the default policy for most active-active storage devices", "Round Robin is the default policy for many arrays" (i.e., via vendor-specific SATP claim rules), and "The Most Recently Used policy does not use the preferred path setting." vSphere 8.0 "VMware SATPs": VMW_SATP_ALUA is the "SATP for ALUA-compliant arrays." Broadcom KB 339621 (ESXi 7.x/8.x): MRU "is the default policy for Logical Unit Numbers (LUNs) presented from an Active/Passive array."

3) Broadcom KB 323068 (Products: VMware vSphere ESXi; Environment: "VMware vSphere ESXi 7.x" and "VMware vSphere ESXi 8.0.x"). Title: "In a DAS configuration, after patching or updating qlnativefc adapters to v4.1.37.0 or above, the qlnativefc HBA is unable to log into fabric and see the available storage devices." Symptoms: "In a configuration where the storage target is connected directly to the ESXi host (i.e. Direct Connect/DAS/N2N topology), running Marvell FC HBA driver qlnativefc v4.1.37.0 or above, the qlnativefc driver loads and claims the HBAs on the host but is unable to log into fabric and see the available storage devices." Log signature: "qla24xxReportIdAcquisition:3534:RIDA: format 2/N2N Primary port id xxxxxx." with the "qlnativefcUpdateFcport ... ONLINE" line absent. Affected: "This issue affects qlnativefc driver version 4.1.37.0 onwards in ESXi 7.0." "As well as drivers 5.2.46.0/5.3.1.0/5.3.2.0 in ESXi 8.0". Cause: "A change was introduced in the qlnativefc driver to skip session creation before the adapter is marked online" (in direct-attach the target login can complete before that point, so no direct-attached storage is discovered). Resolution: "For ESXi 7.0 this issue is resolved in version : 5.3.80" and "For ESXi 8.0 this issue is resolved in version : 5.4.80". Workaround: "For ESXi 7.0 rollback to a qlnativefc to a version earlier than qlnativefc 4.1.37.0". The KB does not say which ESXi 8.0 build carries 5.4.80 inbox, and Broadcom's ESXi 8.0 GA (build 20513097), 8.0 U1 (build 21495797) and 8.0 U2 (build 22380479) release notes list no qlnativefc version at all. OEM evidence: HPE Synergy ESXi 8.0 U1 (May 2023) custom image lists "qlnativefc: 5.4.80.0-1OEM.800.1.0.20143090"; Lenovo 8.0 U1a custom ISO (build 21813344) lists MRVL-QLogic-FC "5.4.80.0-1OEM.800.1.0.20143090".
- Corrected claim: ESXi 8.0: the advanced setting Disk.MaxLUN defaults to 1024 and is an exclusive upper bound: "the SCSI scan code does not scan the LUNs with IDs greater than or equal to the value you enter" (to discover LUN IDs 0-100, set 101), so the default scan window is LUN IDs 0-1023. ESXi scans LUN IDs 0 to 16,383 at most and "ignores LUN IDs greater than 16,383", so the maximum useful value is 16384 (Dell's PowerStore KB states "a maximum of 16384 (LUN ID 0-16383)"; VMware's own pages give the ceiling as the ID range, and Broadcom KB 398604 loosely says "less than or equal to 16383"). Disk.MaxLUN also caps the per-ID INQUIRY walk used only when a target does not support REPORT LUNS. Multipathing: in vSphere 8.0 "the default PSP for all devices claimed by VMW_SATP_ALUA is VMW_PSP_MRU"; MRU selects an active/optimized path as reported by the SATP, does not use the preferred-path setting, and vendor/model-specific SATP claim rules (or an explicit rule shipped by the storage vendor) are what make Round Robin "the default policy for many arrays"; certain ALUA arrays require VMW_PSP_FIXED. Broadcom KB 323068 (Environment: ESXi 7.x and ESXi 8.0.x): with the storage target "connected directly to the ESXi host (i.e. Direct Connect/DAS/N2N topology)", qlnativefc "loads and claims the HBAs on the host but is unable to log into fabric and see the available storage devices"; affected are qlnativefc 4.1.37.0 onward on ESXi 7.0 and 5.2.46.0/5.3.1.0/5.3.2.0 on ESXi 8.0; cause is a driver change "to skip session creation before the adapter is marked online"; resolved in qlnativefc 5.3.80 (ESXi 7.0) and 5.4.80 (ESXi 8.0); the ESXi 7.0 workaround is rolling back to a version earlier than 4.1.37.0. The KB does not use the term "point-to-point"; N2N is its name for the direct-attach login mode.
- Design impact: No change to the LUN-ID policy: LUN IDs 0-255 sit entirely inside ESXi 8's default scan window (0-1023), so the design must not ask ESXi admins to touch Disk.MaxLUN, and because LIO answers REPORT LUNS the INQUIRY-walk clause never applies; the document should quote the exclusive-bound rule and cite the 0-16,383 ceiling rather than "max 16384" as a VMware statement (attribute 16384 to Dell, or phrase it as "16384 = scan IDs 0-16383"). The SATP round-robin claim rule stays necessary: an OpenTAP LUN (LIO with TPGS/ALUA on, no vendor-specific VMware rule) will be claimed by the generic VMW_SATP_ALUA rule and get VMW_PSP_MRU, which pins I/O to one active/optimized path and never rebalances; the design must ship a vendor/model-matched VMW_SATP_ALUA claim rule assigning VMW_PSP_RR (with the usual iops tuning) and state that MRU is the fallback behavior if the rule is not installed, plus note that some ALUA targets need FIXED, which OpenTAP does not. The direct-attach client matrix must express the qlnativefc requirement as a minimum version (ESXi 8.0.x: qlnativefc >= 5.4.80; ESXi 7.0: >= 5.3.80, or < 4.1.37.0 as the KB's rollback workaround), not as "avoid 5.2.46.0/5.3.1.0/5.3.2.0", because the KB phrases the 7.0 range as "4.1.37.0 or above" and gives no assurance that its 8.0 list is exhaustive; the matrix must also name the topology in the KB's own terms ("Direct Connect/DAS/N2N"), give the log signature ("RIDA: format 2/N2N Primary port id" with no "ONLINE" fcport update) as the diagnostic, and require operators to verify the installed driver on the host, since Broadcom's ESXi 8.0 GA/U1/U2 release notes do not publish the inbox qlnativefc version (OEM 8.0 U1 images from HPE and Lenovo are known to carry 5.4.80.0-1OEM.800.1.0.20143090). If the design asserts which ESXi 8.0 update carries the fix inbox, that remains unverified and should be removed or marked as such.
- Sources: https://techdocs.broadcom.com/us/en/vmware-cis/vsphere/vsphere/8-0/vsphere-storage/managing-esxi-storage-devices/rescan-operations-for-esxi-storage/change-the-number-of-scanned-luns.html ; https://techdocs.broadcom.com/us/en/vmware-cis/vsphere/vsphere/8-0/vsphere-single-host-management-vmware-host-client/managing-storage-in-the-vsphere-host-client-vSphereSingleHostManagementVMwareHostClient/performing-storage-refresh-and-rescan-operations-in-the-vmware-host-client-vSphereSingleHostManagementVMwareHostClient/change-the-number-of-scanned-luns-in-the-vsphere-host-client-vSphereSingleHostManagementVMwareHostClient.html ; https://techdocs.broadcom.com/us/en/vmware-cis/vsphere/vsphere/8-0/vsphere-storage/managing-esxi-storage-devices/rescan-operations-for-esxi-storage.html ; https://knowledge.broadcom.com/external/article/342823 ; https://knowledge.broadcom.com/external/article/398604/vmfs-datastores-missing-from-new-hosts-t.html ; https://www.dell.com/support/kbdoc/en-us/000199943/container-storage-modules ; https://techdocs.broadcom.com/us/en/vmware-cis/vsphere/vsphere/8-0/vsphere-storage/understanding-multipathing-and-failover-in-the-esxi-environment/using-claim-rules-to-control-esxi-multipathing-modules/multipathing-considerations.html ;
