On an unplanned takeover B raises a NAS LIF only after `arping -D -c 3 -w 1 -I <parent> <addr>` returns 0 (no reply in DAD mode) [verified: https://manpages.debian.org/trixie/iputils-arping/arping.8.en.html], with Consensus's `WatchdogDeadlinePassed` (5 s margin plus 3 s reset) as the backstop, so a wedged A delays B by at most 8 s instead of fighting it; this is Consensus's fence-evidence item 5.

**P3 (BUILTIN and well-known SIDs). ACCEPT**, with C33's correction: `net idmap set mapping` is a stub in 4.22, so `nbladed` seeds `winbindd_idmap.tdb` with `net idmap restore` (fixed id lines with the HWMs above them) and creates the BUILTIN aliases with `net groupmap add sid=S-1-5-32-{544,545,546} ... type=local` plus `net sam addmem` for the memberships smbd would have added, from one Raft table, before the first winbindd start and on every rehost. Exit test: `wbinfo -S` for S-1-5-32-544, S-1-5-32-545, S-1-1-0 and S-1-5-11 identical across same-domain SVMs.

**P4 (a throttled NAS volume consumes the node-wide dirty pool). ACCEPT.** Each NAS volume's ublk device gets `/sys/class/bdi/<dev>/max_bytes` = bucket drain rate x `dirty_expire` (floor 64 MiB) and `strict_limit=1`, so a 1,000 IOPS volume holds at most 8 MiB dirty and its writers block alone [verified: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/Documentation/ABI/testing/sysfs-class-bdi]. Metadata is exempt from the bucket: 6.12 passes `UBLK_IO_F_META` (1 << 11) to the daemon [verified: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/include/uapi/linux/ublk_cmd.h] and XFS log writes always carry `REQ_META` in `xlog_write_iclog` [verified: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/fs/xfs/xfs_log.c], so COMMIT latency is not held by the bucket.

**P5 (PDL only if every path reports it). ACCEPT**, scoped by C01. `strict` (new unit serial, hence new NAA, new LUN number, old LUN unmapped) is the default for every dirty block volume after an unplanned Phase B or A takeover, because the dead node's path can never answer 25h/00h; `pdl` (unmap, 05h/25h on all paths) stays the default for Phase C dirty boots and planned cases, where the same node returns and no dead path remains, and `nvfail clear` under `pdl` refuses to remap until `otap-host-check` sees PDL on every registered ESXi host.

**P6 (`ublks_max` 64). ACCEPT.** `options ublk_drv ublks_max=4096` in the platform profile; the device budget counts own LUNs, standby replicas and snapshot clones.

**P7 (rpcbind `-w`). ACCEPT.** `rpcbind -f -w` on the private `/run`.

**P8 (`passdb.tdb` regeneration discards password changes). ACCEPT.** The root-volume tdbsam is the authority; Raft holds the declared user list and the initial sealed hash; `otapctl user` writes through `pdbedit` inside the namespaces; regeneration happens only when the tdb is absent.

**P9 (latency bar). ACCEPT.** One ladder measured at the initiator: engine 3 to 5 us, initiator 100 to 150 us p50 (4 KiB QD1 write, 10GbE), in-guest 150 to 250 us; exit test p50 at most 150 us and p99 at most 1 ms at the initiator, p50 at most 250 us in the guest.

###### Opus-Fabrics

**P1 (unmapping LUN 0 gives DATA PROTECT, not PDL). ACCEPT.** Data LUNs are mapped at 1 to 255; LUN 0 is LIO's virtual LUN 0; the Raft validator refuses a data LUN at mapped LUN 0 per (TPG, ACL) (C02); the C4 exit test asserts 05h/25h/00h on the wire for the lowest data LUN.

**P2 (SendTargets discloses every SVM). ACCEPT.** `attrib/demo_mode_discovery=0` and `attrib/generate_node_acls=0` on every TPG at creation; exit test: SendTargets from an initiator with an ACL in SVM-A lists no other SVM's IQN or portal.

**P3 (`*` idmap per SVM). ACCEPT**, the same change as Storage P3.

**P4 (tenant daemons run as unconfined root). ACCEPT the goal, change the mechanism.** systemd's mount-based sandboxing cannot be used on a unit that enters a pinned mount namespace (C15, C16), and `RestrictNamespaces`, `SystemCallFilter` and a bounding set lacking `CAP_SYS_ADMIN` and `CAP_SYS_CHROOT` are applied before `execve` and would stop the `setns`. So the wrapper is `otap-nsexec` (otap-blade): `setns` into the pins, drop the bounding and permitted sets to the daemon's profile (caps 0.5.6 [verified: https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/caps]), `PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS`, a per-daemon seccomp allow-list (seccompiler 0.5.0 [verified: https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/seccompiler]), `execve`. The unit keeps the cgroup and seccomp-only options (`DevicePolicy=closed` with `DeviceAllow`, `RestrictAddressFamilies`, `LockPersonality`, `RestrictRealtime`, `RestrictSUIDSGID`, `NoNewPrivileges`); the view masks `/dev` (seven nodes), has no `/sys`, remounts `/proc/sys` read-only, binds `/usr`, `/lib` and `/bin` read-only and shows only the SVM's own `/run/opentap/svm/<id>`. Profiles: smbd and winbindd `NET_BIND_SERVICE DAC_OVERRIDE DAC_READ_SEARCH CHOWN FOWNER SETUID SETGID SYS_RESOURCE KILL`; the NFS helpers `NET_BIND_SERVICE DAC_READ_SEARCH`; versitygw a per-SVM uid with `NET_BIND_SERVICE`.

**P5 (`no_path_retry` 12 versus `queue`). REJECT `queue`.** With `queue` an nvfailed LUN hangs forever and the I/O queued in dm-multipath is replayed against the rolled-back LUN the moment `nvfail clear` remaps it: the exact hazard. The REPORT LUNS DATA HAS CHANGED unit attention does not remove the device: 6.12 logs "The Linux SCSI layer does not automatically remap LUN assignments", sets `expecting_lun_change` and queues `SDEV_EVT_LUN_CHANGE_REPORTED` [verified: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/scsi/scsi_error.c]; no Debian udev rule acts on it [believed]. I ship no `multipath.conf`: the built-in `LIO-ORG` entry (`no_path_retry 12`, `path_checker directio`, `prio alua`) applies (C17), I/O fails about 60 s plus detection after the last path drops, qemu stops the VM, and the recipe says reset, never resume.

**P6 (Phase B block move is a LIF move). ACCEPT**, as Storage P1.

**P7 (TCP back-off, SMB handles). ACCEPT.** Before a NAS address is removed, `nbladed` runs `ss -K` inside the netns on every established connection to it (`CONFIG_INET_DIAG_DESTROY=y` in Debian's 6.12.111-1 config [verified: https://sources.debian.org/data/main/l/linux/6.12.111-1/debian/config/config]), so clients reconnect on their first probe after the LIF returns. Durable handles live in `smbXsrv_open_global.tdb` under the lock directory with `TDB_CLEAR_IF_FIRST` and do not survive an smbd restart (C34): every planned move and `svm stop/start` is documented as handle loss.

**P8 (ESXi NFSv3 re-MOUNT). ACCEPT the test; C20 settles the mechanism.** ESXi never re-runs MOUNT by itself, but a rebooted host remounts by server and path. The fence is therefore server-side: the export stays withheld until `nvfail clear`, and the fsid generation forces unmount and remount (VMs powered off, Broadcom KB 344470) on hosts that did not reboot; a rebooted host started its VMs from scratch, which is safe.

**P9 (three memory numbers, three QD1 numbers). ACCEPT.** Storage owns the memory table; my inputs are in 3.11 and `svm.slice` is derived from it (Phase C: DRAM minus engine minus 4 GiB host; Phase B: half of that so both nodes' SVMs fit on a survivor).

###### Opus-Consensus

**P1 (the pins cannot be created as written). ACCEPT; blocker fixed.** A process cannot bind its own mount-namespace file (`mnt_ns_loop`, EINVAL) and pins made inside the pivoted view never reach the host (C16). `nbladed` spawns util-linux 2.41.5 `unshare --net=P/net --uts=P/uts --mount=P/mnt --propagation slave --fork -- otap-nsinit <id>`: unshare's pinning child stays in the host mount namespace and binds `/proc/<ppid>/ns/*` once the parent's namespace changes, and `otap-nsinit` then builds the view and pivots, which `setns` honours because it resolves the namespace root at entry [verified: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man1/unshare.1.html and C16].

**P2 (one lockd thread for every SVM). ACCEPT as a documented limit; no in-box fix.** 3.4 records the single global `lockd` thread, global grace and ports, and the union of NLM and NFSv4 grace (C13). Mitigations: Proxmox datastores are recommended as NFSv4.1 (locks served by per-netns nfsd threads); `nfsdcld` runs on every NFS SVM so an empty reclaim table skips the v4 grace, and `grace-time=20` caps it otherwise; a stalled volume is unexported before any other ladder step.

**P3 (the move ships after it stops). ACCEPT.** `otap-ctl` refuses `svm move` unless the relationship is Steady with lag under one CP; the ladder is pre-copy to Steady, block Transitioning plus NAS RST and address removal, units down, unmount, final CP of at most one interval, ship, receiver commit `Immediate`, ALUA flip and NAS start on B. Published: "ladder 4 to 6 s plus one CP ship plus switch".

**P4 (every Phase B NAS takeover pays XFS log replay). ACCEPT the number; the mechanism is Storage's.** The timer table says "NAS unplanned takeover 15 to 60 s" until measured; I ask Storage for receiver-side pre-replay or a periodic fsfreeze-cut CP.

**P5 (BUILTIN SIDs). ACCEPT**, as Storage P3.

**P6 (NFSv4 scope welded to the NetBIOS name). ACCEPT, different mechanism.** `rpc.nfsd --scope` is honoured only on a cold start and every scope-less thread write rewrites `nfsd_name` from the caller's nodename (C14). So the UTS nodename is `<svm>.<cluster-uuid8>` (Samba's `netbios name` stays the 15-character SVM name), `nfsdctl autostart` inside the view reads `[nfsd] scope=<nodename>` from the SVM's own `/etc/nfs.conf`, every later thread change is issued from inside that UTS namespace so the scope cannot drift, and `nfsdctl threads` printing `scope:` is the post-condition.

**P7 (NFS nvfail row mislabelled, clear gap). ACCEPT.** Removing the export gives `nfserr_stale` at once, not a hang; the `nvfail_generation` lives in the volume table from day one (Storage says yes) and is part of the `fsid` string on every export, so a reconciler cannot re-add an export without it.

**P8 (nfsdcld must hold the pipe within 1 s). ACCEPT.** `-nfsd@` requires `-nfsdcld@`, whose readiness is "the nfsdcld PID holds `rpc_pipefs/nfsd/cld` open" (`/proc/<pid>/fd`); C5 injects a 2 s cold-start delay and asserts reclaims succeed.

##### 2. Fact-check consequences

- **C01, C02** (PDL and LUN 0): applied in Storage P5 and Fabrics P1; the sense list is the KB 318712 set (25h/00h and 68h/00h regardless of sense key, plus 4Ch/00h, 3Eh/01h and 3Eh/03h under NOT READY or HARDWARE ERROR), ALUA Unavailable never appears in nvfail text, `Disk.PathEvalTime` is an upper bound rather than a guard, the unmap is applied on every TPG, and the mixed dead/PDL case is a lab item.
- **C09, C10**: `nbladed` never writes `emulate_write_cache` on iblock and checks `/sys/block/ublkbN/queue/write_cache == "write back"` and `fua == 1` instead; `ublks_max` goes in the platform profile and, with no live resize on 6.12, standby and clone devices are pre-sized.
- **C11**: confirms the netns binding; adds no wildcard portals, IPv6 duplicates compared without scope, `np_exports` at zero before the pins go, nvmet's namespace captured at the subsystem link with the address present first (no freebind), a post-create `ss -ltn` check, and IPv6 link-local deferred for both protocols.
- **C12, C13, C14**: per-netns nfsd confirmed, with `v4_end_grace` read, written and polled until `Y` (`-EBUSY` means ended, shutting down or not running) and the mount namespace justified by nfs-utils' paths rather than the kernel; the lockd limit and `grace-time=20`; the statd, sm-notify and nfsdcld flag set of 3.4.
- **C15, C16, C17**: the wrapper and pin design of 3.1, no mount sandboxing on units, util-linux 2.41 or later, `ProtectHostname=` never set; no shipped `multipath.conf`.
- **C18, C19**: ALUA setup order (group id first, write-once, identical on both nodes), vendor, product and serial written before the first LUN link, `/etc/target/pr` and `/etc/target/alua/tpgs_<group>` created at install; every NFS-visible snapshot gets its own export with a deterministic `fsid=` because all snapshots carry the live volume's XFS UUID and mountd resolves to the first match.
- **C20**: `async` exports forbidden for datastores; the FILE_SYNC budget is "pending capture" (C5); the NFS nvfail fence is server-side withholding; ESXi NFS 4.1 not recommended.
- **C27, C28, C29, C30, C31**: FC step 3 sets `qlini_mode=disabled` at load time, enables the physical `tpgt_1` before any NPIV port, creates NPIV LIFs only on an F_Port fabric (direct attach and loop use the physical target) and tracks `vport_state`; no NVMe-FC target role; LUNs 1 to 255 sit inside ESXi's default scan window; the `VMW_PSP_RR` claim rule is mandatory; Proxmox exit tests target 9.1, `snapshot-as-volume-chain` stays a preview, and the LUN backstore advertises thin provisioning and honours UNMAP.
- **C33, C34, C36, C37**: the idmap seeding of Storage P3; durable-handle test conditions (handle lease, no byte-range lock, smbd not restarted) and `KillMode=control-group`; `arp_notify` never fires on address add, so the GARP sender stays; Linux-on-ESXi guests reach 180 s only on VMware SCSI controllers with open-vm-tools.
- **C38, C39, C40**: versions are a 2026-10-12 snapshot (Debian 13.7 plus trixie-security, sg3-utils 1.48-3 or later); versitygw pinned to a main build at or after commit 5f063c5 or the next tag; `--object-lock-mode` is absent from v1.8.0; retention needs xattr metadata.

##### 3. Revised design

###### 3.1 Namespaces, pins, units

An SVM is three namespaces (net, UTS, mount) pinned under `/run/opentap/svm/<id>/ns/{net,uts,mnt}` on a private bind of `/run/opentap`, created as in Consensus P1; `otap-nsinit` sets the nodename to `<svm>.<cluster-uuid8>`, brings `lo` up, builds the view (3.2), pivots and exits, and the pins hold the namespaces with no holder process. Units are transient (`StartTransientUnit`, zbus 5.19.0) under `svm-<id>.slice` with `ExecStart=/usr/libexec/otap/otap-nsexec <id> <profile> -- <daemon>`; properties as in round 1 plus the hardening set of Fabrics P4 and `KillMode=control-group`, never `ProtectHostname`, `RestrictNamespaces`, `SystemCallFilter` or a mount-based option. The unit table of round 1 stands with three changes: `-rpcbind@` runs `-f -w`, `-nfsdcld@` precedes `-nfsd@` on every NFS SVM, and `-nfsd@` is a oneshot running `nfsdctl autostart`. Cost: about 5 ms and 2 MiB per SVM.

###### 3.2 The view

As in round 1 (`/` tmpfs; host `/usr /bin /sbin /lib /lib64` read-only; `/etc` overlays from `/run/opentap/svm/<id>/etc`; private `/run` with the journal and notify sockets; `/var/lib/nfs` tmpfs with the root-volume state bound; per-netns `/proc/fs/nfsd`; `/vol/<svm>_root` and one bind per top-level junction), with the masking of Fabrics P4. Read-only binds use `mount_remount` per mount (rustix 1.1.5 has no `mount_setattr` [verified: https://docs.rs/rustix/latest/rustix/mount/index.html]). Snapshot mounts stay outside share roots at `/vol/<svm>_root/.otap/snap/<vol>/@GMT-...`, each NFS-visible one with its own export line and `fsid=<hash(snapshot id)>`.

###### 3.3 Root volume versus Raft

Unchanged in principle: daemon-mutated state on the root volume, declared state in Raft rendered into tmpfs. Changes: `passdb.tdb` is authoritative on the root volume; the idmap seed is rendered from a Raft table of well-known and BUILTIN SIDs and applied before the first winbindd start and on rehost; the root volume's nvfail class is `alert` (3.8); the root volume is in the SVM's consistency group and a `secrets.tdb` change requests an early aggregate CP.

```rust
pub enum LifKind { Nas, Block { node: NodeId } }      // NAS LIFs migrate; block LIFs are per node
pub struct LifSpec { pub id: LifId, pub kind: LifKind, pub port: String, pub vlan: Option<u16>, pub r#impl: LifImpl,
    pub addr: IpNet, pub mac: [u8; 6] /* 02:4f:54 + hash(cluster, lif) */, pub services: BTreeSet<Service> }
pub struct LunSpec { pub volume: VolId, pub lun: u8 /* 1..=255; 0 refused */, pub igroup: IgroupId,
    pub class: LunClass, pub nvfail_policy: NvfailPolicy /* Pdl | Strict */ }
pub struct IdentitySeed { pub wellknown: Vec<(Sid, u32)>,
    pub builtin: Vec<(Sid, String /* unix group */, Vec<Sid> /* members */)> }
pub enum Presence { Full, BlockStandby }             // both nodes in Phases A and B; SvmState as in round 1
pub trait SvmLifecycle {
    fn create(&mut self, spec: &SvmSpec) -> Result<(), SvmErr>;
    fn start(&mut self, id: SvmId, presence: Presence) -> Result<(), SvmErr>;      // idempotent
    fn stop(&mut self, id: SvmId, deadline: Duration) -> Result<(), SvmErr>;        // parallel NAS and block halves
    fn apply(&mut self, id: SvmId, delta: &SvmDelta) -> Result<(), SvmErr>;
    fn alua(&mut self, id: SvmId, state: AluaState) -> Result<(), SvmErr>;          // Transitioning, AO, Standby
    fn nvfail(&mut self, id: SvmId, vol: VolId, gen: u32, policy: NvfailPolicy) -> Result<(), SvmErr>;
    fn delete(&mut self, id: SvmId) -> Result<(), SvmErr>;
    fn state(&self, id: SvmId) -> SvmState;
}
```

###### 3.4 knfsd per netns

`nfsdctl autostart` inside the view reads the SVM's `nfs.conf` (`scope`, `threads`, `grace-time=20`, `lease-time=10`, versions, listeners) and sends `THREADS_SET` with `NFSD_A_SERVER_SCOPE` over generic netlink. `nfsdcld -s /vol/<svm>_root/.otap/nfs/nfsdcld -p /var/lib/nfs/rpc_pipefs` runs on every NFS SVM before nfsd with pipe-held readiness; an empty reclaim table skips the v4 grace, so a datastore SVM's NLM grace is lockd's 20 s alone. `rpc.statd -F -L -P <root dir> -n <svm fqdn> -p 32765 -o 32766`; after a start on a new node `sm-notify -f -P <root dir> -v <svm fqdn>`, the fqdn resolving through `/etc/hosts` to a current LIF so `mon_name` and source address match what clients monitored. Early grace end: read `v4_end_grace`, write `Y` once `/proc/fs/nfsd/clients` shows every nfsdcld client reclaimed, poll until `Y`. One global lockd thread serves every SVM's NLM, so a cold-inode open on a stalled volume blocks every SVM's NLM_LOCK for the stall; Proxmox datastores are recommended as NFSv4.1.

###### 3.5 Samba

smb.conf as in round 1 with `netbios name = <SVM>`, `dns hostname` from Raft, `logging = systemd@1` through the bound journal socket, `kernel oplocks = no`, `kernel share modes = no`, the seeded `*` tdb and `rid` per domain with a Raft base, trusted domains enumerated at join. Rule 5 now reads: rid for domain RIDs, the seeded tdb for well-known SIDs, seeded group mappings for BUILTIN. Durable handles: lost on every smbd restart, kept across a LIF blip shorter than the negotiated timeout (60 s default) when the handle holds a lease and no byte-range lock.

###### 3.6 versitygw

Flags as in round 1 minus `--object-lock-mode`; metadata in xattrs; TLS per SVM; IAM from Raft; `GOMEMLIMIT` 0.8 x `MemoryMax`; pinned past PR #2479.

###### 3.7 Block targets

One target per SVM instantiated on both nodes of a pair in the SVM's netns, each node with its own block LIFs and ALUA target port group (`tg_pt_gp_id` fixed per node and written once, `alua_access_type=1`, `implicit_trans_secs` = the worst-case cutover, `preferred` on the home node). Vendor `LIO-ORG`, the round-2 product string and `vpd_unit_serial=<volume uuid>` are written before the first LUN link; per TPG `demo_mode_discovery=0`, `generate_node_acls=0`, `emulate_tpu=1`, `emulate_tpws=1`, never `emulate_write_cache`. Portals: cluster-unique `ip:port`, no wildcard, IPv4 only in Phase C, created inside the netns and checked there with `ss -ltn`; teardown removes sessions and portals, waits for `np_exports` to reach zero, then the LIF devices, then the pins. Planned cutover: 15 on the old owner's group, `Immediate` commit on the receiver, 0 on the new group, 2 on the old.

###### 3.8 nvfail from the client's side

| Protocol, client | Policy and action | What the client sees | After clear |
|---|---|---|---|
| iSCSI and FC, Phase C dirty boot or planned | `pdl`: LUN (1 to 255) unmapped on every TPG | ESXi PDL on all paths; Linux EIO after about 60 s plus detection, qemu stops; Windows errors after 60 s | remap only after host-check shows PDL on every ESXi host; VMs restart, never resume |
| iSCSI and FC, unplanned Phase B or A takeover | `strict`: new unit serial `<uuid>-g<gen>` (new NAA), new LUN number, old LUN unmapped | ESXi: a new device (VMFS resignature), the old one APD until rescan; Linux: new WWID, LVM finds the PV; Windows: new disk, same NTFS volume | re-register VMs on the resignatured datastore |
| NFSv3 and NFSv4.1 | export withheld; `fsid=<uuid>-g<gen>` on re-export | ESTALE at once; ESXi datastore inaccessible, APD after about 125 s, no self-remount; a rebooted host remounts and starts its VMs fresh | hosts unmount and remount with VMs powered off |
| SVM root volume | class `alert`: start anyway, CRIT if the root's CP generation is older than the one recorded at the last successful start | clients that first connected in the lost interval get `RECLAIM_BAD` and re-open; a rotated machine password is covered by the early CP | none |

SMB (share `available = no`, STATUS_BAD_NETWORK_NAME) and S3 (versitygw stopped, Veeam retries) are unchanged from round 1. The NAA changes with the serial because LIO builds the NAA IEEE Registered Extended designator from the company id and the hex digits of `unit_serial` [verified: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/target/target_core_spc.c].

###### 3.9 LIFs and the ladders

NAS LIFs are macvlan (bridge mode) on `bond0.<vlan>` with the persistent Raft MAC, created with `IFLA_NET_NS_FD` into the netns (rtnetlink 0.23.0) and announced by `nbladed`'s own GARP at 0, 300 ms and 1 s; block LIFs never move. Planned move (Phase B): M0 `otap-ctl` checks Steady and lag under one CP; M1 write 15 to A's ALUA group, `ss -K`, remove NAS addresses; M2 stop NAS units (smbd 1 to 2 s, versitygw at most 5 s, `nfsdctl threads 0`); M3 unmount (at most 2 s with 2 GiB dirty); M4 final CP, ship, `commit: Immediate` (0.3 to 0.5 s HDD); M5 on B: ALUA 0, NAS start, addresses up, GARP, `sm-notify`; M6 ALUA 2 on A. Client-visible: block 1.5 to 2.5 s p50, NFSv3 4 to 8 s, NFSv4.1 plus grace unless early end, SMB handle loss and reconnect 10 to 20 s. Unplanned: B promotes at the applied CP, flips its group to AO, raises NAS LIFs after the `arping -D` gate, applies `strict` to every dirty block volume and withholds every dirty NFS export. A `Stuck` at M3 aborts the move before any ownership change (A back in about 1 s).

###### 3.10 Governance and QoS

Slices govern userspace only; lockd and nfsd kthreads are node-wide and unattributed; the per-volume token bucket (`QosPolicy { max_iops, max_mbps, burst_ms }`, 1 ms refill, delay never fail, 1 s hold cap) runs in the ublk handler, exempt from the 2 s stall detector and re-checking the epoch at release; REQ_META requests bypass it; NAS volumes add per-bdi `max_bytes` and `strict_limit`. Template defaults: datastore `CPUWeight=200`, file 100, backup 50; `MemoryMax` from Storage's table.

###### 3.11 Memory inputs for Storage's table

Per SVM: namespaces and view 2 MiB; NFS helpers 14 MiB; nfsd threads 18 MiB (16) or 35 MiB (32), unattributed; smbd 12 MiB plus 10 MiB per connection [believed]; winbindd 25 MiB plus 5 MiB per domain; versitygw 150 MiB idle [believed]; fixed cost 25 MiB standalone, 60 MiB with AD, at most 4 GiB for 64 SVMs. `svm.slice MemoryMax` = DRAM minus Storage's engine budget minus 4 GiB in Phase C, half of that in Phase B.

###### 3.12 Crates and interfaces (2026-10-12 snapshot)

rustix 1.1.5, nix 0.31.3, zbus 5.19.0, rtnetlink 0.23.0, tokio 1.53.2, nftables 0.6.3, toml 1.1.8, inotify 0.11.5 (C39), caps 0.5.6, seccompiler 0.5.0, socket2 [believed]. Kernel interfaces as in round 1 plus `/sys/class/bdi/<dev>/{max_bytes,strict_limit}`, the `nfsd` genetlink family, `attrib/{demo_mode_discovery,generate_node_acls}`, `alua/<group>/*`, `wwn/vpd_unit_serial` and `ublk_drv.ublks_max`.

##### 4. Phase C work items and what Phases B and A add

- **C1 `svm::ns`.** Exit: 1,000 create and destroy cycles leak no namespace or mount; the pins exist on the host after `unshare --fork` returns and `nsenter --mount=<pin>` sees the pivoted view; build time at most 5 ms; the view is invisible on the host; `/run/opentap` is private.
- **C2 LIFs and firewall.** Exit: as before, plus `ss -K` closes every client connection before the address goes and an NFSv3 client reconnects within 2 s of the LIF's return; the `arping -D` gate fails while another host answers for the address and passes within 1 s of silence.
- **C3 Junctions and volumes.** Exit: unchanged, plus a snapshot exported with its own `fsid=` resolves to the snapshot's data, never the live volume's (C19).
- **C4 iSCSI blade.** Exit: the step 1 table with the P9 ladder; LUN 0 refused; 05h/25h/00h on the wire for the lowest data LUN at nvfail; SendTargets isolation; `write_cache == write back` and `fua == 1` on every LUN; the ALUA group in C18 order with Standby exercised; `strict` yields a new NAA on ESXi 8.0 U3 and a new WWID on Debian 13 and Proxmox 9.1; ESXi reaches PDL under `pdl` on a single node within 10 s.
- **C5 NFS blade.** Exit: the step 2 NFS rows; `nfsdctl threads` prints the SVM scope after a thread change; nfsdcld readiness holds with a 2 s injected delay; a datastore SVM's NLM grace is 20 s, not 90; `sm-notify -v` reclaims every Proxmox 9.1 lock within grace after 50 restarts; a pktcap-uw capture records ESXi 8's `stable_how`; ESXi stays ESTALE across `nvfail clear` until remount; a throttled 1,000 IOPS volume holds at most 8 MiB dirty while another volume's 4 KiB FILE_SYNC p99 stays under 2 ms.
- **C6 SMB blade.** Exit: the step 2 SMB and AD rows; `wbinfo -S` identical for S-1-5-32-544, S-1-5-32-545, S-1-1-0 and S-1-5-11 across same-domain SVMs; Domain Admins are in BUILTIN\Administrators on a seeded SVM; the 10 s LIF-blip test passes with a leased, lock-free handle and smbd running; a password change survives `svm stop/start`.
- **C7 S3 blade.** Exit: the Veeam row with the pinned build; `GetObjectLockConfiguration` sane; a `svm stop/start` mid-job retried to completion.
- **C8 Slices and QoS.** Exit: as before, plus the C5 dirty-pool test and a REQ_META bypass test (COMMIT p99 under 5 ms on a throttled volume).
- **C9 Lifecycle, hardening, `otapctl svm`.** Exit: 1,000 lifecycle cycles; `Stuck` reported with an injected D-state volume; inside tenant smbd `CAP_SYS_ADMIN` is absent, `/dev/ublkb*` and other SVMs' pins are invisible, `unshare` and `mount` fail.
- **C10 FC client targets** with Fabrics: the step 3 criteria plus the C27 and C28 rules (physical `tpgt_1` first, NPIV only on F_Port, `vport_state` tracked).

**Phase B adds**: `BlockStandby` on the partner with the ALUA flip; the NAS move of 3.9 with the pre-copy veto and `commit: Immediate`; the `arping -D` gate; `strict` nvfail and NFS withholding after unplanned takeovers; the root volume in the consistency group with the early CP; NPIV FC LIFs on F_Port fabrics; `volume rehost` with the seeded-identity check; timer rows: planned block 1.5 to 2.5 s p50, NFSv3 4 to 8 s, NFSv4.1 plus grace, SMB 10 to 20 s with handle loss, NAS unplanned 15 to 60 s until replay is measured, lease 10 s, grace 20 s, sm-notify retry 15 min.

**Phase A adds**: the same block presence on shared SAS, PR policies per R9, XFS mounts on the survivor after fence evidence, NAS as an SVM restart on the partner without the ship step.

##### 5. Open disagreements

- **Fabrics says** ship `no_path_retry queue` and deliver nvfail by LUN deletion plus a unit attention. **I say** the kernel only logs that unit attention, and `queue` replays held writes onto the rolled-back LUN after clear. **Settle**: the C4 test on Proxmox 9.1 with `queue`: write under nvfail, clear, show the replayed bytes; then the owner sizes the no-quorum hold at or under 60 s (D7), since a longer hold stops Proxmox VMs under the built-in entry.
- **Storage says** per-(LIF, node) MACs with GARP for unplanned takeovers. **I say** a persistent MAC plus the `arping -D` gate, because a MAC change needs every client to accept an unsolicited ARP. **Settle**: the C2 wedged-node measurement (kernel alive, `dbladed` hung): NAS pause with the gate versus with a MAC change.
- **Fabrics and Storage say** the SVM root volume's nvfail class is `on`. **I say** `alert` with the content check, because an unmounted root is a certain outage for every share while a one-CP-stale root costs a few reclaims. **Settle**: owner decision D5 with the class table presented once.
- **Consensus says** every Phase B NAS takeover pays log replay. **I say** the replay belongs on the receiver or in a periodic fsfreeze-cut CP. **Settle**: Storage measures replay time for 20 volumes with 128 MiB logs on the replica with and without pre-replay; the timer row follows the measurement.
- **Storage says** `strict` for every nvfail. **I say** `pdl` with the host-check gate for the single node and planned cases. **Settle**: the C4 lab test of all-paths PDL on ESXi 8.0 U3, including the rescan case C01 flags as undocumented.

##### 6. Answers to the other personas' asks

**Storage.** (1) An out-of-band CP of one volume does not exist: accepted; a `secrets.tdb` change triggers an early aggregate CP. (2) The bucket stays in the ublk handler at about 20 ns per request, held completions exempt from the stall detector and epoch-checked at release: accepted, with REQ_META bypass and per-bdi caps. (3) `.snapshot` inside the junction through `crossmnt` in Phase C: no; C19 makes an auto-exported snapshot resolve to the live volume, so Phase C exposes snapshots through SMB Previous Versions and explicit per-snapshot NFS exports with their own `fsid`; the in-junction view is Phase B on those exports. (4) Class table: LUN `on`, NAS datastore `on`, NAS file `on` (withholding plus fsid generation, agreeing with Fabrics C7), object `alert`, root `alert`.

**Fabrics.** (1) Should iSCSI follow the ONTAP SAN model? Yes: per-node block LIFs, both nodes carry the target, ALUA does the cutover, and the NPIV vport on the partner is the FC standby path on fabrics that allow it. (2) Is the physical-port target acceptable for step 3? Yes: ESXi and Proxmox claim and multipath rules match vendor and model, not port identity, and the SATP rule assigning `VMW_PSP_RR` ships with step 1.

**Consensus.** (1) The warm-standby skeleton is the pin set, the private `/run` and inactive transient units: about 5 ms and 2 MiB per SVM, no `ProtectHostname` or `NetworkNamespacePath`. (2) `NasServing` is S1 to S9 of the start ladder plus `sm-notify` and the early grace end: 0.5 s on clean logs, up to 60 s with replay. (3) The witness may hold the SVM placement table (small, written only on moves); cursors and bases stay on the aggregates, and a relationship per SVM over the aggregate CP matches my consistency group. (4) `otap-ctl` drives `SvmLifecycle::stop` (10 s per step) and `start` (15 s) through `nbladed`; a `Stuck` at M3 aborts the move with the SVM back on A in about 1 s; keeping the NFSv4 identity across a move is right because reclaim then fails only on rolled-back volumes, and the scope is now cluster-unique so a DR cluster can never alias it.

### Opus-Fabrics

#### Opus-Fabrics, Session 03 round 3: responses, consequences and the revised transport and FC design

Short version: I accept every hole. One change absorbs most of them: the chunk is Storage's self-describing stripe image, and the transport owns only the envelope, the cursor, the credits and the connections. TLS becomes mandatory, which deletes the zero-copy-from-the-arena path and three kernel-version hazards with it. FC positions stand, corrected on LUN 0, `emulate_write_cache`, the nvfail presentation and NPIV topology.

##### 1. Responses to holes raised against me

###### Raised by Opus-Storage

**F1 (manifest not stable, per-extent CRC not free). ACCEPT.** The chunk becomes the post-merge stripe image the CP assembler stages (its summary page carries the per-4 KiB CRC, volume, LBA, birth and a 2-bit `kind`). Patches are merged before a stripe exists, so "chunk `(cp_id, idx)` is always the same bytes" holds by construction: staging copy and on-disk stripe are identical, and a reclaimed slot is re-read as the same stripe from cache or disk. `ManifestEntry`, `ExtentSrc`, the manifest frame and `crc32c_combine` are deleted; the chunk CRC is one PCLMUL pass, 0.07 core at 1 GB/s [believed].

**F2 (discards and volume events absent). ACCEPT.** Two frame kinds: `VolEvent` (create with geometry and class, resize, delete, snapshot tag) and `Holes` (16 B entries `vol u32, len u32, lba u64`), ordered inside the delta before any chunk that references the volume. `Abort(UnknownVol)` is retried every 1 s for 60 s while the receiver's Raft follower applies `VolState`, then Broken with that reason.

**F3 (shipping holds back HDD ingest). ACCEPT.** The retention budget and the read-cache write-through are Storage's; the stream promises only that it never reads the HDD pool itself: every re-read goes through `DeltaSource::read_chunk`, routed by `MediaProfile.ship_readback` (default `cache`). The throughput table carries Storage's HDD pair figures: 0.5 GB/s empty, 0.3 GB/s aged.

**F4 (receiver apply is a full CP; pending table and socket buffers undersized). ACCEPT.** `commit(cp)` is a replica CP (map leaves, segment table, superblock) with the source's map-page budget, triggered by `DeltaEnd` (`ShipApply`), not by the receiver's timer. The 48 B pending table is deleted; the landing index is Storage's 16 B per block structure (42 MB for a 2.6 M-block CP). The sysctl line was wrong: `tcp_rmem`/`tcp_wmem` maxima are 16 MiB (25GbE x 1 ms RTT is 3 MB of BDP [believed]), so 256 MiB worst case stands. Land rate is reported as min(link, staging drain, leaf-write rate).

**F5 (coalescing drops snapshots). ACCEPT.** Coalescing never crosses a tagged snapshot: ship `K -> snap`, then `snap -> newest`. `VolEvent::SnapTag{uuid, name, retention}` rides inside the delta; the receiver pins the tag at `commit` and the catalogue replicates.

**F6 (sender restart cannot resume). ACCEPT.** With the stripe image as chunk and a `cp_id` nonce (Protocols S1) in `DeltaBegin`, every `Chunk`, `DeltaEnd` and the cursor, a restarted sender resumes at `landed_contig` from disk bytes identical to those already landed; a CP that never reached its superblock has no `cp_id` on the sender, so a `DeltaBegin` with the same `cp_seq` and a different `cp_id` makes the receiver discard the partial. No manifest digest is needed.

**F7 (1 MiB O_DIRECT landings on a hardware RAID VD). ACCEPT.** `WRITE_FIXED` per chunk is deleted. `land()` hands blocks to the engine's CP assembler and segment writer, which builds full stripes for the receiver's own geometry and commits through `Backstore::commit`, attestation included. `Landed` means the segment writer has written the staging stripes holding the chunk, not that they are flushed.

**F8 (cloning registered buffers needs a sparse source table). ACCEPT the rule; the revised design no longer clones.** Verified on 6.12: `io_clone_buffers` copies the whole table including `dummy_ubuf` entries and `__io_sqe_buffers_update` needs only `ctx->buf_data`, which the clone sets, so "register sparse, clone, update per ring" works [verified: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/io_uring/rsrc.c]; the crate exposes `register_buffers_sparse`, `register_buffers_clone` and `register_buffers_update` [verified: https://docs.rs/io-uring/0.7.15/io_uring/struct.Submitter.html]. With TLS mandatory the arena is never a send source; each connection ring registers only its own 4 KiB-page-backed bounce and read-back buffers.

###### Raised by Opus-Protocols

**F1 (`emulate_write_cache=1` is EINVAL on iblock). ACCEPT**, confirmed by C09. `blade_fc` and `blade_lio` never write it; `dbladed` sets `UBLK_ATTR_VOLATILE_CACHE | UBLK_ATTR_FUA` before `START_DEV`; the reconciler asserts `/sys/block/ublkbN/queue/write_cache == "write back"` and `queue/fua == 1` before linking any LUN; no OpenTAP rule ever writes `queue/write_cache`.

**F2 (two stream formats). ACCEPT.** Envelope, cursor and credits are mine; the payload is Storage's stripe image; `DeltaSource` is Storage's trait, `DeltaStream` mine, `DeltaSink` merged with per-chunk `Landed` credits. `otap-stream` v1 freezes the envelope and treats the payload as opaque bytes with a CRC; Storage's `otap-format` v2 freezes the stripe image. One owner decision (item 0) precedes both item 1s.

**F3 (sized for two relationships, Raft for a hundred). ACCEPT.** The transport session is a pipe per (source aggregate, destination aggregate) with its own connections, credits and buffers; a Phase B node has two. Relationships multiplex by `rel`: the pipe's steady-state delta covers every outbound volume of the aggregate CP at once (detach is per pipe, because the CP is one object); consistency groups (an SVM's volumes, Protocols S9) get their own `rel` sessions only for catch-up and resync walks. Memory stays under 0.5 GiB (3.1).

**F4 (direct attach shares one TPG; one WWNN per node). ACCEPT.** Direct attach: one SVM per physical port, refused otherwise; `shared_port = true` is an opt-in with node-wide LUN IDs and no tenant guarantee. WWNN per SVM `2A:SS:<OUI+serial of the home node's lowest WWPN>`, LIF WWPNs `2B:LL:<same six bytes>`, both stored in Raft at creation; physical QLogic ports use `20:00`, `21:00` and `21:01` in the vendor field, so neither collides [believed]. Data LUN IDs are 1 to 255 (C02).

**F5 (`no_path_retry 12`; Unavailable lets writes replay). ACCEPT.** `12` stays, `queue` is withdrawn; a Proxmox VM gets EIO about 65 s after the last path fails (60 s plus `fast_io_fail_tmo` 5 s [believed]). Nvfail on a LUN is an unmap of the non-zero data LUN from every TPG and ACL on the surviving node (25h/00h, C02) plus an identity change for unplanned takeovers (Storage P5), because the dead node's paths keep the device in APD (C01). `stop` and ordinary takeovers use Unavailable and Standby.

**F6 (no online growth on 6.12). ACCEPT with one amendment.** NAS volumes are created at `size_max` (thin). Client-visible LUNs present `size`: a Standby path answers READ CAPACITY(10) and (16) in LIO [verified: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/target/target_core_alua.c], so both paths must report the same number, and a LUN presenting `size_max` would let ESXi lay VMFS over space the engine refuses. LUN growth on 6.12 is a device re-create: on a pair, standby first with its backstore torn down (C10), group flip, then the other side; in Phase C a planned pause of 3 to 5 s (unlink, delete backstore, `STOP_DEV`/`START_DEV`, relink, rescan) [believed].

###### Raised by Opus-Consensus

**F1 (specified against a delta Storage does not produce). ACCEPT**, as Storage F1. Two requirements go to Storage (S3): a 2-bit `kind` (`Ingest | Relocate | Applied | Merge`) per summary entry and a per-stripe volume bitmap, so the sender ships only stripes holding `Ingest` blocks of outbound volumes and the receiver drops non-inbound entries; outbound ingest packed into its own stripes, else the shipper repacks at one copy (about 0.1 core per GB/s [believed]).

**F2 (`tls = false` contradicts R21). ACCEPT.** TLS 1.3 with mutual authentication against the cluster CA on every endpoint; `tls` and `direct` are deleted. `Hello` carries the pipe's direction epoch and is refused when stale. Cost: 0.4 to 0.5 core per side at 10GbE [believed].

**F3 (`Committed` means two things). ACCEPT.** `applied` is the replica CP done (roots switched, superblock durable); `ShipApply` fires at `DeltaEnd` when no own CP is in flight, else at the next; the receiver's CP timer is 2 s while a delta lands. The stream reports `landed_age_s` and `applied_age_s` separately on Consensus's 1 s heartbeat; the gate reads `applied_age_s`.

**F4 (credits for memory landing). ACCEPT.** Credits are 4 KiB units of free receiver staging, granted per staged stripe, so the sender is bounded by the landing rate. The staging size is Storage's; the stream needs at least 64 MiB per pipe at 10GbE, 256 MiB at 25GbE.

**F5 (standby paths or LIF moves). ACCEPT.** Standby paths for every block protocol: FC vport pairs and iSCSI portals inside the SVM netns (C11), static per node; takeover is the ALUA flip; LIF moves are NAS-only.

**F6 (corrupt source re-sends forever). ACCEPT.** After three `Abort(Corrupt, idx)` for one chunk the sender re-reads the stripe from disk, bypassing cache, and verifies every 4 KiB CRC: cache-only corruption resends and counts `cache_corruption`; an on-disk mismatch makes the relationship `Broken(MediaError{pba})` with a media alert. The chunk is never skipped; a replica missing a block is not a replica.

##### 2. Fact-check consequences

- **C01 (PDL rules).** Forces the nvfail change in Protocols F5: Unavailable is never called "PDL-style" again; PDL needs 25h/00h or 68h/00h on every path, which a dead partner's paths cannot give, so unplanned nvfail defaults to unmap plus a new `vpd_unit_serial`, allowed only while `export_count == 0`, which the unmap guarantees [verified: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/target/target_core_configfs.c]. `Disk.PathEvalTime=30` is a revival accelerator, not a guard. Lab item: dead-path plus PDL behaviour on ESXi 8.
- **C02 (virtual LUN 0).** Forces: no data LUN at mapped LUN 0, IDs 1 to 255, a Raft validator rule, the TMR asymmetry in the failure-injection matrix. Lab item: ESXi 8 with LIO's virtual LUN 0.
- **C09, C10, C11.** Force Protocols F1; `options ublk_drv ublks_max=4096` and the standby-only re-create rule (`UPDATE_SIZE` on 6.16 or later is the forward path); the ip:port uniqueness invariant for portals, which FC vports do not need because the driver refuses a duplicate WWPN.
- **C17.** Confirms `LIO-ORG`; the shipped Proxmox file is empty plus `find_multipaths "strict"`; `directio` and `detect_checker no` are the built-in values; the recipe verifies with `multipath -t | grep -A12 LIO-ORG`.
- **C18.** Adds the setup order (`tg_pt_gp_id` write-once and identical on both nodes, support bits, `alua_access_type=1` because the default 3 accepts STPG, `preferred`, `implicit_trans_secs=10`, then state), the installer-created `/etc/target/pr` and `alua/tpgs_<g>` directories, and `vpd_unit_serial` before the first link.
- **C24, C25.** Confirm the rules: `SEND_ZC` only, never `SENDMSG_ZC` with a fixed buffer; `MSG_WAITALL`; the notification is a buffer-lifetime event; 4 KiB-page-backed bounce buffers, so the folio truesize caveat cannot apply; `ReadvFixed`/`WritevFixed` forbidden.
- **C26.** Forces nothing: userspace rustls, not kTLS; a future kTLS path must use plain `SEND` and release at the send CQE.
- **C27, C28.** `qlini_mode` is load-time only, so the sysfs refusal text goes and the installer validates the spelling; the physical TPG, whose enable logs out every vport, is enabled before any NPIV TPG and never disabled while vports serve; NPIV needs an F_Port fabric login; `max_npiv_vports` defaults to 63, not my 254; `vport_state` is the LIF's operational state.
- **C29.** Precision: no NVMe-FC target role; the initiator role exists.
- **C30.** `Disk.MaxLUN` is an exclusive bound over IDs 0 to 16,383; the claim rule is mandatory because MRU is the default PSP; the direct-attach matrix states minimum driver versions (8.0.x: qlnativefc 5.4.80 or later; 7.0: 5.3.80 or later, or below 4.1.37.0), the "Direct Connect/DAS/N2N" name and the log signature.
- **C31.** The Proxmox test targets PVE 9.1, enables `snapshot-as-volume-chain` before any disk exists, machine version 10 or later, LIO `emulate_tpu`/`emulate_tpws`, and checks that a deleted snapshot returns space.
- **C38, C39.** Pins confirmed as a 2026-10-12 snapshot; Cargo.lock is the authority.
- **No change:** C03, C04 (Storage's ublk path), C05 to C08 and C21 to C23 (hardware RAID and md durability reach the receiver only through the engine's segment writer, which F7 mandates), C12 to C16, C19, C20, C32 to C37, C40.

##### 3. Revised design

###### 3.1 The pipe, the delta, the chunk

A pipe is a TLS session set between two aggregates. A delta is `(rel, base, target, cp_id)`: steady state ships one committed CP's stripes in staging order; catch-up, resync and coalesced deltas are map walks in PBA (segment) order per consistency group, chunked as the live blocks of each on-disk stripe born after `base`, so every chunk is re-derivable from disk, with the delta's segment list GC-pinned from `describe()` to `DeltaEnd` (requirement on Storage). A chunk is one stripe image, at most 8 MiB (2.5 MiB on a 12-drive HDD RAID6, 256 KiB on flash), opaque to the transport except for its CRC.

**Framing.** A 64-byte little-endian header laid out with zerocopy 0.8.62: `magic u32, ver u16, kind u8, flags u8 | rel u32, idx u32 | cp_seq u64 | base u64 | cp_id u64 | owner_epoch u64 | wire_len u32, raw_len u32 | payload_crc u32, hdr_crc u32`; `flags` carries the codec. Kinds: `Hello, HelloAck, DeltaBegin, VolEvent, Chunk, Holes, DeltaEnd, Landed, Committed, Abort, Ping, Pong`. `Hello` carries node id, pipe id, direction epoch and caps; `HelloAck` the cursor; `DeltaBegin` chunk count, bytes, snapshot tags and `cut_age_ms` so both ages are measured from `cut_mono` (Consensus C4); `DeltaEnd` a BLAKE3 digest over the summary pages, sent only after the sender's superblock write completed. Golden vectors and property tests freeze the format first; the parser is safe Rust, fuzzed.

**Cursor and resume.** The receiver owns the cursor (sketch below), persisted in a 4 KiB page per pipe at every receiver CP. Landing is idempotent by `(cp_id, idx)`; a sender restart resumes at `landed_contig`; a different `cp_id` for the same `cp_seq` discards the partial; a receiver restart re-lands whatever its last CP did not record.

**Credits.** One budget per pipe in 4 KiB units of free receiver staging, granted in `Landed` frames as the segment writer writes staged stripes; initial grant 64 MiB, cap at the staging size. TCP windows are the second layer (`tcp_rmem`/`tcp_wmem` max 16 MiB, autotuned).

**Integrity.** Per 4 KiB CRC in the summary page (the engine's unit, verified at landing and on every later read); CRC32C per chunk (crc-fast 1.10.0); BLAKE3 1.8.7 over the summary pages per delta. A bad header CRC drops the connection; a bad chunk CRC is `Abort(Corrupt, idx)` with the Consensus F6 escalation.

**TLS and zero copy.** rustls 0.23.45 with aws-lc-rs, unbuffered API: `WriteTraffic::encrypt(plaintext, outgoing)` writes TLS records straight into a registered bounce buffer [verified: https://docs.rs/rustls/0.23.45/rustls/unbuffered/struct.WriteTraffic.html], called per 16 KiB record. The bounce (two 8 MiB halves per connection, 4 KiB pages) goes out as one `IORING_OP_SEND_ZC` with `IORING_RECVSEND_FIXED_BUF`, `MSG_WAITALL` and `IORING_SEND_ZC_REPORT_USAGE`; the half is reused at the `IORING_CQE_F_NOTIF` completion. Peers reporting `ZC_COPIED` on 500 of 1,000 sends (tap ports, no-SG devices, tcpdump) fall back to `IORING_OP_SEND`. Sender cost: one AES pass, no kernel copy. Receiver: `IORING_OP_RECV` into an 8 MiB buffer, in-place decrypt, CRC, then `land()`, whose copy into the engine's staging is the third pass. Compression (`auto`: zstd 3 on two workers at 1GbE, LZ4 behind a sampled ratio gate at 10GbE, off at 25GbE) adds one pass into an 8 MiB scratch before encryption.

**Connections and endpoints.** `connections = auto`: one at 10GbE and below, four at 25GbE and above; chunks round-robin; control frames on connection 0; a dead connection re-queues its unlanded chunks. Endpoints in priority order (DAC, then LAN): connect budget 1 s including TLS and `Hello`, dead after 3 s of silence with data pending, `Ping` every 1 s when idle, two reconnects then the next endpoint, back-off 1 to 30 s, fail-back after 30 s of good probes; active/standby, never striping.

**Throughput targets** (TLS on, 1500-byte MTU, destination not limiting):

| Link | Payload ceiling | Target | Connections | Cores per side (AES-GCM 2 to 4 GB/s per core, recv copy 5 to 10 GB/s [believed]) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1GbE | 118 MB/s | 110 MB/s | 1 | 0.2 |
| 10GbE | 1.18 GB/s | 1.0 GB/s | 1 | sender 0.8, receiver 1.3 |
| 25GbE | 2.95 GB/s | 2.0 GB/s | 4 | sender 2, receiver 3 to 4 |
| 40 and 100GbE | 4.7 and 11.8 GB/s | 3 GB/s, not promised | 8 | needs `RECV_ZC` (6.15) |

HDD destinations cap the pair at 0.5 GB/s empty and 0.3 GB/s aged regardless of link (Storage F3). Lag: `applied_age = CP interval + max(delta / link, delta / land rate) + receiver CP`; 300 MB/s ingest, 10 s CPs, 10GbE and an HDD receiver landing 0.5 GB/s gives a 3 GB delta, 6 s ship, 1 to 3 s apply, so `applied_age` oscillates between 8 and 19 s and a takeover rolls back at most 19 s plus the 3 s lease. Coalescing after two queued CPs bounds the backlog by the changed set and never crosses a snapshot tag.

**Memory, per node, one outbound and one inbound pipe, four connections each:**

| Consumer | Size |
|---|---|
| Send source | 0 (Storage's staging pool and retention budget) |
| TLS send bounce, 2 x 8 MiB x 4, registered, 4 KiB pages | 64 MiB |
| Compression scratch, 8 MiB x 4, codec only | 32 MiB |
| Catch-up read-back, 8 MiB x 4, registered | 32 MiB |
| Receive buffers, 2 x 8 MiB x 4 | 64 MiB |
| Receiver staging and landing index | Storage's lines (2 GiB; 16 B per block) |
| Socket buffers, 16 MiB max x 2 x 8 | 256 MiB worst, 64 MiB typical |
| Transport total | about 220 MiB typical, 450 MiB worst |

**State tables.** Sender session, one per pipe:

| State | Event | Action | Next |
|---|---|---|---|
| Idle | committed CP above `applied`, or a catch-up order | pick the preferred healthy endpoint | Connecting |
| Connecting | TLS, `Hello`/`HelloAck` within 1 s | read cursor; resume if `cp_id` matches; coalesce if more than 2 CPs queued and no tag between | Describing |
| Connecting | two failures | next endpoint; back-off 1 to 30 s when all fail | Connecting / Idle |
| Describing | `DeltaBegin`, `VolEvent`s, `Holes` sent | start at `landed_contig` | Streaming |
| Streaming | credits cover the next chunk | `read_chunk`, compress, encrypt, `SEND_ZC` | Streaming |
| Streaming | `Landed(idx, credits)` / `NOTIF` CQE | advance, report `landed_contig` / reuse the bounce half | Streaming |
| Streaming | third `Abort(Corrupt, idx)` | re-read from disk, verify 4 KiB CRCs; media alert if bad | Streaming / Broken |
| Streaming | all landed, CP superblock durable | `DeltaEnd(digest)` | Ending |
| Ending | `Committed(cp)` | move base pin; report both ages | Idle |
| Streaming / Ending | endpoint dead | keep delta; mark endpoint | Connecting |
| any | `Abort(NoSpace / BaseMismatch / Version / StaleEpoch / UnknownVol after 60 s)` | report | Broken |
| Broken | resync order from Consensus | rebase to the common snapshot | Connecting |

Receiver, one per inbound pipe:

| State | Event | Action | Next |
|---|---|---|---|
| Listening | `Hello`, valid cluster certificate, current direction epoch | `HelloAck(cursor)` | Sessioned |
| Sessioned | `DeltaBegin`, `base == applied`, bytes under free space minus GC reserve | discard a partial with another `cp_id`; open landing | Landing |
| Sessioned | base mismatch, no space, stale epoch | `Abort(reason)` | Sessioned |
| Landing | `VolEvent` for a volume Raft does not yet know | `Abort(UnknownVol)` | Landing |
| Landing | chunk, CRC ok, new / duplicate `(cp_id, idx)` | `land()` into the CP assembler, `Landed` when its stripes are written / drop, `Landed` | Landing |
| Landing | `DeltaEnd`, digest ok, all landed | `ShipApply` replica CP; `Committed(cp)` | Sessioned |
| Landing | connection lost or restart | cursor from the last receiver CP; re-land the rest | Listening |

Endpoint selection is unchanged (Preferred, Secondary, Down with the 3 s, 30 s and 1 to 30 s rows).

**Traits.**

```rust
pub struct DeltaDesc { pub rel: RelId, pub base: CpSeq, pub target: CpSeq, pub cp_id: CpId,
                       pub chunks: u32, pub bytes: u64, pub tags: Vec<SnapTag>, pub cut_mono: Mono }
pub trait DeltaSource {              // Storage's trait; what the stream needs from it
    fn describe(&self, rel: RelId, base: CpSeq, target: CpSeq) -> Result<DeltaDesc, SrcErr>; // GC-pins segments
    fn events(&self, d: &DeltaDesc) -> Vec<VolEvent>;      fn holes(&self, d: &DeltaDesc) -> Vec<Hole>;
    fn read_chunk(&self, d: &DeltaDesc, idx: u32, dst: &mut [u8], bypass_cache: bool) -> Result<u32, SrcErr>;
    fn landed_up_to(&self, d: &DeltaDesc, idx: u32);        // retention hint only
    fn pin(&self, rel: RelId, cp: CpSeq) -> Result<SnapId, SrcErr>;   fn unpin(&self, s: SnapId);
}
pub struct Cursor { pub applied: CpSeq, pub applied_epoch: u64, pub landing: Option<(CpSeq, CpId)>,
                    pub landed_contig: u32, pub landed_sparse: Vec<(u32, u32)>, pub credits: u32 }
pub enum Event { Sent(BounceHalf), Landed { idx: u32, credits: u32 }, Committed(CpSeq),
                 Reconnected(Cursor), Dead(EndpointId), Aborted(AbortReason, u32) }
pub trait DeltaStream: Send {        // Fabrics; impl TlsTcp; never leaks sockets, TLS state, codec, timers
    fn open(&mut self, pipe: PipeId, epoch: u64) -> Result<Cursor, StreamErr>;
    fn begin(&mut self, d: &DeltaDesc, ev: &[VolEvent], holes: &[Hole]) -> Result<(), StreamErr>;
    fn send(&mut self, d: &DeltaDesc, idx: u32, stripe: &[u8]) -> Result<(), StreamErr>;  // Err(Window)
    fn end(&mut self, d: &DeltaDesc, digest: [u8; 32]) -> Result<(), StreamErr>;
    fn poll(&mut self, out: &mut Vec<Event>) -> usize;      fn close(&mut self);
}
pub trait DeltaSink {                // receiver; Storage implements the engine half
    fn cursor(&self, pipe: PipeId) -> Cursor;
    fn begin(&mut self, d: &DeltaDesc) -> Result<(), SinkErr>;           // BaseMismatch, NoSpace, cp_id discard
    fn vol_event(&mut self, d: &DeltaDesc, e: &VolEvent) -> Result<(), SinkErr>;   // UnknownVol
    fn land(&mut self, d: &DeltaDesc, idx: u32, stripe: &[u8]) -> Result<u32, SinkErr>; // idempotent; credits
    fn holes(&mut self, d: &DeltaDesc, h: &[Hole]) -> Result<(), SinkErr>;
    fn commit(&mut self, d: &DeltaDesc) -> Result<(), SinkErr>;          // replica CP; returns when durable
    fn abort(&mut self, d: &DeltaDesc);
}
```

**Configuration.**

```toml
[[pipe]]
name = "aggr1 -> node-b/aggr1";   connections = "auto";   window_mib = 64
endpoints = ["10.255.0.2:7430", "192.168.10.12:7430"]   # priority order; TLS and mTLS always
[[relationship]]
pipe = "aggr1 -> node-b/aggr1";   group = { svm = "hv" }  # consistency group = SVM, root included
schedule = "every-cp";   coalesce_after_cps = 2;   compression = "auto"
```

**Crates** (2026-10-12 snapshot, all [verified: C39]): io-uring 0.7.15, rustls 0.23.45 with aws-lc-rs, crc-fast 1.10.0, blake3 1.8.7, lz4_flex 0.14.0, zstd 0.14.2, zerocopy 0.8.62, rustix 1.1.5, postcard 1.1.3, memmap2 0.9.11, tokio 1.53.2 for the control plane only. The data path is io_uring threads on the non-isolated cores at a `CPUWeight` below the ublk reactors: one sustains 10GbE with TLS, four sustain 25GbE.

###### 3.2 FC as a transport

Unchanged: not built in Phases C, B or A. The envelope is transport-blind (chunks addressed by `(cp_id, idx)`), so an FC landing ring could follow v0.3 if an FC-only interconnect ever appears. qla2xxx has no NVMe-FC target role on 6.12, only the initiator role, and Marvell has said none is coming (C29). The `FcLink` capability bits are dropped.

###### 3.3 FC client targets

Module profile: `options qla2xxx qlini_mode=disabled ql2xnvmeenable=0 ql2xmqsupport=1`, `ql2xfwloadbin=1` per the ISP25xx rule, `ql2xexchoffld=4096` on 16G and 32G cards; `qlini_mode` is load-time only and validated by the installer (C27). Firmware table, inventory and floors unchanged. The physical TPG is enabled once at boot, before any NPIV TPG, and never disabled while vports serve.

NPIV FC LIFs exist only behind an F_Port fabric login; direct attach and loop use the physical TPG with one SVM per port. Names: `qla2xxx_npiv/<phys wwpn colon form>@<16 hex>:<16 hex>/tpgt_1`; at most 32 vports per port (firmware default 63); `vport_state` is the LIF's operational state; LIFs do not move: each SVM gets one vport per node and ALUA decides the live path. Vport migration stays a Phase B opt-in experiment, now also the only FC mechanism that could answer PDL on the dead node's paths without an identity change.

Revised tree, shared with `blade_lio`:

```
core/iblock_0/vm-ds1/     control <- "udev_path=/dev/ublkb3"   (ublk params VOLATILE_CACHE | FUA, asserted via sysfs)
  wwn/{vendor_id=LIO-ORG, product_id=OpenTAP, revision=0001, vpd_unit_serial=<uuid, same on both nodes>}  before any link
  attrib/{emulate_tpu=1, emulate_tpws=1, block_size=512|4096}          never emulate_write_cache
  alua/otap_n1/  tg_pt_gp_id=1 -> support bits -> alua_access_type=1 -> preferred=1 -> implicit_trans_secs=10 -> state 0
  alua/otap_n2/  tg_pt_gp_id=2 ... state 2 (Phases B and A)
  enable <- 1
qla2xxx/21:00:00:24:ff:3a:1b:c0/tpgt_1/                                  physical port
qla2xxx_npiv/21:00:00:24:ff:3a:1b:c0@2b010024ff3a1bc0:2a010024ff3a1bc0/tpgt_1/   SVM 1, LIF 1
  attrib/{generate_node_acls=0, cache_dynamic_acls=0, demo_mode_write_protect=1, demo_mode_login_only=1}
  lun/lun_1 -> core/iblock_0/vm-ds1 ; lun/lun_1/alua_tg_pt_gp <- otap_n1       data LUNs 1..255, never 0
  acls/<initiator wwpn>/lun_1 -> ../../lun/lun_1 ;  enable <- 1
```

The installer creates `/etc/target` with `pr/` and `alua/tpgs_otap_n1/` before `target_core_mod` loads, so `dbroot` never needs a write. Nvfail: unmap the data LUN on every TPG and ACL (25h/00h on live paths), then, for unplanned takeovers, a new `vpd_unit_serial` on clear; ordinary takeovers and `stop` use Unavailable. ESXi recipe: `esxcli storage nmp satp rule add -s VMW_SATP_ALUA -V LIO-ORG -M OpenTAP -P VMW_PSP_RR -O iops=1 -c tpgs_on -e OpenTAP` (`-c tpgs_on` with `-s/-V/-M` [verified: https://docs.oracle.com/cd/E19373-01/E39235/z40002861117562.html]; `-P/-O` [believed: vendor examples]), `Disk.PathEvalTime=30`, guest disk timeouts 180 s, `Disk.MaxLUN` untouched. Proxmox: empty `multipath.conf` plus `find_multipaths "strict"`, `multipath -a`, `multipath-tools-boot`, PVE 9.1 volume-chain snapshots with the C31 preconditions.

###### 3.4 Process topology

Unchanged: `otap-ringd` is retired, the arena is a hugetlbfs file created by systemd units, and the shipper and receiver are reactors in `dbladed` (`catch_unwind` per reactor, mTLS peers only, fuzzed parser). Storage agrees; Consensus's "arena owner under a new name" is section 5, item 3.

##### 4. Work items

Phase C, in order, each with an exit test:

0. Owner decision: envelope (Fabrics) plus stripe-image payload (Storage), `kind` bits and volume bitmap in the summary page, GC pinning per delta. Exit: written into the format document before either item 1 starts.
1. `otap-stream` v1: header, kinds, cursor, credits, `cp_id`, `VolEvent`, `Holes`, golden vectors, property tests (reordering across connections, duplicates, truncation, torn frames, N and N+1, `cp_id` mismatch discards the partial), cargo-fuzz on the parser. Exit: 10,000 synthetic deltas round-trip bit-exact through a loopback mTLS pair; one million mutations without a panic; no change without a `ver` bump.
2. Shipper and receiver reactors in `dbladed`, aggregate 1 to aggregate 2 on one node over loopback TLS. Exit: 100 CPs at 1 GB/s on flash and 0.5 GB/s on HDD; `kill -9` at random points in 50 of them, including between staging and the superblock write; every restart leaves the replica at a CP boundary with BLAKE3 equality per committed CP; duplicate counter equals resend count; sender at most 0.8 core and receiver at most 1.5 cores per GB/s.
3. HBA inventory and boot profile. Exit: 20 reboots each on QLE2562 and QLE2692 pairs; target mode within 15 s; no initiator FLOGI in the switch log; no ISP abort after the boot-time enable; a misspelled `qlini_mode` is caught by the installer.
4. `blade_fc`. Exit: ESXi 8.0 U3 with qlnativefc 5.4.80 or later sees the LUN through a Brocade F_Port and N2N direct attach; `VMW_SATP_ALUA` with our RR rule; VMFS6; one hour of fio at 700 MB/s on 8G, 1.4 GB/s on 16G, 50,000 4 KiB IOPS at p99 under 2 ms on flash; tree applied in under 5 s; lab checks recorded: ESXi with LIO's virtual LUN 0, unmap of LUN 1 giving 25h/00h on every live path, the path list after a rescan with one dead path.
5. Proxmox recipe on PVE 9.1. Exit: live migration on the FC LVM; volume-chain snapshot create, rollback and delete with space returned; `multipath -ll` shows `prio alua` with the OpenTAP path active.
6. NPIV vports per SVM on a fabric. Exit: two SVMs on one port, zoning separation holds, create to online under 3 s, 100 create and delete cycles without a base-port ISP abort or a path flap on the other SVM.
7. Transition under load: Transitioning 2 s then Active/Optimized, 100 times against ESXi and Proxmox. Exit: no client error; I/O resumes within 2.5 s.
8. Reboot persistence. Exit: a from-scratch install plus import yields a byte-identical configfs tree, the same WWNNs and WWPNs, the APTPL file under `/etc/target/pr`, `rtslib-fb-targetctl.service` absent or masked.

Phase B adds: B1 the stream on real links (1.0 GB/s at 10GbE with TLS, sender at most 0.8 core, receiver 1.3, `ZC_COPIED` under 1% on a physical NIC, fallback on a tap-port peer); B2 compression (200 MB/s raw over 1GbE at 2.5:1 with zstd); B3 fallback and resume (100 cable pulls at 80% of line rate, every delta completes, resume within 3 s, zero duplicate applies, a sender crash before its superblock yields exactly one discarded partial); B4 cursor persistence at the receiver CP and both ages on the heartbeat; B5 the timer rows (connect 1 s, dead 3 s, back-off 1 to 30 s, fail-back 30 s, receiver CP 2 s while landing) handed to `otap-ctl`; B6 byte-identical FC trees, partner group Standby, equal replica capacity, ALUA-rolled LUN growth with at most 3 s client-visible pause; B7 the nvfail lab on ESXi: unmap plus serial change with the dead node's paths present ends in a new device, never a resumed one; B8 the vport-migration experiment behind a flag.

Phase A adds: PR for FC LUNs with APTPL under a `dbroot` both nodes can read (identical serials, pre-created `pr/`), `pr_survival` for WSFC-class initiators, the shared-shelf standby presenting the same serial and capacity on Standby paths, and the FC rows of the NDO matrix re-measured on the shelf.

##### 5. Open disagreements

1. **Phase B block presentation.** Protocols says iSCSI LIFs move and a standby path is a lie; I say standby paths with ALUA for FC and iSCSI, portals static per node inside the SVM netns. Settle: owner decision on R9's 3 s planned bound, C01 (PDL needs every path) and C11 (portals bind in the SVM netns).
2. **LUN capacity.** Protocols says pre-size every ublk device to `size_max`; I say client-visible LUNs present `size` and grow by re-create. Settle: Protocols confirms whether a LUN may present more than its usable size to VMFS; if not, the ALUA-rolled re-create stands and B6 measures the pause.
3. **Arena owner process.** Consensus wants one under a new name; Storage and I say the hugetlbfs file needs none. Settle: Phase C exit test 2; 50 of 50 `kill -9` recoveries from the file alone means no process.
4. **Receiver staging size.** Storage's F7 says two segments (160 MiB) per inbound relationship; other Storage and Consensus texts say 2 GiB; I need at least 64 MiB per pipe at 10GbE, 256 MiB at 25GbE. Settle: Storage owns the number; credits adapt.
5. **Stripe packing.** Consensus S3 asks Storage to pack outbound ingest into its own stripes; I need that or I repack at one copy. Settle: Storage's decision, repack cost measured in item 2.
6. **Stream liveness.** Consensus wants the ages on its 1 s control heartbeat; I keep `Ping`/`Pong` on the data link too, because DAC and control LAN fail independently. Settle: both rows in the timer table, owner `otap-ctl`.
7. **PDL on FC after an unplanned takeover.** Storage's identity change versus vport takeover by the survivor. Settle: B7 and B8; identity change is the default until B8 shows better.

##### 6. Answers to questions addressed to me

The other personas' original section 6 texts are not on disk; these are the questions visible in the cross-examinations.

- **Storage, hold release (quoted in Protocols S2):** holds are released on `Landed` (the chunk's blocks written into the receiver's staging stripes), not on the TCP notification and not on apply; the stream reports `landed_contig` to Storage's retention policy, which may free earlier because any chunk can be re-read identically.
- **Storage, `ship_readback`:** the shipper reads back only through `read_chunk`, default `cache`; it never issues I/O to the pool itself.
- **Storage, "state commit as a replica CP":** yes; `commit()` returns when the replica superblock is durable, which is what `Committed` and `applied_age_s` mean.
- **Protocols, which `multipath.conf`:** the empty file with `find_multipaths "strict"`; the built-in `LIO-ORG` entry supplies the rest; `queue` is withdrawn.
- **Protocols, INQUIRY identity:** `LIO-ORG`/`OpenTAP` is permanent.
- **Protocols, one LIF record:** yes, `LifState.transport: Ip{..} | Fc{wwpn, wwnn}`, MACs and WWNs allocated at creation.
- **Consensus, which number the gate reads:** `applied_age_s`, measured from the target CP's `cut_mono`; `landed_age_s` is for the dashboard.
- **Consensus, cursors and witness:** cursors stay on the destination aggregate; the witness stores relationship names, direction epochs and base snapshot UUIDs only.
- **Consensus, thresholds:** Lagging and Broken thresholds and hysteresis live in `otap-ctl`; the stream exposes raw values at 1 Hz.
- **Consensus, no-quorum posture:** the stream keeps shipping; a stale direction epoch in `Hello` is refused with `Abort(StaleEpoch)` and reported Broken, so the stream never fences anyone and never creates a promotable replica without quorum.
- **Consensus, FC `stop_exporting`:** partner group Standby, own group Unavailable, under 50 ms, no ISP abort; TPG disable is teardown only, a 2 to 5 s reset that logs out every vport.


### Opus-Consensus

#### Opus-Consensus, round 3: quorum, failure domains and SVM migration

Scope note: the other personas' round-3 originals are not on disk in this session, so section 6 answers what reached me through their cross-examinations. Facts checked this round that the revised design leans on: `target_wwn_vpd_unit_serial_store` returns `-EINVAL` while `dev->export_count` is non-zero [verified: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/target/target_core_configfs.c]; `boot_id` is "a UUID generated the first time this is retrieved, and unvarying after that" [verified: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/Documentation/admin-guide/sysctl/kernel.rst]; Debian's 6.12.111-1 config has `CONFIG_INET_DIAG_DESTROY=y` [verified: https://sources.debian.org/data/main/l/linux/6.12.111-1/debian/config/config], `tcp_abort()` sends an active reset for ESTABLISHED, CLOSE_WAIT, FIN_WAIT1/2 and SYN_RECV [verified: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/net/ipv4/tcp.c], and `ss -K` "attempts to forcibly close sockets" [verified: https://manpages.debian.org/trixie/iproute2/ss.8.en.html]; `arping -D` "Returns 0, if DAD succeeded i.e. no replies are received" [verified: https://manpages.debian.org/trixie/iputils-arping/arping.8.en.html]; VMW_SATP_ALUA `action_OnRetryErrors` "is set to off by default" and then "the path remains in an on state even after the I/O is retried indefinitely" [verified: https://knowledge.broadcom.com/external/article/310442]; vSphere HA VMCP responses for PDL and APD default to disabled [verified: https://developer.broadcom.com/xapis/virtual-infrastructure-json-api/8.0.3/data-structures/ClusterVmComponentProtectionSettings/]; ESXi flags a snapshot LUN when it "does not confirm the identity of the LUN with what it expects to see in the VMFS metadata" [verified: https://knowledge.broadcom.com/external/article/323142]; ONTAP nvfail "returns a stale file handle (ESTALE) error to NFS clients" and brings LUNs offline [verified: https://pubs.lenovo.com/mcc-metrocluster_management_and_disaster_recovery_guide/40D04B8A-01F7-4E87-8161-E30BD80F5B7F_]; openraft 0.9.25 `Config` has `enable_elect`, `snapshot_policy` and `max_in_snapshot_log_to_keep` [verified: https://docs.rs/openraft/0.9.25/openraft/struct.Config.html]; `genetlink` 0.3.0 exists [verified: https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/genetlink].

##### 1. Responses to holes raised against me

###### Opus-Storage

**C1 (manual window longer than every client's hold): ACCEPT.** Takeover is never gated on lag. The gate decides the *posture*: within `nvfail_force_lag` (60 s) each volume follows its class posture (3.3); beyond it, or when lag is Unknown, every volume of the SVM is promoted into `hold`. A held promotion acknowledges nothing, so it is reversible: if A returns with an intact superblock before `nvfail clear`, Raft commits `Revert{svm, to: A, epoch e+2}`, A resumes from its own head K+m (loss: its DRAM window, handled by Phase C's dirty-boot nvfail) and B resyncs from base K. Auto-revert is the default because it never loses more than clearing would. `TakeoverPending` is deleted; the irreversible decision is `nvfail clear`, where the printout lives.

**C2 ("Unavailable with PDL-style presentation"): ACCEPT.** ALUA Unavailable is retried with the path left On (KB 310442, C01): right for `stop` and ordinary takeovers, wrong for nvfail. `hold` on a block LUN is: unlink the LUN from the survivor's TPG (05h/25h on that path; data LUNs never at LUN 0, C02) and, when A is off the wire, answer on A's block LIF too so every path says 25h/00h (3.3). `nvfail clear` returns the LUN under the same identity only when PDL was reached on all paths; otherwise it bumps `vpd_unit_serial` (unlink, write, relink: writable only at `export_count == 0`), which ESXi treats as a snapshot LUN to resignature and Linux hosts as a new WWID.

**C3 (hardware RAID stall becomes a 5 s self-takeover): ACCEPT.** A stalled backstore is a Storage-reported condition (`backstore_stall_tolerance` in `MediaProfile`, 60 s for a hardware VD), never a takeover trigger; round 2's self-takeover at 5 s is withdrawn. Takeover is proposed only on partner silence (2 s on every direct path plus W's view) or after the wedge path (no pet, reset, then silence); a 45 s controller reset is a 45 s pause with a WARN naming the drain rate. NAS ublk devices queue during any hold and never return errors (XFS would shut down); block LUNs go Transitioning at 2 s and Unavailable at 10 s as R7 says.

**C4 (`cp_age_at_send` understates loss by one flush): ACCEPT.** Age is measured from `cut_mono`; the heartbeat carries the cut times of the newest committed and the oldest unshipped CP, and `unshipped_bytes` includes frozen-but-unshipped CPs (3.4).

**C5 (page bitset too small; aggregate placement contradicts SVM mobility): ACCEPT.** Slots, leases, epochs and placement are per SVM (aggregate slots are load-bearing only for Phase A media ownership), with the rule that an SVM's root and data volumes sit on one aggregate. The per-volume nvfail set leaves the page: Storage's `nvfail_generation` per volume in the superblock is the truth and the slot carries only `nvfail_seq` so the engine re-reads the list.

**C6 (pre-copy converges on link rate, floor is landing rate): ACCEPT.** Convergence is tested against `land_rate = min(link, receiver landing rate over the last three CPs)` from the stream heartbeat; one final round may run under the 2 s hold when the delta is at most 2 s × `land_rate` (500 MB at 250 MB/s); otherwise the migration is refused with delta, rate and ETA.

**C7 (file class `off` lets NFSv4.1 clients write holes): ACCEPT.** File class defaults to `fence`: served immediately but under a new NFS `fsid` generation (ESTALE drops cached state with EIO to applications) and after an smbd restart (durable handles are gone by construction, C34); the shape ONTAP uses. `off` remains for scratch volumes.

**C8 (`ProtectHostname=` cannot name an SVM): ACCEPT.** The warm-standby skeleton is Protocols' pin set (net, uts, mnt) entered with `nsenter`, with C16's correction that pins are made by a helper that stays in the host mount namespace; `ProtectHostname=` is never set.

###### Opus-Protocols

**C1 (scope per SVM, identical on both nodes): ACCEPT, with one addition.** `nbladed` sets scope = SVM UUID through `NFSD_CMD_THREADS_SET` with `NFSD_A_SERVER_SCOPE` (plus `gracetime` 20 s, `leasetime` 10 s) at every cold start from inside the SVM netns, using `genetlink` 0.3.0. Because `nfsd_svc()` rewrites the scope from the caller's UTS nodename on every scope-less thread write and refuses a scope on a running server (C14), the pinned UTS namespace keeps nodename = SVM UUID, later thread changes are issued from inside it, and `otap-ctl` reads `scope:` back with `THREADS_GET`: the UTS namespace is a guard, not the mechanism.

**C2 (`TakeoverPending` has no client budget): ACCEPT** (as Storage C1). The reminder runs every 30 s for ten minutes, then every 5 minutes, and lists which client classes have passed their timers (3.10).

**C3 (incoherent presentation; resume bounded by `PathEvalTime`): ACCEPT the first half, REJECT the second for `stop`.** Under `stop` the paths go ALUA Unavailable, which ESXi retries with the path left On (KB 310442); when the groups flip back the next retry succeeds, so resume is one I/O, not 300 s. `Disk.PathEvalTime` governs transport-Dead paths, the giveback and node-reboot case; the recipe sets it to 30 for that, and it is never an nvfail guard (C01).

**C4 (planned cutover assumes an apply point Storage does not provide): ACCEPT.** `DeltaSink::end(commit: Immediate)` and the generation ring (Storage S3) are prerequisites; preflight gains "no CP older than 2 s in flight". The budget is Storage's own: final 256 MiB CP 0.6 to 0.9 s on HDD RAID6, apply 0.3 to 0.5 s, Raft 0.1 to 0.25 s, ALUA flip 0.1 to 0.3 s: 1.5 to 2.5 s p50, 3 s cap.

**C5 (portals and LIF identity under-specified): ACCEPT.** One `LifState` with `transport: Ip{addr, vlan, mac} | Fc{wwpn, wwnn}`, MACs `02:<cluster>:<lif>` allocated at creation; iSCSI portals live in the SVM netns (C11), one block LIF per SVM per node, static; ALUA does every cutover, the `hold` impersonation (3.3) being the one exception.

**C6 (numbers that do not add up): ACCEPT.** One memory table, Storage's, with my survivor rule: SVM slices 18 GiB per node in Phase B, 36 GiB in Phase C. The page bitset is gone. Bottleneck 1 is corrected: catch-up is bounded by the replica's landing rate and PBA-sorted read-back, 150 to 250 MB/s on aged HDD, so 360 GB is 25 to 40 minutes, and the alert carries the measured rate and ETA; what breaks a relationship early is Storage's base-pin space rule, not `break_after`, and the alert names it.

**C7 (dirty bitset only as exact as `write_active`): ACCEPT.** The heartbeat carries `acked_bytes` since the last shipped CP per volume; the printout lists volumes with `acked_bytes > 0` as affected and the rest of `write_active` as "idle, bit not yet cleared".

###### Opus-Fabrics

**C1 (`recv_mono` is garbage after a replica reboot): ACCEPT, blocker.** The replica superblock records `(recv_boot_id, recv_mono)`; a `boot_id` mismatch makes lag `Unknown`, which the gate treats as beyond `nvfail_force_lag` (every class held) with the printout "replica rebooted since last apply; last applied CP K cut at sender wall time W". `recv_mono` is refreshed only by live heartbeats.

**C2 (`stop` ignores the guests): ACCEPT.** The no-quorum row carries the guest timers and the recipe's preconditions (C37, 3.7): a VMware SCSI controller plus open-vm-tools gives 180 s, NVMe-controller guests need `nvme_core.io_timeout=180`, Windows guests 60 s [believed]. `stop` stays because the alternative is a split brain; D7 goes to the owner with these numbers.

**C3 (portals node-level versus per-SVM; standby paths): ACCEPT.** `BlockStandby` from Phase B; P3 and P7 stand.

**C4 (warm-standby mechanism): ACCEPT.** One mechanism, Protocols' (Storage C8, Protocols C1).

**C5 (`base` in Raft wears the witness or lies): ACCEPT.** `base` leaves Raft; the relationship keeps `src_epoch` and its label; the common base comes from the two superblocks' snapshot tables, and `otapctl rel show` reads it from the engine.

**C6 (nvfail defaults disagree; the root has no class): ACCEPT.** One table (3.3) for owner decision D5 with three values; the root volume sits in the SVM's consistency group and gets `fence`, not `hold`: its rewind costs refused reclaims and possibly a machine-account re-join, both alerts, never a tenant-wide block (section 5).

**C7 (P5 assumes commit on `CpEnd`): ACCEPT** (Protocols C4).

**C8 (gate inputs missing; two lag bounds): ACCEPT.** S11's heartbeat; one default, 60 s, now named `nvfail_force_lag`, with the CP-derived value shown in the alert.

**C9 (arena owner): ACCEPT.** Struck; Phase C item 3 names R4's mechanism and no holder process.

##### 2. Fact-check consequences

**C01, C02 (PDL rules, LIO LUN 0):** the nvfail presentation is rebuilt (1.C2, 3.3): PDL needs 25h/00h or 68h/00h on every path including the dead node's, so the survivor answers on A's block LIF during `hold`; data LUNs never at mapped LUN 0, enforced by the Raft validator per (TPG, ACL); `Misc.APDTimeout` 140 s only fast-fails non-VM I/O; VMCP is off by default, so the ESXi recipe enables its PDL and APD responses.
**C03, C04, C05, C09, C10 (ublk copy path, flush stripping, LIO WCE, `ublks_max`, no resize):** no control-plane change except that warm-standby devices count toward `ublks_max` (platform profile 4096), every ublk device is created at `size_max`, and the reconciler asserts `queue/write_cache == "write back"` instead of writing `emulate_write_cache`.
**C06, C07, C08 (controller caches, learn cycles):** the gate's arithmetic is unchanged; the protection alert attributes a lag rise to a known write-through window on the replica (attested learn schedule plus Storage's `drain_rate`).
**C11 (portals bind in the creator's netns and coalesce across IQNs):** per-SVM block LIFs in the netns are confirmed; the SVM stop ladder deletes every portal and waits for `np_exports` to reach zero before unpinning; cluster-wide ip:port uniqueness is a Raft invariant that the `hold` impersonation relies on.
**C12 to C16 (nfsd per netns, one global `lockd`, scope rewriting, systemd, pins):** `end_grace` polls `v4_end_grace` until it reads Y and treats `-EBUSY` as "already ended or not running"; NLM grace is one global sysctl pair (`fs.nfs.nlm_grace_period` 20, `nlm_timeout` 10) and the single `lockd` thread is a node-wide head-of-line risk; `sm-notify -P <root-volume state dir> -v <svm name> -f` runs after the LIF is up; pins are made from the host mount namespace with `/run/opentap` a private mount.
**C17 (built-in LIO-ORG entry: `no_path_retry 12`, `directio`):** every ladder's Linux row reads "EIO about 60 s plus detection after the last path fails"; `queue` is withdrawn from my 2.7 argument (section 5 keeps the test).
**C18 (ALUA configfs):** cutover writes are 15 to the old group, 0 to the new, 2 to the old; `tg_pt_gp_id` and `vpd_unit_serial` identical on both nodes before the first link; `implicit_trans_secs` 10; `/etc/target/{pr,alua}` created at install.
**C19, C20 (snapshot fsid, ESXi NFSv3):** an fsid bump is a notification, not a gate (a rebooted host remounts by path), so `hold` on an NFSv3 datastore withholds the export until clear, while `fence` on file volumes is acceptable precisely because a remount is the wanted outcome.
