**C21, C22, C23 (md write hole, flush ordering, PERC transfer size):** Phase A's md assembly after a crash with a missing member needs `--force`; the Phase A policy becomes journal-or-refuse, decided with Storage.
**C24 to C31, C33 to C35, C40 (io_uring, kTLS, qla2xxx, ESXi scan, Proxmox 9.1, Samba, VPD, versitygw):** nothing in my area changes except that FC block LIFs cannot be impersonated, so FC LUNs always take the `strict` clear path; the client matrix names Proxmox 9.1 (kernel 6.17); and the drain step kills the whole smbd cgroup so the `TDB_CLEAR_IF_FIRST` wipe is deterministic.
**C32 (openraft, redb):** pin `openraft = "0.9"`; the witness state machine uses the persistent-snapshot mode (`apply()` with `Durability::None`, snapshots `Immediate`, `save_committed` unpersisted, truncate and purge `None`): one witness fsync per configuration append plus a snapshot fsync every `LogsSinceLast(64)`; "steady-state heartbeats perform no storage call".
**C36 (`arp_notify`, `ndisc_notify`):** the GARP sender stays; IPv6 LIFs set `ndisc_notify=1`, are added without `nodad`, and `nbladed` still sends three NAs; citations corrected to `devinet.c`, `ndisc.c` and `addrconf.c`.
**C37 (open-vm-tools 180 s):** preconditions in the recipe with `cat /sys/block/sd*/device/timeout` as the check; the Launchpad remark is dropped.
**C38, C39 (Debian 13.7 snapshot, Pi OS kernel 6.18, crates):** the witness runs on Debian 13 arm64 userland with whatever kernel the Pi image ships (6.18 today) and depends on nothing kernel-specific; 64-bit only; versions dated 2026-10-12 with the pins in `Cargo.lock`.

##### 3. Revised design

###### 3.1 Units and the failure matrix

The SVM is the unit of ownership, lease, epoch, relationship (consistency group: root plus data volumes, on one aggregate) and mobility; the aggregate is the unit of CP and, in Phase A, of media ownership; the transport session is per aggregate pair with SVM relationships multiplexed by `rel` in Fabrics' frame header. Raft membership `{A, B, W}` on openraft 0.9.25, W with `enable_elect = false`, leases granted after `ensure_linearizable()` with no log write and renewed in one batched RPC per node per 500 ms, `heartbeat_interval` 100 ms, election 1 to 2 s, the relay through W for Raft and lease RPC unchanged. The eleven-row matrix of my original 2.1 stands with two edits: "A isolated" ends in a promotion whose posture the gate decides, and "A-B severed, both reach W" is a non-event for ownership and a `Lagging` event for protection.

###### 3.2 Takeover: always promote, lag decides the posture

```rust
pub enum Lag { Known(Duration), Unknown { reason: &'static str } }   // Unknown: boot_id mismatch, or no heartbeat ever received
pub enum NvPosture { Hold, Fence, Off }
pub struct Posture { pub per_vol: Vec<(VolId, NvPosture)>, pub revertible: bool, pub loss: Loss }
pub struct Loss { pub seconds: f32, pub bytes_min: u64, pub bytes_max: u64, pub affected: Vec<VolId>, pub idle_unknown: Vec<VolId> }
pub fn takeover_posture(svm: &SvmState, lag: Lag, policy: &TakeoverPolicy, live: &RelLive) -> Posture;
// lag <= policy.nvfail_force_lag (60 s): each volume keeps its class posture; otherwise, or Unknown: every volume Hold.
// revertible = every volume Hold (nothing is acknowledged on the survivor until a clear).
// lag = (now_mono - recv_mono) + ship_duration_measured_by_receiver + (send_mono - cut_mono) reported by the sender.
```

| Step | Time (A dies at 0) | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| silence | 2 s | A silent on LAN and DAC, and W has not heard A for 2 s |
| election | 1.0 to 2.2 s | only if A led; B wins with W's vote fsync |
| L1 / L2 | 4.3 s p50, 5.3 s p99 | TTL plus margin after the term, or last grant plus 3.1 s |
| gate | under 1 ms | `takeover_posture` from the replica superblock and `RelLive`; no RPC, no wall clock |
| commit | 4.5 s | `Takeover{svm, B, e+1, promote_cp, posture, loss}`; W's append fsync on the path |
| exports | 5 s p50, 9 s p99 | `Off` and `Fence` LUNs Active/Optimized; `Hold` LUNs unlinked, A's block LIF answered by B once `arping -D` on it gets no reply within 1 s (PDL on ESXi at about 7 s); NAS plus 2 to 5 s, `Fence` volumes under a new fsid |
| revert | A's boot plus 1 s | every volume still held and A's superblock intact: `Revert{svm, A, e+2}`; A serves from its own head; B resyncs from base K |
| clear | operator | `otapctl nvfail clear --svm X`: same identity only after PDL on every path with `host_class = esxi`; otherwise a `vpd_unit_serial` bump (unlink, write, relink) |

The wedged-A ladder (11 to 13 s, hard 15 s), the returning node's roles (`Fenced` at boot; `Owner` when Raft's `(owner, epoch)` equals its superblock; `Divergent` otherwise, local head pinned as `divergent-e<epoch>-cp<K+m>`, map rolled back to base K) and resync rules R-a to R-f are unchanged.

###### 3.3 nvfail postures (owner decision D5)

| Class | Default | Block presentation | NAS presentation | Cleared by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| datastore LUN (iSCSI, FC) | `hold` | unlinked on every path; PDL when all paths answer (iSCSI via impersonation; FC always `strict`) | n/a | `nvfail clear`: same identity for ESXi-only iSCSI LUNs after PDL; otherwise serial bump (Linux and mixed classes always; LVM re-finds the VG by PV UUID) |
| NFSv3 datastore | `hold` | n/a | export withheld (C20) | `nvfail clear`, new fsid |
| file (NFSv4.1, SMB) | `fence` | n/a | new fsid generation, smbd restarted; served at once; CRIT with the window | nothing |
| object | `fence` | n/a | versitygw restarted | nothing |
| SVM root | `fence` | n/a | reclaims refused for the rewound nfsdcld; machine-password mismatch raises CRIT with the re-join command | nothing |
| any | `off` | old identity | old fsid | lab only |

`host_class` (`esxi | linux | windows | mixed`) and `serial_gen` live in `LunIdentity`; `nvfail_policy = strict` forces the bump everywhere.

###### 3.4 Protection and relationship state

Protection per SVM relationship from the 1 s heartbeat, never in Raft: `Single`, `Protected`, `Exposed` (lag over `insync_lag_max` or link dead 3 s; WARN sustained 30 s), `Exposed(CRIT)` (lag over `nvfail_force_lag`: "a failure of this node now holds every volume of SVM X until you clear"; hourly reminder), `Unprotected` (Broken). `insync_lag_max` = CP interval plus maximum ship plus apply = 25 s HDD, 12 s flash (Protocols S2, Fabrics S5), so steady state does not flap.

```rust
pub struct Relationship { pub ver: u16, pub id: RelId, pub svm: SvmId, pub src: NodeId, pub dst: NodeId,
    pub src_epoch: u64 /* direction epoch */, pub policy: RelPolicy, pub state: RelState }   // no base: the superblocks hold it
pub enum RelState { Baseline, Idle, Quiesced, Resync { from: NodeId, to: NodeId }, Broken { reason: BreakReason } }
pub struct RelLive { pub src_committed_cp: u64, pub dst_applied_cp: u64, pub cut_mono_newest: u64, pub cut_mono_oldest_unshipped: u64,
    pub unshipped_bytes: u64, pub acked_bytes: Vec<(VolId, u64)>, pub dirty_vols: VolBitSet, pub land_rate_bytes_s: u64,
    pub apply_stalled_ms: u32, pub link: LinkHealth, pub recv_boot_id: [u8; 16], pub recv_mono: u64 }
// Replica superblock, written in the same FUA as the apply (Storage item 5): applied_cp_seq, applied_owner_epoch,
// recv_boot_id, recv_mono, sender_cut_wall_ns, ship_duration_ms, acked_cp.
```

Transitions are the original table minus `TakeoverPending`, plus `Idle -> Resync{B->A}` on `Revert`. Eligibility is no longer a state: everything but `Baseline` and `Broken` promotes; `Resync` promotes from the newest complete CP of the current epoch, held.

###### 3.5 Mobility and LIFs

Block: `BlockStandby` from Phase B. Each SVM has one block LIF per node inside its netns, identical ALUA group IDs and `vpd_unit_serial` on both nodes, Standby on the replica; planned cutover is 15 / 0 / 2 on the two groups. NAS LIFs move with GARP and NA sent by `nbladed`. Namespaces: pinned net, uts (nodename = SVM UUID) and mnt entered by `nsenter`, pins made from the host mount namespace, `/run/opentap` private.

```rust
pub trait SvmMobility {                      // nbladed; idempotent; driven by Raft SvmState
    fn ensure_standby(&mut self, svm: &SvmSpec) -> Result<(), MobErr>;  // pins, inactive units, block LIF Standby, ublk devices at size_max
    fn drain(&mut self, svm: SvmId, deadline: Duration) -> Result<DrainReport, MobErr>;
        // smbd cgroup SIGTERM, `ss -K` on NAS LIF sockets, NAS LIFs down, versitygw SIGTERM, nfsd threads 0, clean unmounts
    fn activate(&mut self, svm: SvmId, posture: &Posture) -> Result<ActivateReport, MobErr>;
        // mounts; THREADS_SET{scope, grace 20, lease 10, threads}; smbd; versitygw; LIFs up plus GARP and NA; sm-notify -v; per-posture exports
    fn impersonate_block_lif(&mut self, lif: &LifSpec) -> Result<(), MobErr>;   // hold only, after arping -D reports silence
    fn end_grace(&mut self, svm: SvmId) -> Result<(), MobErr>;                 // write Y, poll until Y
}
```

Planned sequence, revised: P0 preflight adds "no CP older than 2 s in flight" and the landing-rate check; P1 pre-copy to at most 256 MiB or one final round under the 2 s hold; P2 drain in the order above (RST first, so NFSv3 clients reconnect on their first probe instead of a back-off; whether `ss -K` reaches sunrpc's kernel-owned sockets is [believed], with an `AF_PACKET` RST per connection as the fallback); P3 to P7 block 1.5 to 2.5 s p50; P8 to P10 NFSv3 2 to 4 s, NFSv4.1 at most 8 s on reclaimed state; P11 SMB 10 to 20 s, open handles lost (C34).

###### 3.6 Slot table and Raft content

```rust
#[repr(C, align(64))] pub struct Slot {   // /run/opentap/slots: 1,024 slots, MAP_SHARED, written by otap-ctl only
    pub kind: u32,                        // Svm | Agg (Agg is load-bearing only in Phase A)
    pub id: u64, pub epoch: u64,
    pub role: u32,                        // Single | Owner | Replica | Divergent | Fenced
    pub state: u32,                       // Owned | Standby | Transitioning | Fenced   (checked at submission and completion)
    pub lease_expiry_mono_ns: u64, pub gate_seq: u64,
    pub nvfail_seq: u64,                  // bumped when the engine must re-read per-volume nvfail_generation from its superblock
    pub protection: u32, pub _pad: [u8; 12] }
// check(slot, now_ns): role in {Single, Owner}, state == Owned, now_ns < lease_expiry (Single: no lease); about 5 ns [believed; measured in C1]
```

Raft keeps nodes, aggregates (`owner, home, media, mode`, Phase A), SVMs (`owner, home, epoch, mode: Serving | Migrating | Held{since} | Reverting | Down`, netns, protocols, slice, priority), volumes (`nvfail: Hold | Fence | Off`, `size_max`), LIFs (transport body, MAC), LUN identities (`serial_gen`, `host_class`), relationships without a base, policies, sealed secrets and the last 30 rehearsals; about 200 KiB. Not in Raft: leases, heartbeats, lag, bases and cursors, snapshot instances, nfsdcld, `secrets.tdb`, per-volume nvfail state, the divergent snapshot's contents.

###### 3.7 No-quorum posture (owner decision D7)

Unchanged in substance: `stop` in Phase B (the lease is the only arbiter between two private copies), `freeze` in Phase A (PR arbitrates), `freeze` in Phase B only behind a confirmed power fence. Under `stop` (hold at 3 s, Transitioning at 5 s, Unavailable at 13 s, resume on the next I/O after quorum): ESXi retries with paths On and guests fail at 180 s (SCSI controller plus open-vm-tools), 30 s (NVMe controller without the modprobe line) or 60 s (Windows); Linux and Proxmox hosts get EIO about 60 s after the last path fails; Windows iSCSI 60 s; NAS clients hang and retry. A 60 s witness reboot is survived by ESXi SCSI guests and NAS clients and by nothing else; the owner decides with these numbers.

###### 3.8 Phase C and the witness

Phase C is membership `{A}`, identical binary, zero network RPC, one slot read per I/O, fsync only on configuration changes (one append per change, a snapshot every 64), watchdog and daemon-restart budget kept, `otap-ctl` and `nbladed` at most 64 MiB each. The witness fsyncs on votes and appends only; steady-state heartbeats perform no storage call. It stores the vote, the log, the `ClusterState` snapshot, its mTLS material and rehearsal records, never leases, lag, cursors or data. Form factors: Pi 4 or 5 on Raspberry Pi OS 64-bit (Debian 13 userland, the image's own kernel), a Proxmox LXC, or a 1 vCPU VM, never on a data node's hypervisor host.

###### 3.9 Memory and crates

`otap-ctl` at most 128 MiB RSS (`MemoryMax=256M`), `nbladed` at most 128 MiB (`512M`), slot table 64 KiB, relay buffers 4 MiB, `RelLive` 2 KiB plus 16 B per volume per relationship; SVM slices from Storage's table, 18 GiB per node in Phase B and 36 GiB in Phase C, so both nodes' SVMs fit a survivor. Crates (2026-10-12): openraft 0.9.25, redb 4.3.0, tokio 1.53.2, rustls 0.23.45, postcard 1.1.3, axum 0.8.9, rtnetlink 0.23.0, genetlink 0.3.0, nix 0.31.3 or rustix 1.1.5, zbus 5.19.0, toml 1.1.8, proptest 1.12.0, madsim 0.2.34, turmoil 0.7.2, stateright 0.31.0.

###### 3.10 Timer table (rows that changed; the rest of my original 2.10 stands)

| Item | Value | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Election timeout | 1 to 2 s | was 0.5 to 1 s; for the relay; recorded against R7 |
| `insync_lag_max` | 25 s HDD, 12 s flash | CP plus maximum ship plus apply |
| `nvfail_force_lag` | 60 s | replaces `max_auto_takeover_lag`; beyond it, or Unknown, every class held |
| Takeover; revert; clear reminder | automatic; automatic until clear; 30 s for 10 min then 5 min | posture per class; loss figure plus timed-out client classes |
| Unplanned block resume | 5 s p50, 9 s p99 (`fence`, `off`); PDL about 7 s (`hold`) | wedged 11 to 13 s, hard 15 s |
| Planned block | 1.5 to 2.5 s p50, 3 s cap | Immediate commit, generation ring |
| Planned NAS | NFSv3 2 to 4 s; NFSv4.1 at most 8 s; SMB 10 to 20 s, handles lost | `v4_end_grace` polled |
| Linux hosts, any ladder | EIO about 60 s plus detection | built-in entry, `no_path_retry 12` |
| ESXi Dead-path recovery | up to `Disk.PathEvalTime`, recipe 30 s | giveback and reboot only; ALUA flips resume on the next I/O |
| Guest disk timeouts | Linux 180 s or 30 s; Windows 60 s | check `/sys/block/sd*/device/timeout` |
| NLM | grace 20 s, one global `lockd` thread | node-wide head-of-line risk |
| Backstore stall | Storage's tolerance; never a takeover | NAS queues; block Transitioning 2 s, Unavailable 10 s |

##### 4. Work items

Phase C, in order, each with its exit test:

1. **`otap-ctl` single voter**: openraft 0.9 on redb 4.3.0, `Raft::initialize({a})`, local leases, the slot table, persistent-snapshot state machine. Exit: 10,000 configuration operations show one append fsync each and a snapshot fsync every 64; `perf trace` over 60 s of I/O shows zero `otap-ctl` syscalls on the data path; the slot check measures under 10 ns and passes loom.
2. **Watchdog, data-path check-ins, dirty-boot nvfail with the three postures.** Exit: 1,000 simulated and 50 real power cuts produce the right posture per class; `hold` LUNs answer 25h/00h on every path and ESXi 8 U3 reports PDL; `fence` NFS volumes return ESTALE to a Debian client and a fresh mount works; a 6 s SIGSTOP fires the watchdog and ESXi sees the node again within 15 s.
3. **Daemon restart** via `USER_RECOVERY` and `REISSUE`, no holder process. Exit: 50 `kill -9` at 1 GB/s, serving again p99 2 s, worst 5 s, zero duplicate applies.
4. **SVM lifecycle and LIF manager**: pins from the host mount namespace, `nsenter` units, scope via `genetlink`, GARP and NA sender with `arping` fallback, `ss -K` drain, `sm-notify -v`, `end_grace` polling. Exit: 100 SVM restarts with an ESXi NFSv3 datastore pause at most 3 s; `THREADS_GET` reads back the SVM UUID after a thread change; a Debian NFSv4.1 client is back on reclaimed state within 8 s; `tcpdump` shows three GARPs within 300 ms of the address add.
5. **Declarative state and reconciler.** Exit: killed mid-apply 100 times, desired and actual hashes equal, no device ever deleted, `queue/write_cache == "write back"` asserted before every LUN link.
6. **Alerts and metrics** with the four facts and the client-timeout list. Exit: every alert in the matrix carries what, seconds, bytes and the command.
7. **TLA+ (Apalache) and madsim harness** for 1 and 3 voters: leases, epochs, postures, `Revert`, `Divergent`. Exit: "no two nodes acknowledge writes for one SVM in overlapping real time", "a held promotion never acknowledges" and "`Revert` happens only before any acknowledgement" hold over 10,000 schedules.
8. **arm64 witness lane.** Exit: a 2 × amd64 plus 1 × arm64 CI cluster survives 24 h with hourly changes under 100 witness fsyncs.
9. **Upgrade dry run** `{a}` to `{a, b, w}`. Exit: no I/O interruption on the single node's clients.

Phase B adds: the witness and relay in production; leader leases L1 to L4 per SVM with batched renewal; relationship and protection state machines over Fabrics' heartbeat; the posture gate with `(boot_id, recv_mono)`; `Hold`, impersonation, `Revert` and both `nvfail clear` paths; `BlockStandby` on both nodes; warm-standby pins; resync rules and the divergent snapshot. Exit: 100 unplanned takeovers per fault class at 5 s p50 and 9 s p99 for `fence` LUNs and PDL on every ESXi path within 10 s for `hold` LUNs, with exact loss printouts; 50 returns of A during a held promotion each revert with loss equal to A's DRAM window; a replica reboot before a takeover yields `Unknown` and a held promotion; the no-quorum test (both nodes hold at 3 s, resume within one I/O of quorum, no epoch bump) with the guest timers observed as the table says; 100,000 madsim schedules with zero violations; 30 nightly rehearsals at most 3 s client-visible.

Phase A adds: the `ScsiPr` fence and `ShelfMailbox`; the `freeze` default; aggregate slots load-bearing; md assembly on takeover under a journal-or-refuse policy (a dirty, degraded array needs `--force`, C21); the stripe-cache drain test; lossless takeover when the shelf holds the last CP, with nvfail limited to the DRAM window.

##### 5. Open disagreements

- **Linux `no_path_retry`.** Fabrics says ship `queue` and make nvfail explicit by LUN deletion plus a REPORT LUNS DATA HAS CHANGED unit attention; Protocols says keep the built-in `12`. I say keep `12` (nothing to ship, C17), give Linux-class LUNs the identity bump at clear, and state the 60 s consequence for `stop`. Settle on Proxmox 9.1: under `queue`, does qemu receive EIO within 10 s of unlink plus unit attention? If yes, `queue` becomes the shipped override and the `stop` row improves.
- **Same identity after PDL.** Storage says `strict` (new WWID) after every unplanned takeover; I say same identity for ESXi-only iSCSI LUNs once every path reported PDL, because a resignature plus VM re-registration after a 30 s rollback is a cost ONTAP users do not pay. Settle on ESXi 8 U3: dead path on A, impersonated path on B, `esxcli storage core device list` must show PDL, and a remap must return the same datastore with no snapshot-LUN prompt and the VMs powered off.
- **`PathEvalTime` as the resume bound.** Protocols says client resume after `stop` is up to 300 s; I say ALUA Unavailable paths stay On and resume on the next I/O (KB 310442). Settle by flipping Unavailable to Active/Optimized after 90 s and timing the first successful guest write.
- **Root volume posture.** Fabrics says `hold`; I say `fence`. Owner decision D5.
- **`stop` versus `freeze` in Phase B.** Owner decision D7, argued with the guest numbers in 3.7.

##### 6. Answers to the questions addressed to me

The other personas' original section 6 lists are not on disk; these are the items their cross-examinations put to Consensus.

- **Storage ("Consensus's table should carry the same row" for the root; fence granularity per SVM):** yes, the root volume is a row (`fence`, 3.3), and lease, epoch and slot are per SVM (1.C5).
- **Storage (my Q1 and Q2 answered "yes"):** then the gate reads only the replica superblock, the common base is `acked_cp` on the source's superblock, and `Relationship.base` is gone from Raft.
- **Protocols ("one row in the timer table, Consensus owns it"; 18 GiB "provided the memory table is reconciled"):** `insync_lag_max` 25 s HDD and 12 s flash, WARN sustained 30 s, `nvfail_force_lag` and CRIT at 60 s (3.10); the slice cap is derived from Storage's table (3.9).
- **Protocols (nvfail per protocol):** your mechanisms are adopted as written (unmap with the LUN 0 placeholder, fsid generation, `smbcontrol close-share`); mine is the state machine around them.
- **Fabrics (election timeout against R7; heartbeat union; `DeltaSink::end(commit)`; link hysteresis):** recorded in 3.10; the union is `RelLive` in 3.4; `Immediate` is required for P5 and for every promotion; 3 s fail-over and 30 s fail-back accepted.
- **Fabrics (my Q3 to you, the relay on a Pi 4 under rustls 0.23):** unanswered; "Pi 5 or container recommended" stays [believed] until you measure.


## Critics

### critic:completeness

#### Completeness critique: OpenTAP Session 03, after the rebuttals

Scope: the four designs, four revised positions and forty fact-check verdicts, read against the owner's charter (`04-project-brief-async-svm.md`) and the round-2 rulings that still stand (`03-architecture-brainstorm-02.md`, Part 6). "Covered" means a persona owns the item, states the mechanism and gives a Phase C exit test; "partial" means one or two of those. Versions I introduce are a 2026-10-12 snapshot and marked individually; versions the personas already marked are not repeated.

##### 1. Gaps: what nobody covers, or two personas cover inconsistently

###### 1.1 Summary

| # | Topic | State after rebuttals | Phase C or later | Proposed owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Installer and first boot | Absent as a unit; "the installer refuses/prints/creates" appears throughout with no installer | C: v0.1 is sold as an appliance | Consensus (`otapctl cluster create`), inputs from Storage (probe, attestation) and Protocols (platform profile, default SVM) |
| 2 | Upgrade and rollback of OpenTAP | Partial: N/N-1 format tests (Storage), N/N+1 wire (Fabrics), version-locked witness .deb (Consensus); no procedure, no downgrade rule, no kernel-update story | C: every DSA kernel is a reboot of the only node | Consensus; Storage for format versioning |

###### 1.2 Detail

**1. Installer and first boot.** Referenced but never specified: the ISO flow for one node (boot disk versus pool disks; R12 refuses USB boot); management-interface configuration in `init_net` (Protocols leaves data ports to `nbladed` and `bond0` to Raft; nothing configures the management port); the reboot that hugepage reservation, `isolcpus` and the `ublk_drv ublks_max=4096` and `qla2xxx qlini_mode=disabled` drop-ins plus `update-initramfs` require; the mandatory geometry probe (7 candidates x 16 GiB at QD 8, about two minutes, destructive, so empty backstores only); the `cache_protection` dialogue, whose answers cannot be checked in-box because `perccli` and `storcli` are vendor downloads (C06 to C08); the attestation capture (sd "Write cache" lines, `queue/write_cache`, `cache_type`, `max_hw_sectors_kb`); cluster-key generation (`/etc/opentap/cluster.key`, R23); `Raft::initialize({a})`; `/etc/target/{pr,alua}` before `target_core_mod` loads (C18); masking `rtslib-fb-targetctl.service` (Fabrics); the default SVM; the admin credential; and the first-boot health check that every ublk device reads `write_cache == "write back"` and `fua == 1` (C09). Exit test to add: unattended install from ISO to a serving iSCSI LUN on a PERC VD and on an mdadm RAID6, with the probe result and attestation stored in the pool.

**2. Upgrade and rollback.** Three unanswered questions. (a) A package upgrade of `dbladed` on one node: is it the supervised 2 s/5 s restart with `USER_RECOVERY` (Consensus item 3), and does the arena survive a package-managed stop the way it survives `kill -9`? (b) Kernel updates: trixie-security moved 6.12.94 to 6.12.111 in weeks (C38) and 6.12.107-1 changed ublk `SET_PARAMS` semantics (C09); on a single node a kernel update is a clean shutdown (final CP, `run_state = CleanShutdown`), a reboot and a rebuild of the ublk devices and LIO tree, so clients see the planned-stop numbers. That needs a published maintenance-reboot ladder and a mechanism behind R22's "apt pin and hold": `unattended-upgrades` 2.12 [verified: https://packages.debian.org/trixie/unattended-upgrades] must be pinned off for kernel and OpenTAP packages. (c) Downgrade: `otap-format` v2 carries `ver` and an N/N-1 read test, but no rule says when an upgrade rewrites the superblock at a new version and thereby forbids rollback. Propose: a release never writes a format that N-1 cannot read until the operator runs an explicit `otapctl format upgrade`.

**3. Observability.** Each persona names a few numbers (Storage: `drain_rate_bytes_s`, `replication_hold_bytes`, `applied_age_s`; Fabrics: `ZC_COPIED`, `cache_corruption`, ship and land rate; Protocols: restart counts, stale `sm` entries, root rewound; Consensus: protection state and the four-fact alert). Missing: which process exports Prometheus, on which port and in which namespace (an SVM's daemons live in their own netns, so per-SVM scrapes need `nbladed` to proxy or a node-level exporter); a catalogue with labels (volume, SVM, relationship) covering arena occupancy, throttle delay histogram, CP duration and bytes, QoS holds, per-LUN latency, nvfail state, posture and lag; `prometheus-node-exporter` 1.9.0-1 [verified: https://packages.debian.org/trixie/prometheus-node-exporter] for host metrics and the `prometheus` crate 0.14.0 [verified: https://crates.io/crates/prometheus] or equivalent for the daemons; structured logs (`tracing` 0.1.44 [verified: https://crates.io/crates/tracing]) and journald retention on the boot SSD; a dashboard definition (round-2 exit test 10 says "shown on the dashboard"); and a support bundle, which Fabrics mentions once and nobody defines: configfs dump, sysfs geometry and attestation report, superblock and intent slots, CP-log statistics, relationship cursors, `lsns`, `multipath -t` from clients, secrets redacted. Alert severities contradict across personas (section 2, row 4).

**4. Secrets.** R23 seals secrets in Raft under `/etc/opentap/cluster.key`. Open: who generates it, whether it is backed up (losing the boot SSD loses every CHAP secret, S3 key and NT hash), TPM2 sealing, which trixie's systemd 257.13 offers through `systemd-cryptenroll --tpm2-device`, `--tpm2-pcrs` and `--tpm2-with-pin` [verified: https://manpages.debian.org/trixie/systemd-cryptsetup/systemd-cryptenroll.1.en.html], rotation of CHAP and S3 keys without client disruption, and the consequence of Protocols P8: `passdb.tdb` is now authoritative on the root volume, so local NT hashes live unsealed on a replicated, unencrypted volume. New and unowned: Protocols' `otap-host-check` must log into every registered ESXi host to confirm PDL before `nvfail clear` remaps, which needs a host registry, stored vSphere credentials and an API choice; none is designed, and `nvfail clear` under `pdl` depends on it.

**5. Cluster-state backup and DR import.** Where does redb live? Consensus persists votes, log and snapshot but never says on which device; invariant 9 forbids load-bearing `/var` for SVM state, yet a single node's Raft store on the boot SSD is exactly that. If the boot SSD dies the pool still holds engine state (superblocks, snapshot table, the policies Storage mirrors), but SVM specs, LIFs, LUN identities and sealed secrets are gone unless an export exists. Propose: `otap-ctl` writes its snapshot (under 1 MB) into a reserved aggregate region at every commit so a pool is self-describing, and `otapctl aggregate import` on a fresh install rebuilds `ClusterState` from it plus the restored cluster key. Storage's Phase A "aggregate import and export" should move to Phase C for this reason.

**6. UI, API, RBAC.** `otapctl` verbs appear everywhere (`volume nvfail-clear`, `rel baseline`, `svm move`, `witness check`) and axum 0.8.9 sits in Consensus's crate list, but no persona defines the resource model, versioning, authentication (mTLS client certificates for `otapctl`, or a unix socket on the node) or roles. Pivot 3 makes the SVM the tenant unit "exactly as in clustered ONTAP", which implies a cluster admin and an SVM admin whose world is one SVM's volumes, shares, exports, LIFs, snapshots and users. Protocols defers RBAC to Phase B; the authorization model should exist in the Phase C API so every verb carries its scope from the first commit, or Phase B retrofits a check into every handler. Audit: the Raft log records ownership ops, but `ClusterOp` has no actor field, so "who cleared nvfail" is unanswerable. The web UI stays Phase 2.

**7. QoS.** Protocols specifies the per-volume bucket precisely (1 ms refill, 1 s hold, `UBLK_IO_F_META` bypass, per-bdi `max_bytes`); Storage accepts it at about 20 ns per request and then omits it from all eleven Phase C work items, so Protocols' C8 exit test (1,000 IOPS within 5% over 10 min, no hold over 1 s) has no implementer. Unspecified: whether reads are metered (a `max_mbps` that ignores reads lets a backup SVM's restore starve a datastore), whether snapshot-mount ublk devices inherit the parent's policy, and how the bucket arbitrates with Storage's catch-up read cap (30% of pool reads) and the scrub budget: three governors on one pool with no arbitration rule.

**8. Capacity.** Storage defines `used`, `snapshot_used`, `replication_hold_bytes`, `unique(snap)` and the 70/80/90 reserves. Three holes. (a) C10 makes every NAS volume an XFS of `size_max` on a thin LUN, so `df` on every client reports `size_max`, while R18 says file volumes are thick-reserved; either the reservation is `size_max` (thin NAS does not exist) or clients see space that is not there and the first refusal arrives as an XFS hang inside the SVM, because NAS devices "queue and never return errors" (Consensus). (b) Thin LUNs: R18 promises VPD B2h and threshold unit attentions; Protocols sets `emulate_tpu`/`emulate_tpws` but nobody sets the threshold or says what ESXi sees at `write_stop`. (c) Accounting must include relocation tables (about 14 GB per day at 0.4 GB/s, Storage 3.4), map pages (0.4%) and the deferred-reuse float of one CP, or the round-2 "usable = 0.8 x physical" is unmeasured. Quotas (XFS project quotas per directory, user quotas per SVM) are absent; defer to B but reserve the API now.

**9. Encryption.** In flight: the stream is mTLS always (Fabrics F2), control is mTLS, S3 has a per-SVM certificate. Not stated: the SMB3 encryption default (`smb encrypt`), that NFS `sec=sys` and iSCSI with CHAP are plaintext until Kerberos and NVMe/TCP TLS arrive, and that arena and staging are plaintext by design. At rest: R23 defers dm-crypt above md to Phase 2, and session 03 never asks what it does to this round's design. dm-crypt stacks block sizes and `io_min` through `crypt_io_hints` [verified: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/drivers/md/dm-crypt.c] and is believed to pass empty flushes and discards through and to preserve FUA on cloned bios [believed: `crypt_map`, not read], so the probe, attestation and commit protocol should survive it, but `GeomSource` would then read a dm device and the `BLK_FEAT_WRITE_CACHE` inheritance of C05 applies. `cryptsetup` 2:2.7.5-2 [verified: https://packages.debian.org/trixie/cryptsetup] with TPM2 enrolment is in-box. Decide in C whether the backstore is `dm-crypt(md)` or `md(dm-crypt)` so the probe runs at the right layer; ship in B.

**10. Pool growth and drive replacement.** Absent this session. Replacement on md is `--fail`, `--remove`, `--add` and a rebuild at roughly 100 to 200 MB/s per member [believed], a day on 16 TB drives, competing with CP flushes; Storage's WARN after three CPs under 50% of the probed drain (F-S8) fires during every rebuild unless rebuild joins the learn cycle as a known cause. Hot spares, `sync_speed_max` throttling and the `mdadm --monitor` wiring of R22 are unmentioned. On a hardware VD a failed member is invisible to Linux: with no `perccli`, the in-box signals are `megaraid_sas` controller-event lines in dmesg [believed] and `smartctl -d megaraid,N` through the controller [believed]; the design has no drive-failure detection for its own recommended controller class. Growth: md reshape (`--grow --raid-devices`, needing `--backup-file` on a separate device when no spare exists, re-presented at assembly after a crash in the critical section [verified: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man8/mdadm.8.html]) changes the full stripe, so segments born earlier keep their geometry (R19); Storage's v2 sketch shows no per-segment geometry record, which must be in the format before item 1 freezes it. Hardware VD online capacity expansion changes the device size under a running engine; a lone NVMe cannot grow at all.

**11. SMART and scrubbing.** Storage's scrub is summary-driven: it reads live blocks and verifies CRCs, which catches bit rot in data and never touches parity or free stripes. R22 disabled `checkarray` because "our scrub replaces it"; it does not, so latent sector errors on parity and in free space surface only during a rebuild, the classic RAID6 double fault. Needed: a scheduled md `check` (`md/sync_action`, which "reads all blocks and checks them", with `mismatch_cnt` and per-array `sync_speed_max` [verified: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/v6.12/Documentation/admin-guide/md.rst]) under the same read budget as catch-up; on hardware RAID, patrol read and consistency check are controller-internal and uncontrollable in-box (F-S8); `smartd` 7.4-3 [verified: C38] with per-member `-d megaraid,N` [believed] and NVMe attributes; `xfs_scrub -n` for SVM filesystems, online but "an immature utility" by its own man page [verified: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man8/xfs_scrub.8.html].

**12. UPS.** Storage's `UpsOnBattery` trigger reads "immediate, then CleanShutdown", which shuts the appliance down on every one-minute blip. NUT's model is two-stage, `OB` then `OB LB`. Propose: on battery, CP timer to 2 s, WARN, keep serving; on low battery or after a configured runtime, final CP, stop exporting, `CleanShutdown`; on power return, BIOS or iDRAC power-on, boot, no nvfail because the shutdown was clean. Packages: `nut-server` 2.8.1-5 and `apcupsd` 3.14.14-5 [verified: https://packages.debian.org/trixie/nut-server, https://packages.debian.org/trixie/apcupsd]; `upsmon`'s shutdown command calls `otapctl node shutdown --reason ups`. The witness must not share the node's UPS (Consensus's install check covers hosts, not power). R5's auto-clear opt-in only makes sense once this exists.

**13. Certificates.** Everyone uses "the cluster CA"; nobody creates it (`otapctl cluster create` with rcgen 0.14.10 [verified: https://crates.io/crates/rcgen]), sets lifetimes, rotates node and witness certificates, or exports the CA so Veeam, browsers and a laptop's `otapctl` trust it. SVM S3 certificates (SAN = SVM FQDN, sealed in Raft, rotation by restart) need operator import or ACME; Veeam will not trust a self-signed per-SVM certificate without the CA. The management API's client authentication is unspecified; a single node needs at least a local socket for `otapctl` and a bootstrap for remote mTLS.

**14. Time sync.** No persona names a time source. It matters for snapshot schedules (`*:05`), `@GMT-` names (UTC), `wall_ns` in nvfail alerts and `sender_cut_wall_ns` in the loss printout, certificate validity, S3 request signing (15-minute skew) and, in B, Kerberos (5-minute skew). All SVMs share the node clock (no time namespace), so two SVMs joined to domains with divergent time are impossible; say so. Choose `chrony` 4.6.1-3+deb13u2 [verified: https://packages.debian.org/trixie/chrony] for its step-versus-slew policy and alert on large steps, because the gate uses `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` but the alert text does not.

**15. Documentation.** "Documented" is the stated mitigation for single-path direct-attach FC, unnotified NLM clients, SMB handle loss, ESXi NFS remount, the PERC attestation and the loss window, with no document named. Phase C needs the hardware guide (attestation, probe, "flush-opaque"), the client recipes (ESXi SATP rule and `PathEvalTime`, Proxmox empty `multipath.conf` and PVE 9.1 preconditions, Windows), per-protocol nvfail runbooks with the exact `otapctl` output, and the operations runbook (shutdown, upgrade, drive replacement, DR import). No exit test mentions any of them.

##### 2. Contradictions that survived the rebuttals

| # | Topic | Who says what | What must be decided |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | nvfail vocabulary and class defaults (D5) | Storage and Protocols: `{on, alert, off}` per class, plus Protocols' per-LUN `{pdl, strict}`; Consensus: `{hold, fence, off}`. File class: Storage `alert` (serve, CRIT), Protocols `on` (export withheld until clear), Consensus `fence` (serve at once under a new fsid). Root volume: Storage and Protocols `alert` plus content check, Consensus `fence`, Fabrics `hold` | One enum with the client-visible behaviour of each value written down, then the class table, presented to the owner once |
| 2 | Identity after an unplanned takeover | Storage, Protocols, Fabrics: `strict` (new serial and NAA) by default; Consensus: same identity for ESXi-only iSCSI LUNs after PDL, obtained by impersonating A's block LIF; Protocols: block LIFs never move | Whether impersonation exists in Phase B; `strict` until lab B7 |
| 3 | `Revert` versus rollback | Consensus: a held promotion is revertible, A resumes from its own head, B resyncs from K; Storage: the fenced old owner always rolls back to the common snapshot and becomes the receiver, and a superblock epoch below Raft's means `Divergent` | Storage must confirm B's held promotion writes nothing beyond the e+1 superblock and that `Revert{e+2}` names A owner without rollback, or Consensus drops `Revert` |
| 4 | Lag thresholds | Storage's Phase B inputs: warn 60 s, crit 600 s; Consensus: WARN at `insync_lag_max` sustained 30 s, CRIT at 60 s. `insync_lag_max` flash: Storage 15 s, Consensus 12 s (HDD agrees at 25 s) | One timer-table row each, `otap-ctl` owner (R7) |
| 5 | `max_auto_takeover_lag` | Storage "concedes 60 s for `max_auto_takeover_lag`"; Consensus deleted it and `TakeoverPending` in favour of always-promote with `nvfail_force_lag` | Adopt always-promote with posture and purge the old name from Storage's and Protocols' text |
| 6 | Send source and hold release | Storage 3.6: staged stripes sent with `SEND_ZC` plus `FIXED_BUF` from the hugetlbfs staging pool, freed on disk completion plus `NOTIF`; Fabrics: TLS mandatory through userspace rustls, the staging pool is never a send source, the 4 KiB-paged bounce is sent, holds release on `Landed` | Staging is the plaintext input to `encrypt()`; define the hold-release event (encrypted into the bounce, or `Landed` for retention); C25's truesize test then applies to the bounce only |
| 7 | ublk device size | Storage C10 and Fabrics F6: LUNs at advertised size, NAS at `size_max`, LUN growth by standby-first re-create; Consensus: "every ublk device is created at `size_max`" | Storage and Fabrics stand; fix Consensus's `ensure_standby` |
| 8 | NAS thick versus thin | R18 thick file volumes versus C10 `size_max` XFS on thin LUNs (section 1.8) | Reservation policy and what `df` reports |
| 9 | SVM slice memory, Phase C | Storage 34 GiB; Protocols "DRAM minus engine minus 4 GiB" (about 30 GiB); Consensus 36 GiB | Derive from Storage's 3.9 and delete the other two numbers |
| 10 | NFSv4 scope string and writer | Protocols: UTS nodename `<svm>.<cluster-uuid8>`, `nfsdctl autostart` reading the SVM's `nfs.conf`; Consensus: scope = SVM UUID via `genetlink` `THREADS_SET` from `nbladed` | Both work (C12, C14), but the scope is also `so_major_id` and must be identical on both nodes forever: one string, one writer |
| 11 | Throttle under a controller write-through window | Storage: R7's 2 s cap then Transitioning, cause named; Consensus's revised C3 covers a stall as a pause with `backstore_stall_tolerance` 60 s but not a multi-hour learn window where ingest exceeds a 150 to 300 MB/s drain | After Storage item 5: Transitioning flaps for hours (honest, R7) or a longer hold (breaks R7) |
| 12 | `--write-journal` on RAID6 | C21: the only in-md closure; Storage: strict full-stripe allocation suffices; Consensus Phase A: journal-or-refuse | Item 5's forced dirty-degraded test; a lost committed block makes the journal mandatory and drops the bitmap |
| 13 | NAS unplanned takeover time | Consensus: plus 2 to 5 s; Protocols: 15 to 60 s until replay is measured | Storage measures 20 volumes with 128 MiB logs, with and without receiver pre-replay |
| 14 | LIF MAC on takeover | Storage (cross-exam): per-(LIF, node) MACs with GARP; Protocols and Consensus: persistent MAC plus the `arping -D` gate | C2's wedged-node measurement |
| 15 | Receiver staging size | Storage's F7 answer: two segments (160 MiB); Storage's table: 2 GiB; Fabrics needs at least 64 MiB at 10GbE and 256 MiB at 25GbE | Storage states one number |
| 16 | Slot granularity | Consensus moved slots, leases and epochs to per-SVM; Storage's engine still checks a per-aggregate epoch at CP submit and superblock completion | Phase B needs a LUN-to-SVM-to-slot mapping in the ublk handler; Storage has not acknowledged it |
| 17 | nvfail set at promotion inside the lag bound | Storage: only volumes not provably idle; Consensus: class posture for every volume | Combine: class posture unless provably idle |

Resolved but still carried as open in someone's text: Fabrics' items 1 (Protocols accepted standby block paths), 3 (Consensus struck the arena owner) and 5 (Storage accepted per-group packing), and Consensus's "Fabrics says ship `queue`" (Fabrics withdrew it). The synthesis should delete these rather than re-argue them.

##### 3. Load-bearing claims still not CONFIRMED, and the interim rule
